If the tower is not dismantled and removed as required, the county may do so and assess the costs against the property for collection in the manner as a property tax.

Towers are a permitted conditional use in the Agricultural (A-1, A-2) district with height not exceeding 500 feet; height exceeding 500 feet requires a special exception, with total height not to exceed 150% of the maximum height permitted as a conditional use. This applies to wind turbine towers as part of wind farms, which are defined as connected wind turbine generators supplying electrical energy to the grid.
Any wind turbine within a wind farm shall be located not less than the total height from property lines abutting non-participating properties.

Any wind turbine within a wind farm shall be located not less than the total height from a road right-of-way line. TOTAL HEIGHT: The height from grade to the highest vertical point of the swept rotor arc. In the case of a wind turbine with a horizontal axis rotor, the total height includes the distance from grade to the rotor axis of rotation within the nacelle plus one-half the swept rotor diameter.

No commercial wind turbine shall be located at a distance less than 1,000 feet from the nearest occupied dwelling. Wind generator towers may be setback less than 1,000 feet from a dwelling if the property owner signs a waiver agreeing to the reduced setback distance. No commercial wind turbine shall be located less than 1,000 feet from the nearest occupied dwelling. Wind generator towers may be setback less than 1,000 feet from a dwelling if the property owner signs a waiver agreeing to the reduced setback distance. The setback distance with respect to property lines shall not apply to wind turbines located within a wind farm where the property line nearest to any given wind turbine define and separate properties belonging to two or more participating landowners. Any wind turbine within a wind farm may be located straddling the property lines separating two participating properties.

summary: Section 9 states: "WECS shall to the extent reasonably possible, use materials, color, and texture that will blend with the natural setting and existing environment. In the event of abandonment or discontinued use of one or more devices within the WECS, the owner/developer of the WECS shall be responsible for dismantling the abandoned or discontinued use WECS device(s) and returning the property to its original use. All abandoned or discontinued use WECS device(s) and accessory facilities for the abandoned or discontinued use WECS devices shall be removed within 180 days of the discontinuation of use. Each WECS project shall have a decommissioning plan outlining the anticipated means of removing the WECS devices upon the WECS device becoming a discontinued use. The WECS shall make the following financial assurances to the County: Financial Assurance may be in the form of cash deposited with County, a performance bond, or surety bond, as long as the form of the Financial Assurance is mutually agreeable between the County and the WECS and the security is equal to or greater than the net amount set forth in the Decommissioning Plan or provided for by this Article.

The maximum height for Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) projects requiring a conditional use permit is 600 feet measured from the base to the rotor tip in its highest position. Owner/developers seeking to construct a WECS height greater than 600 feet will require a variance from the Board of Adjustment and an independent review by a third party engineering firm.

Sound produced by any wind energy devices under normal operating conditions as measured at the exterior of the Human Occupied Dwelling nearest to the WECS shall not exceed 45 dBA, except during short term events out of anyone’s control such as utility outages and/or severe windstorms.

The Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) devices shall be set back a distance equal to 110% or 1.1 times the height of the WECS turbine from the base to the rotor tip in its highest position from the property lines, nor at any time shall any part of the wind turbine and meteorological tower overhang an adjoining property without securing appropriate easements from adjoining property owners.

The Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) is to be placed 1.1 times the height of the WECS turbine from the base to the rotor tip in its highest position from the nearest point of the public road right of way. This measurement to be taken from the center of the turbine base.

A report prepared by a qualified third-party using the most current modeling software available must establish that no Human Occupied Residence will experience more than thirty (30) hours per year, or more than thirty (30) minutes per day on average, of shadow flicker from the centroid of the Human Occupied Residence based on the assessment modeling.

Section 10 states: 'The WECS shall not be used for display of any advertising except for reasonable identification of the manufacturer or project owner/operator and any safety signs. Documentation showing any signage is required with the application.' This signage requirement applies to Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) projects requiring a conditional use permit as outlined in the ordinance.

All wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) projects shall be located only in the Agricultural (A-1) District under a conditional use permit. Applicants shall follow the procedures and requirements outlined herein. If a property owner in the A-1 Agricultural District requests to construct a single turbine on their property for primarily personal use, or if a WECS owner/developer requests to construct a meteorological tower, any requirements of this Section 5. D may be waived by the Board of Adjustment.

summary: The Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) is to be placed no less than the greater of two times the total height of the WECS turbine measured from the base to the rotor tip in its highest position, or 1200 feet, from any human occupied dwelling. A human occupied dwelling is defined as one capable of being occupied for residential purposes. The measurement between the dwelling and turbine is to be taken from the nearest point of the human occupied dwelling to the center of the turbine base.

The Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) is to be placed 1.1 times the height of the WECS turbine from the base to the rotor tip in its highest position from the overhead utility line or structure. This measurement to be taken from the center of the turbine base.

A general visual simulation of the project area is required at the time of application. This applies to all Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) projects located in the Agricultural (A-1) District under a conditional use permit. The WECS shall use materials, color, and texture that will blend with the natural setting and existing environment to the extent reasonably possible.

No WECS will be allowed on private lands within 1/8 mile (660') of lands and waters owned and/or managed or under control of the IDNR (subject to Dickinson County Board of Adjustment approval and the section 14 variance clause). This setback is intended to protect wildlife habitats and sensitive water quality areas near public lands and waters.

No blades may extend over parking areas, driveways, or sidewalks. No blade may extend within 20-feet of the nearest tree, structure, or above ground utility facilities.

All towers, poles, and anchor points must be unclimbable by design or protected by anti-climbing devices such as fences with locking portals at least 6-feet high or anti-climbing devices 12-feet from base of pole.

summary: All USWECS permit applications shall include a Decommissioning and Reclamation Plan that includes the anticipated start and completion dates and manner of decommissioning, projected decommissioning costs certified by an Iowa licensed engineer, and a method of ensuring funds will be available for site decommissioning and restoration. The plan shall be reviewed and approved by the Board of Supervisors and recorded as a binding agreement. The USWECS shall be removed if not operated for greater than 12 months or if the permit is revoked, with the project owner/operator required to provide sufficient surety to cover removal and disposal costs. Physical removal includes removal of systems 4-feet below ground and above, and restoration of the location to its natural condition. The Board of Supervisors may revoke permits and require removal within specified timeframes.
Lighting of towers is only allowed when required by the FAA. The lighting method allowed shall be an FAA approved dual lighting system.

Audible noise due to USWECS site operations shall not exceed fifty (50) dBA for any period of time, when measured at any residential dwelling, school, hospital, church, public library, or Iowa DNR regulated Animal Feeding Operation (AFO) existing on the date of approval of any Project permit. If the noise contains a steady pure tone, the standard is reduced by five (5) dBA. Ambient noise levels may adjust the standard to equal the ambient noise level. Waivers may be granted with written consent and recorded easements.

summary: USWECS shall be a minimum 1,320-feet or 115% of the tower and rotor height whichever is greater from any property lines and road right-of-way lines or residential dwellings not included in the USWECS application, or any public park and/or recreation property line with the following exceptions: Any public park or recreational land when approved by the appropriate County, State, or Federal administrative staff, boards, and/or commissions for a demonstrated public purpose.

The units for the annual limit are hours per year (hr/year).

All signs, both temporary and permanent, are prohibited on WECS, except as follows: Manufacturer’s identification on the wind turbine cowling; Appropriate warning signs and placards including visible warning sign of  "High Voltage"  placed at the base of all conversion systems with at a minimum 6-inch letters with ¾-inch stroke; Identifying name or logo of the owner/operator on the base of some project turbines may be approved by the zoning administrator.

Section 5-20 (Decommissioning and Reclamation) mandates restoration of the site and soil for agricultural use, including "restoration of the pre-construction surface grade and soil profile" and "re-vegetation of restored soil areas with crops, native seed mixes, plant species suitable to the area." These requirements apply explicitly to Utility Scale Wind Energy Conversion Systems (USWECS).

Section 4, subsection m states: 'Any commercial wind energy device tower must be designed to prevent climbing within the first ten feet (10’).' This is a clear and specific climbing prevention requirement applicable to commercial wind energy devices as defined in the ordinance.

Section 4(h) states: 'Any wind energy device shall remain painted or finished the color or finish that was originally applied by the manufacturer, unless approved in the special exception permit.' This requirement applies to commercial wind energy devices as defined in the ordinance.

Section 10. Discontinuance or Abandonment requires each application for a commercial wind energy device to have a decommissioning plan outlining the anticipated means and proposed financing methods adequate to remove such structure(s) upon becoming a discontinued use. Any commercial wind energy device that is out-of-service for a continuous one (1) year period will be deemed to have been abandoned and discontinued for use. At such time the wind energy device is determined to be abandoned, the owner shall remove the wind energy device at the owner’s expense within one (1) year of receipt of notice. If the owner fails to remove the wind energy device, the zoning administrator may pursue legal action against the owner of such wind energy devices.

Section 4, subsection g states: 'Any wind energy device shall not be artificially lighted unless such lighting is required by the Federal Aviation Administration.' This lighting requirement applies to Commercial Wind Energy Devices as defined in Section 3.b: 'any wind energy device with a nameplate capacity of more than 100kw of which its primary intent is to generate electrical power to be sold to utility or power companies.'

Section 4(a) states that commercial wind energy devices shall be limited to a total height of 250 feet within 1,250 feet of any residential zoned district. Outside of that proximity, no height limitations apply except for restrictions related to airport airspace.

Sound produced by any wind energy devices under normal operating conditions, as measured at the property line, shall not produce sound at a level that would constitute a nuisance. Industry standards support that wind energy noise should not exceed 50 dBA at a distance of 1,250 feet, the setback distance in Emmet County to a human occupied dwelling.

Commercial wind energy devices shall be set back a distance equal to 110% its total height from any public right of way, overhead utility lines or adjacent property lines not under the same ownership unless written consent is granted by the property owner or entity with jurisdiction over the street, utilities or adjacent properties.
section: Section 4. Wind Energy Requirements b. Setbacks.

summary: Commercial wind energy devices shall be set back a distance equal to 110% its total height from any public right of way. The total height is defined as the vertical distance from ground level to the tip of a wind generator blade when the tip is at its highest point.
section: Section 4. Wind Energy Requirements b. Setbacks.

summary: All signs shall be prohibited other than the manufacturer or installer’s identification sign and appropriate warning signs. Signs indicating the 911 rural addressing of each commercial wind energy device or grouping of multiple wind energy devices shall be placed at each wind energy device site and/or the entry points of access roads as per the Emmet County 911 rural addressing signage requirements.

summary: Section 5 states that commercial wind energy devices may be granted as a special exception and approved by the board of adjustment after a public hearing in any zoning district. Conditions or requirements for the special exception permit must not be more lenient than the wind energy requirements in Section 4 and must be clearly stated in the permit.

Commercial wind energy devices shall be setback a distance of no less than 1,250 feet from any human occupied dwelling. A human occupied dwelling is defined as one that is currently occupied or capable of being occupied for residential purposes. A greater setback may be required to minimize shadow flicker, nuisance noise, and other possible documented effects to humans living in these dwellings.

summary: Commercial wind energy devices shall be set back a distance equal to 110% its total height from any public right of way, overhead utility lines or adjacent property lines not under the same ownership unless written consent is granted by the property owner or entity with jurisdiction over the street, utilities or adjacent properties.

The text enacts a moratorium on accepting, approving applications, or issuing permits for utility-scale wind energy systems in Floyd County, Iowa. This moratorium has been extended multiple times and is currently in effect until October 7, 2025.
The ordinance explicitly requires that "From the lower tip of the blade to ground level must be 75 feet or greater" for commercial wind energy conversion systems (CWECS) in Franklin County.
All turbines and towers that are part of a commercial WECS shall be white or grey. Finishes shall be matte or non-reflective.

Section 6 titled "Discontinuance or Decommissioning" details the conditions under which a commercial WECS component is considered discontinued (e.g., one continuous year of non-operation or permit revocation) and mandates removal. Each building permit application must be accompanied by a decommissioning plan including: (1) Description of the project components and removal activities; (2) A report by a qualified third-party estimating net removal and restoration costs; (3) Cash, irrevocable letter of credit, or performance bond in an amount no less than the estimated costs; (4) Updates to the report at least every five years and upon transfer of the zoning permit; (5) No transfer or assignment of the zoning permit without corresponding transfer of obligations and financial security. Existing wind projects must submit a decommissioning plan within 12 months of the chapter's adoption.

Lighting, including lighting intensity and frequency of strobes, shall adhere to, but not exceed, requirements established by the FAA permits and regulations. Lighting shall have Airline Detection Lighting System (ADLS) or have applied for ADLS to be installed within 60 days of the application’s approval by the FAA.
The number of turbines is limited to 330 towers in the County. This is a clear maximum installation size restriction that an energy system developer must abide by.

Noise from a wind turbine may not exceed 45 decibels (dba) as measured from the closest setback distance, ground level to a residence. This provision directly sets a noise limit applicable to commercial wind turbines, as the entire chapter governs commercial WECS projects.

Wind energy conversion systems (WECS) are prohibited in all zoning districts within Franklin County. No person shall construct, operate, or locate a wind energy conversion system within the unincorporated areas of Franklin County. However, wind energy uses are limited to a conditional use in the Agricultural District, subject to supplemental standards and conditional use permits. The prohibition does not have an expiration date and applies generally except where conditional use permits are granted under the specified regulations.

Setbacks from adjacent property lines for Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems (CWECS) shall be 120% of the total height, measured from the center point of the tower to the nearest property line of any protected area.

Section 8 titled "Repowering" requires that prior to repowering any permitted WECS, the permit holder shall submit repowering plan(s) to the Zoning Administrator for review. The Zoning Administrator may issue a Certificate of Compliance if the repowering plan results in no material change in the components or design elements of the turbine originally permitted. If a plan to repower a permitted WECS materially changes any component(s) or design element(s) of the turbine, the permit holder must apply for a new Conditional Use Permit pursuant to Sections 70.07(3), (4), and (5). Repowering construction shall not be authorized in the absence of a Certificate of Compliance or Conditional Use Permit and issuance of building permits.

The setback distance from public road rights-of-way for Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems (CWECS) must be 120% of the total height of the turbine. "Public Road Right-of-Way 120% of the total height". Total height is defined as the highest point above ground level reached by a rotor tip or any other part of a turbine.

No dwelling will experience more than 25 hours per year, and no more than 30 minutes per day, of shadow flicker from the centroid of the dwelling caused by the individual turbines in the project. This limit applies to commercial wind energy conversion systems (CWECS).

All turbine sites shall be required to have individual 911 rural addresses at each access road. All other signs except those required for safety and directional purposes (or otherwise authorized by the County) shall be prohibited in the project area.

Commercial wind energy conversion systems are permitted as a conditional use in the Agricultural District. A Conditional Use Permit is required for each individual structure (tower) and must be approved prior to seeking any building permits. Wind energy uses are limited to a conditional use in the Agricultural District. The permit application requires submission of a site plan and compliance with supplemental standards and County ordinances.

The setback from any dwelling or occupied non-residential building for Commercial wind energy conversion systems (CWECS) is 1,900 feet or three times the total height of the turbine, whichever is greater. For agricultural operation buildings, the setback is 120% of the total height. All measurements are from the center point of the tower to the nearest point on any dwelling or occupied non-residential building.

The ordinance requires that the application for a Conditional Use Permit for a commercial wind energy conversion system include "a report prepared by a qualified third-party acceptable to the Board using the most current modeling software available establishing that no dwelling will experience more than 25 hours per year, and no more than 30 minutes per day, of shadow flicker from the centroid of the dwelling based on a 'real world' or 'adjusted case' assessment modeling." The report must show the locations and estimated amount of shadow flicker caused by the turbines, and the applicant must specify a shadow flicker control system if limits are exceeded.

Wind ordinances often include a provision requiring the project owner to take responsibility for and bear the costs of decommissioning at the end of a wind project’s useful life. The following recent example is from Poweshiek County’s ordinance, updated in March of 2017: Discontinuation and Decommissioning. A C-WECS shall be considered a discontinued use after one (1) year without energy production, unless a plan is developed and submitted to the Zoning Administrator outlining the steps and schedule for returning the C-WECS to service. All C-WECS and accessory facilities shall be removed to a depth of four (4) feet below ground level within one year of discontinuation of use. 1. Decommissioning Plan. Each C-WECS shall have a Decommissioning Plan outlining the anticipated means and cost of removing the C-WECS at the end of their serviceable life or upon becoming a discontinued use. The cost estimates shall be made by a professional engineer licensed in the State of Iowa. The plan shall also identify the financial resources that will be available to pay for the decommissioning and removal of the C-WECS and accessory facilities. 2. Decommissioning Fund. Commencing on the fifteenth (15th) year after commencement of commercial operations, and annually thereafter, the operator shall continuously maintain a financial assurance mechanism(s) in the form of performance bond, letter of credit, and/or other security approved by the County Attorney, for the remaining life of the facility. The amount of the security shall be equal to the total decommissioning cost, net of reasonable residual value of the C-WECS, as determined by a professional engineer licensed in the State of Iowa.

Setbacks from non-participating property lines, lot lines, facility perimeters, parcels, and/or subdivisions for large wind energy systems are generally expressed as the greater of a fixed minimum distance or a multiplier of the turbine's total height. For example, Dickinson County requires the "greater distance of 1,200 feet or 2x total height of turbine," while Madison, Poweshiek, and Story counties require the "greater distance of 1,000 feet or 2x total height of turbine." Additionally, some counties specify that turbines "may not overhang adjacent property lines without securing appropriate easements" (Dickinson County) or require setbacks "not less than the rotor radius from non-participating properties" (Carroll and Greene counties). These provisions establish a minimum threshold setback distance that must be met in all cases, ensuring safety and minimizing impacts to non-participating landowners.

Setbacks for property lines and other rights of way should be approximately 1.1 times the turbine height, or about 600 feet. Most counties also have specified minimum setbacks for roads and other public rights of way; mandated setbacks for these categories of property are generally either identical or comparable to the setbacks described above for property lines.

Counties require the largest setback distances for turbines from residential dwellings and human-occupied buildings (e.g., schools and hospitals). Most ordinances’ required setbacks from these structures are in the range of 1,000 to 1,250 feet. It is crucial that counties establish setbacks for such structures that will protect occupants from unlikely but hazardous events such as the collapse of a turbine tower or the  "throwing"  of a turbine blade. Therefore, a minimum setback of 1,000 feet from occupied structures is recommended for safety purposes. The setback distance is often expressed as the greater of 1,000 feet or a multiple of the turbine height, e.g., 'greater distance of 1,000 feet or 2x total height of turbine.' Waivers or negotiated setbacks may be allowed, but the minimum threshold remains to protect public safety and quality of life.

Any proposed wind turbine shall be set back a minimum of three hundred percent (300%) the height of the wind turbine from any property line. For property line waivers, this form shall be accompanied by a current survey approved by the Latah County Surveyor of the property line relevant to the setback. This form shall be recorded in the Latah County Recorder's Office by the Planning Department.

Any proposed wind turbine shall be set back a minimum of three hundred percent (300%) the height of the wind turbine from any public road, public right-of-way. Setbacks from any public road or public right-of-way shall not be waived.

A warning sign no larger than three (3) square feet and no smaller than two (2) square feet must be placed on the fencing access/gate. It must contain the name of the owner and operator of the facility, and a phone number for cases of emergency as well as any other information required by law.

The ordinance states that "Commercial, multiple residential, or other wind turbine" uses "may be permitted by the Zoning Commission upon the issuance of a conditional use permit as provided by chapter 9-7A of this title." It outlines detailed application requirements, conditions, and considerations for approval, including setbacks, noise reduction, easements, and compliance with other laws. The Zoning Commission has discretion to impose additional conditions and to waive certain setbacks with property owner consent. Building permits are required for each wind turbine and repairs. The ordinance also addresses removal and abandonment procedures for wind turbines. No specific zoning districts or abbreviations are mentioned in the text for these uses.

Any proposed wind turbine shall be set back a minimum of three hundred percent (300%) the height of the wind turbine from any residential, public, or commercial structure. At a minimum, the wind turbine shall be at least one thousand feet (1,000') away from any residential, public, or commercial structures.

The Board of County Commissioners declares an emergency moratorium upon the issuance of permits and zoning approvals for Large-Scale Energy Projects, defined as projects capable of producing 10 megawatts (MW) or more, or projects that encumber 5 or more acres of land, or structural improvements exceeding 60 feet in height that produce power via wind, solar, or other energy forms. No expiration date is provided for this moratorium.

The tip of the blade shall be, at its slowest point, have a ground clearance of no less than 75 feet. Additionally, the minimum distance between the ground and any part of the rotor blade system shall be 75 feet.

Commercial Wind Turbines shall not be climbable up to fifteen (15) feet above ground level. All access doors to the Wind Turbine Towers and electrical equipment shall be lockable and locked when unattended.
Commercial Wind Turbines shall be painted a non-reflective, non-obtrusive color.

Section 10.5.8 requires an appropriate continuous renewal bond amount with a minimum amount of one million dollars ($1,000,000) for each Commercial Wind Turbine for decommissioning should the owner/operator fail to comply with this Chapter’s requirements or the Commercial Wind Turbine does not operate for a period of 12 consecutive months. The bond must be active for the life of the Commercial Wind Turbine project.

Lighting: Shall not be artificially lighted, except to the extent required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) or other applicable authority. During the night time and overcast daytime conditions, strobe lighting may be required to satisfy tower facility lighting requirements for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).
Section 10.4.4 states: 'Height: Tower height cannot exceed 150 300 feet.' The most restrictive maximum turbine height allowed for Commercial Wind Turbines is 150 feet.

Property Line: Three (3) times its total height from the nearest property line unless mitigation has taken place and agreed by owner/operator and affected property owners involved and recorded in the Madison County Recorder’s Office which describes the benefited and burdened properties and which advises all subsequent owners of the burdened property.
Each Commercial Wind Turbine shall comply with the following requirements: Railroads: Two (2) times its total height from all railroads and right-of-ways.
Each Commercial Wind Turbine shall comply with the following requirement for Public Roads: One and a half (1.5) plus 100 feet times the total height from the nearest public road and right-of-way.
Section 10.4.13 states: 'Appropriate warning signage shall be in place on all Commercial Wind Turbine Towers, electrical equipment and facility entrances.'

Each Commercial Wind Turbine shall be set back one (1) mile from the nearest existing residence, school, church, hospital, place of employment or public library (facility), unless mitigation has taken place and agreed by owner/operator and affected property owners involved and recorded in the Madison County Recorder’s Office.

Section 10.4.2 states: 'Commercial Wind Turbines shall have a minimum separation distance of two (2) times the total height of the tallest Commercial Wind Turbine tower from other Commercial Wind Turbines.' The units are expressed as a multiplier of the turbine's total height (tip height).

Each Commercial Wind Turbine shall comply with the following requirements: Communication and Electrical Lines: Two (2) times the total height from the nearest above-ground public electric line or telephone line.

Commercial Wind Generating Facilities shall provide a digital elevation model-based project visibility map showing the impact of topography upon visibility of the project from other locations throughout the region, to a distance of five (5), ten (10) and twenty (20) miles from the center of the project. Color photographs taken from several locations within a five (5), ten (10) and twenty (20) mile radius of the boundaries of the commercial facility site shall be provided and computer enhanced to simulate the appearance of the as-built above ground site facilities as such would appear from said locations.
The tip of a blade shall, at its lowest point, have a ground clearance of no less than fifty feet (50').
section: 7-2-8: LARGE (COMMERCIAL) TURBINE SYSTEM AND WIND FARMS

summary: All wind turbines shall not be climbable on the exterior up to fifteen feet (15') above ground level.

The wind turbine system shall remain painted or finished the color or finish that was originally applied by the manufacturer, unless other nonreflective, nonobtrusive colors or finishes (colors that blend with the natural landscape or background) are approved in writing by the administrator.

Applicants are required to hold a performance bond, completion bond, decommissioning bond or other financial assurance with an A rated firm in the amount of five percent (5%) of the WTS's/tower's value. Applicants are required to present, with their application, a detailed decommissioning and reclamation plan, in accordance with state and federal law. The owner/operator of large (commercial) WTS or wind farms is responsible for removing the wind turbines and related facilities when no longer useful. They must remove the turbines and facilities within two (2) years of the end of electricity generation, unless a new plan is proposed to reuse the turbine(s). Reclamation shall be restored to its original state as was before the WTS/wind energy facility site construction. All decommissioning requirements transfer with ownership of the WTS/turbine(s) or ownership of the WTS/wind facility.
section: 7-2-8: LARGE (COMMERCIAL) TURBINE SYSTEM AND WIND FARMS

summary: WTS exterior shall not be artificially lit, except to the extent required by the federal aviation administration (FAA) or other applicable authority.

WTS shall be located with relation to property lines so that the level of noise produced during any wind turbine operation shall not exceed sixty five (65) dBA, measured at the boundaries of all adjacent parcels that are owned by adjoining property owners or at any point past the property line of the lot on which the turbine is to be erected. This level may only be exceeded during short term events such as utility outages and/or severe windstorms.

Large (commercial) WTS and wind farms will be permitted in agricultural heavy and outlying zones only, and by special use permit only, upon demonstration to the county building department and county planning and zoning commission of compliance with all of the performance standards. All large (commercial) WTS and wind farm projects shall require a special use permit, subject to public hearing by the county planning and zoning commission.
section: 7-2-8: LARGE (COMMERCIAL) TURBINE SYSTEM AND WIND FARMS

summary: Towers or other structures associated with the large (commercial) WTS or wind farm project shall be set back from the external boundaries of the project property a distance of not less than one and one-half (1.5) times the total overall height of the tallest structure. For purposes of this calculation, overall height shall include total tower height, plus total blade length.
section: 7-2-8: LARGE (COMMERCIAL) TURBINE SYSTEM AND WIND FARMS

summary: Towers or other structures associated with the large (commercial) WTS or wind farm project shall be set back from the external boundaries of the project property a distance of not less than one and one-half (1.5) times the total overall height of the tallest structure. For purposes of this calculation, overall height shall include total tower height, plus total blade length. A siting permit shall be obtained from the county building department ensuring compliance with this setback requirement.
section: 7-2-8: LARGE (COMMERCIAL) TURBINE SYSTEM AND WIND FARMS

summary: Section 7-2-5(J) states: 'WTS shall not be used for displaying any advertising, except for reasonable identification of the manufacturer, installer or operator. Any such identification shall not appear on the blades or other moving parts or exceed six (6) square feet. All signs, other than the manufacturer's or installer's identification, appropriate warning signs, or owner identification on a wind turbine, tower, building or other structure associated with a WTS visible from any public road shall be prohibited.' Section 7-2-5(O) requires: 'Appropriate warning signage shall be placed on all wind turbine towers, electrical equipment and facility entrances warning of high voltage and cautionary instructions to unauthorized persons to stay away from such structures.'

Large (commercial) WTS and wind farms will be permitted in agricultural heavy and outlying zones only, and by special use permit only, upon demonstration to the county building department and county planning and zoning commission of compliance with all of the performance standards. All large (commercial) WTS and wind farm projects shall require a special use permit, subject to public hearing by the county planning and zoning commission.
section: 7-2-8: LARGE (COMMERCIAL) TURBINE SYSTEM AND WIND FARMS

summary: The tip of a blade shall, at its lowest point, have a ground clearance of no less than seventy five feet (75').

Section K requires applicants to hold a decommissioning bond or other financial assurance with an A rated firm in the amount of five percent (5%) of the tower's value. A detailed decommissioning and reclamation plan in accordance with state and federal law must be provided. The owner/operator of commercial wind energy facilities is responsible for removing the wind turbines and related facilities when no longer useful, within three (3) years of the end of electricity generation unless a new plan is proposed to reuse the turbines. Reclamation shall be restored to its original state before wind energy facility site construction.

Towers or other structures associated with the wind farm project shall be set back from the external boundaries of the project property a distance of not less than one and one-half (1½) times the total overall height of the tallest structure. For purposes of this calculation, overall height shall include total tower height plus total blade length. If the external boundary is along a public road right of way, this setback applies directly; if not, an easement may be obtained from the adjoining landowner to meet this distance.

Wind farms, commercial and large turbines and associated structures; allowed by special use permit in agricultural zones only. All commercial wind farm projects shall require a special use permit, subject to public hearing by the planning and zoning commission. Special use permits granted for commercial wind farms will be valid for two (2) years from the issuance of the permit, with extensions available in one year increments upon a showing of reasonable cause for the extension.

Commercial generating facilities shall provide a digital elevation model based project visibility map showing the impact of topography upon visibility of the project from other locations throughout the region, to a distance of five (5) miles from the center of the project.
The turbine or tower shall not be illuminated.
section: 44. Wind Energy System (A-20, A-2.5, C-1, C-2, C-3, M-1)

summary: The tower (pole) shall not be taller than 60 feet determined from the grade of the fixed portion of the tower, excluding the turbine, where a system is visible from the nearest county road or state highway and not located on a ridgeline.
section: 44. Wind Energy System (A-20, A-2.5, C-1, C-2, C-3, M-1)

summary: There shall be no more than one (1) wind energy system per parcel, effectively limiting the maximum project size or total installation allowed for Wind Farm to one system per parcel.
Minimum parcel size shall be 2.5 acres for Wind Energy Systems, which are defined as networks of densely arranged, high speed, wind turbines for generating electricity.
section: 44. Wind Energy System (A-20, A-2.5, C-1, C-2, C-3, M-1)

summary: Sound produced by the turbine under normal operation conditions shall not exceed 60 decibels at the property boundary (sound levels may be exceeded during short-term events such as utility outages or severe windstorms).
section: 44. Wind Energy System (A-20, A-2.5, C-1, C-2, C-3, M-1)

summary: The system shall be set back a minimum of the tower height plus the length of one blade (i.e. the turbine’s total height) from a property boundary. Tower supports (i.e. guy anchors), if any, shall be at least ten (10) feet from any property boundary. There shall be no more than one (1) wind energy system per parcel; and minimum parcel size shall be 2.5 acres.
section: 44. Wind Energy System (A-20, A-2.5, C-1, C-2, C-3, M-1)

summary: The system shall be set back a minimum of the tower height plus the length of one blade (i.e. the turbine’s total height) from a property boundary, utility line, or road right-of-way.
section: 44. Wind Energy System (A-20, A-2.5, C-1, C-2, C-3, M-1)

summary: Wind Farm is permitted as a Conditional Use (CU) in the A-20 district. Wind Energy Systems are Permitted with Conditions (PC) in A-20, A-2.5, C-1, C-2, C-3, and M-1 districts. "Wind farms and commercial wind turbines are subject to individual review within a required conditional use permit review." Conditions include submitting a site plan, architectural rendering, engineering drawings, setbacks, sound limits, and other requirements. Off-grid systems may be exempt from some requirements, but interconnected systems require utility notification and permitting. No more than one wind energy system per parcel and minimum parcel size is 2.5 acres.
The system shall be set back a minimum of the tower height plus the length of one blade (i.e. the turbine’s total height) from a property boundary, utility line, or road right-of-way;
section: 44. Wind Energy System (A-20, A-2.5, C-1, C-2, C-3, M-1)

summary: Utility-grade wind projects (wind projects with a total nameplate capacity of more than twenty (20) kilowatts) must be designed so that, at the closest point, the sweep of the blades is at least twenty (20) feet above the tallest existing or foreseeable obstruction to blade movement.

Utility-grade wind projects (wind projects with a total nameplate capacity of more than twenty (20) kilowatts) must be designed to minimize visual impact by "using turbine towers of uniform design, color and height" and "using the minimum lighting necessary for safety and security purposes in addition to aviation warning lights required by federal or state law" with techniques to prevent casting glare. Additionally, the project must "use materials and colors that blend with the background unless otherwise required by the Federal Aviation Administration."

Section 8-8B-5, subsection N ('Termination and Decommissioning') requires the applicant to submit a plan that ensures the site will be restored to a useful, non-hazardous condition without significant delay when operations cease. The plan must include removal of aboveground and underground equipment and foundations, restoration of surface grade and soil, revegetation with native seed mixes, protection of public health and safety, and a schedule for completion. Prior to permit issuance, a performance bond equal to 125% of the estimated restoration cost must be provided. If the project ceases operation or construction is not completed in a reasonable time, the landowner must restore the site according to an approved plan. These requirements apply to utility-scale wind projects (wind projects with a total nameplate capacity of more than twenty (20) kilowatts).
section: 8-8B-5: GENERAL STANDARDS FOR OTHER ENERGY PROJECTS

summary: The proposed wind energy project has been designed so that all aboveground parts of the nearest wind turbine structure are set back from the property line by a distance that is at least one hundred twenty-five (125) percent of the height of the wind turbine structure, including the rotor-swept area, except when the wind energy project extends onto the abutting property.

The ordinance explicitly states in 8-8B-5 L. that within the energy project site, the applicant agrees not to erect billboards (off-premises signs). Allowed on-premises signs include: 1. Signs required for public or employee safety or otherwise required by law. 2. No more than two signs which comply with the requirements of Article 8I. 3. Other signs specifically approved in the conditional use permit. These signage requirements apply to utility-scale wind turbine projects (wind projects with a total nameplate capacity of more than twenty (20) kilowatts) as part of the general standards for other energy projects.
section: 8-8B-5: GENERAL STANDARDS FOR OTHER ENERGY PROJECTS

summary: Section 8-8B-5.E requires the applicant to have an NPDES permit and an erosion and sediment control plan before beginning construction. The plan must include both general  "best management practices"  for erosion control during and after construction and permanent drainage and erosion control measures to prevent damage to local roads or adjacent areas and to minimize sediment run-off into waterways. Section 8-8B-6.A.1.e requires minimizing the amount of land used for new roads and locating roads to reduce visual impact and other adverse environmental impacts, such as erosion. Section 8-8B-8.A.10 requires a drainage and erosion control plan for construction and operation.
section: 8-8B-5: GENERAL STANDARDS FOR OTHER ENERGY PROJECTS

summary: Wind power generation projects exceeding a single wind turbine with a nameplate capacity of twenty or fewer kilowatts are listed as conditional uses requiring a conditional use permit and approval by the Commission. For example, 8-6A-3(V) states: 'Power generation projects (other than a single wind turbine with a nameplate capacity of twenty or fewer kilowatts...)' may be granted a conditional use permit. Similar language appears in 8-6C-3(4) and 8-6D-3(O). Principal allowed uses consistently limit wind turbines to a single turbine of twenty or fewer kilowatts.

The ordinance requires that utility-scale wind turbine projects (with a total nameplate capacity of more than twenty (20) kilowatts) must reduce visual impact to the extent practical by methods including avoiding scenic areas, using natural topography or vegetation to obscure views, setting back the project from public rights-of-way, using underground electric collection lines, uniform turbine design, minimizing lighting, and minimizing new roads. The conditional use permit application must include maps showing physical features and land uses before and after construction to support visual impact assessment.
section: 8-8B-5 GENERAL STANDARDS FOR OTHER ENERGY PROJECTS and 8-8B-6 STANDARDS FOR UTILITY-SCALE WIND PROJECTS

summary: All WECS Towers must be unclimbable by design or protected by anti-climbing devices such as: a. Fences with locking portals at least ten (10) feet high in A1 zoning district or the maximum allowed in other zoning districts; or b. Anti-climbing devices fifteen (15) feet vertically from the base of the WECS Tower.
Towers and blades shall be painted white or gray or another non-reflective, unobtrusive color.

The Applicant must formulate a Decommissioning and Site Reclamation Plan to ensure that the Commercial Wind Energy Facility is properly decommissioned. The Plan shall be binding upon the Applicant and its successors-in-interest and assigns, and shall apply to all participating parcels. A signed Plan must be submitted prior to the granting of the Special Use Permit. The Applicant shall ensure decommissioning within twelve (12) months of the end of the Facility life, including removal of all physical material to a depth of sixty (60) inches beneath the soil surface and restoration in accordance with the Agricultural Impact Mitigation Agreement. The Plan shall include: methodology and cost to remove all above and below ground WECS facilities; provisions for removal; methodology and cost to restore all areas to pre-construction condition; work schedule and permit list; methodology to manage hazardous materials; and submission of Financial Security equal to the total cost minus salvage value. Financial Security shall be phased in over the first eleven (11) years of the project, reaching 100% by the eleventh anniversary of Commercial Operation Date. Provisions trigger decommissioning upon inactivity, abandonment, disrepair, or failure to pay landowners. The County has rights to access the site and financial assurances to ensure decommissioning. Failure to comply may result in revocation of the Special Use Permit.
section: DECOMMISSIONING AND SITE RECLAMATION PLAN REQUIRED

summary: WECS Projects shall utilize minimal lighting that is compliant with the applicable FAA regulations, as amended by the FAA. To the extent that such tower lighting is available, and is approved by the FAA for a WECS Project, the Applicant shall install Aircraft Detection Lighting Systems ("ADLS") or other similar technology to reduce light pollution and visual impacts caused by the WECS Towers.

Boundary Lines of Nonparticipating Property: 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest point on the property line of the nonparticipating property. The setback distances are measured from the center of the base of the WECS Tower. The largest applicable multiplier from property lines, lot lines, facility perimeters, parcels, and/or subdivisions is 2.1 times the maximum blade tip height. No static distance value is added to the multiplier result.

WECS Towers shall be sited as follows, with setback distances measured from the center of the base of the WECS Tower; Public Road Rights-of-Way: 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the center point of the public road right-of-way. The setback requirements may be waived by the written consent of the owner(s) of each affected property.

The Applicant shall appropriately demonstrate to the County Board through industry standard modeling that no occupied community building or non-participating residence will experience an expected duration of 30 hours or more per year of shadow flicker. An occupied community building owner or a non-participating residence owner may waive this shadow flicker mitigation requirement by executing a written waiver filed with the Boone County Clerk and Recorder's Office against title to the affected real property.
A reasonably visible warning sign concerning voltage shall be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations, and at all entrances to Wind Towers.

The ordinance explicitly enacts soil, erosion, and sediment control requirements for Commercial Wind Energy Facilities (≥ 0.5 MW) in Boone County. It requires submission of soil and geotechnical boring reports for each WECS Tower location, following guidelines from the County Soil and Water Conservation District; submission of grading plans for proposed substations for review and comment by the County Soil and Water Conservation District prior to issuance of any WECS Building Permit; annual soil testing at turbine sites with remediation if contaminants are found; repair of all waterways, drainage ditches, agricultural drainage systems, field tiles, or other infrastructure damaged during construction, maintenance, and operation phases in accordance with the Agricultural Impact Mitigation Agreement; a soil erosion control plan approved by the Boone County Soil and Water Conservation District as part of the Decommissioning and Site Reclamation Plan; and compliance with all applicable stormwater management, floodplain, and other surface water rules, regulations, and ordinances.
section: 4.8.6 DESIGN AND INSTALLATION; 4.8.7 OPERATION; 4.8.9 DECOMMISSIONING AND SITE RECLAMATION PLAN REQUIRED

summary: Participating Residences: 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure;

For Overhead Communication and Electric Transmission and Distribution Facilities (Not Including Overhead Utility Service Lines to Individual Houses or Outbuildings), the required setback is 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest edge of the property line, easement, or right of way containing the overhead line. Overhead Utility Service Lines to Individual Houses or Outbuildings require no setback.

The ordinance requires a Special Use Permit application containing a WECS Project Summary with details such as maximum height of the WECS Tower(s) and maximum diameter of the WECS(s) rotor(s), a site plan showing planned locations of each WECS Tower and surrounding features, and other information necessary to evaluate the siting application and operation of the WECS Project. It includes aesthetic standards to mitigate visual impact, such as painting towers and blades white or gray or another non-reflective, unobtrusive color, and utilizing minimal lighting compliant with FAA regulations. The Applicant must present a model study on potential shadow flicker demonstrating that no occupied community building or non-participating residence will experience an expected duration of 30 hours or more per year, with waivers possible by affected property owners.
section: 4.8.5 SPECIAL USE PERMIT APPLICATION; 4.8.6 DESIGN AND INSTALLATION; 4.8.7 OPERATION

summary: All WECS Towers must be unclimbable by design or protected by anti-climbing devices such as: a. Fences with locking portals at least six feet high; or b. Anti-climbing devices 12 feet vertically from the base of the WECS Tower. All WECS facilities will have a maximum height not to exceed 450 feet.
section: VI. DESIGN AND INSTALLATION, G. Climb Prevention

summary: Towers and blades shall be painted white or gray or another non-reflective, unobtrusive color.

Prior to receiving siting approval under this Ordinance, the County and the Applicant, Owner, and/or Operator must formulate a Decommissioning Plan to ensure that the WECS Project is properly decommissioned. The Decommissioning Plan shall include: Provisions describing the triggering events for decommissioning the WECS Project; Provisions for the removal of structures, debris and cabling, including those below the soil surface; Provisions for the restoration of the soil and vegetation; An estimate of the decommissioning costs certified by a Professional Engineer; Financial Assurance, secured by the Owner or Operator, for the purpose of adequately performing decommissioning, in an amount equal to the Professional Engineer’s certified estimate of the decommissioning costs; or $50,000.00 whichever is greater; Identification of and procedures for County access to Financial Assurances; A provision that the terms of the Decommissioning Plan shall be binding upon the Owner or Operator and any of their successors, assigns, or heirs; and A provision that the County shall have access to the site, pursuant to reasonable notice, to effect or complete decommissioning.
All WECS facilities will have a maximum height not to exceed 450 feet, as explicitly stated in the ordinance. The unit of measurement for this height restriction is feet.
All WECS Towers shall be set back a distance of at least 1.10 times the WECS Tower height from adjacent property lines. The affected adjacent property owner may waive this setback requirement.

All WECS Towers shall be set back a distance of at least 1.10 times the WECS Tower Height from public roads. WECS Tower Height means the distance from the rotor blade at its highest point to the top surface of the WECS foundation. The maximum height of WECS facilities will not exceed 450 feet.
section: VI. DESIGN AND INSTALLATION, H. Setbacks

summary: All WECS Towers shall be set back at least 2000 feet from any Primary Structure. The owner of the Primary Structure may waive this setback requirement; but in no case shall a WECS Tower be located closer to a Primary Structure than 1.10 times the WECS Tower Height. The distance for the setback is measured from the point of the Primary Structure foundation closest to the WECS Tower to the center of the WECS Tower foundation.
section: VI. DESIGN AND INSTALLATION, H. Setbacks

summary: Wind Towers must be unclimbable by design or protected by anti-climbing devices.
Non-reflective, unobtrusive colors shall be used. Black blades are acceptable for mitigation of icing. Wind Towers shall also be consistent in color and direction with nearby facilities.

The Conditional Use permit(s) application shall include a Decommissioning Plan. The Decommissioning Plan shall be a plan prepared by a professional engineer licensed in the State of Illinois, at the Facility Owner’s expense, which includes: (a) the estimated deconstruction cost per Wind Tower, in current dollars at the time of filing, for the Facility, taking into account, among other things: (1) the number of Wind Towers and related items which make up the Facility, (2) the original construction costs of the Facility, (3) the size and capacity of the Wind Towers, (4) the salvage value of the Commercial Wind Energy Facility, and (5) the construction method and techniques for the Wind Towers and related items that make up the Facility; and (b) a comprehensive detailed description of how the Facility Owner plans to pay for the deconstruction of the Commercial Wind Energy Facility. Decommissioning shall include removal of all structures and debris to a depth of five feet (5’), restoration of the soil, and restoration of vegetation (consistent and compatible with surrounding vegetation) within eighteen (18) months after the end of useful life of the Facility or abandonment of the Facility. The Decommissioning Plan shall also recite an agreement between the Facility Owner and the County that the financial assurance for decommissioning shall be deposited in a cash escrow account with an escrow agent acceptable to the Zoning Enforcing Officer. The financial assurance shall be phased in over the first 11 years of the Commercial Wind Energy Facility’s operation. The County may reevaluate the estimated costs of deconstruction after the tenth anniversary and every five years thereafter. The County shall have access to the escrow account funds to complete decommissioning if the Facility Owner fails to do so within eighteen (18) months after the end of the useful life or abandonment. The Decommissioning and Site Restoration Plan must be approved and adopted by the County Board prior to approval of any Conditional Use permit(s) related to the Facility. If a Conditional Use permit(s) is granted, the Facility Owner shall file a second Decommissioning Plan on or before the end of the tenth year of the Commercial Operation Date.

A Facility shall utilize minimal lighting that is compliant with applicable FAA regulations (as amended by the FAA from time-to-time). To the extent that such Wind Tower lighting is available, and is approved by the FAA, the Facility Owner shall install Aircraft Detection Lighting Systems ("ADLS") or other similar technology to reduce light pollution and visual impacts caused by the Facility.

Setbacks from property lines, lot lines, facility perimeters, parcels, and subdivisions for Commercial Wind Energy Facilities are specified as multiples of the maximum blade tip height of the wind tower. For example, setbacks from nonparticipating property lines are 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height, setbacks from fish and wildlife areas are 2.1 times the maximum blade tip height, and setbacks from unincorporated platted communities or rural subdivisions are fixed distances measured from the tower base to the subdivision perimeter. Distances are generally measured from the center of the base of the wind tower. No static distance value is added to these multipliers.

The setback distance from public road rights-of-way for Commercial Wind Energy Facilities is 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the wind tower, measured to the center point of the public road right-of-way. Unless otherwise noted, distance shall be measured from the center of the base of the Wind Tower. A Variation of the setback requirement may be granted for little-used public roads.

The Facility Owner must conduct shadow flicker modeling and analysis to demonstrate that any occupied community building or nonparticipating residence will not experience more than 30 hours per year of shadow flicker under planned operating conditions. Post-construction analysis must also confirm compliance with this 30 hr/year limit, with violations subject to enforcement unless waived in writing by affected property owners.

The Facility Owner, at its expense, shall provide soil boring reports to the County Engineer with respect to each Wind Tower location, as part of its building permit application. The Facility Owner shall follow the guidelines for Conservation Practices Impact Mitigation submitted by the Bureau County Soil and Water Conservation District. Also, the grading plans for the proposed substations must be approved by the Bureau County Soil and Water Conservation District prior to the issuance of any building permit for the construction of proposed substations.

Setback distances for Commercial Wind Energy Facilities are measured as a multiple of the maximum blade tip height of the wind tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure. Specifically, setbacks are 2.1 times the maximum blade tip height for occupied community buildings and nonparticipating residences, and 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height for participating residences.
Setback from participating residences is 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the wind tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure.

Setback distance from overhead communication and electric transmission and distribution facilities must be 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the wind tower to the nearest edge of the property line, easement, or right of way containing the overhead line (excluding overhead utility service lines to individual houses or outbuildings). Projects shall utilize minimal lighting. No exterior tower lighting other than normal security lighting shall be permitted except as may be required by the FAA. Section 2.16 requires a written restoration (decommissioning) agreement with Henry County and/or property owner, with performance/surety bonds or other financial assurance documents to guarantee restoration before a building permit can be issued.

If more than one lighting alternative is available, the alternative that causes the least visual disturbance must be used.

Additionally, no CWEF shall be installed within the County unless all decommissioning agreements have been entered into with each applicable governmental agency and all required financial assurances have been posted and provided to the County or applicable governmental agency.

The applicant shall apply for an Aircraft Detection Lighting System ("ADLS") or other similar technology to reduce light pollution and visual impacts caused by the CWEF. section: VIII. BUILDING PERMIT REQUIREMENTS, K. Lighting

summary: Setback distances shall be measured beginning from the center of the base of a wind turbine or meteorological tower. A minimum setback of 2.1 times the maximum blade tip height to the nearest point on the property line of protected land (Fish and Wildlife Areas and Illinois Nature Preserve Commission Protected Lands) applies. For boundary lines of nonparticipating property, a minimum setback of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height to the nearest point on the property line is required.
Public Road Rights-of-Way: A minimum setback of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height to the center point of the public road right-of-way line.
Shadow flicker shall not affect any occupied community building or nonparticipating residence more than 30 hours per year under planned operating conditions.

A 9-1-1 warning sign which conforms to the specifications of the Iroquois County Zoning Ordinance for size, color and reflectivity shall be placed and maintained by the facility owner at the entrance to each wind turbine access road from a public road. A sign or posting no more than four square feet in area shall be placed and maintained in conjunction with, but in a subordinate position of, that same 9-1-1 sign, and shall provide the tower numbers and a toll-free telephone number, answered by a person 24 hours a day, seven days a week, for emergency calls and informational inquiries. A 9-1-1 compliant, visible warning sign concerning voltage must be affixed to any fencing at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and supporting facilities. Warning signs identifying underground wire locations shall be placed at all road crossings, creek, waterway, and ditch crossings, and at the base of wind turbines and supporting facilities. No wind turbine or meteorological tower sites shall include any advertising signage or logos exceeding four square feet. The wind turbine manufacturer name shall not be considered  "advertising"  for the purpose of this Ordinance.

Commercial Wind Energy Facilities (CWEFs) shall only be located in A1 or A2 districts and must obtain a conditional use permit prior to the submission of any application of a building permit. The design standards and bulk regulations applicable to A1 and A2 districts for setbacks, lot size, lot coverage, lot area, height, and signage shall be suspended for all CWEFs and the regulations herein shall apply instead. Any wind turbine or meteorological tower proposed within 1.5 miles of the corporate limits of any incorporated village or city shall require an approval sign-off by that corporate authority.

Setback distances shall be measured beginning from the center of the base of a wind turbine or meteorological tower. Occupied Community Buildings: A minimum setback of 2.1 times the wind turbine's maximum blade tip height to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure. Participating Residences: A minimum setback of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height to the nearest point on the outside wall of the residence. Nonparticipating Residences: A minimum setback of 2.1 times the maximum blade tip height to the nearest point on the outside wall of the residence.
Participating Residences: A minimum setback of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height to the nearest point on the outside wall of the residence.
section: VIII. BUILDING PERMIT REQUIREMENTS, D. Setbacks

summary: A minimum setback of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height to the nearest edge of the property line, easement, or right-of-way containing the overhead line is required for overhead communication and electric transmission and distribution facilities.

All WECS towers must be unclimbable by design or protected by anti-climbing devices such as: (1) Fences with locking portals at least six feet high; or (2) Anti-climbing devices 12 feet vertically from the base of the WECS tower.
Towers and blades shall be painted white or gray or another non-reflective, unobtrusive color.

The plan shall ensure financial resources equal to 125% of the entire cost of decommission, and approved by the Code Official and the state's attorney, in a surety performance bond that is readily convertible into cash at face value and that names Jersey County and its officials as the insured. This surety shall be retained by the county to cover the cost of the decommissioning requirements herein. Following initial submittal of the surety, the cost calculation shall be reviewed bi-annually, and adjusted accordingly based upon an updated estimate, excluding the salvage value, by an Illinois licensed engineer under seal; provided however, that any such periodic adjustment must be approved by the County Board. The county shall hire the engineer and the applicant shall be required to cover the cost. Failure to comply with any requirement of this section shall result in the immediate termination and revocation of all prior approvals and permits; further, the county shall be entitled to make immediate demand upon, and/or retain any proceeds of, the surety, which shall be used for decommissioning and/or removal of the wind energy conversion system, even if still operational. The decommissioning agreement and financial assurances shall comply with 55 ILCS 5/5-12020.

WECS projects shall utilize minimal lighting that is compliant with the applicable FAA regulations, as amended by the FAA. To the extent that such tower lighting is available, and is approved by the FAA for a WECS project, the applicant shall install Aircraft Detection Lighting Systems ("ADLS") or other similar technology to reduce light pollution and visual impacts caused by the WECS towers.
WECS towers shall be sited as follows, with setback distances measured from the center of the base of the WECS tower: Boundary lines of participating property: none;
WECS towers shall be sited with a setback distance from public road rights-of-way of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS tower to the center point of the public road right-of-way.

The applicant shall appropriately demonstrate through industry standard modeling that no occupied community building or nonparticipating residence will experience an expected duration of 30 hours or more per year of shadow flicker. This sets a maximum shadow flicker duration of less than 30 hours per year unless waived in writing by the affected property owner.

A reasonably visible warning sign concerning voltage shall be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations, and at all entrances to wind towers. Signage regulations are to be consistent with ANSI and AWEA standards.

§ 157.06(I) requires the applicant, at its expense, to provide soil and geotechnical boring reports to the County Code Administrator with respect to each WECS tower location as part of its WECS building permit. The applicant shall follow the guidelines for conservation practices and impact mitigation submitted by the County Soil and Water Conservation District (or equivalent regulatory agency). The applicant shall submit grading plans for the proposed substations for review and comment by the County Soil and Water Conservation District prior to the issuance of any WECS building permit for the construction of said substations.

WECS towers shall be sited with setback distances measured from the center of the base of the WECS tower. For nonparticipating residences, the setback is 2.11 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure. For occupied community buildings, the setback is 2.1 times the maximum blade tip height, and for participating residences, it is 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height. These setback requirements may be waived by written consent of the affected property owners.

WECS towers shall be sited as follows, with setback distances measured from the center of the base of the WECS tower: Participating residences: 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure.

WECS towers shall be sited with a setback of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS tower to the nearest edge of the property line, easement, or right-of-way containing the overhead communications and electric transmission and distribution facilities (not including overhead utility service lines to individual houses or outbuildings).

The ordinance requires the applicant to submit a "sketch elevation of the premises accurately depicting the proposed wind energy conversion system and its relationship to structure on adjacent land" (§157.05(B)(5)), identify "scenic and natural areas within 1,500 feet of the proposed WECS" (§157.05(B)(6)), and follow recommended standards to mitigate visual impact including tower and blade coloring, turbine consistency, and lighting (§157.06(D)). Additionally, a shadow flicker model study must be presented to demonstrate that no occupied community building or nonparticipating residence will experience an expected duration of 30 hours or more per year (§157.07(D)). These requirements are part of the special use application process for commercial wind energy conversion systems of 500 kilowatts or greater.

All WECS towers must be unclimbable by design or protected by anticlimbing devices such as: (1) Fences with locking portals at least six feet (6') high; or (2) Anticlimbing devices twelve feet (12') vertically from the base of the WECS tower.
Towers and blades shall be painted white or gray or another nonreflective, unobtrusive color.

A proposed Decommissioning Plan for the WECS Project including cost estimations is required as part of the special use permit application for Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS) Facilities.

WECS Projects shall utilize minimal lighting that is compliant with the applicable FAA regulations, as amended by the FAA. To the extent that such tower lighting is available, and is approved by the FAA for a WECS Project, the Applicant shall install Aircraft Detection Lighting Systems ("ADLS") or other similar technology to reduce light pollution and visual impacts caused by the WECS Towers.

Setbacks: All setbacks for commercial wind energy facility towers shall be measured from the center of the base of the wind tower. Boundary Lines of Nonparticipating Property: 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest point on the property line of the nonparticipating property. Boundary Lines of Participating Property: None.
Boundary Lines of Participating Property: None.

Setbacks: All setbacks for commercial wind energy facility towers shall be measured from the center of the base of the wind tower: Public Road Rights-of-Way: 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the center point of the public road right-of-way. The setback requirements may be waived by the written consent of the owner(s) of each affected property.
A reasonably visible warning sign concerning voltage must be placed at the base of all pad mounted transformers and substations, and at all entrances to the Wind Towers.

All setbacks for commercial wind energy facility towers shall be measured from the center of the base of the wind tower: Occupied Community Buildings: 2.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure; Participating Residences: 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height; Nonparticipating Residences: 2.1 times the maximum blade tip height.

Setbacks for commercial wind energy facility towers from participating residences shall be 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure.

Setbacks: All setbacks for commercial wind energy facility towers shall be measured from the center of the base of the wind tower: Overhead Communication and Electric Transmission and Distribution Facilities (Not Including Overhead Utility Service Lines to Individual Houses or Outbuildings): 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest edge of the property line, easement, or right of way containing the overhead line. Overhead Utility Service Lines to Individual Houses or Outbuildings: None. No building or tower that is part of a wind power generation facility shall encroach onto any recorded easement prohibiting the encroachment unless the grantees of the easement have given their approval.

All WECS Towers must be unclimbable by design or protected by anti-climbing devices such as: (a) Fences with locking portals at least six (6) feet high; or (b) Anti-climbing devices twelve (12) feet vertically from the base of the WECS Tower.
Towers and blades shall be painted white or gray or another non-reflective, unobtrusive color.

The Applicant must formulate a Decommissioning and Site Reclamation Plan to ensure that the Commercial Wind Energy Facility is properly decommissioned. The Plan shall be binding upon the Applicant and its successors-in-interest and assigns, and shall apply to all participating parcels. A signed Plan must be submitted prior to the granting of the Special Use Permit. The Applicant shall ensure that the Commercial Wind Energy Facility is properly decommissioned within twelve (12) months of the end of the Commercial Wind Energy Facility life, including removal of all physical material to a depth of sixty (60) inches beneath the soil surface and restoration in accordance with the Agricultural Impact Mitigation Agreement. The Plan shall be prepared by an independent Illinois Certified Professional Engineer and include methodology and cost to remove all facilities, provisions for removal, restoration methodology and cost, work schedule, permit list, and management of hazardous materials. Financial Security in the form of a surety bond, irrevocable letter of credit, or cash escrow naming the County as beneficiary must be submitted, covering the total cost of decommissioning minus salvage value, with phased-in requirements over the first eleven (11) years of the project. Triggers for decommissioning include inactivity, lack of electricity generation, abandonment, or disrepair. The County has rights to access the Financial Security and the site to complete decommissioning if necessary. The Applicant's obligations under the Special Use Permit, including decommissioning, are binding on successors and assigns.

summary: WECS Projects shall utilize minimal lighting that is compliant with the applicable FAA regulations, as amended by the FAA. To the extent that such tower lighting is available, and is approved by the FAA for a WECS Project, the Applicant shall install Aircraft Detection Lighting Systems ("ADLS") or other similar technology to reduce light pollution and visual impacts caused by the WECS Towers.

No WECS Project, WECS or Substation governed by this Ordinance shall be constructed, erected, installed, or located within the County, unless prior siting approval has been obtained for each individual WECS Project, WECS and Substation or for a group of WECS Projects and Substations under a joint siting application pursuant to this Ordinance. The Special Use authorizing the construction and operation of the WECS Project shall be automatically revoked and void if the Applicant fails to commence and actively pursue construction of the Project within thirty-six (36) months from the date of the granting of the Special Use. The Special Use shall be subject to revocation if the WECS ceases to operate for more than twelve (12) consecutive months for any reason.

WECS Towers shall be sited with setback distances measured from the center of the base of the WECS Tower. The setback from boundary lines of nonparticipating property is 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest point on the property line of the nonparticipating property. There is no setback from boundary lines of participating property.
Boundary Lines of Participating Property: None.
