The Applicant shall appropriately demonstrate to the County Board through industry standard modeling that no occupied community building or non-participating residence will experience an expected duration of 30 hours or more per year of shadow flicker. An occupied community building owner or a non-participating residence owner may waive this shadow flicker mitigation requirement by a written waiver filed with the County Recorder of Deeds Office.

Signage regulations are to be consistent with ANSI and AWEA standards. A reasonably visible warning sign concerning voltage shall be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations, and at all entrances to Wind Towers.

The ordinance explicitly enacts soil, erosion, and sediment control requirements for Commercial Wind Energy Facilities (WECS Projects). Section J (Site Assessment) requires soil and geotechnical boring reports and adherence to Conservation Practices Impact Mitigation guidelines by the Kane-DuPage Soil and Water Conservation District. Section F (Drainage Systems) mandates compliance with the Kane County Stormwater Management Ordinance and repair of damaged waterways and drainage systems. Section D under Decommissioning and Site Reclamation Plan requires soil restoration, erosion control plans approved by the Kane-DuPage Soil and Water Conservation District, and compliance with stormwater management and surface water rules. These requirements apply specifically to WECS Projects as defined (commercial facilities with capacity ≥ 500 kW).

WECS Towers shall be sited as follows, with setback distances measured from the center of the base of the WECS Tower; Occupied Community Buildings: 2.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure. Nonparticipating Residences: 2.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure. Participating Residences: 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure.
Participating Residences: 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the WECS Tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure;

Overhead Utility Service Lines to Individual Houses or Outbuildings: None.

All commercial wind energy facilities shall fully comply with Public Act 102-1123 as amended and all other state and federal laws, rules, and regulations that pertain to siting, construction, operating and maintaining the facility. Required submittals include a decommissioning plan and surety bond in an amount reflected in the decommissioning plan. This decommissioning plan, the surety bond amount, and intervals of review and renewal shall be identical to those specified in the executed Agricultural Impact Mitigation Agreement (AIMA).

summary: Prior to receiving siting or special use permit approval, the Applicant, Owner, and/or Operator must formulate a Decommissioning Plan to ensure the WECS Project is properly decommissioned. Examples include Mason County: "must formulate a Decommissioning Plan to ensure that the WECS Project is properly decommissioned"; Ogle County: "must formulate a decommissioning plan to ensure that the WECS project is properly decommissioned"; Tazewell County: "decommissioning plan ... recorded as part of the chain of title"; Winnebago County: "A decommissioning plan prepared by a professional engineer licensed in the State of Illinois, setting forth the proposed method of decommissioning and establishing an estimate of the total cost of decommissioning."

The text explicitly enacts maximum turbine height limits for large wind energy systems in certain jurisdictions. For example, Mason County states 'The maximum WECS Tower Height shall not exceed 525 feet,' Ogle County states 'Maximum height of a WECS tower shall not exceed 550 feet,' Piatt County states 'Not to exceed 500 feet,' Stephenson County states '500 feet,' and Will County states '500 feet.' The most restrictive maximum turbine height allowed is 500 feet.

At the time of application, wind turbines shall be set back from all occupied buildings located on a non-participating landowner's property a distance of not less than one-thousand two hundred (1,200) feet or two-hundred fifty percent (250%) of total turbine height, whichever is greater.
All wind turbines shall be set back from the nearest property line a distance of not less than one-hundred ten percent (110%) of the turbine height including maximum blade height.

Setbacks from public roads for large wind energy systems shall be at least 1.10 times the WECS tower height (tip height). Examples include Boone County requiring setbacks of at least 1.10 times the WECS tower height from public roads, Henry County requiring 1.1 times total tower height from any public/private right-of-way lines, Mason County requiring 1.10 times the WECS tower height from public roads, Ogle County requiring 1.10 times the WECS tower height from public roads, Logan County requiring 1.10 times the WECS tower height from public roads, and Winnebago County requiring 110% (1.10 times) of the turbine height from the nearest public road. No additional static distance is added to these multipliers. Waivers may be granted by property owners or counties in some cases.

The text references approval processes such as variances, waivers, siting approval applications, and compliance with regulatory bodies like the Illinois Pollution Control Board and FAA. For example, Boone County requires the applicant to obtain a variance or waiver from the County or property owner; Henry County requires variances approved by the board; Mason County requires a siting approval application process; Ogle County requires municipal approval within 1.5 miles of corporate limits; and Winnebago County requires waivers signed by landowners and a decommissioning plan. However, no specific zoning district names or abbreviations where wind energy projects or wind farms are permitted as special use or similar are explicitly mentioned.

Set back from all occupied buildings located on a non-participating landowner's property a distance of not less than one-thousand two hundred (1,200) feet or two-hundred fifty percent (250%) of total turbine height, whichever is greater.

Set back from all occupied buildings and barns, garages, machine sheds, and livestock buildings located on a participating landowner's property a distance of not less than one-hundred ten percent (110%) of the turbine's height.

Setbacks from overhead electrical transmission lines, utility lines, power lines, electrical lines, and transmission lines for large wind energy systems are generally required to be at least 1.1 times the WECS tower height, sometimes up to 1.5 times the tower height as noted in LaSalle County. Examples include Boone County requiring '1.10 times the WECS tower’s height' from primary party transmission lines; Ford County requiring '1.10 times height of tower from nearest ledge of right of way'; Mason County requiring 'at least 11.10 times the WECS Tower Height from public roads, third party transmission lines, and communication towers'; and Ogle County requiring 'at least 1.10 times the WECS tower height from public roads, third-party transmission lines, and communication towers.' Waivers are sometimes allowed with consent from affected parties or authorities. No static distance values are added to these multipliers.

The vertical distance from the ground level to the tip of a wind turbine blade when the longest blade is at its lowest point must be at least 25 feet. This minimum blade clearance applies to wind energy systems regulated under this ordinance, including commercial wind energy facilities over 2,000 kilowatts (kW).
Any wind tower located in a wind energy system, including any climbing aids, shall be secured against unauthorized access by means of a locked barrier or security fence.

The exterior surface of any visible components of a wind energy system must be a non-reflective neutral color. Wind towers and turbines in an established wind farm system that are located within 1000 feet of each other must be of uniform design, including tower type, color, number of blades, and directions of blade rotation unless a variance is approved by the board.

The ordinance explicitly enacts decommissioning requirements for commercial wind energy facilities (including systems over 2,000 kW). Section 1.08 Restoration Requirement mandates removal of turbines, foundations, underground wiring, and hazardous materials within 8 months of abandonment or termination notice. Section 1.07(4)(b) authorizes financial assurance to guarantee restoration. Section 1.10(3) requires a surety bond set to the amount of costs of decommissioning prior to issuing a permit for construction. Section 1.19 Decommissioning limits the decommissioning payment to the cost identified in the decommissioning or deconstruction plan, minus salvage value, and requires a surety bond before construction permit issuance.

Lighting: As required by the Federal Aviation Administration. Required lighting must comply with FAA minimum requirements and whenever possible be at the lowest intensity allowed using red lights at night. If more than one lighting alternative is available, the alternative that causes the least visual disturbance must be used.

A county may require a wind tower of a commercial wind energy facility to be sited with setback distances measured from the center of the base of the wind tower. The setback from the boundary lines of nonparticipating property is 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the wind tower to the nearest point on the property line of the nonparticipating property. The setback from fish and wildlife areas and Illinois Nature Preserve Commission protected lands is 2.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the wind tower to the nearest point on the property line of the fish and wildlife area or protected land.

A wind tower of a commercial wind energy facility must be sited with a setback distance from public road rights-of-way of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the wind tower to the center point of the public road right-of-way.

Section 1.06, subsection 2 states that a wind tower of a commercial wind energy facility must be sited so that industry standard computer modeling indicates that any occupied community building or nonparticipating residence will not experience more than 30 hours per year of shadow flicker under planned operating conditions. This sets a maximum shadow flicker limit of 30 hr/year for commercial wind energy facilities, which include systems over 2,000 kilowatts.

No wind turbine, tower, building or other structure associated with a wind energy system must be used to advertise or promote any product or service. No word or graphic representation, other than appropriate warning signs and owner identification may be placed on a wind turbine, tower, building or other structure associated with a wind energy system so as to be visible from any public road.

A large wind system may only be located in areas that are zoned A-Agriculture, C-Conservation, an M-Restricted Industrial, or M-2 Heavy Industrial District with a Conditional Use and Building Permits.

A wind tower of a commercial wind energy facility must be sited with a setback distance from participating residences of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the wind tower to the nearest point on the outside wall of the structure.

Section 1.06, item 3 states: 'A wind energy system shall be separated from any other wind energy system by a minimum of 200 feet measured from the tips of the blades when the blades are parallel with the ground.' This is the explicit minimum spacing requirement between individual turbines for wind energy systems, including those over 2,000 kilowatts (kW).

A wind tower of a commercial wind energy facility must be sited with a setback distance of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height of the wind tower to the nearest edge of the property line, easement, or right of way containing the overhead communication and electric transmission and distribution facilities (not including overhead utility service lines to individual houses or outbuildings).

The ordinance requires that turbines have a "Non-reflective, unobtrusive color," with "Black blades acceptable for mitigation of icing," and that turbines be consistent in color with nearby facilities.

The decommissioning plan shall ensure that the facility is properly decommissioned upon the end of the project life or facility abandonment. Decommissioning shall include: removal of all structures and debris to a depth of four (4) feet, restoration of the soil, and restoration of vegetation (consistent and compatible with surrounding vegetation) within six (6) months of the end of project life or facility abandonment. The decommissioning plan shall state how the facility will be decommissioned, the structural engineer’s estimated cost of decommissioning, the financial resources to be used to accomplish decommissioning and the provision of sufficient security, to be determined by the Zoning Director, to ensure that the project could be decommissioned if the applicant fails to fulfill the decommissioning plan. The county shall have access to the security for the expressed purpose of completing decommissioning if decommissioning is not completed by the applicant within (6) months of the end of project life or facility abandonment. The county is granted the right of entry onto the site, to seek injunctive relief, and to file a lien against any real estate owned by applicant or applicant’s successor for decommissioning costs in excess of the amount deposited in escrow.
Projects shall utilize minimal lighting. No tower lighting other than normal security lighting shall be permitted except as may be required by the FAA.
Applications for special use for wind power facilities shall contain no more than 100 wind power turbine sites per application.

Setback from property lines must be at least 1.25 times its height, with distance measured from the foundation at the base of the tower. A waiver of the setback requirement may be granted for the property line of an adjoining property owner upon written consent of the property owner participating in the particular wind power facility being developed.

Public Roads (from right-of-way) 1.50 times its height. Distance shall be measured from the foundation at the base of the tower. A waiver of the setback requirement may be granted for little used public roads.

Signage regulations are to be consistent with ANSI and AWEA standards. Signs warning of high voltage shall be posted at the base of all pad mounted transformers and at substations. Signage, including anything in the tower or nacelle, shall comply with other county ordinances pertaining to signage.

Setback Requirements. Residence... 1200 feet. Other Structures... 1.50 times its height. Distance shall be measured from the foundation at the base of the tower. A waiver of the setback requirement may be granted for a residence or structure of no less than 1.25 times the turbine height upon written consent of the property owner.

A waiver of the setback requirement may be granted for a residence or structure of no less than 1.25 times the turbine height upon written consent of the property owner. A waiver of the setback requirement may also be granted for the property line of an adjoining property owner upon written consent of the property owner participating in the particular wind power facility being developed and who agrees to the waiver.

Tower-mounted wind energy facilities less than 200 feet in height are considered an accessory use to principal residential and nonresidential uses. They are permitted by right in nonresidential zoning districts with a height limit of less than 200 feet, subject to certain conditions such as a 125-foot height limit if located within 500 feet of a nonparticipating residentially zoned property. The Use Table in Section 6.2 indicates that tower-mounted turbines are permitted (P) in nonresidential districts, but no specific district names or abbreviations are provided.

summary: The facility’s surface finish shall be flat or matte, so as to reduce incidence of sun glint.

Article 13, Section 13.9.5 Decommissioning of Wind Facilities: If a wind energy facility is not completely removed within 90 days of the finding of abandonment, Lake County may remove all facility components at the owner’s expense. Lake County has the right to file a lien for reimbursement, including attorney fees and accrued interest.

The facility shall not be artificially lighted, except as required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) or necessary for workers involved in maintenance or repairs. At the time of Siting Approval Permit application, the County and the Applicant must formulate a Decommissioning and Site Reclamation Plan to ensure that the WECS Project is properly decommissioned. The Decommissioning and Site Reclamation Plan shall be binding upon the Applicant (WECS Permittee), and its successors-in-interest and assigns, and shall apply to all participating parcels in the WECS Project. A signed Decommissioning and Site Reclamation Plan must be submitted to the Regional Planner prior to the granting of the Siting Approval Permit. The Applicant shall ensure that the WECS facilities are properly decommissioned within twelve (12) months of the end of the WECS Project life or the facility abandonment; however, upon written request supported by evidence that the Applicant has diligently pursued activities toward decommissioning the WECS Project and that any delay in completion of decommissioning the WECS Project is due to conditions out of its control, the Applicant shall receive a day-for-day extension of the aforementioned twelve (12)-month deadline for any such documented delay. Subject to compliance with removal requirements, the Applicant shall include removal of all physical material of the project improvements to a depth of forty eight (48) inches beneath the soil surface and the restoration of the area as near as practicable to the same condition prior to construction. The plan shall include provisions describing triggering events for decommissioning, methodology and cost to remove all above ground and below ground WECS facilities, restoration of all areas used for construction, operation and access, work schedule and permit list, methodology to identify and manage hazardous materials, and submission of financial security in the form of a surety bond, irrevocable letter of credit or cash escrow account naming Morgan County as beneficiary. The amount of financial security shall be equal to the positive difference between the total cost of all decommissioning and restoration work and the net salvage value of all removed WECS equipment or materials, plus a ten percent (10%) contingency. The County shall have immediate access to use the financial security if the Applicant fails to address a health and safety issue or fails to decommission the abandoned turbine(s) or the entire WECS Project in accordance with the plan. The obligations and liabilities under a Siting Approval Permit shall be binding upon the Applicant and its successors-in-interest and assigns, including decommissioning obligations.

Individual turbines shall be set back one thousand (1,000) feet or more from any existing or occupied residence. This minimum distance must be met regardless of any multiplier applied to the turbine height. Setbacks still apply to existing residence, church or school in this case.

Section 1006.2 states: 'Installation of any WECS may not be nearer than three hundred fifty (350) feet or one and one-tenth (1.1) times the height of the WECS tower height, whichever is greater, to ... overhead electrical transmission or distribution lines. A project owner may not install or locate a wind power device in a unit unless the project owner submits to the permit authority a decommissioning and site restoration plan, and posts a surety bond, or equivalent means of security ... in an amount equal to the estimated cost of decommissioning the wind power device ... Lighting. Add new subsection (c) Light Mitigation. summary: Prior to receiving an Improvement Location Permit and Building Permit, the applicant must submit a decommissioning plan outlining the anticipated means and cost of removing a WECS at the end of their serviceable life or upon becoming a discontinued or abandoned use to ensure proper decommissioning. All WECS shall be considered discontinued after one year without energy production unless a plan is submitted to return the WECS to service. Removal of all physical material to no less than four feet below ground level must be completed within 365 days of discontinuation or abandonment, with restoration of the site. The County may remove the WECS at the owner's expense if necessary, and may sell salvage to defray costs. Written notice and a reasonable time period for negotiation must be provided before County action.

All lighting, including lighting intensity and frequency of strobe, shall adhere to but not exceed requirements established by Federal Aviation Administration permits and regulations. summary: Commercial WECS shall be no greater than sixty (60) decibels for a Non-participating property measured from the nearest property line. This level may only be exceeded during short term events such as utility outages and/or severe wind storms. The unit for noise level is dBA.

The setback for residential dwellings on participating properties shall be no less than 1.5 times the total height of the WECS Tower, provided that the distance is no less than one thousand (1,000) feet of a COMMERCIAL WECS Tower, measured from the center of the WECS Tower to the nearest corner of the structure, if on a participating property.

Minimum setback distance from railroads for Commercial WECS Towers is 3 times the total height of the WECS Tower (where the blade tip is at its highest point). A WECS Tower may be placed up to the public right-of-way if a fully executed and recorded written waiver agreement is secured from owner or whomever oversees the right-of-way.

The minimum setback distance for Commercial WECS Towers from public road rights-of-way is three times the total height of the WECS Tower (where the blade tip is at its highest point), provided that the distance is no less than one thousand eight hundred feet (1800). A WECS Tower may be placed up to the public right-of-way if a fully executed and recorded written waiver agreement is secured from the owner or whomever oversees the right-of-way.

The ordinance requires that for all Commercial WECS: signs must be posted on the pad-mounted transformer and Substation(s) warning of high voltage; private roads providing access must have posted an Emergency-911 address road sign; a sign must be posted on the WECS tower listing an emergency telephone number; guyed towers must have visible and reflective objects or fencing around anchor points. Additionally, identification signs relating to the WECS Project development may be located on each side of the total WECS Project area, with no more than four signs on any one site, and no other advertising signs or logos shall be placed or painted on any structure or facility that is part of the WECS Project.

Commercial WECS (item 17) are permitted as a "Special Use" (denoted by "S") in the AG (Agricultural) district only, and are not permitted ("X") in all other listed districts. This indicates that in the AG district, Commercial WECS require special approval, such as by a zoning appeals board or through a special permitting process, while in other districts they are not allowed.

For participating properties, the setback may be reduced to no less than 1.5 times the total height but not less than one thousand (1,000) feet. If future residential dwellings or buildable land splits occur near a WECS Tower, they shall keep the 3 times the total height or no less than 1,800 feet setback or a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) must be signed, notarized and recorded with the Deed.

The setback for residential dwellings shall be no less than 1.5 times the total height of the WECS Tower provided that the distance is no less than one thousand (1,000) feet of a COMMERCIAL WECS Tower, measured from the center of the WECS Tower to the nearest corner of the structure, if on a participating property.

Minimum setback distances for COMMERCIAL WECS TOWERS from above-ground electric transmission lines and public utility easements are 3 times the total height of the WECS Tower (where the blade tip is at its highest point). A WECS Tower may be placed up to the transmission lines or public right-of-way if a fully executed and recorded written waiver agreement is secured from the affected owners. For poles carrying overhead wiring connecting Commercial WECS Towers to a Substation, there are no setback requirements from property lines as long as the poles are located within a recorded easement for such purpose.

Setback from Wabash or Eel River measured from the center of the WECS Tower to the shoreline is one-half (1/2) mile. Setback from wetlands, as defined by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, is determined by a permit obtained from the Army Corps of Engineers.

The plan "must be updated and approved by the Area Plan Commission every five years" and "shall include assurance that the facilities are properly decommissioned upon the end of the project life or facility abandonment," including "removal of all physical material, with the exception of subsurface Collectors, pertaining to the project improvements to a depth of 48"  beneath the soil surface, and restoration of the area occupied by the project improvements." Section 405.03 A requires the Owner or Operator to secure a "Decommissioning Security" equal to "one hundred twenty-five percent (125%) of the estimated cost of decommissioning the WECS pursuant to the Decommission Plan," adjusted annually. Section 405.03 D states a WECS or turbine is "presumed at the end of its useful life and/or abandoned if the WECS or the individual turbine generates no electricity for a continuing period of 9 months" and such WECS or turbine "shall be subject to removal pursuant to the Decommissioning Plan." summary: All WECS Towers shall be equipped with lighting in compliance with applicable Federal Aviation Administration regulations and the lighting requirements in UDO Section 524. All lighting shall be shielded so that no glare extends substantially beyond the boundaries of the wind farm facilities.

At any non-Co-Applicant residentially zoned lot, public school, or public library, the audible A-weighted sound pressure levels as a result of the sound emitted by the WECS shall not exceed 45 decibels. Noise and vibration levels shall also be in compliance with all other applicable County, state and Federal regulations. The unit for noise level is dBA, the standard unit for A-weighted sound pressure levels.

The Wind Energy Conversion System Overlay District is intended to define areas, which because of their location and wind resources, are recommended and best suited for the establishment of Commercial WECS. This district will permit and regulate the development of WECS to minimize impact on underlying district and potential for conflict with other uses. Section 535 states that Commercial WECS are permitted within the WECS Overlay district. The Land Use Matrix shows Commercial WECS as prohibited in all base zoning districts except where a WECS Overlay District has been created according to UDO Section 405, where they are permitted.

Section 403.11 states that "Wind energy systems" are prohibited uses in the Primary Tier Overlay Zone. However, section 302.18 and section 405 establish a "Wind Energy Conversion System Overlay District" intended to permit and regulate the development of Commercial WECS. The prohibition applies outright in the Primary Tier Overlay Zone unless the property is rezoned to the WECS Overlay District. There is no expiration date or moratorium specified for this prohibition.

The minimum setback distance for all turbines, substations, maintenance structures, storage yards, permanent MET Towers, and other buildings that are a direct functional part of the WECS shall not be less than 1,520 feet or the manufacturer’s recommended minimum setback, whichever is greater, from any non-Co-Applicant property line. Installation of any WECS may not be nearer than 1.1 times the height of the WECS including the blade at its highest point to any non-Co-Applicant property lines. Distance shall be measured from the center of the foundation at the base of the tower.

No WECS shall be constructed in any setback, dedicated public easement or dedicated public right-of-way without prior written authorization from the County.

The maximum wind turbine shadow flicker experienced at a non-Co-Applicant dwelling, residentially zoned lot, public school, or public library may not exceed 30 hours per year or 30 minutes in a single day. Measurements to assess shadow flicker shall be for all non-Co-Applicant dwellings, residentially zoned lots, public schools or public libraries located within 0.6 miles or 3,168 feet of a turbine. If shadow flicker will exceed these levels then a shadow flicker mitigation plan must be submitted for each affected non-Co-Applicant dwelling, residentially zoned lot, public school, or public library.

Section 405.02 A 4 mandates "Using concrete armoring techniques at each and every location where County regulated drains and subsurface power transmission lines of any type cross." Prior to receiving location approval under this Ordinance, the County and the applicant, owner, and or operator must formulate a Decommissioning Plan to ensure that the WES project is properly decommissioned. Prior to issuance of an Improvement Location Permit, the applicant shall provide a contractor cost estimation for demolition and removal of the WES facility and will provide financial assurance in an amount at least equal to said demolition and removal contractor cost estimate, through the use of a bond, letter of credit or other security acceptable to the County Commissioners. Section G.12 Lighting requires that except for obstruction lighting required by the FAA or other government agencies, all lighting shall be shielded so that no light exists beyond the boundaries of the wind farm facilities. Obstruction lighting is required for all WES towers on the periphery of the development and for interior towers as necessary to ensure no unlighted separation or gaps of more than one-half (1/2) mile. Lighting shall be by Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) L-864 aviation red-colored flashing lights with a minimum intensity of 2000 candelas or by an equivalent lighting solution if approved by the FAA and the DeKalb County Airport Authority. All obstruction lights shall be synchronized to flash simultaneously so as to delineate the WES development as a single, large development. Each lighted WES tower shall only require one fixture if the site is manned daily and a non-functioning light can be replaced within the next working day; otherwise, two lights are required. Non-functioning obstruction lights must be repaired or replaced within two working days unless a more restrictive law requires faster action.

The noise level will not exceed 45 decibels at the nearest property line. The noise level will not exceed 35 decibels as measured from the nearest residential structure. Sound levels shall be measured with a calibrated audiometer manufactured and used in compliance with standards prescribed by the American National Standards Institute.

No WES shall be constructed in any setback, dedicated public easement or dedicated public right-of-way.

The ordinance applies to Wind Energy Systems (WES) with an aggregate generating capacity of 1 MW or greater that generate electricity to be sold to a utility. It requires a site restoration plan to reduce soil compaction, remove and replace topsoil, and address damage to drainage, streams, wetlands, and natural habitat with approval from the DeKalb County Soil and Water Conservation District and/or Surveyor/Drainage Board. A drainage plan must be developed and approved by the DeKalb County Drainage Board. An erosion control plan must be developed in consultation with the DeKalb County Soil and Water Conservation District and the Indiana Department of Environmental Management covering all soil disturbances including road cuts, access roads, and construction sites. Damages to waterways, drainage ditches, field tiles, or other infrastructure must be repaired to original condition within six months. Soil compaction mitigation is required where temporary access crosses agricultural ground, returning it to original compaction levels in a timely manner.

summary: The ordinance requires a drainage plan approved by the Hamilton County surveyor and drainage board to ensure that all newly constructed WECS access roads shall not impede the flow of water and will comply with the county drainage ordinance and highway department requirements. No residential dwelling shall be constructed within 1.1 times the height of a meteorological tower or WECS. This setback is reciprocal and no variance may be granted in conflict with the rules established by the Federal Housing Administration.
A WECS shall be separated from any other WECS by a minimum of 200 feet, measured from the tip of the blades when the blades are parallel to the ground.

The furthest horizontal extension of a WECS (including guy wires) shall not extend into a required setback of the zoning district or be closer than 12 feet to any above-ground telephone line, or electrical transmission or distribution line.

1.5 SETBACK REQUIRMENTS
1.5.1 Minimum setback distances for COMMERCIAL Wind Energy Conversion Systems

summary: The minimum setback distance from a road right-of-way for Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS) is 1.1 times the total height (where the blade tip is at its highest point), provided that the distance is no less than three hundred and fifty (350) feet. The setback shall be measured from future rights-of-way width if a planned road improvement or expansion is known at the time of application.

For all COMMERCIAL WECS, a sign or signs shall be posted on the tower, transformer and substation warning of high voltage. Signs with emergency contact information shall also be posted on the turbine or at another suitable point. No sign shall exceed sixteen (16) square feet in surface area. No sign shall exceed eight (8) feet in height. The manufacturers or owner's company name and/or logo may be placed upon the compartment containing the electrical equipment. An identification sign relating to the wind farm development may be located on each side of the total project area, provided that there are no more than four (4) signs located on any one project site. No other advertising signs or logos shall be placed or painted on any WECS.

Section 2.5.4 requires an erosion control plan developed in consultation with the Natural Resources Conservation Services (NRCS), and any storm water quality management plan adopted by the applicable jurisdiction. Section 2.6.2 mandates reasonable storm water best management practices as required by the approved Drainage Plan/Agreement on file with the Spencer County Surveyor during construction of a COMMERCIAL WECS.

Commercial, non-commercial, and micro-WECS will be permitted, or not permitted, in various districts as prescribed by the Official Schedule of Uses (Appendix A). Any NON-COMMERCIAL WECS or meteorological tower greater than two hundred (200) feet in height shall require a special exception use permit. For COMMERCIAL WECS there is no limitation on height, except those height limitations imposed by FAA rules and regulations.

The minimum setback distance from residential dwellings (measured from the center of the WECS to the nearest corner of the structure) is one thousand (1,000) feet for non-participating landowners. The setback for residential dwellings shall be reciprocal in that no residential dwelling shall be constructed within one thousand (1,000) feet of a COMMERCIAL WECS.

The minimum setback distance for Commercial WECS from utility easements and overhead utility lines is 1.1 times the total height of the WECS (where the blade tip is at its highest point), provided that the distance is no less than three hundred and fifty (350) feet. Additionally, the furthest horizontal extension of a WECS (including guy wires) shall not be closer than twelve (12) feet to any right-of-way easement for any above-ground telephone, electrical transmission or distribution lines.

Wind Energy Facility (WEF) is allowed only as a special use (SU) in designated districts after approval, and is not permitted as an accessory use. According to the Use Table for Wind Energy Conversion Systems (154.506(B)), WEF is permitted as a special use in Agricultural (A), Single Family Residential (R), Commercial (C), Industrial (I), and University (U) districts. Section 154.508(A) states that a wind energy facility (WEF) requires a special exception use and approval by the County Council. Accessory use status is explicitly given only to Small Wind Energy Conversion Systems (SWECS), not to WEF.

The exterior surface of any visible components must be a non-reflective, neutral color, and blend into the surrounding environment as practical as possible. White or light grey is the color of preference unless the manufacturer's color preference is proven to better blend into the environment. Rotors (blades) or vanes may be painted black to better assist in the prevention of ice build-up. Decorative items, such as flags, streamers and holiday and commemorative decorations are prohibited.

Section 154.510 WIND ENERGY FACILITY - ABANDONMENT, DISCONTINUATION OR DECOMMISSIONING OF WIND TURBINES AND REMOVAL OF WIND ENERGY FACILITIES requires that wind turbines and facilities not used for a continuous 24-month period be deemed abandoned and removed per the decommissioning plan. The ordinance aims to "minimize the height, obtrusiveness, and the visual impacts of WECS" (§ 154.505(B)) and to "ensure that the height of WECS have the least visual impact" (§ 154.505(D)). It requires a "site plan showing the location of floodplains; wetlands; forested areas; on-site structures; structures within 500 feet of the development site; streams and legal ditches; utility lines, cables and pipelines" (§ 154.508(B)(5)) and a detailed site plan including "the location and height (including the top of the arc of the blade) of the wind turbines" and "location of all structures on adjacent properties, within 300 feet of all property lines" (§ 154.509(B)(1)). These requirements are part of the approval process for a Wind Energy Facility (WEF).

Horizontal-axis Large WECS shall have a minimum ground clearance of forty (40) feet. Vertical-axis Large WECS shall have a minimum ground clearance of twenty (20) feet. Large WECS are defined as systems with a nameplate capacity greater than one hundred (100) kW or with a total height of two hundred (200) feet or greater, which typically applies to Wind Farm systems.

The ordinance explicitly requires that "The tower shall not be climbable for a height of twenty (20) feet above the ground unless the applicant proves it would not be a public hazard." This climbing prevention requirement applies to Large WECS, defined as systems with a nameplate capacity greater than one hundred (100) kW or with a total height of two hundred (200) feet or greater, which are consistent with Wind Farm systems. Additionally, all access doors to towers and exterior electrical equipment must be locked when not attended.

Large WECS shall be a non-obtrusive, non-reflective color. Alternative color schemes may be approved without requiring a variance if the proposed color scheme is consistent with FAA guidelines, darker colored blades may be allowed to reduce icing concerns, and the proposed color scheme will better serve the intent of this Ordinance. The system shall be maintained in good condition at all times, consistent or better than industry standards.

Section 09A.05(i) Decommissioning/Removal requires that any Large WECS which has not produced electricity for a period of twelve (12) months shall be considered abandoned and must be removed or reconditioned at the owner’s expense within twelve (12) months notice to take action. Unsafe Large WECS shall be removed or made safe within a reasonable time as determined by the Plan Director. The County may remove any abandoned or unsafe Large WECS not removed or reconditioned by the owner within the allowed time at the owner’s expense. All structures, equipment, and waste associated with the Large WECS shall be disposed of properly. Land shall be restored to a depth of three (3) feet below grade and disturbed land shall be revegetated within a reasonable period of time. Decommissioning requirements may be reduced without requiring a variance if certain conditions are met. Section 09A.06(a)(6) requires adequate financial security to provide for decommissioning costs for Wind Farms.

Section 09A.05(h)(4) Lighting: Large WECS shall have the minimum lighting required by the FAA. Tower lighting shall be the lowest intensity allowable by the FAA. The Safety Zone "shall in no event be less than that specified by the supplier and/or manufacturer of the WECS in its standard safety specifications in effect at the time of project permitting." Section 7.6.10(1) states: 'Color and Finish. The Board of Appeals shall have discretion over the turbine color, although a neutral, non-reflective exterior color designed to blend with the surrounding environment is encouraged.'

Subsection (f)(4) states that "Clearing of natural vegetation shall be limited to that which is necessary for the construction, operation and maintenance of the wind facility and as otherwise prescribed by applicable laws, regulations, and other ordinances." Physical modifications to an existing large wind energy facility that materially alter its type, number, location, height or configuration shall also require a special permit from the Planning Board.

Wind turbines shall be set back a distance equal to three (3) times the height of the wind turbine from any existing residential or occupied building.
