These criteria are measured both at the property line and at the nearest inhabited residence.

The minimum distance from the base of the tower to any property line, unless shared with an abutting property in common ownership with that on which the CWECF is located, shall be 1.25 times the Height of the Wind Turbine. The Height is measured from existing average grade to the tip of the Rotor blade at its highest point.

The minimum distance from the base of the tower to any street or way, public or private, shall be 1.25 times the Height of the Wind Turbine. Height is measured from existing average grade to the tip of the Rotor blade at its highest point.

Signs at any CWECF shall be limited to: (i) those needed to identify the property and the owner/operator of the facility, and to warn of any danger; and (ii) educational signs providing information on the technology of the CWECF and renewable energy usage. Wind Turbines shall not be used for the display of advertising, except for reasonable identification of the manufacturer thereof or of the owner/operator of the CWECF, as aforesaid, provided the same is approved by the SPGA. All signs shall be subject to and comply with Article 9 of the General Bylaws, the Town’s Sign Bylaw.

The minimum distance from any Wind Turbine, measured from the base of the tower, to any Habitable Structure, known as the Clear Area, shall be equal to 1.5 times the Height of the Wind Turbine, measured from existing average grade to the tip of the Rotor blade at its highest point. The Clear Area shall be kept free of all Habitable Structures.

Section 6.7.5.4 states: 'The applicant shall demonstrate through project siting and proposed mitigation that the CWECF minimizes its impact on the visual character of surrounding neighborhood(s) and the community.' Section 6.7.8 outlines detailed application requirements for a special permit for CWECF, including 'Visualizations' with 'actual pre-construction photographs and accurate post-construction simulations' and a description of the technical procedures used. These requirements are explicitly for Commercially-scaled, Land-based Wind Energy Conversion Facilities and are part of the special permit application process.
section: 6.7 COMMERCIALLY-SCALED, LAND-BASED WIND ENERGY CONVERSION FACILITIES

summary: No building permit shall be issued for a windmill until plans are approved by a registered professional engineer. The highest point of the structure shall not exceed 75 feet above grade, measured at the center of the structure.
A Clear Area, being the distance from the lowest point of the blade tip to the ground, shall not be less than fifteen (15) feet.
section: SECTION XX – GENERAL WIND FACILTIES (WFs) - G. Safety Standards

summary: Climbing access to any tower shall be limited by placing climbing apparatus no lower than ten (10) feet from the ground.
WFs shall be of non-reflective muted colors that blend with the sky, without graphics or other decoration. A single color shall be used on the blades and a single color on the tower.

If a wind facility has been abandoned, left in disrepair, or not maintained in accordance with the approved maintenance plan, the owner shall be notified in writing to bring the WF up to standard. If repairs are not made within forty-five (45) days, the WF shall be deemed condemned and removed from the site within ninety (90) days. "Removed from site" means removal of the wind turbine and tower, all machinery, equipment, equipment shelters, security barriers and all appurtenant structures; proper disposal of all solid or hazardous materials and wastes; and restoration of the location to its natural condition, except landscaping and grading may remain at the discretion of the SPGA. The SPGA may require a cash escrow or bond equal to one-hundred and fifty percent (150%) of the cost of removal and disposal and site restoration, to be maintained until removal is complete or the Town has removed the WF. Any unexpended balance shall be returned to the applicant or successor(s).
section: SECTION XX – GENERAL WIND FACILTIES (WFs) - H. Condemnation

summary: Wind turbines shall be lighted only if required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The applicant shall provide a copy of the FAA’s determination to establish the required markings and/or lights for the structure. Lighting of equipment, structures and any other facilities on site (including lighting required by the FAA, if possible) shall be shielded from abutting properties.
section: SECTION XX – GENERAL WIND FACILTIES (WFs) - E. Design Standards - 4. Lighting and Signage

summary: No WF (Wind Facility) may exceed seventy-five (75) feet in height, except in District C where they may not exceed one-hundred (100) feet. The height is measured from the natural grade to the tip of the rotor blade at its highest point, or blade-tip height.

The WF and associated equipment shall not generate sound in excess of ten (10) decibels (DB) above ambient sound level at the property line. The applicant shall provide an analysis consistent with Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection guidance for sound measurement (310 CMR 7.10).

The base of any Wind Facility (WF) shall be set back from any property line by not less than one-hundred percent (100%) of the proposed height of the WF. Guy wires or any WF-related construction not wholly below grade shall be set back at least twenty (20) feet from property lines.

The base of any Wind Facility shall be set back from any road layout line by not less than one-hundred percent (100%) of the proposed height of the WF. Guy wires or any WF-related construction not wholly below grade shall be set back at least thirty (30) feet from road layout lines.

Under SECTION XX – GENERAL WIND FACILTIES (WFs), E. Design Standards, 4.c: "No signage except as allowed by the SPGA." This explicitly enacts signage requirements for Utility Scale Wind Facilities, limiting signage to what the Special Permit Granting Authority allows.

Municipal Wind Facilities (MWFs) shall require a building permit. The construction of any MWF may be permitted in zoning district H subject to issuance of a special permit by the Planning Board and provided the proposed use complies with provisions of this section and any other applicable provisions of this chapter. Any subsequent change or modification of a MWF shall be subject to Planning Board approval of a modification to the original special permit.

The applicant shall demonstrate through project siting, facility design and proposed mitigation that the WF minimizes any impact on the visual character of surrounding neighborhoods and the community. This may include, but not be limited to, information regarding site selection, turbine design, buffering and lighting.

The ordinance permits installation of Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS) with towers not exceeding 150 feet, subject to requirements including that "the tower shall be designed and installed so as not to provide step bolts or ladders readily accessible to the public for a minimum height of eight (8) feet above the ground."
WECS units shall be painted a non-reflective color that blends with sky and clouds. Only towers not exceeding 150 feet in total tower height shall be allowed.

Only towers not exceeding 150 feet in total tower height shall be allowed. A WECS that is out of service for a continuous 12-month period will be deemed to have been abandoned and the Building Inspector may issue a Notice of Abandonment to the owner. If the WECS is determined to be abandoned, the owner shall remove the WECS equipment at the owner's sole expense within 90 days of the Notice of Abandonment. If the owner fails to remove the WECS the Building Inspector may pursue legal action to have the tower and equipment removed at the owner's expense.

The WECS shall not be artificially lighted unless such lighting is required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). A temporary light used to inspect a WECS and associated equipment is permissible provided said light is used only for inspection purposes and not in operation for an extended period of time. Only towers not exceeding 150 feet in total tower height shall be allowed.
Only towers not exceeding 150 feet in total tower height shall be allowed for Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS).
When more than one WECS may be installed on a lot there shall be a minimum of one acre allotted for each unit. This applies to WECS with towers not exceeding 150 feet in total tower height.

WECS towers shall be set back a distance equal to 1.25 times the Total Tower Height from all front, side and rear property lines unless written permission is granted by abutters to reduce this requirement.

WECS towers shall be set back a distance equal to 1.25 times the Total Tower Height from any public road or private right of way. Only towers not exceeding 150 feet in total tower height shall be allowed.

All signs, other than manufacturers or installers identification, warning signs or owner identification on a WECS tower, or other structure visible from any public road shall be prohibited. All signs shall comply with Section 6-5.10 of Town of Essex bylaws. Only towers not exceeding 150 feet in total tower height shall be allowed.

WECS towers shall be set back a distance equal to 1.25 times the Total Tower Height from any overhead utility lines, unless written permission is otherwise granted by the affected utility to reduce this requirement.

Wind turbines or other structures part of a WEF shall be designed to prevent unauthorized access. For instance, the tower shall be designed and installed so as to not provide step bolts or other climbing means readily accessible to the public for a minimum height of 8 feet above the ground.
Wind facilities shall be painted a neutral, non-reflective color designed to blend with the surrounding environment.

The owner, his successors in interest shall remove any WEF the use of which has been discontinued. At the time of removal, the WEF site shall be restored to its natural state or to any other legally authorized use. The SPGA shall require that a bond, escrow account or other suitable surety be established to ensure adequate funds are available for removal. Municipal wind facilities shall be exempt from the surety requirement. The SPGA may require the applicant for utility scale wind facilities to provide a form of surety, either through escrow account, bond or otherwise, to cover the cost of removal or failure to maintain in the event the town must remove or maintain the facility, of an amount and form determined to be reasonable by the Special Permit granting authority, but in no event to exceed more than 125 percent of the cost of removal and compliance with the additional requirements set forth herein, as determined by the applicant.

Night lighting shall be prohibited unless required by state or federal law and shall be the minimum necessary. Lighting shall be designed to minimize glare on abutting properties and except as required by the FAA be directed downward with full cut-off fixtures to reduce light pollution.
The WEF shall have a maximum tip height (MTH) no greater than 265 feet above the current grade of the land.
The maximum nameplate rating shall not exceed 660kW for Utility-Scale Wind Energy Facilities, as explicitly stated in section H (2).
The WEF shall be located on a parcel of land that contains a minimum of ten (10) acres. This is a clear minimum lot size requirement specifically for Utility-Scale Wind Energy Facilities.

The WEF and associated equipment shall conform with the provisions of the Department of Environmental Protection‘s (DEP), Division of Air Quality Noise Regulations (currently 310 CMR 7.10), unless waived. A source of sound will be considered violating these regulations if it increases the broadband sound level by more than 10 dB(A) above ambient, or produces a pure tone condition exceeding adjacent frequency bands by 3 decibels or more. These criteria are measured at the property line and nearest inhabited structure. 'dB(A)' refers to A-weighted decibels, a standard noise measurement unit.

The WEF shall, at all times while in operation, meet the setback of a distance equal to one and one-half (1.5) times the (MTH) of the turbine from the nearest non participating property line and private way(s) that are not part of the WEF. The SPGA may allow non participating property within the minimum required setbacks only if the SPGA agrees based on site-specific considerations and with written consent of all affected abutting property owners.
The WEF shall, at all times while in operation, meet the setback of a distance equal to four (4.0) times the (MTH) of the turbine from the nearest ... public way.

There shall be no signs, except announcement signs, no trespassing signs or any signs required to warn of danger. A sign is required that identifies the owner and operator with an emergency telephone number where the owner and operator can be reached on a twenty-four hour basis.

Clearing of natural vegetation shall be limited to that which is necessary for the construction, operation and maintenance of the WEF and is otherwise prescribed by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances. The applicant shall submit a plan for maintenance of access roads and storm water controls, as well as detailed procedures for operational maintenance of the WEF.

The WEF shall, at all times while in operation, meet the required setback of a distance equal to four (4.0) times the maximum tip height (MTH) of the turbine from the nearest off site residential, commercial structure. The MTH is defined as the height of a wind turbine measured from natural grade to the tip of the rotor blade at its highest point.

The WEF shall, at all times while in operation, meet the required setback of a distance equal to one and one-tenth (1.1) times the (MTH) of the wind turbine from principal structures, critical infrastructure such as but not limited to power lines, natural gas or distribution infrastructure.

Section H(7) Visualizations requires the applicant to submit color view representations including actual pre-construction photographs and accurate post-construction simulations of the WEF from selected sight lines within a 2-mile radius, including a description of the technical procedures followed in producing the visualization and a site balloon test. These are explicit visual impact assessment requirements for Utility-Scale Wind Energy Facilities.

Large wind energy systems (LWES) may be permitted in Public Use or Light Industrial Zoning Districts and only freestanding monotube tower designs are permitted for LWES. WES may only be permitted when accessory to a principal land use. The purpose of § 240-9.8 is to accommodate wind energy systems as accessory land uses to supplement the power used by residents, municipal government bodies, and businesses.

The Planning Board shall require the applicant for any LWES to provide surety, either as a bond or escrow account, to cover the cost of removal in the event the Town must remove the LWES together with a right-of-entry onto the property in the event of default. The applicant shall submit a fully inclusive estimate of the costs associated with removal, prepared by a qualified engineer. The amount shall be adjusted for inflation.

No wind energy system shall be constructed or modified with a rated capacity greater than 250 kilowatts in any zoning district (§ 240-9.8(2)(a)). This sets a maximum project size limit for Large Wind Energy Systems (LWES) based on rated capacity in kilowatts.

No wind energy system as defined shall be constructed or modified, and no special permit shall issue, for any wind energy system under this bylaw: a. that has a rated capacity greater than 250 kilowatts in any zoning district; c. where the primary use of the facility is electrical generation to be sold to the power grid or accounted for through net metering.

Large wind energy systems (LWES) may be permitted in Public Use or Light Industrial Zoning Districts and only freestanding monotube tower designs are permitted for LWES. Wind energy systems as defined shall only be constructed or modified through a special permit issued by the Planning Board as the Special Permit Granting Authority (SPGA). The purpose of § 240-9.8 is to accommodate wind energy systems as accessory land uses and to provide standards through a special permitting process based on the procedures, provisions, and requirements established herein.
The minimum distance between the ground and any protruding blades utilized shall be 15 feet, as measured at the lowest point of arc of the blades.
All towers shall have adequate anti-climb devices.

The wind machine tower shall be set back from every property line by a distance equal to its height as measured to the highest tip of the blades (hereinafter "fall area"), except when a fall area easement has been obtained from the appropriate abutters.
The installation shall not be erected nearer to any public way ... than the total height of the structure.
section: § 675-1040 Wind energy conversion systems, C. Setbacks

summary: In all cases, the installation shall not be erected nearer to any public way or public utility wires (excluding service wires to the windmill owner's dwelling and accessory building) than the total height of the structure.
section: § 675-1040 Wind energy conversion systems. C. Setbacks.

summary: The construction of an accessory commercial wind energy conversion facility shall be permitted in the MI, GI and BP zoning districts and on municipally owned property, subject to the issuance of a Special Permit by the City Council and provided that the use complies with all requirements set forth in this section of the zoning ordinance (see Section II, 2.3.7, Accessory Use Number 15).
section: 5.22 - COMMERCIAL LAND-BASED WIND ENERGY CONVERSION FACILITIES

summary: Wind energy conversion facilities shall be painted a non-reflective color that blends with the sky and clouds.

Section 5.22.15 ABANDONMENT or DISCONTINUATION of USE requires the owner to notify the city by certified mail of proposed abandonment or discontinuation. If no notice is given, the facility is considered abandoned if inoperable for 180 days or deemed a safety hazard. The owner may be required to physically remove the facility within 180 days, including removal of turbines, towers, equipment, proper disposal of waste, and restoration of the site to its natural pre-existing condition. The city may remove the facility if the owner fails to do so. The City Council may require surety equal to 150 percent of removal costs, including cost of living adjustments.

Section 5.22.6(f) Lighting and Signage: 1. Wind turbines shall be lighted only if required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The proponent shall provide a copy of the FAA's determination to establish the required markings and/or lights for the structure. 2. Lighting of equipment structures and any other facilities on site (except lighting required by the FAA) shall be shielded from abutting properties.

Commercial wind energy conversion facilities shall be no higher than 500 feet above the existing average grade. The height of all wind energy conversion facilities shall be measured from the existing average grade to the highest point reached by the rotor blades. The City Council may allow this height to exceed 500 feet as part of the special permit process if the project proponent can demonstrate additional height is needed and meets other criteria.

In the R-80, R-40, and R-30 residential districts, with the exception of city-owned land, the minimum lot size for a wind energy conversion facility shall be 12.5 acres and the minimum lot frontage shall be 100 feet.
section: 5.22 - COMMERCIAL LAND-BASED WIND ENERGY CONVERSION FACILITIES

summary: The minimum distance from property lines shared with abutting properties shall be 150 feet; and in no case shall be less than the length of an individual rotor blade measured from the hub of the wind turbine, whichever is greater. Setbacks shall be measured from the outside surface at the base of the turbine tower. The City Council may reduce the setbacks as appropriate, based on site specific considerations, and only after review of substantial evidence, including but not limited to detailed engineering reports or product engineering certification, which demonstrate that safety concerns have been minimized and that setbacks have been complied with to the maximum extent practicable.

The minimum distance from the base of any wind turbine tower to a public or private way shall be 100 feet; and in no case shall be less than the length of an individual rotor blade measured from the hub of the wind turbine, whichever is greater.

Signs on the facility shall be limited to: i) Those needed to identify the property and the owner/operator, and to warn of any danger; and ii) Educational signs providing information on the technology and renewable energy usage. All signs shall comply with the plans approved and incorporated by reference in a special permit granted under this section.

Section 5.22.7(c) states: 'Stormwater run-off and erosion control shall be managed in a manner consistent with all applicable state and local regulations.' This requirement applies to Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Facilities as defined in the ordinance.

The construction of a commercial wind energy conversion facility shall be permitted in the R-80, R-40, and R-30 zoning districts and on municipally owned property, subject to the issuance of a Special Permit by the City Council and provided that the use complies with all requirements set forth in this section of the zoning ordinance. The construction of an accessory commercial wind energy conversion facility shall be permitted in the MI, GI and BP zoning districts and on municipally owned property, subject to the issuance of a Special Permit by the City Council and provided that the use complies with all requirements set forth in this section of the zoning ordinance.
section: 5.22 - COMMERCIAL LAND-BASED WIND ENERGY CONVERSION FACILITIES

summary: The minimum distance from the base of any wind turbine tower to the nearest building on the lot, or on contiguous commonly owned lots, shall be 50 feet; and in no case shall be less than the length of an individual rotor blade measured from the hub of the wind turbine, whichever is greater. In the R-80, R-40, and R-30 residential districts, the minimum distance of a proposed turbine to any existing residential dwelling shall be equal to the height of the wind turbine to the tip of its rotor blade at its highest point. Setbacks shall be measured from the outside surface at the base of the turbine tower. The City Council may reduce the setbacks as appropriate, based on site specific considerations, and only after review of substantial evidence, including but not limited to detailed engineering reports or product engineering certification, which demonstrate that safety concerns have been minimized and that setbacks have been complied with to the maximum extent practicable.

Section 5.22.6(c) requires the proponent to demonstrate through project siting and proposed mitigation that the wind energy conversion facility minimizes impact on the visual character of surrounding neighborhoods and the community. Section 5.22.9(d) mandates the submission of visualizations including pre- and post-construction view representations from multiple sight-lines, with color photographs and accurate simulations. Additional requirements include elevations, materials and colors, and a balloon or crane test to illustrate the height of the proposed facility. These provisions explicitly constitute visual impact assessment requirements for Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Facilities.
section: 5.22 - COMMERCIAL LAND-BASED WIND ENERGY CONVERSION FACILITIES

summary: Minimum blade elevation shall be not less than fifteen (15) feet above the ground at the lowest point of blade arc for Utility Scale Wind Energy Facilities.

To prevent unauthorized climbing, tower access shall be restricted by either: (a) a secured fence and locked gate, both at least six (6) feet high, constructed around the perimeter of the base of the supporting structure, provided that such barrier is not required for any Wind Turbine erected on dwelling or other structure which provides no opportunity for climbing for at least six (6) feet; or (b) removal of climbing apparatus on the support structure to at least ten (10) feet above the ground; or (c) anti-climbing shrouds over the bottom portion of the structure.

Decommissioning shall consist of: 1. Physical removal of all Wind Turbines, structures, equipment, security barriers and transmission lines from the site; 2. Disposal of all solid and hazardous waste in accordance with local, state, and federal waste disposal regulations; 3. Stabilization or re-vegetation of the site as necessary to minimize erosion. The Planning Board may allow the owner to leave landscaping or designated below-grade foundations in order to minimize erosion and disruption of vegetation; 4. Decommissioning shall occur after one (1) year of discontinued use without written consent from the permit granting authority. If the applicant fails to remove the facility in accordance with the requirements of this Section within one hundred fifty (150) days of abandonment or proposed date given by the applicant, the Town may enter the property and physically remove the facility at the applicant’s cost through the financial surety set by the Town and applicant during site plan review or special permit process, as applicable.

Section 7.4.8(16) Lighting. Wind Turbines shall be lighted only if required by the FAA. Lighting of other parts of Wind Energy Facilities, such as appurtenant Structures, shall be limited to that required for safety and operational purposes, and shall be reasonably shielded from abutting properties. Except as required by the FAA, lighting of Wind Energy Facilities shall be directed downward and shall incorporate full cut-off fixtures to reduce light pollution.
The height of Wind Turbine shall not exceed three hundred twenty-five (325) feet from natural grade to the tip of the rotor blade at its highest point.

Utility Scale Wind Energy Facilities are permitted by right in the Commercial Overlay District (COD), subject to nondiscretionary site plan review under Section 10.6, and do not require a special permit. Outside the COD, a special permit from the Zoning Board of Appeals is required. The COD is defined as the designated location where 'As of Right Siting' applies, meaning development may proceed without the need for a special permit, variance, amendment, waiver, or other discretionary approval.

A Wind Turbine for a Utility Scale Wind Energy Facility may not be sited within one and one-half (1.5) times the height of the Wind Turbine from the nearest property line. The applicable permit granting authority may reduce the minimum setback distance as appropriate based on site-specific considerations, or written consent of the affected abutter(s), if the project satisfies all other criteria for the granting of a building permit under the provisions of this Section.

A Wind Turbine for a Utility Scale Wind Energy Facility may not be sited within a distance equal to the height of the Wind Turbine from private or public ways that are not part of the Wind Energy Facility. The applicable permit granting authority may reduce the minimum setback distance as appropriate based on site-specific considerations, or written consent of the affected abutter(s), if the project satisfies all other criteria for the granting of a building permit under the provisions of this Section.

Wind Turbines shall not be used for displaying any advertising except for reasonable identification of the manufacturer or operator of the wind energy facility. Signs on Wind Energy Facilities shall comply with Section 6.3. The following signs are required: (a) At least one (1) sign shall be posted near ground level on the tower structure warning of high voltage and any danger; (b) Signage necessary to identify the owner, including a twenty-four (24) hour emergency contact phone number; and (c) Educational signs providing information about the facility and the benefits of renewable energy. In addition, the following information shall be posted on a label on the generator or alternator of the Wind Turbine, and on the Wind Turbine control panel: maximum power output of system and wind speed at which it is achieved; nominal voltages and maximum current; manufacturer’s name and address, model number and serial number; normal and emergency shutdown procedures; and maximum wind speed the Wind Turbine can sustain without damage or loss of function.

Section 7.4.8(19) states that "Clearing of natural vegetation shall be limited to that which is necessary for the construction operation and maintenance of the wind energy facility or otherwise prescribed by applicable laws, regulations and bylaws." Section 7.4.9(3) requires "Stabilization or re-vegetation of the site as necessary to minimize erosion" during decommissioning.

Utility Scale Wind Energy Facilities (referred to as Wind Energy Facilities) require a special permit from the Zoning Board of Appeals when located outside the Commercial Overlay District. Within the Commercial Overlay District (COD), Wind Energy Facilities are permitted by right subject to site plan review by the Planning Board, and a special permit is not required. The COD is the designated location where as of right siting applies, and outside this district, the Zoning Board of Appeals is the Special Permit Granting Authority.

A Wind Turbine for a Utility Scale Wind Energy Facility may not be sited within three times the height of the Wind Turbine from the nearest existing residential or commercial Structure. The height of the Wind Turbine is measured from natural grade to the tip of the rotor blade at its highest point.

Section 7.4.7 requires submission of a plan and supporting data including location of the Wind Turbine, nearby buildings, existing tree cover, proposed landscape changes, and a dimensional representation of the Wind Turbine. Section 7.4.14 requires that the site be appropriate considering "visual impact" among other factors. Section 7.4.8(8) requires siting to minimize flicker impacts. These requirements apply to Utility Scale Wind Energy Facilities, defined as commercial facilities with blade-tip height over 150 feet.
Wind turbines shall be painted a non-reflective and non-glare color, which shall be approved by the SPGA.

Wind turbine(s) shall be lighted only if required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The proponent shall provide a copy of the FAA’s determination to establish the required marking and/or lights for the structure. Lighting of equipment structures and any other facilities on site (except lighting) required by the FAA shall be shielded from abutting properties.

Wind turbines shall have a maximum height of three hundred and fifty (350) feet, as measured from the pre-construction grade to the highest point reached by the nacelle. This applies to free-standing wind turbines, which shall be of monopole design.
The minimum distance from the base of any wind turbine tower to any property line in a residential district shall be equal to the total height of the turbine to the highest point.

Signs on the facility shall be limited to those needed to identify the property and the owner and warn of any danger; and educational signs providing information on the technology and renewable energy usage. All signs shall comply with the requirements of the Town’s Sign Bylaw unless relief is granted by the SPGA.

The construction of any wind turbine in the Town of Hanover shall be permitted in all zoning districts, subject to issuance of a Special Permit under this Section, and provided the proposed use complies with all Dimensional Requirements of Section 7 (Dimensional Regulations) and Section 10 (Site Plan Approval), except where alternative requirements are specified herein. The Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA) shall be the Special Permit Granting Authority (SPGA).
section: 6.14.3 Special Permit & Site Plan Approval Required

summary: No free-standing wind turbine shall be constructed within one hundred and fifty (150) feet of any existing or proposed structure except for structures accessory to said tower.

Industrial-Scale Wind Turbine Installation is defined as any wind turbine installation with a maximum height greater than 100 feet. All Industrial-Scale Wind Turbine installations are disallowed in the Town of Heath, effectively limiting maximum turbine height allowed to 100 feet or less. The maximum height is defined as the distance from natural grade to the tip of the wind turbine blade at its highest point.
All Industrial-Scale Wind Turbine installations are hereby not allowed in the Town of Heath, effectively setting the maximum project size or total installation allowed at zero installations.

Section 6.9.4 states that 'All Industrial-Scale Wind Turbine installations are hereby not allowed in the Town of Heath,' establishing a standing prohibition without an expiration date. Additionally, Section 6.7 imposed a 'temporary moratorium' on building permits for large scale wind energy systems until July 1, 2013, but this moratorium has expired.
All Industrial-Scale Wind Turbine installations are hereby not allowed in the Town of Heath, effectively setting the maximum shadow flicker allowed to 0 hours per year.

Construction and use of a Wind Energy System, Meteorological Tower or any part thereof shall be permitted in all zoning districts subject to the requirements set forth in this section (§ 210-196). A WES may be erected upon the issuance of a special permit by the Board of Appeals, provided that the WES is an accessory use to the primary use of the lot (§ 210-198.A).
section: ARTICLE XXX Wind Energy Systems (§ 210-196 and § 210-198)

summary: Unauthorized climbing access to the tower shall be limited by one or more of the following methods: a) by placing climbing apparatus no lower than 10 feet from the ground; b) by placing shielding over climbing apparatus or access; or c) by installation of a fence.

A WES shall be deemed to have been discontinued if it is out of service for a continuous 24-month period. Upon receipt of a Notice of Discontinuance from the Director of Municipal Inspections, the owner shall remove the system at the owner's sole expense within three months of receipt of the Notice of Discontinuance. The Board of Appeals may approve the special permit with conditions, which may include, but shall not be limited to, a performance bond ... to guarantee proper maintenance and/or removal of the WES.
Tower lighting shall not be permitted unless required by the Board of Appeals.

In no instance may the noise level at the lot line exceed 10 dB(A) over the average ambient nighttime sound level. This applies to Wind Energy Systems (WES), which are defined as equipment that converts and then stores or transfers energy from the wind into useable forms of energy.

A WES shall be set back from property lines a distance which is equal to the total height of the WES, measured from the point of a tower base which is closest to the property line. Any WES which is located at least 600 feet from a property line shall be presumed to meet this requirement.
The applicant/owner shall ensure that all related components of the WECS are protected from unlawful access.
All components of the WECS and its support structure shall be painted plain non-reflective muted colors without graphics or other decoration.

A WECS shall be considered to be abandoned if it is not operated for a period of two years, or if it is designated a safety hazard by the Inspector of Buildings. Once a WECS is designated as abandoned, the owner shall be required to physically remove the RWES within 90 days of written notice. "Physically remove" shall include, but not be limited to: Removal of WECS, any equipment shelters and security barriers from the subject property; Proper disposal of the waste materials from the site in accordance with local and state solid waste disposal regulations; Restoring the location of the WECS to its natural condition, except that any landscaping and grading shall remain in the after-condition. The Planning Board may require the posting of a bond or other security to assure satisfactory fulfillment of the above.

The minimum setback for the wind turbine shall be maintained equal to the overall engineer designed fall zone from all boundaries of the site on which the WECS is located. No part of the WECS support structure, including guy wire anchors, may extend closer to the property boundaries than the standard structure setbacks for the zone where the land is located.
WECS shall be setback a distance of four times the blade length from ways, drives, access easements, trails, ascertainable paths and above ground utility lines.

The minimum setback for the wind turbine shall be maintained equal to the overall engineer designed fall zone from all boundaries of the site on which the WECS is located. summary: The ordinance explicitly enacts decommissioning requirements for Commercial Wind Energy Facilities (CWEFs) in the Town of Bethel. Each wind turbine shall be set back at least 200% of the height of the wind turbine from the property line of any non-participating parcel. Property owners may waive this setback with a written mitigation waiver agreement. All set-back distance measurements shall be based on horizontal distances.
Each wind turbine shall be set back at least 200% of the height of the wind turbine from any public way.

Section 14.8.6.3. Shadow Flicker Performance Standards states: 'No more than 10 hours of flicker per year on any non-participating residential parcel.' and 'No more than 10 hours of flicker per year on any roadway (except intersections).' Shadow flicker is not allowed at the intersection of any roadways, effectively zero hours there. These limits apply to Large Wind Energy Facilities of 100 kilowatts or greater.

Each wind turbine shall be set back at least 200% of the height of the wind turbine from the property line of any non-participating parcel. Additionally, each wind turbine shall be set back not less than 4,000 feet from any sensitive receptor on any non-participating parcel. Property owners may waive these setbacks with a written mitigation waiver agreement.

Each wind turbine shall be set back at least 300% from any above-ground electric power line or telephone line except that a lesser setback shall be permitted if the utility agrees, in writing, and this agreement is approved by the Planning Board. This provision does not apply to on site utility lines that are part of the project.

Section 14.8.5.1.12 requires the applicant to provide a Visual Impact Assessment including modeling of the modification of the ridgeline that will result from the placement of the wind turbines. The assessment shall describe the existing character of the surrounding area, including scenic views of the wind energy facility site, and include the scope and scale of potential effect on, as well as distances from, scenic resources as defined in Article 18.

The minimum distance between the blades of a Wind Energy Facility (WEF) and the ground or objects permanently fixed to the ground shall be 25 feet as measured at the lowest point in the arc of the blades.

The ordinance explicitly enacts color or finish requirements for large wind energy systems defined as Wind Energy Facilities (WEFs). Specifically, Section 5.0 Standards, A. Construction, item 6 states: "The color of WEF and MT components shall be off-white, grey or another neutral color approved by the Planning Board." This is a clear and specific color requirement applicable to WEFs, which are defined as systems for the production of electrical power using wind.
The ordinance states that turbines with a capacity exceeding 1 kW shall be mounted on monopole towers, and the overall height of an installation including blades shall not exceed 80 feet.

Sound levels at the property lines of abutters due to the operation of the turbine shall not exceed 35 dBA. This maximum sound level is set for Cushing’s low, rural background noise level and is an adjustment between MDEP and World Health Organization standards for acceptable noise levels at abutters’ property lines.
MTs and WEFs shall be set back from all property lines at least 1.5 times the maximum height of the installation above grade.
WEFs shall not display signs or advertising except to identify the turbine manufacturer, the WEF owner’s emergency contact information, and warnings required by law.

The Town of Cutler has enacted a Moratorium Ordinance regarding Commercial Wind Energy Facilities, defined as facilities that use one or more wind turbines to convert wind energy to electrical energy for the purpose of exporting the energy. The moratorium prohibits acceptance or approval of applications, plans, permits, licenses, and/or fees for any new construction or uses governed by this ordinance. The moratorium took effect on February 15, 2024, and was originally set to expire on August 14, 2024, but was extended by the Selectboard an additional 180 days from August 8, 2025, making the new expiration date February 4, 2026.
The minimum distance between the ground and any wind turbine blades of a WES shall be 25 feet as measured at the lowest arc of the blades.

The ordinance regulates the placement and construction of Wind Energy Systems (WES) to protect public health, safety, and welfare. It includes design standards such as: 'The WES shall be designed and installed such that unauthorized public access via step bolts or a ladder is prevented for a minimum of 12 feet above the ground.' Other standards address height limits, setbacks, noise, and visual impact.

The ordinance regulates Wind Energy Systems (WES) to preserve visual character and minimize environmental impacts. It includes a design standard that "The WES shall incorporate a non-reflective surface to minimize any visual disruptions."

A WES which is not generating electricity for twelve (12) consecutive months shall be deemed abandoned and shall be dismantled and removed from the property by the owner with 120 days of receipt of notice from the town. A WES owner may request in writing to the Code Enforcement Officer an extension of up to one (1) year if the owner is actively pursuing the repair of the WES for future use.
The ordinance states that 'The WES shall not be lighted unless required by the FAA.' This is found in EXHIBIT 10: DESIGN STANDARDS, section (h).

Section 4(a) states: 'A WES shall have a maximum height of 150 feet as measured from the ground to the tower’s highest point.' This applies to Wind Energy Systems (WES) used for electricity generation, including non-residential use, and thus covers large wind energy systems. The unit of measurement is feet.

The ordinance limits the number of Wind Energy Systems (WES) allowed per lot based on lot size: on lots less than five (5) acres, no more than one (1) WES is allowed; on lots five (5) acres or more, one (1) WES is allowed for every additional five acres, with a maximum of three (3) WES on any single lot. This sets a maximum lot size ratio for large systems, with the unit of measurement being acres.

The ordinance limits the number of wind energy systems (WES) allowed per lot: no more than one WES on lots less than five (5) acres, one WES for every additional five acres on larger lots, and no more than three (3) WES on any single lot. This restricts the total installation allowed for large wind energy systems in the Town of Dedham, Maine.

The ordinance states that on lots less than five (5) acres, no more than one (1) WES shall be allowed, and on lots five (5) acres or more, one (1) WES shall be allowed for every additional five acres. This establishes a minimum lot size of five acres per WES for large wind energy systems.
The WES shall not exceed 45 dBA as measured at the adjoining property lines and habitable structures, except during short-term weather events such as severe wind storms.

A WES is a permitted use in all districts. A WES for either residential or non-residential use shall be permitted through the Planning Board. On lots less than five (5) acres, no more than one (1) WES shall be allowed. On lots five (5) acres or more, one (1) WES shall be allowed for every additional five acres. No more than three (3) WES shall be allowed on any single lot.

All parts of a WES shall be setback from all adjoining property lines a minimum distance equal to 150 percent of the height of the tower and blade length (when blades are vertical) as measured from the ground.

All parts of a WES shall be setback from roads and rights-of-way (ROW) a minimum distance equal to 150 percent of the height of the tower and blade length (when blades are vertical) as measured from the ground.

The ordinance regulates the placement and construction of Wind Energy Systems (WES) to preserve visual character and protect public health and safety. It includes detailed site plan review requirements, design standards, and operational rules. Specifically, EXHIBIT 10: DESIGN STANDARDS (i) states that the WES "shall not display any permanent or temporary signs, writing, symbols, logos or any graphic representation of any kind except appropriate manufacturer’s or installer’s identification and warning signs."

All parts of a WES shall be setback from habitable structures a minimum distance equal to 150 percent of the height of the tower and blade length (when blades are vertical) as measured from the ground.

The ordinance requires a scenic assessment for a Wind Energy System (WES) consisting of one or more of the following: a visual analysis composed of elevation drawings showing height above ground level, color treatment, and visual screening; a landscaping plan indicating placement, existing trees, and fencing; and a narrative discussing visibility from designated scenic resources. These requirements apply to all WES, which are defined as systems consisting of a wind turbine, tower, and associated electronics, with a maximum height of 150 feet and blade diameter not exceeding 50 feet.

The minimum distance between the ground and all blades of a Wind Turbine shall be 25 feet as measured at the lowest arc of the blades. This applies to all Wind Energy Facilities, including Type 3 facilities, which are defined as having a generating capacity of 100kW or greater and requiring a state permit.

Section 5.17.10.5.1 defines when a Wind Energy Facility shall be considered Decommissioned, including end of useful life, casualty loss, or failure to operate for six consecutive months. The Code Enforcement Officer must declare the Date of Decommissioning and notify the landowner to remove the facility and restore the site within 120 days. Decommissioning includes removal of all Wind Energy Facility materials and site restoration unless otherwise agreed in writing. Before issuance of any building permit, a Decommissioning Bond equal to 125 percent of the estimated cost must be provided and maintained throughout the facility's lifetime. The bond guarantees the municipality's authority to access funds to perform decommissioning if the landowner fails to do so. The landowner must notify the Code Enforcement Officer if the bond is revoked and provide a replacement bond within 90 days or risk permit voidance. The municipality may recover any excess decommissioning costs through legal means, including special tax or tax lien.

Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities, defined as having a generating capacity of 100 kW or greater and requiring a state permit, are not allowable within the boundaries of the Town of Denmark, Maine. This effectively sets the maximum project size or total installation allowed for Type 3 facilities to zero turbines or zero generating capacity.

Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities are not allowable within the boundaries of the Town of Denmark. Section 5.17.6.1.3 states: 'Type 2 and Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities are not allowable within the boundaries of the Town of Denmark.' The prohibition is absolute and unconditional, with no expiration date provided. The ordinance became effective on January 1, 2017.

Section 11.2.6 states: 'The minimum distance between the ground and all blades of a Wind Turbine shall be twenty-five (25) feet as measured at the lowest arc of the blades.' This is a clear minimum blade clearance requirement for Wind Energy Facility Systems (WEFS).

Section 11.2.4 explicitly enacts climbing prevention requirements for Wind Energy Facility Systems (WEFS) by stating: "A Tower shall not be climbable up to a minimum of fifteen (15) feet above ground surface."

Section 11.4.1 explicitly enacts color or finish requirements for Wind Energy Facility Units (WEFUs), which are components of Wind Energy Facility Systems (WEFS). It requires that all WEFUs "shall be a non-obtrusive color such as white, off-white or gray, or as may otherwise be required by another governmental agency with jurisdiction over the WEFUs." Additionally, Section 11.8.2.H requires the shadow flicker and blade reflection study to include a paint sample demonstrating the color, texture, and gloss of the proposed surface coating and a certification that the surface coating will not create a reflective surface conducive to blade reflection.

Section 10.33 requires a Decommissioning and Site Restoration plan as part of the permit application for a WEFS. The Appendix details that the plan must include triggers for decommissioning such as no electricity generation for 12 months or cessation of operation for 6 months without communication; a description of removal and lawful disposal of all WEFS components and site restoration; an independent engineer's cost estimate; financial assurance covering 100% of decommissioning costs maintained throughout the life of the WEFS; written authorization for Town access to implement decommissioning if the Permittee fails to do so; and transfer of the plan obligations to subsequent owners/operators.

No WEFU or WEFS shall be located so as to generate post-construction sound levels that exceed forty-two (42) dBA at night (7:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.) or fifty-five (55) dBA during the day (7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.) at any Sensitive Receptor in the Town located within four thousand (4,000) feet of any WEFU, except on Project Parcel(s) or on a Participating Parcel(s) which is subject to a Mitigation Waiver which specifies different sound limits.

WEFUs shall be setback a horizontal distance equivalent to one hundred and fifty percent (150%) of the Turbine Height from Project Boundaries, Occupied Buildings, public and private rights-of-way and overhead utility lines that are not part of the proposed WEFS. No waiver of this standard is permitted.

Each WEFU shall be setback a horizontal distance equivalent to one hundred and fifty percent (150%) of the Turbine Height from public and private rights-of-way. No waiver of this standard is permitted.

The application shall not be approved if the shadow flicker study estimates that the duration and location of flicker will exceed any of the limitations: More than thirty (30) hours of flicker per year on any Non-participating Occupied Building unless a Mitigation Waiver is obtained; More than thirty (30) hours of flicker per year on any Town Way; Flicker occurs at intersections of any Town Way in such a manner that traffic safety will be impaired. These limitations shall continue to apply to all WEFS once constructed and throughout the duration of their operation.

Section 11.3.3 states: 'Erosion of soil and sedimentation shall be minimized by employing  "best management practice"  as published in the most current version of the Maine DEP’s  "Maine Erosion Control Handbook for Construction: Best Management Practices" . Access to the WEFUs or WEFS and construction area(s) shall be constructed and maintained following a detailed erosion control plan in a manner designed to control erosion and to provide maneuverability for service and emergency response vehicles.' This requirement explicitly applies to Wind Energy Facility Systems (WEFS) as defined in the ordinance.

All WEFUs shall be set back a horizontal distance of four thousand (4,000) feet from any Occupied Building in Dixfield (Section 11.1.1). Each WEFU shall be setback a horizontal distance equivalent to one hundred and fifty percent (150%) of the Turbine Height from Occupied Buildings (Section 11.1.4). If more than one setback requirement applies, the greater setback distance shall be met (Section 11.1). No waiver is permitted for the 150% Turbine Height setback, while a waiver of the 4,000 feet setback may be granted with a signed waiver and supporting evidence.

Each WEFU shall be setback a horizontal distance equivalent to one hundred and fifty percent (150%) of the Turbine Height from overhead utility lines that are not part of the proposed WEFS. No waiver of this standard is permitted.

Section 11.8 Shadow Flicker and Blade Reflection Assessment and Requirements mandates a detailed shadow flicker and blade reflection study as part of the permit application for WEFS. The study must be prepared by a registered professional, examine areas within a one (1) mile radius of any WEFU, use specified modeling inputs, estimate locations and durations of Shadow Flicker, and include a paint sample demonstrating the proposed surface coating. The Application shall not be approved if the study estimates that the duration and location of flicker will exceed any of the limitations, including more than thirty (30) hours of flicker per year on any Non-participating Occupied Building unless a Mitigation Waiver is obtained. These provisions constitute explicit visual impact assessment requirements for Wind Energy Facility Systems (WEFS).

summary: An Application for a WEF Site Permit shall include a decommissioning and site restoration plan containing the information and meeting the requirements in this section. The plan shall provide for the removal from the Project Parcels, and lawful disposal or disposition of, all Wind Turbines and other structures, hazardous materials, electrical facilities, and all foundations. The plan shall provide for the removal of all access roads. The plan shall provide for the restoration of the Project Parcels to a condition similar to that which existed before construction of the WEF. The plan shall provide for the decommissioning of the site upon the expiration or revocation of the WEF Permit, or upon the abandonment of the WEF. The WEF shall be deemed abandoned if its operation has ceased for twelve consecutive months. The plan shall include provisions for financial surety to ensure completion of decommissioning and site restoration, in form and amount satisfactory to the Planning Board. A performance bond or a cash escrow account held by the Town with 10% of the estimated cost of decommissioning to be added by the WEF on an annual basis shall be acceptable surety, the total amount to be based on the estimated cost of completing the decommissioning and site restoration in accordance with the approved plan, adjusted for inflation, and as approved by the Planning Board. The plan shall include written authorization from the WEF Permittee and all owners of all Project Parcels for the Town to access the Project Parcels and implement the decommissioning and site restoration plan, in the event that the WEF Permittee fails to implement the plan.

These sound limits apply everywhere within one mile (5280 feet) of any WT, except on Project Parcel(s) or on a Participating Parcel(s) which is subject to a Mitigation Waiver. Section 20.12 Decommissioning: The Applicant shall prepare a decommissioning plan in conformance with Appendix C, including provisions for financial assurance. The Applicant shall, at its expense, commence and complete decommissioning of the Wind Energy Facility or portion thereof within: twelve (12) months after the end of the useful life of the facility or portion thereof; or as otherwise specified in the facility proposal as approved by the Planning Board. A Wind Energy Facility is presumed to have reached the end of its useful life if it does not generate electricity for a continuous period of twelve (12) months or for 12 months in a 15-month period. Appendix C Decommissioning Plan: Pursuant to section 20.12, the Applicant shall provide a plan for decommissioning a Type 2 or Type 3 Wind Energy Facility. The decommissioning plan must include, but shall not be limited to the following: a description of the trigger for implementing the decommissioning plan; a description of the work required to physically remove all Wind Turbines, associated foundations to a depth of 36 inches, buildings, cabling, electrical components, and any other Associated Facilities; an estimate of the total cost of decommissioning less salvage value; and demonstration of financial assurance for 100% of the total cost of decommissioning, less salvage value.

The ordinance explicitly sets the maximum turbine height allowed for a Wind Energy Facility, Type 3, as 500 feet. This is stated clearly in Section 18.2 Maximum Turbine Height: 'for a Type 2 or Type 3 WEF: 500 feet.'

Noise resulting from a Type 3 Wind Energy Facility is subject to and controlled in accordance with the provisions of Appendix B. The most restrictive maximum noise level allowed is 40 dBA between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. within 660 feet of any Protected Location. The noise limits include adjustments for tonal and short duration repetitive sounds. These standards apply explicitly to Type 2 and Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities.

A Type 3 wind turbine must be set back a horizontal distance of at least 150% of the turbine height from all property boundaries. The Planning Board may reduce this setback to no less than 110% of the turbine height from a property boundary if the abutting landowner agrees in writing.

A Type 3 wind turbine must be set back a horizontal distance of at least 150% of the turbine height from all property boundaries, public and private rights-of-way. The Planning Board may establish a reduced setback from a private right-of-way owned by a Participating Landowner if the Applicant submits a signed and notarized statement attesting to the landowner’s agreement to a waiver or reduction in the setback requirement.

Type 2 and Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities may not cause an unreasonable adverse shadow flicker or blade reflection effect at any Occupied Building or residence located on a Non-Participating Landowner’s property. "Unreasonable adverse shadow flicker or blade reflection" means shadow flicker or blade reflection occurring for 3 days or more in any one month that, if annualized, would total more than 10 hours of flicker or reflection per year.

Section 18.13 titled "Erosion Control Measures" mandates that erosion of soil and sedimentation must be minimized by employing  "best management practices"  in the  "Maine Erosion Control Handbook for Construction: Best Management Practices" , March 2003, or successor edition if issued by the date of filing of an application for a wind energy facility. Section 17.14(3) requires a maintenance plan for access roads, erosion and sedimentation controls and storm water management facilities as part of the application for Type 2 and Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities.

A Type 3 wind turbine must be set back a horizontal distance of at least 150% of the turbine height from buildings. The Planning Board may reduce this setback to no less than 110% of turbine height if the abutting landowner agrees in writing. Additionally, no Type 3 wind turbine may be constructed or operated within 5,280 feet of any Sensitive Receptor, which includes residences or other places intended for human habitation.

Section 20.5 ('Effect on Scenic Resources') requires that if a Type 3 Wind Energy Facility is proposed for location in or is visible from a Scenic Resource, the applicant shall provide to the Planning Board a visual impact assessment as part of its application. The assessment must address the evaluation criteria set forth in subsection 20.5.3. Section 17.14(4) requires a visual impact assessment, if required pursuant to section 20.5, for Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities.
