Wind turbines and towers shall have a color or finish that is non-reflective and non-obtrusive (galvanized steel, brushed aluminum, or white) as was originally applied by the manufacturer, unless otherwise required by the Federal Aviation Administration or another governmental agency.

Section 2-13.9.4 states: "Wind Energy Systems shall not be artificially lighted, except to the extent required by the Federal Aviation Administration or other applicable authority." This lighting requirement applies to Wind Energy Systems, including Type 3 Wind Energy Systems defined as "A wind energy system generating more than 100kw which requires a State permit issued by the Maine Department of Environmental Protection."
Section 2-13.7.2 states that 'Type 2 Wind Energy Systems are a permitted use in the Rural and Rural-Manufactured zones.'

Section 2-13.7.3 states that "Type 3 Wind Energy Systems are not a permitted use." This is a clear and unconditional prohibition on Type 3 Wind Energy Systems with no expiration date or conditional exceptions mentioned.

The Towers for a Wind Energy System shall be set back a distance equal to 1.5 times the maximum Turbine Height, measured from the center of the base of the tower, to all property lines, unless appropriate easements are secured from adjacent property owners. In no case shall Wind Energy Systems be permitted within the front, side, or rear setback of any property.

The Towers for a Wind Energy System shall be set back a distance equal to 1.5 times the maximum Turbine Height, measured from the center of the base of the tower, to other right-of ways, including railroads.

The Towers for a Wind Energy System shall be set back a distance equal to 1.5 times the maximum Turbine Height, measured from the center of the base of the tower, to public and private road right-of-ways, unless written permission is granted by the owner(s) with jurisdiction over said right-of-way(s).

The Towers for a Wind Energy System shall be set back a distance equal to 1.5 times the maximum Turbine Height, measured from the center of the base of the tower, to all inhabited or inhabitable residential structures, other than those owned or inhabited by the owner.

The Tower of any Wind Energy System’s wind tower shall be set back from the Tower of any other Energy Systems’ wind towers a distance equal to 1.5 times the rotor diameter. This establishes the minimum allowed spacing between individual turbines, including Type 3 Wind Energy Systems.

The Towers for a Wind Energy System shall be set back a distance equal to 1.5 times the maximum Turbine Height, measured from the center of the base of the tower, to all overhead public utility and telephone lines, unless written permission is granted by the affected utility or Telephone Company.

The ordinance requires, as part of the permit and site plan review process for Type 3 Wind Energy Systems, submission of elevation drawings, photo representations showing color and screening, and a narrative discussing visibility from abutting properties and designated scenic resources. These are detailed under 'Wind Energy Systems – Additional Plan Requirements' and include: elevation drawings of the proposed wind tower system in relation to other structures and existing vegetation; photo representations taken from perspectives determined by the Site Plan Review Committee or Town Planner; and a narrative discussing the tree line elevation within 100 feet and the extent of visibility from abutting properties and scenic resources.
section: Wind Energy Systems – Additional Plan Requirements

summary: The minimum distance between the ground and all blades of a wind turbine shall be 25 feet as measured at the lowest arc of the blades. This applies to Commercial Wind Energy Facilities (CWEF), which are defined as wind energy facilities whose primary purpose is to sell electricity to the regional electric power grid.
A wind turbine shall have a non-obtrusive color such as white, off-white or gray, with a matte finish, or as may otherwise be required by another governmental agency with jurisdiction over the CWEF.

The CWEF shall be decommissioned within twelve months after it ceases to generate electricity, is discontinued, or as the result of legal action as provided for in Section 1-110.2. At least six (6) months from the anticipated start date of decommissioning the owner of the CWEF shall submit to the planning board a final decommissioning plan for review and approval. The final decommissioning plan shall include but not limited to the following: anticipated start and completion dates, methods to remove all parts of the CWEF including foundations and how they will be disposed of, areas and methods to restore disturbed land areas, time period to complete decommissioning, and cost for decommissioning. Decommissioning shall include removal and disposal off-site of all parts of the CWEF (including foundations) in accordance with local, state and federal laws and regulations. No permit for a CWEF shall be issued until decommissioning funds have been posted by the Applicant with a bonding company or a Federal or State-chartered lending institution approved by the Selectmen. Estimates shall be redone every two years and the owner/operator shall maintain decommissioning funds at least equal to the most recent estimate. If the owner/operator does not complete decommissioning within the prescribed time period, the Town may take necessary action to secure the posted funds and ensure completion of decommissioning.

Radar-activated obstruction lighting systems shall be used on all towers and all lighting of towers shall conform to the Federal Aviation Administration standards. A wind turbine shall not be lighted artificially, except to the extent consistent with Federal Aviation Administration recommendations or other applicable authority that regulates air safety or as is otherwise required by another governmental agency with jurisdiction over the CWEF.
The maximum turbine height shall not exceed 250 feet as measured from the surface (top) of the tower base to the highest point of any turbine rotor blade measured at the highest arc of the blade.

The ordinance sets audible sound level limits for routine operation of Commercial Wind Energy Facilities (CWEF) measured at non-participating landowner’s property lines: 35 dBA between 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. (daytime hourly limit), and 25 dBA between 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. (nighttime hourly limit). The most restrictive limit is 25 dBA at night. These limits are explicitly stated to protect public health, safety, and welfare from noise impacts of CWEF.
The minimum setback from any tower to a non-participating landowner’s property line shall be a minimum of one (1) mile, measured horizontally per 100 feet of tower height, or portion thereof.

Shadow flicker and blade reflection shall not result in more than 30 hours of flicker per year on any non-participating occupied building and not more than 10 hours of flicker per year on any public or private road that interferes with traffic movement safety. The most restrictive maximum shadow flicker allowed is 10 hr/year on roads.
section: K. Shadow Flicker and Blade Reflection

summary: A clearly visible warning sign that conform to applicable ANSI and OSHA standards concerning voltage must be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations. A wind turbine shall not be used to support signs and shall not display advertising except for reasonable and incidental identification of the turbine manufacturer, facility owner and operator, and for warnings.
section: H. Voltage Warnings and I. Visual Appearance

summary: The ordinance applies to Commercial Wind Energy Facilities (CWEF) and requires a visual impact assessment as part of the application materials (Section 1-201.1.A, item 14). It mandates that if a CWEF is proposed for location in or is visible from a scenic resource, the Applicant shall provide a visual impact assessment that addresses the evaluation criteria in subsection 3 (Section 1-701.3.J). The Planning Board may require a visual impact assessment for portions of the CWEF located more than three miles and up to eight miles from a scenic resource if it finds it necessary to determine potential significant adverse effects. The Planning Board shall consider factors such as the significance of the scenic resource, existing character of the area, expectations of viewers, and the scope and scale of the potential effect of views of the CWEF on the scenic resource.

Any wind turbine that is not operated for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months shall be considered abandoned and shall be removed by the owner within ninety (90) days of receipt of notice from the Code Enforcement Officer. Upon abandonment or the end of the useful life of the wind turbine, the owner shall remove the wind turbine and all associated equipment and restore the site to its original condition.
No lighting shall be installed on wind turbines except as required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

The maximum height of any wind turbine, as measured from the ground to the tip of the blade at its highest point, shall not exceed 100 feet. This applies to wind turbines including those defined as Wind Energy Facilities.

Wind turbines shall not exceed 50 decibels (dBA), as measured at the property line. This applies to Wind Energy Facilities, defined as facilities consisting of one or more wind turbines supplying electricity to off-site customers.
Wind Turbine, Commercial is permitted by right (PB) in the HCV, RR, and SHV districts (4.6.1). Additionally, wind turbines shall be a permitted use in all Districts (5.3.39.1.a).

Wind Energy Facilities, as defined in this Ordinance, are prohibited in all districts. Section 5.3.39.C states: 'Wind Energy Facilities, as defined in this Ordinance, are prohibited in all districts.' The prohibition is unconditional and does not have an expiration date. Additionally, section 4.6.2 shows 'Wind Energy Facility' use is marked as 'No' in all listed districts.

Wind turbines shall be set back from all property lines ... a distance equal to 1.5 times the total height of the wind turbine, as measured from the ground to the tip of the blade at its highest point.

Wind turbines shall be set back from all public ways a distance equal to 1.5 times the total height of the wind turbine, as measured from the ground to the tip of the blade at its highest point. This applies to Wind Energy Facilities, defined as facilities supplying electricity to off-site customers.

Wind Energy Facilities, as defined in this Ordinance, are prohibited in all districts (Section 4.6.2 and 5.3.39.C), effectively setting the maximum shadow flicker allowed to 0 hours per year. For commercial wind turbines, the ordinance requires that "Wind turbines shall be sited in a manner that minimizes shadow flicker on adjacent properties" (Section 5.3.39.D.4), but no explicit numerical limit is provided. The units for shadow flicker are assumed to be hours per year (hr/year).

No advertising or signage shall be placed on any wind turbine. Wind Energy Facilities, as defined in this Ordinance, are prohibited in all districts. All wind turbines require a permit from the Planning Board and must comply with all applicable standards in this Ordinance.

Wind Turbine, Commercial is listed as 'PB' in districts HCV, RR, and SHV, indicating that it requires Planning Board approval. Section 5.3.39.1.a states that 'Wind turbines shall be a permitted use in all Districts,' but the commercial classification and 'PB' designation clarify that commercial turbines require approval by the Planning Board, constituting a special use or conditional use permitting process.

Wind turbines shall be set back from occupied buildings not on the same lot a distance equal to 1.5 times the total height of the wind turbine, as measured from the ground to the tip of the blade at its highest point.

All WECS shall be protected against unauthorized access by one or more of the following: a. Anti-climbing shroud; b. Removal of tower climbing apparatus to a height of at least ten feet; c. Fence of at least six feet in height; or d. Other device approved by the code enforcement official to prevent unauthorized access.

The ordinance explicitly limits the maximum project size for large wind energy systems by stating 'One WECS shall be permitted per lot,' thereby restricting the total installation to one wind energy conversion system per lot.
WECS shall be permitted in all districts except the neighborhood conservation 'B' district, centreville district and urban enterprise district.
WECS shall be set back from all lot lines a minimum distance equivalent to the distance between the ground level elevation and the highest point on the WECS plus ten feet.

Upon abandonment or the end of the useful life of the wind turbine or meteorological tower, the owner shall remove the structure and restore the site to its original condition within ninety (90) days. Any wind turbine or meteorological tower that is not operated for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months shall be considered abandoned, and the owner shall remove the structure within ninety (90) days of receipt of notice from the Code Enforcement Officer.
Wind turbines and meteorological towers shall not be artificially lighted except as required by the Federal Aviation Administration.
The maximum height of a wind turbine or meteorological tower shall be 150 feet, as measured from the ground to the highest point of the blade or tower.

Section 9.13.7 states that 'Wind turbines shall not exceed 55 decibels (dBA) as measured at the property line.' This is the maximum noise level allowed for large wind energy systems, with units explicitly given as dBA.

Wind turbines and meteorological towers shall be set back from all property lines a distance equal to 1.5 times the total height of the structure, as measured from the ground to the highest point of the blade or tower.
Wind turbines shall be set back from all public ways a distance equal to 1.5 times the total height of the structure, as measured from the ground to the highest point of the blade or tower.

Wind turbines and meteorological towers shall be set back from occupied buildings a distance equal to 1.5 times the total height of the structure, as measured from the ground to the highest point of the blade or tower.
The minimum distance between the ground and any part of a rotor blade system shall be fifty (50) feet.

All access doors to towers and electrical equipment shall be lockable. The tower and all ground-level equipment such as transformers and substations shall be enclosed within a security fence at least eight (8) feet in height.

The Owner/Operator of any Wind Energy Facility shall, at their expense, be responsible for complete decommissioning of the project and site restoration within twelve (12) months after it ceases to generate electricity, or after its permit has been revoked. Decommissioning shall include the removal of all parts of the project (including foundations) in accordance with local, state and federal laws and regulations. A professional engineer shall be chosen by the Applicant and approved by the Planning Board to produce a detailed cost estimate of the total decommissioning cost. No permit will be issued until decommissioning funds have been posted. Estimates shall be redone annually and at ownership transfer. Decommissioning Funds may be in the form of a performance bond, surety bond, letter of credit or other financial assurance. If decommissioning is not completed timely, the Town may take necessary actions to secure funds and ensure completion. Any facility unused or out of service for more than eighteen (18) continuous months shall be considered abandoned and removed, with costs assessed as a lien against the property.

Towers shall not be artificially lighted, except as required by the FAA or other applicable authority. All lights shall be designed to minimize visibility from the ground to the extent allowed by the FAA or other applicable authority.
Facilities will be required to meet a minimum setback distance from all property lines equal to 1.5 times the height of the tower plus the length of one blade.

Towers and turbines shall not contain advertising except for reasonable identification of the manufacturer and/or operator of the wind energy facility. Appropriate warning signs shall be placed on electrical equipment and facility entrances.
Towers shall be set back at least 2,500 feet from wetlands of high value for waterfowl and wading bird habitat as identified by Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife.

Maine law requires wind energy developments of at least 100 kW to submit a decommissioning plan detailing turbine and component dismantling, removal of subsurface components to 24 inches, site revegetation, and plans for any components left on-site. The law also mandates financial assurances for total decommissioning costs and requires the licensee to reassess these costs at least every two years, with decommissioning triggered if the facility does not generate electricity for twelve consecutive months.
The minimum distance between the ground and any part of a rotor blade system shall be fifty (50) feet.
The tower and all ground-level equipment such as guide wires, transformers, and substations shall be enclosed within a security fence at least eight (8) feet in height.

All facilities shall employ materials and colors that blend with the surroundings insofar as possible. They shall be initially painted and thereafter repainted as necessary with a non-reflective  "flat"  paint. The color selected shall be one that will minimize their visibility to the greatest extent feasible.

Towers shall not be artificially lighted, except as required by the FAA or other applicable authority. All lights shall be designed to minimize visibility from the ground to the extent allowed by the FAA or other applicable authority.

For facilities on non-farmland, the minimum setback distance from all property lines is equal to 1.5 times the height of the tower plus the length of one blade. For facilities sited on existing farmland, towers shall be a minimum setback distance from all surrounding property lines equal to 1.25 times the height of the tower.

Towers and turbines shall not contain advertising except for reasonable identification of the manufacturer or operator of the wind energy facility. Appropriate warning signs shall be placed on electrical equipment and facility entrances.
The blades of a free standing LWES shall have a minimum clearance of 25 feet above the ground.
The LWES shall be installed so that no step bolts or ladders are less than 15 feet above ground, to prevent public access.
The LWES shall be of a solid, neutral, non-reflective color, such as off-white or light gray.

A LWES that has not generated electricity for twelve consecutive months and/or fallen into disrepair may be deemed abandoned, and shall be removed by the facility owner/operator within 120 days of receipt of notice from the Town of Monson. The Town may require that the owner/operator post a performance guaranty prior to construction in order to assure funds for turbine removal and site restoration in case of abandonment or other cessation of operations of the facility.
No LWES or its mounting shall be lighted unless required by the FAA.

The LWES shall not cause audible noise in excess of 5dBA, or low frequency noise in excess of 20dBC, above the ambient, non-operating noise levels as measured at the nearest property line. The units for the most restrictive noise level are dBA.

Large Scale Wind Energy Facility/System (LWES) is marked as 'P' (permitted) in the I/COM, IFD, and RR districts, indicating it is allowed as a primary use in these districts. The ordinance states: 'j. Large Scale Wind Energy Facility/System          N        N        P          P    P' under the Schedule of Uses. Additional standards and requirements for LWES are detailed in SECTION V but do not negate the permitted status.
A LWES must have a minimum setback of 1.5 times its maximum height from the nearest property line.
A LWES must have a minimum setback of 1.5 times its maximum height from the nearest publicly traveled road.

A LWES shall be designed and sited such that shadow/reflections (changes in light intensity or shadows on the ground or structures caused by LWES blade rotation) shall not affect an off-site occupied structure for more than 10 hours per year.
No signs are permitted on the LWES or its mounting except those appropriate for manufacturer or installer identification and information, or the safety warnings.

Large Scale Wind Energy Facility/System (LWES) is permitted (marked as 'P') in the I/COM, IFD, and RR districts. The ordinance includes special considerations stating that 'the Planning Board may require an escrow fund or other performance guaranty from the applicant' and may require various studies related to environmental impact, noise, and public health and safety. These provisions imply a permitting or approval process by the Planning Board, similar to a special use or conditional use approval. The ordinance also details site requirements, system design requirements, visual appearance, public health and safety standards, and abandonment/decommissioning rules for LWES.
section: SECTION IV: SCHEDULE OF USES and SECTION V: LAND USE STANDARDS

summary: A LWES must have a minimum setback of 1.5 times its maximum height from the nearest occupied structure at the time of submission of the site plan.
A LWES must have a minimum setback of 1.5 times its maximum height from the nearest public utility line.
The minimum distance between the ground and all blades of a Wind Turbine shall be 100 feet as measured at the lowest arc of the blades.
Wind Turbines shall be a non-obtrusive color such as white, off-white or gray, or as may otherwise be required by another governmental agency with jurisdiction over the WTG.

Section 22.0 Decommissioning Standards requires the Owner/operator to complete decommissioning of the WTG within twelve (12) months after the end of the useful life of the WTG, or as specified in the materials provided at the time of application, or pursuant to remedies described in Section 21.8. Decommissioning includes removal of wind turbines and foundations to a depth of 36 inches, removal of buildings, cabling, electrical components, roads, and other associated facilities unless plans for continued beneficial use are approved by the Planning Board. Disturbed earth shall be graded and re-seeded unless the Participating Landowner requests otherwise. An independent and certified Professional Engineer shall estimate decommissioning costs and submit these estimates biennially. The Owner/operator must post and maintain decommissioning funds equal to Net Decommissioning Costs, with bonding or financial assurance acceptable to the Town of Montville. If decommissioning is not completed within prescribed periods, the Town may take necessary measures including court action to ensure completion. The escrow agent releases funds when decommissioning is satisfactorily completed or upon written approval of the Town. Section 28.1.3 references the decommissioning bond requirement, and Section 28.2.48 requires submission of a decommissioning plan compliant with Section 22.0 as part of the application.

No WTG turbine shall be located so as to cause an exceedence of the pre-construction/operation background sound levels by more than 5 dBA or dBC. Audible noise levels (dBA) due to wind turbine operation will not exceed the pre-construction ambient noise level by more than 5 dBA as measured at any property line. Low frequency noise levels (dBC) due to wind turbine operation as measured inside or at any Property Line will not exceed 20 decibels (measured as dBC) above the pre-development ambient noise level (measured as dBA) and a maximum not-to-exceed level of 50 dBC. Property owners may waive these noise restrictions with a written Mitigation Waiver.
section: 12.0 Standards for Setbacks, Noise, Shadow Flicker, and Mitigation Waivers

summary: Setbacks to property lines are a minimum buffer of one mile from the Project Boundary. The Setback Distance is defined as the larger of one mile or 13 times the Turbine Height, measured horizontally from the Project Boundary to the nearest property line. WTGs must be located no closer than the Setback Distance from non-participating property lines. Property owners may waive this setback with a written Mitigation Waiver.
section: 12.0 Standards for Setbacks, Noise, Shadow Flicker, and Mitigation Waivers

summary: Wind Turbines will be set back from any public road a distance no less than 4 times the turbine height, measured horizontally. Setbacks for public roads are based on an approximation of an 1800-foot debris field for ice throw.

Section 12.3.1 states that WTGs shall be designed and sited so that shadow flicker and/or blade reflection will not fall on a receptor except where it does not exceed 10 hours per year for any given receptor. Property owners may waive the Shadow Flicker and Blade Reflection restriction with a written Mitigation Waiver.
section: 12.0 Standards for Setbacks, Noise, Shadow Flicker, and Mitigation Waivers

summary: The WTG will be designed, constructed and maintained in accordance with accepted erosion and sedimentation control methods. The acceptability of the proposed methods will be judged utilizing the  "Maine Erosion Control Handbook for Construction: Best Management Practices" , March 2003. Whenever sedimentation is caused by stripping vegetation or grading it shall be the responsibility of the Owner/operator to remove it from all adjoining surfaces, drainage systems and watercourses and to repair any damage at the Owner/operator’s expense as quickly as possible.

Section 15.3.1 requires that if a WTG is proposed for a location in, or is visible from, a Scenic or Special Resource, the Applicant shall provide the Planning Board with a visual impact assessment that addresses the evaluation criteria in subsection 15.3.3. Section 28.2.28 requires a visual impact assessment pursuant to Section 15.3 as part of the application submission standards. Section 28.2.30 requires sight line, photographic, and elevation information from occupied buildings within the setback and from Scenic or Special Resource locations, including photographs with proposed Wind Turbines superimposed to simulate the WTG when built.

The minimum distance between the ground and all blades of a Wind Turbine shall be twenty-five (25) feet as measured at the lowest arc of the blades. This applies to Large Scale Residential and Commercial Wind Energy Facilities.
section: 6-29 LARGE SCALE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL WIND ENERGY FACILITIES

summary: A Wind Tower shall not be climbable up to a minimum of fifteen (15) feet above ground surface.
section: 6-29 LARGE SCALE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL WIND ENERGY FACILITIES

summary: A Wind Turbine shall be a non-obtrusive color such as white, off-white or gray, or as may otherwise be required by another governmental agency with jurisdiction over the Wind Energy Facility.

The applicant shall submit a decommissioning plan to ensure the removal of the wind energy facility when it is no longer in use. The decommissioning plan shall include a description of the trigger for implementing the decommissioning plan, a description of the work required to physically remove all Wind Turbines, associated foundations, buildings, cabling, electrical components, and any other Associated Facilities, an estimate of the total cost of decommissioning less salvage value, and a demonstration of financial assurance for 100% of the total cost of decommissioning. There is a rebuttable presumption that decommissioning is required if no electricity is generated for a continuous period of twelve (12) months. The municipality may remove the turbine at the Applicant’s expense if not removed within 120 days of notice. The Applicant shall pay all site reclamation costs deemed necessary and reasonable to return the site to its preconstruction condition.
section: 6-29 LARGE SCALE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL WIND ENERGY FACILITIES

summary: Wind energy facilities, including Commercial Wind Energy Facilities, shall not exceed 55 dBA at the property line.
section: 5-44 WIND ENERGY FACILITIES and 6-29 LARGE SCALE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL WIND ENERGY FACILITIES

summary: Wind energy facilities are prohibited in the Shoreland Zone. This prohibition is categorical and unconditional, with no expiration date provided. Outside the Shoreland Zone, Commercial Wind Energy Facilities are subject to permitting, setback, noise, and other operational standards as outlined in the ordinance.

Commercial Wind Energy Facilities must be set back a minimum of 1.5 times the total height of the facility from all public rights-of-way. Additionally, wind turbines in a Commercial Wind Energy Facility shall be setback at least 1,500 feet from any public way.
section: 5-44 WIND ENERGY FACILITIES and 6-29 LARGE SCALE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL WIND ENERGY FACILITIES

summary: Large Scale Residential and Commercial Wind Energy Facilities shall be designed so that shadow flicker will not fall on a Non-Participating Landowner’s property more than fifteen (15) hours per year.
section: 6-29 LARGE SCALE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL WIND ENERGY FACILITIES

summary: Erosion of soil and sedimentation shall be minimized by employing  "best management practices"  in the  "Maine Erosion Control Handbook for Construction: Best Management Practices" , March 2003. Applications for Commercial Wind Energy Facilities shall include a maintenance plan for access roads, erosion and sedimentation controls and storm water management facilities, as well as a stormwater management plan stamped by a Maine-licensed professional engineer.
section: 6-29 LARGE SCALE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL WIND ENERGY FACILITIES

summary: Table 4-1 shows that 'Wind Energy Facilities - Commercial' require Planning Board (PB) approval in LC, SP, LR, RD, and VD districts and are not permitted in RP. Section 5 states that 'The Mount Vernon Planning Board is authorized to review all applications for Large Scale Residential and Commercial Wind Energy Facilities and may approve, deny or approve such applications with conditions in accordance with SECTION 6 Site Plan Review of this Ordinance.' All Wind Energy Facilities require a permit issued in accordance with this Ordinance.
section: SECTION 4 LAND USE DISTRICTS and SECTION 5 LAND USE STANDARDS

summary: Wind Turbines in a Commercial Wind Energy Facility shall be setback a horizontal distance of one mile from the property line of any nonparticipating parcel.

summary: Wind Turbines in a Commercial Wind Energy Facility shall be setback a horizontal distance of at least one thousand five hundred (1,500) feet from any public way or overhead utility lines.

summary: Applications for Commercial Wind Energy Facilities shall include a visual impact assessment, including photographic simulations. The ordinance requires site line representations and photographs with superimposed scaled representations of turbines to assess visual impact. Wind energy facilities shall be designed and located to minimize visual impacts on neighboring properties and public views.
section: 5-44 WIND ENERGY FACILITIES and 4-A. ADDITIONAL DATA REQUIREMENTS FOR LARGE SCALE RESIDENTIAL WIND ENERGY FACILITIES AND COMMERCIAL WIND ENERGY FACILITIES

summary: The minimum distance between the ground and the blades of a WEF shall be 25 feet as measured at the lowest point in the arc of the blades.

The color of WEFTs and MTs shall be off-white or grey or some other unobtrusive color approved by the Town of New Portland Planning Board. The Shadow Flicker Hazard Report must include a paint sample demonstrating the color, texture and gloss of the proposed surface coating and a certification that the proposed surface coating will not create a reflective surface conducive to blade glint. Blade glint is prohibited.

The Owner/Operator of a Type 3 WEF shall, at his/her expense, be responsible for complete Decommissioning of the WEF and site restoration within twelve months after it ceases to generate electricity, or after its operational license has been revoked. Decommissioning shall include removal and disposal outside the Town of New Portland of all parts of the WEF (including foundations) in accordance with local, state and federal laws and regulations. Areas of disturbed earth shall be graded, seeded, or otherwise re-vegetated following guidelines provided by the CEO. A Professional Engineer shall estimate the total cost of Decommissioning without consideration of the salvage value of the equipment. No permit for a Type 3 WEF shall be issued until Decommissioning Funds have been posted by the Applicant with a bonding company or a Federal or State-chartered lending institution approved by the Town of New Portland Planning Board and Board of Selectmen. Estimates shall be redone annually and funds maintained accordingly. Decommissioning funds may be in the form of a performance bond, surety bond, letter of credit or other form of financial assurance acceptable to the Town. If the Owner/Operator does not complete Decommissioning within the prescribed time, the Town may take action to secure the posted funds and ensure completion. The Escrow Agent shall not release the Decommissioning Funds except upon written approval of the Town of New Portland Planning Board and Board of Selectmen.

All WEFs shall be designed and sited to minimize nighttime light pollution and shall not exceed the minimal requirements by the Federal Aviation Authority. Red lights shall be used instead of white if possible and shall be shielded to the greatest extent possible from viewers on the ground. An applicant for a WEF shall provide a plan showing all lighting on and around the WEF.
Sound levels due to the operation of the WEF shall not exceed 30 dBA or 50 dBC at property lines or structures in the Town of New Portland. The most restrictive maximum noise level allowed is 30 dBA.

All set-back distance measurements shall be based on horizontal distances between the center axis of any WEF Turbine and a property line. The setback distance for Falling & Debris Hazard is calculated as S = Ho x 1.5, where Ho is the overall turbine height (measured to the top of an upright blade). If more than one set-back requirement applies, the greatest set-back distance shall be met.

WEFs shall be designed and sited so that shadow flicker will not fall on a Flicker Receptor as defined in Section 6.0. An exception to this standard may be made based on the following condition only, namely that the total flicker from all proposed WEF towers does not exceed 1 hour per year for any given Flicker Receptor.
section: 9.9 Flicker Hazard Limits and Flicker Hazard Report/study

summary: WEFs shall not be used to display signs or advertising except for signs at ground level identifying the turbine manufacturer, the WEF Owner/Operator, emergency contact information, and appropriate warnings as required by national, state, and local laws.

Section 10.5 states that Type 3 WEFs "shall be designed, constructed, and maintained in accordance with accepted erosion and sediment control methods as set out in the Maine Erosion Control Handbook for Construction; The Best Management Practices, dated March (2003)." Section 10.3 requires that "The design, construction, and maintenance of a WEF shall protect all environmentally sensitive areas that may be affected by its siting," including wetlands, steep slopes, and watersheds, with appropriate measures for protection during construction and operation.

A Visual Impact Assessment shall be submitted as part of the initial application for a Wind Energy Facility within the Town of New Portland. The Preliminary Application for a Wind Energy Facility shall include: Project Description including detailed characteristics of proposed turbines and their locations; Viewshed analysis map showing all areas from which any part of the proposed facility would potentially be visible; Virtual Simulations of how the facility will appear from residences; Field assessment and Inventory of views. The applicant shall pay for the services of all consultants that the Planning Board deems necessary to evaluate the application. The Visual Impact Assessment is specified in section 9.10 and required for Type 3 WEF applications as per section 14.2.1.
The minimum distance between the ground and all blades of a Wind Turbine shall be 25 feet as measured at the lowest arc of the blades.

A Wind Turbine shall have a non-obtrusive color such as white, off-white or gray, with a matte finish, or as may otherwise be required by another governmental agency with jurisdiction over the Wind Energy Facility.

The Wind Energy Facility shall be decommissioned within twelve months after it ceases to generate electricity, or after any permit has been revoked. Decommissioning shall include removal and disposal off-site of all parts of the Wind Energy Facility (including foundations) in accordance with local, state and federal laws and regulations. Areas of disturbed earth shall be graded, reseeded, or otherwise re-vegetated, unless the landowner of the affected land requests otherwise in writing. A Licensed Professional Engineer shall be retained by the Planning Board and paid for by the Applicant to estimate the total cost of decommissioning and itemization of the estimated major expenses. No permit for a Wind Energy Facility shall be issued until Decommissioning Funds have been posted by the Applicant with a bonding company or a Federal or State-chartered lending institution approved by the Selectmen. Estimates shall be redone every two years and the Owner/Operator shall maintain Decommissioning Funds at least equal to the most recent estimate. Decommissioning funds may be in the form of a performance bond, surety bond or other form of financial assurance acceptable to the Selectmen. If the Owner/Operator does not complete decommissioning within the prescribed time period, the Town may take necessary action to secure the posted Decommissioning Funds and ensure completion of the decommissioning.

A Wind Turbine shall not be lighted artificially, except to the extent consistent with Federal Aviation Administration recommendations or other applicable authority that regulates air safety or as is otherwise required by another governmental agency with jurisdiction over the Wind Energy Facility.

Wind Turbines shall be set back, at a minimum, a horizontal distance equivalent to 150% of the Turbine Height from public and private rights-of-way, regardless of the municipality in which located, except that the Planning Board may allow a reduced setback if the Applicant submits, in writing a legally binding waiver of the property boundary setback signed by the pertinent abutting landowner.

Shadow flicker and blade reflection shall not result in more than 30 hours of flicker per year on any non-participating occupied building and not more than 10 hours of flicker per year on any public or private road that interferes with traffic movement safety. The most restrictive maximum shadow flicker allowed is 10 hr/year on roads.

A clearly visible warning sign that conform to applicable ANSI and OSHA standards concerning voltage must be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations. A Wind Turbine shall not be used to support signs and shall not display advertising except for reasonable and incidental identification of the turbine manufacturer, facility owner and operator, and for warnings.

Wind Turbines shall be set back, at a minimum, a horizontal distance equivalent to 150% of the Turbine Height from ... overhead utility lines that are not part of the proposed Generating Facility, regardless of the municipality in which located.

The ordinance requires a Visual impact assessment (item 11) as part of the additional information for Commercial Wind Energy Facilities. It also mandates site line, photographic and screening information (item 7), including Sight Line Representations, color photographs with superimposed turbine images, and depiction of proposed screening devices. These requirements apply explicitly to Commercial Wind Energy Facilities as defined in the ordinance.
The minimum distance between the ground and all blades of a Wind Turbine shall be 25 feet as measured at the lowest arc of the blades.

Pursuant to section 13.12, the Applicant shall provide a plan for decommissioning a Type 2 or Type 3 Wind Energy Facility. The decommissioning plan shall include, but shall not be limited to the following: 1. A description of the trigger for implementing the decommissioning plan. There is a rebuttable presumption that decommissioning is required if no electricity is generated for a continuous period of twelve (12) months. 2. A description of the work required to physically remove all Wind Turbines, associated foundations to a depth of 24 inches, buildings, cabling, electrical components, and any other Associated Facilities to the extent they are not otherwise in or proposed to be placed into productive use. 3. An estimate of the total cost of decommissioning less salvage value of the equipment and itemization of the estimated major expenses. 4. Demonstration in the form of a performance bond, surety bond, letter of credit, parental guarantee or other form of financial assurance as may be acceptable to the Planning Board that upon the end of the useful life of the Wind Energy Facility the Applicant will have the necessary financial assurance in place for 100% of the total cost of decommissioning, less salvage value. If a permit for a Type 3 Wind Energy Facility expires, the Applicant shall implement pertinent provisions of the approved decommissioning plan.

Noise emanating from a Type 3 Wind Energy Facility shall be controlled in accordance with Appendix B. The hourly sound levels resulting from routine operation of the facility shall not exceed 50 dBA between 7:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. at any Protected Location in an area for which the zoning, or, if unzoned, the existing use or use contemplated under a comprehensive plan, is not predominantly commercial, transportation, or industrial. This is the most restrictive maximum noise level explicitly stated for Type 3 facilities.

Wind Turbines shall be set back a horizontal distance equivalent to 150% of the Turbine Height from property boundaries. The Turbine Height is defined as the distance from the surface of the Tower foundation to the highest point of any turbine rotor blade measured at the highest arc of the blade. A reduced setback may be allowed with a waiver from the abutting landowner or evidence demonstrating the reduced setback is appropriate.

Wind Turbines shall be set back a horizontal distance equivalent to 150% of the Turbine Height from public and private rights-of-way. The setback may be reduced if the Applicant submits a waiver signed by the pertinent abutting landowner or evidence from a licensed professional engineer or manufacturer demonstrating the reduced setback is appropriate.

Erosion of soil and sedimentation shall be minimized by employing  "best management practices"  in the  "Maine Erosion Control Handbook for Construction: Best Management Practices" , March 2003. A stormwater management plan stamped by a Maine-licensed professional engineer is required for Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities. A maintenance plan for access roads, erosion and sedimentation controls and storm water management facilities must be included in the application for Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities.

Section 13.5 Effect on Scenic Resources requires that if a Type 3 Wind Energy Facility is proposed for location in or is visible from a Scenic Resource, the Applicant shall provide the Planning Board a visual impact assessment that addresses the evaluation criteria in subsection 14.5.3. The Planning Board shall determine whether the Type 3 Wind Energy Facility significantly compromises views from a Scenic Resource such that the proposed facility has an unreasonable adverse effect on the scenic character or existing uses related to scenic character of that Scenic Resource.

The minimum distance between the ground and all blades of a Wind Turbine shall be 25 feet as measured at the lowest arc of the blades. This applies to Wind Energy Facilities including Type 3, which are defined as facilities having a generating capacity of 100kW or greater and requiring a state permit issued by the Department of Environmental Protection under the Site Location of Development Act.

Additionally, if a permit for a Type 3 Wind Energy Facility expires, the Applicant shall implement pertinent provisions of the approved decommissioning plan.

Noise emanating from a Type 3 Wind Energy Facility shall be controlled in accordance with the provisions of Appendix B. The most restrictive maximum noise level allowed is 45 dBA between 7:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. at any Protected Location in an area for which the zoning, or, if unzoned, the existing use or use contemplated under a comprehensive plan, is not predominantly commercial, transportation, or industrial. These limits apply explicitly to Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities (≥100 kW and requiring a state permit under the Site Location of Development Act).

For Type 3 Wind Turbines, setbacks from property boundaries (including non-participating property lines, lot lines, facility perimeters, and parcels) shall be a horizontal distance equivalent to the Minimum Setback Distance, defined as 1.5 times the turbine hub height plus the turbine rotor diameter. The Orland Planning Board may allow a reduced setback if the Applicant submits a waiver signed by the pertinent abutting landowner (Mitigation Waiver).

For Type 3 Wind Turbines: Wind Turbines shall be set back a horizontal distance equivalent to the Minimum Setback Distance from public and private rights-of-way. The Minimum Setback Distance is equal to: 1.5 times the turbine hub height plus the turbine rotor diameter. The Orland Planning Board may allow a reduced setback if the Applicant submits a report by a qualified third-party engineer demonstrating that the reduced setback will not adversely impact public safety and welfare.

Section 14.7 states that Type 2 and Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities shall be designed and sited to avoid unreasonable adverse Shadow Flicker and/or blade reflection effects at any Occupied Building located on a Non-Participating Landowner’s property. Type 3 wind energy facilities (≥ 100 kW) require a DEP Site Location Permit and local review and approval by the Orland Planning Board, indicating a permitting process and local board review before approval. The text does not specify any district names or abbreviations where these facilities are permitted.

Wind Turbines shall be set back a horizontal distance of ½ mile (2640 feet) from all non-participating Residences or Protected Locations. Non-participating Landowners may waive this setback with a written Mitigation Waiver.

For Type 3 Wind Turbines: Wind Turbines shall be set back a horizontal distance equivalent to the Minimum Setback Distance from overhead utility lines that are not part of the proposed Generating Facility. The Minimum Setback Distance is equal to: 1.5 times the turbine hub height plus the turbine rotor diameter. The Orland Planning Board may allow a reduced setback if the Applicant submits a report by a qualified third-party engineer demonstrating that the reduced setback will not adversely impact public safety and welfare.

The minimum distance between the ground and the blades of a WEF shall be 25 feet as measured at the lowest point in the arc of the blades. This applies to all Wind Energy Facilities, including Type 3: Large/Commercial Wind Energy Facilities.

This explicitly enacts color or finish requirements for Wind Energy Facility Turbines and Meteorological Towers, including Type 3: Large/Commercial Wind Energy Facilities.

The Owner/Operator of a Type 3 WEF shall, at his/her expense, be responsible for complete Decommissioning of the WEF within twelve months after it ceases to generate electricity, or after its operational license has been revoked. If the Owner/Operator does not complete Decommissioning within the prescribed time, the Town of Phillips may take action to secure the posted funds and ensure completion. The Escrow Agent shall not release the Decommissioning Funds except upon written approval of the Town of Phillips.

Sound levels due to the operation of the WEF shall not exceed 30 dBA or 50 dBC at property lines or structures in the Town of Phillips. This is a clear and specific maximum noise level requirement that an energy system developer must abide by for Type 3 WEFs. The units for the maximum noise level allowed are dBA, which is the standard unit for sound level measurement.

Setback Standards. All MTs and WEFs must be sited so as to satisfy the Setback Standards calculated in Table 1 for the following hazards: Falling and Debris Hazard, Flicker Hazard, Acoustic Hazard. For Type 3 WEFs, Falling and Debris Hazard setback distance is Sf/d = Ho × 1.5, where Ho is Height Overall (height from base to highest point including rotating elements). Flicker Hazard setback requires a Flicker Analysis Report. Acoustic Hazard setback is calculated by Ss=10^((Lw+Lu+Ls+4log(n)-.5-30)/20). The applicant shall graphically depict setbacks as circles or arcs centered on each turbine superimposed on town maps identifying lot owners and lot property lines. Sound levels shall not exceed 30 dBA or 50 dBC at property lines. No static distance is added to the multiplier result for setbacks.

Setback Standards require that all WEFs must be sited to satisfy setback distances calculated for hazards including Falling and Debris Hazard, Flicker Hazard, and Acoustic Hazard. For Type 3 WEFs, the Falling and Debris Hazard setback distance (Sf/d) is calculated as Ho x 1.5, where Ho is the overall height of the turbine measured to the highest point on the structure or rotating element. Applicants must compute and graph these setbacks and overlay them on town maps showing rights-of-way affected by the setbacks. The ordinance does not specify a static distance to add to this multiplier-based setback.

Section 10.5 states that Type 3 WEFs shall be designed, constructed, and maintained in accordance with accepted erosion and sediment control methods as set out in the Maine Erosion Control Handbook for Construction; The Best Management Practices, dated March (2003). The ordinance requires that the Final Application for a Type 3 Wind Energy Facility include a Visual Impact Assessment (if required) as specified in section 10.10 of this Ordinance.

WES shall have a color or finish that is non-reflective and non-obtrusive (galvanized steel, brushed aluminum, or white) as was originally applied by the manufacturer, unless otherwise required by the Federal Aviation Administration.

Shadow flicker, caused by moving Wind Turbine blades and the sun, shall be estimated for all Protected Locations within one mile (5280 feet) distance from a proposed facility. Worst case estimation flicker duration shall be less than thirty (30) hours per year at all Protected Locations.

Wind Turbines shall be setback a horizontal distance equal to 200% of the Turbine Height from ... overhead utility lines that are not part of the Proposed Facility; except, the Town review and approval authority may allow a reduced setback if the Applicant submits in writing 1) a waiver of the property setback requirement signed by the pertinent abutting land owner or, 2) evidence such as operating protocols, safety programs, or recommendations from the equipment manufacturer or a licensed professional engineer having relevant experience with Wind Turbines, that demonstrates that the reduced setback does not compromise safety of adjacent Protected Locations existing at the time of application.

Wind turbines shall be set back a horizontal distance equivalent to 150% of the turbine height from property boundaries, except that the entity responsible for review and approval of the application may allow a reduced setback if the applicant submits, in writing: (a) a waiver of the property boundary setback signed by the pertinent abutting landowner; or (b) evidence... that demonstrates that the reduced setback proposed by the applicant is appropriate.

Wind turbines shall be set back a horizontal distance equivalent to 150% of the turbine height from public and private rights-of-way. The entity responsible for review and approval may allow a reduced setback if the applicant submits, in writing: (a) a waiver of the property boundary setback signed by the pertinent abutting landowner; or (b) evidence, such as operating protocols, safety programs, or recommendations from the manufacturer or a licensed professional engineer with appropriate expertise and experience with wind turbines, that demonstrates that the reduced setback proposed by the applicant is appropriate.
The minimum distance between the ground and all blades of a Wind Turbine shall be 25 feet as measured at the lowest arc of the blades.
A Wind Turbine shall be a non-obtrusive color such as white, off-white or gray, or as may otherwise be required by another governmental agency with jurisdiction over the Wind Energy Facility.

Decommissioning shall include removal of wind turbines and foundations to a depth of 36 inches. All buildings, cabling, electrical components, roads, and any other associated facilities shall be removed unless plans for continued beneficial use are approved by the Planning Board. An independent and certified Professional Engineer shall estimate the total cost of decommissioning, and the Owner/operator shall post and maintain decommissioning funds in an amount equal to Net Decommissioning Costs. If the Owner/operator fails to complete decommissioning within the prescribed period, the Participating Landowner has an additional six (6) months to complete it. Failure by both parties results in violation of the Ordinance and potential Town action to ensure completion. The escrow agent shall release funds upon satisfactory completion or Town approval.

Noise from Type 3 Wind Energy Facilities shall be controlled with hourly sound levels not exceeding 75 dBA at any property line, and at any Protected Location in non-commercial areas, limits are 55 dBA daytime (7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.) and 45 dBA nighttime (7:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.). These limits are expressed in decibels A-weighted (dBA).

Wind Turbines shall be set back a horizontal distance equivalent to 150% of the Turbine Height from property boundaries ... except that the entity responsible for review and approval of the application may allow a reduced setback if the Applicant submits, in writing: 1) a waiver of the property boundary setback signed by the pertinent abutting landowner or; 2) evidence ... that demonstrates that the reduced setback proposed by the Applicant is appropriate.

Wind Turbines shall be set back a horizontal distance equivalent to 150% of the Turbine Height from public and private rights-of-way. Erosion of soil and sedimentation shall be minimized by employing  "best management practices"  in the  "Maine Erosion Control Handbook for Construction: Best Management Practices" , March 2003. An application for a Type 3 Wind Energy Facility shall include a written summary of operation and maintenance procedures for the Wind Energy Facility and a maintenance plan for access roads, erosion and sedimentation controls and storm water management facilities. A stormwater management plan stamped by a Maine-licensed professional engineer is also required.

Section 14.5 Effect on Scenic Resources requires that if a Type 3 Wind Energy Facility is proposed for location in or is visible from a Scenic Resource, the Applicant shall provide the Winter Harbor Planning Board a visual impact assessment that addresses the evaluation criteria in subsection 14.5.3. There is a rebuttable presumption that a visual impact assessment is not required for those portions of a Type 3 Wind Energy Facility that are located more than 5 miles, measured horizontally, from a Scenic Resource. The Winter Harbor Planning Board may require a visual impact assessment for portions located more than 5 miles and up to 10 miles if it finds that a visual impact assessment is needed to determine if there is the potential for significant adverse effects on the Scenic Resource.
The lowest point of the arc created by rotating wind vanes or blades on a wind turbine generator shall be no less than twenty (20) feet.

Wind turbines shall be mounted on tubular towers, painted a non-reflective, non-obtrusive neutral color. The appearance of turbines, towers, and buildings shall be maintained throughout the life of the wind energy facility pursuant to industry standards. The design of the wind energy facility’s buildings and related structures shall, to the extent reasonably possible, use materials, colors, textures, screening, and landscaping that will blend facility components with the natural setting and the environment existing at the time of installation.

Section 9.26, subsection 18 titled 'Removal of Wind Turbine Generators' requires the applicant to submit a decommissioning plan including the anticipated life of the project, estimated decommissioning costs, funding methods, and the manner of decommissioning and site restoration. Any wind turbine generator or anemometer tower inoperational for twelve (12) months shall be considered abandoned and must be removed within one hundred eighty (180) days. The owner must restore the site to its original condition, including removal of foundations to a minimum depth of five (5) feet and site vegetation restoration. The Planning Commission may require a performance guarantee equal to the estimated removal and restoration costs, reviewed every five (5) years and adjusted for inflation.

Wind turbine generators shall not be artificially lighted, except to the extent required by the FAA or the MAC or other applicable authority, or otherwise necessary for the reasonable safety and security thereof. If lighting is required, the lighting alternatives and design chosen: (1) Shall be the intensity required under State or federal regulations. (2) Shall not be strobe lighting or other intermittent white lighting fixtures, unless expressly required by State or federal regulations. Such intermittent lighting shall be alternated with steady red lights at night if acceptable to State or federal regulations. (3) May be a red top light that does not pulsate or blink. (4) All tower lighting required by State or federal regulations shall be shielded to the extent possible to reduce glare and visibility from the ground.

The sound pressure level generated by the wind energy system shall not exceed fifty‐five (55) dB(A) measured at neighboring property lines. If the ambient sound pressure level exceeds fifty‐five (55) dB(A), the standard shall be ambient plus five (5) dB(A).

Each wind turbine generator shall be set back from any adjoining lot line a distance equal to the total height of the wind turbine generator including the top of the blade in its vertical position. The Planning Commission may reduce this setback to no less than one hundred (100) feet; provided the adjoining property is owned or leased by the applicant or an easement is obtained.

A wind turbine generator shall, in all cases, be set back from a public or private road right‐of‐way a minimum distance equal to the height of the wind turbine generator total height as defined in the Ordinance.

The wind turbine generator shall be designed in such a manner as to prevent shadow flicker on any existing structures located off the property on which the wind turbine generator is located. If necessary, the wind turbine generator may be programmed to stop rotating during times when the shadow flicker crosses these structures. This effectively limits shadow flicker to zero hours per year on off-property occupied structures unless written agreements allow otherwise.
Appropriate warning signs shall be placed on wind turbine towers, electrical equipment, and facility entrances.

Commercial Wind Energy Facilities and Anemometer Towers are permitted with a Special Use Permit ('S') in the R-1, R-2, R-3, and R-4 zoning districts, indicating these uses require approval through a special permitting process.

This climbing prevention requirement applies to WECS, which includes commercial WECS as defined in the ordinance.

Each WECS and testing facility shall be painted a non-obtrusive (e.g., white, beige or gray) color that is nonreflective. No striping of color or advertisement shall be visible on the blades or tower.

Upon removal of the WES, the ground must be restored and revegetated to blend with the existing surrounding vegetation. For agricultural lands, this explicitly entails restoration of the soils to their original USDA classification, as confirmed by a soil survey conducted in accordance with standards of the National Cooperative Soil Survey. The decommissioning including restoration shall be completed within one (1) year of the end of project life, inoperability of individual WES turbine(s), or facility abandonment. Extensions may be granted upon written request to the Planning Commission prior to expiration of the one (1) year decommissioning period. The Decommissioning Plan shall state (a) how the facility will be decommissioned to meet the criteria above, (b) how the system and its components will be disposed of or recycled, (c) the Professional Engineer’s estimated cost of decommissioning, (d) the financial resources to be used to accomplish decommissioning, and (e) that the resources shall be deposited with the Eaton County Treasurer. A decommissioning financial guarantee shall be posted prior to the start of construction for an amount necessary to accomplish the work specified in the decommissioning plan as agreed upon by the Eaton County Planning Commission and the applicant and may include an annual escalator or increase based on the Consumer Price Index (or the equivalent or its successor). The financial guarantee for decommissioning shall be in the form of a surety bond executed by a reputable surety company authorized to do business in the State of Michigan or a cash bond posted in lieu of a surety bond. summary: The WECS application shall contain a Decommissioning Plan to ensure it is properly decommissioned upon the end of project life, inoperability of individual WECS turbine, or facility abandonment. Section 21.47.5.1(j) requires an application for a WTG – Large special use permit to include "Elevation drawings, computer generated photographic simulations and other images or other visual aids that depict how the WTG – Large tower and all accessory structures will appear as constructed on the proposed site from vantage points north, south, east and west of the WTG – Large tower." This constitutes a visual impact assessment requirement for WIND TURBINE GENERATOR - LARGE (WTG – Large).
In all cases the minimum height of the lowest position of the wind energy conversion system's blade shall be at least thirty (30) feet above the ground.

Any wind energy conversion system facility shall be equipped with anti-climbing devices. Tower climbing apparatus shall not be located within twelve (12) feet of the ground. A locked, protective fence at least six (6) feet high shall enclose a tower capable of being climbed.

Colors and surface treatment of the wind energy conversion systems and supporting structures shall, to the greatest extent feasible, minimize disruption of the natural characteristics of the site. WETS shall be nonreflective, nonobtrusive in color (e.g., white or gray). The appearance of the turbine, tower, and any ancillary facility shall be maintained throughout the life of the WET.

summary: Section 40-906.B.11 and 40-906.B.12 require the applicant to submit a decommissioning plan including the estimated cost, funding method, removal and restoration procedures, and agreements with landowners. Section 40-907.H details decommissioning requirements: completion within twelve (12) months after end of useful life (presumed if no electricity generated for twelve (12) continuous months), all expenses are the responsibility of the owner/operator, city may perform decommissioning if owner fails, removal of turbine, buildings, electrical components, associated facilities, and foundations to a minimum depth of sixty (60) inches below grade, site stabilization and debris clearing, requirement for decommissioning plan and performance bonds, and possible legal agreements to ensure compliance.

summary: If the wind energy conversion systems are two hundred (200) feet tall, they shall be equipped with air traffic warning lights, which adequately warn oncoming air traffic without being unreasonably obtrusive to neighboring properties. WETS shall not be artificially lighted, except to the extent required by the FAA or other applicable authority, or otherwise necessary for reasonable safety and security.

Wind energy conversion systems shall not exceed a total height of one hundred fifty (150) feet unless the parcel on which the wind energy conversion systems is to be located is ten (10) acres or larger, in which case the maximum total height may be two hundred (200) feet. Such total height shall include both support structure and the highest elevation of the windmill rotor. Additionally, for MWET specifically, the total height shall not exceed two hundred (200) feet.
No more than one MWET shall be installed for every two and one-half (2½) acres of land included in the lot. This means the maximum lot size per MWET is 2.5 acres.
No more than one MWET shall be installed for every two and one-half (2½) acres of land included in the lot. This limits the quantity of MWET installations based on acreage.

A wind energy conversion system shall be located on a parcel at least two and one-half (2½) acres in size. No more than one MWET shall be installed for every two and one-half (2½) acres of land included in the lot.

Audible sound from all WETS shall not exceed 45 dB(A), as measured at the exterior of an occupied structure on a nonparticipating landowner's property. The unit dBA refers to the A-weighted decibel scale as defined by the American National Standards Institute.
section: Sec. 40-907. - General requirements for all WETS.

summary: Wind energy conversion systems shall maintain a minimum setback of two (2) times the total height of the wind energy conversion system from any property line. Property line setback shall be equal to the total height of the MWET as measured from the base of the tower, with possible reduction if certified by a registered engineer that the MWET is designed to collapse, fall, curl, or bend within a shorter distance.

Wind energy conversion systems shall maintain a minimum setback of at least three (3) times the wind energy conversion system height from the right-of-way line of any public road or highway. Each MWET shall be set back from the nearest street a distance equal to the total height of the MWET, determined at the nearest boundary of the underlying right-of-way for such street.

Shadow flicker on a building shall not exceed thirty (30) hours per year for MWET (Medium Wind Energy Turbine). The analysis shall identify situations where shadow flicker may affect the occupants of the buildings for more than thirty (30) hours per year, and describe measures that shall be taken to eliminate or mitigate the problems.
section: Sec. 40-907. - General requirements for all WETS.

summary: Wind energy conversion systems shall include no sign or advertising of any kind, except for one sign, not to exceed two (2) square feet posted at the base of the tower, and said sign shall contain the following information: Warning: high voltage; Manufacturer's name; Operator's name; Emergency phone number; Emergency shutdown procedures. Each WET shall have one sign, not to exceed two (2) square feet in area, posted at the base of the tower and on the security fence if applicable. The sign shall contain at least the following: Warning of high voltage; Manufacturer's and owner/operator's name; and Emergency contact numbers (list more than one number).

A MWET shall be a special land use in the WF and I zoning districts. The summary table in Sec. 40-903 states MWET requires a 'Special land use' application process and is permitted in WF, I districts. Sec. 40-906 details siting and design requirements and states MWET 'shall be a special land use in the WF and I zoning districts.' MWET is also listed as a special land use in the Waterfront district (WF) in Sec. 40-416.02.

Wind energy conversion systems shall maintain a minimum distance of at least 1.25 times the wind energy conversion system's height from any habitable structure. Additionally, the setback from all occupied buildings on the applicant's lot shall be a minimum of twenty (20) feet measured from the base of the tower.

summary: Each MWET shall be set back from the nearest above-ground public electric power line or telephone line a distance equal to the total height of the MWET, as measured from the base of the tower.

The ordinance requires an applicant for a MWET to submit "an evaluation of the likely impacts of the proposed facility" including "aesthetic impacts of the windmill on adjoining properties." MWETs must be "designed and placed in such a manner to minimize, to the greatest extent feasible, adverse visual ... impacts on neighboring areas" and avoid placement on "visually prominent ridgelines." Visual appearance standards mandate that WETS "shall be nonreflective, nonobtrusive in color" and maintained throughout the life of the turbine. Detailed site plans and documentation including noise and shadow flicker compliance and environmental impact studies are required for MWET special land use applications.
The minimum vertical blade tip clearance from grade shall be twenty (20’) feet for Commercial WECS employing a horizontal or vertical axis rotor.

Commercial WECS towers shall not be climbable on the exterior. Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems and/or Meteorological Evaluation Towers, greater than the seventy (70’) feet in height, shall only be permitted by Special Use Permit in the I-1 and I-2 Zoning Districts. They shall not be permitted in any other zoning district. The Commercial WECS shall be designed to prevent unauthorized access to electrical and mechanical components and shall have access doors that are kept securely locked at all times when service personnel are not present.

Commercial WECS projects shall use tubular towers and all Commercial WECS in a project shall be finished in a single, non-reflective matte finished color. No lettering, company insignia, advertising, or graphics shall be on any part of the tower, hub, or blades. Nacelles may have lettering that exhibits the manufacturer's and/or owner's identification.

Section 7.42.B.10 requires a Planning Commission approved decommissioning plan indicating a) the anticipated life of the project, b) the estimated decommissioning costs net of salvage value in current dollars, c) a copy of the surety bond ensuring that funds will be available for decommissioning and restoration, and d) the anticipated manner in which the project will be decommissioned and the site restored. Section 7.42.B.11 mandates a Performance Guarantee to ensure decommissioning of the Commercial WECS within twelve (12) months from the time when it has been abandoned or at the end of its useful life, including removal of the Commercial WECS, electrical components, foundation, and all other associated facilities. Section 7.42.C.16 requires a restoration plan for the site after completion of the project with similar supporting documentation.
The total height of the Commercial WECS shall be defined as the tower height which may not exceed four hundred (400’) feet.
The minimum lot size for a property to be eligible to have a Commercial WECS shall be three hundred twenty (320) acres.

The audible noise or sound pressure level from the operation of the WECS shall not exceed fifty-five (55) db(A), or the ambient sound pressure level plus five (5) db(A), whichever is greater at the property line. This sound pressure shall not be exceeded for more than three (3) minutes in any hour of the day.

Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems and/or Meteorological Evaluation Towers, greater than the seventy (70’) feet in height, shall only be permitted by Special Use Permit in the I-1 and I-2 Zoning Districts. They shall not be permitted in any other zoning district. Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems shall be subject to the regulations and requirements of this Section as well as the general Special Use Permit procedures of Article 6 of this Ordinance.
The setback distance between a Commercial WECS and all property lines, or from the lease unit boundary, shall be equal to one hundred fifty (150%) percent of the height of the tower.
The setback distance between a Commercial WECS and public roads shall be equal to one hundred fifty (150%) percent of the height of the tower.

A sign shall be posted near the tower or operations and maintenance office building that will contain emergency contact information. Signage placed at the road access shall be used to warn visitors about the potential danger of falling or ice thrown from the blades.

Commercial WECS shall comply with applicable parts of the Michigan Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act (Act 451 of 1994, M.C.L. 324.101 et seq.) as shown by having obtained each respective permit with requirements and limitations of those permits reflected on the site plan or supporting documents, including but not limited to: Part 91 Soil Erosion and Sedimentation Control (M.C.L. 324.9101 et seq.).

Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems and/or Meteorological Evaluation Towers, greater than the seventy (70’) feet in height, shall only be permitted by Special Use Permit in the I-1 and I-2 Zoning Districts. They shall not be permitted in any other zoning district. Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems shall be subject to the regulations and requirements of this Section as well as the general Special Use Permit procedures of Article 6 of this Ordinance.

The ordinance explicitly requires a minimum separation between towers of not less than three (3) times the turbine (rotor) blade diameter for Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems (cWECS). This is stated as: 'At a minimum, there shall be a separation between towers of not less than three (3) times the turbine (rotor) blade diameter.' The units are a multiplier of the rotor diameter, not a fixed linear measurement.

The setback distance between a Commercial WECS and ... communication or electrical lines, shall be equal to one hundred fifty (150%) percent of the height of the tower. Overhead transmission lines and power poles shall comply with the setback and placement requirements applicable to public utilities.

Section 7.42 Wind Energy Conversion Systems requires that Commercial WECS projects "shall use tubular towers and all Commercial WECS in a project shall be finished in a single, non-reflective matte finished color." The project "shall be constructed using Commercial WECS of similar design, size, operation, and appearance throughout the project." The applicant shall avoid state or federal scenic areas and significant visual resources. The design of the Commercial WECS' buildings and related structures shall, to the extent reasonably possible, use materials, colors, textures, screening, and landscaping that will blend facility components with the natural setting and the existing environment. The Site Plan Review Procedure requires submission of site plans and supporting documents including environmental and visual impact analyses such as Avian and Wildlife Impact Analysis and Shadow Flicker Analysis. These provisions establish explicit visual impact assessment requirements for Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems (cWECS).
The minimum vertical blade tip clearance from grade shall be forty (40) feet for a WES employing a horizontal axis rotor.

Access to all WESs shall be limited either by means of a fence six (6) feet high around the tower base with a locking portal, or by limiting tower climbing apparatus to no lower than twelve (12) feet from the ground.

summary: All Utility Grid WESs shall meet the following requirements: Each Utility Grid WES shall either be white or maintain a galvanized steel finish.

Any WES that is not operated for a continuous period of twelve (12) months shall be considered abandoned. The owner of any WES that is abandoned or in violation of the permit shall repair it to be in compliance or remove the entire unit within six (6) months of receipt of notice from the County of such abandonment or violation. In addition to removing the WES or anemometer tower, the owner shall restore the site of the WES to its original condition (as it was prior to installing the WES), subject to reasonable wear and tear. Any foundation associated with a WES shall be removed to grade. Failure to remove an abandoned WES within the six (6) month period provided in this subsection shall be grounds for the County to remove the WES at the owner's expense. The Schoolcraft County Zoning Board of Appeals shall require the applicant to provide a performance guarantee that is equal to the reasonable cost of removing the WES and attendant accessory structures as a condition of a permit given pursuant to this section.

WESs shall not be artificially lighted, unless required by the FAA or other applicable governmental authority. If lighting is required, the lighting alternatives and design chosen: a. Shall be the lowest intensity allowable under FAA regulations. b. Shall not be strobe lighting or other intermittent white lighting fixtures, unless expressly required by the FAA. Such intermittent lighting shall be alternated with steady red lights at night if acceptable to the FAA. c. May be a red top light that does not pulsate or blink. d. All tower lighting required by the FAA shall be shielded to the extent possible and acceptable to the FAA to reduce glare and visibility from the ground. e. The Planning Commission may require design changes in order to lessen the visual clutter associated with the site location of multiple wind turbines with non-complementary, inconsistent design within sight of each other.
The maximum height for Utility Grid WESs is two hundred feet (200) feet. The minimum vertical blade tip clearance from grade shall be forty (40) feet for a WES employing a horizontal axis rotor.

Any proposed Utility Grid WES shall produce sound pressure levels that are no more than thirty-five (35) decibels as measured on the dB (A) scale at the property lines of the site and generated noises of the system shall not be greater than five (5) decibels above the ambient noise at the site of any neighboring dwelling.

Shadow flicker expected to be visible on a roadway or a portion of a residential parcel may be acceptable only if it will not exceed 30 hours per year, will not be visible within 100 feet from a structure designed for human occupancy, and will not be visible on a county primary road, or state or federal highway. The maximum shadow flicker allowed on existing dwellings is therefore 0 hr/year.
