summary: A sign of no more than four (4) square feet in area displaying an address and telephone number for emergency calls and informational inquiries shall be posted at the WES site. The emergency telephone number shall allow a caller to contact a responsible individual to address emergencies at any time during or after regular business hours, on weekends and holidays. No Utility Grid WES tower or anemometer tower or site shall include any advertising sign.

Utility Grid WESs applications and projects shall require a VARIANCE and may be permitted only if all of the following standards are met. summary: Section 4.3.79.B.2.c states: "Climb Prevention. All Commercial WECS and SES must be unclimbable by design or protected by anti-climbing devices." This is a clear, specific climbing prevention requirement that applies directly to Commercial WECS as defined in the ordinance.

Section 4.3.79.D Decommissioning requires Commercial WECS proposals to contain a Decommissioning Plan acceptable to the Planning Commission to ensure proper decommissioning upon end of operational life, cessation of use, or abandonment. The plan must include a Professional Engineer’s estimated cost, financial resources in the form of a surety bond or letter of credit (Decommissioning Guarantee), and an agreement with the County. The Decommissioning Guarantee shall be 150% of estimated costs with annual CPI increases, and the County has rights to access these funds and seek injunctive relief if decommissioning is not completed. Decommissioning includes removal of all equipment above and below ground to four feet and restoration of the site to pre-use conditions. The Planning Commission oversees abandonment determinations and enforcement. The ordinance explicitly applies to Commercial WECS as defined in the text.

Commercial WECS shall not exceed four hundred and fifty (450) feet in height. This is explicitly stated in Section 4.3.79.B.3.a of the ordinance, which sets the maximum turbine height allowed for Commercial WECS at 450 feet.

A Commercial WECS petitioned for site plan approval shall not have a development area acreage in excess of one hundred twenty (120) acres. Commercial WECS development area acreage shall be calculated as the height of each individual turbine as the diameter of a circle and the acreage calculated within that dimension for each turbine in the development.

The noise generated from a Commercial WECS shall not exceed forty (40) dB(A) (LAMax - not to be calculated as an average) as measured at the closest Non-Participating property line to the WECS. This sound pressure level may be exceeded during short-term events such as utility shortages or severe windstorm. If the ambient sound pressure level exceeds forty (40) dB(A), the standard shall be the ambient dB(A) plus five (5) dB(A) (LAMax - not to be calculated as an average).

The development area of a Commercial WECS shall not be closer than one and a half (1.5) miles from another development area for a Commercial WECS. The distance is calculated by finding the distance between the nearest two points on their respective development area boundary lines.
section: Section 4.3.79 Renewable Energy Facilities, B.4.c. Area and Separation Requirements

summary: All Commercial WECS shall maintain a setback from a Non-Participating Parcel property line a distance equal to or greater than three hundred fifty (350) percent of its height as measured from the base of the structure to a Non-Participating Parcel property line.

Commercial WECS and SES shall not be subject to property line setbacks between Participating Parcels excepting where a right-of-way is located between properties or bisecting a property whereas setbacks from a right-of-way below shall be utilized.

All Commercial WECS must be setback a distance equal to or greater than one hundred (100) percent of the height of the structure as measured from the base of the structure to a public road or railroad right-of-way.

All Commercial WECS must be setback a distance equal to or greater than one hundred (100) percent of the height of the structure as measured from the base of the structure to a public road or railroad right-of-way. If the right-of-way is also associated with a Non-Participating Parcel, the more stringent setback shall apply.

Commercial WECS and SES shall be designed, sited, operated, and equipped with proven technology to eliminate shadow flicker or glare on any Non-Participating Parcel or public right-of-way, effectively setting the maximum shadow flicker allowed to zero hours per year.

Restoration shall include: road repair, if any, and all re-grading, soil stabilization, and re-vegetation necessary to return the subject property to a stable condition consistent with conditions existing prior to establishment of the Commercial WECS or SES. The restoration process shall comply with all federal state, and county regulations, including but not limited to local erosion control, soil stabilization and/or runoff requirements or ordinances and shall be completed within one (1) year of termination of the project, with termination defined as Abandonment or cessation of operations.

Commercial WECS are permitted by issuance of final site plan by the Planning Commission in the RE, Renewable Energy District. The location, development and operation of such systems are to be regulated in a manner that takes into consideration locational needs of the use, relationship to surrounding uses and densities of land uses, future restoration of property to a productive use and to in general protect the public health, safety and welfare. The use is allowed if standards are met, indicating conditional approval rather than outright permitted use.

All Commercial WECS shall maintain a setback of one hundred (100) percent of its height as measured from the base of the structure to the exterior wall of a principal or accessory structure on a Participating Parcel that is used for residential, commercial or assembly purposes. For accessory structures, the Planning Commission may, at its discretion, allow a setback that is less than one hundred (100) percent of a Commercial WECS height as measured from the base of the structure to the exterior wall of accessory structures on a Participating Parcel, depending on the current use of such accessory structures and potential impact on the use of those accessory structures.

All Commercial WECS must be setback a distance equal to or greater than one hundred (100) percent of the height of the structure as measured from the base of the structure to an existing above-ground public electric power line, telephone line or under-ground gas transmission line, unless said utility owner provides a waiver of such setback. Utility lines implemented as part of the application for a Commercial WECS, or those utility lines installed after the approval Commercial WECS, shall be exempt from meeting this requirement.

Section 4.3.79.B.1.e requires the applicant to provide a study identifying through modeling the potential impact of shadow flicker and/or glare that may be caused by a Commercial WECS and the expected durations of the shadow flicker or glare from sun-rise to sun-set over the course of a calendar year. Section 4.3.79.C.2 states that Commercial WECS shall be designed, sited, operated, and equipped with proven technology to eliminate shadow flicker or glare on any Non-Participating Parcel or public right-of-way.

Each wind turbine must be set back from the nearest inhabited structure, including, but not limited to, a residence, school, hospital, church, or public library a distance of the greater of the following: 1.5 times the height of the wind energy turbine tower (including the top of the blade in its vertical position); or 1,000 feet.

summary: Wind turbines shall be set back a minimum of one and one-half (1.5) times the total height of the turbine from all property lines.
Wind turbines shall be set back a minimum of one and one-half (1.5) times the total height of the turbine from public roads.

Wind energy systems shall be sited so that shadow flicker does not exceed thirty (30) hours per year at any occupied building on adjacent property. The units for this restriction are hours per year (hr/year).
No advertising or signage shall be permitted on wind turbines, except for identification of the manufacturer or operator.

For commercial wind energy systems, wind turbines shall be set back a minimum of one and one-half (1.5) times the total height of the turbine from occupied buildings. All WECS facilities shall either have a climbing apparatus located no closer than 12 feet to the ground or be un-climbable by design for the first 12 feet.

Removal includes the complete tower facility including related infrastructures and equipment to ground level not including any base support pad if so desired by the property owner, and restoration to pre-existing vegetative cover. If the discontinued WECS has not been removed from the site within 180 days following the twelve-month period, the County may complete the removal process and site restoration, the cost of which shall be assessed against the property.
The maximum height of the lowest extent of a Commercial WECS blade shall be 130 feet or thirty feet above any obstacles within 300 feet from the WECS tower, whichever is lower.

Commercial WECS are prohibited within 1000 feet from the Ordinary High Water level from any lake, within 500 feet from the Mississippi River, within 300 feet from any river or stream. This prohibition is categorical and not conditional, and no expiration date is provided.
Commercial WECS facilities shall have a minimum distance to the parcel and/or recorded easement boundary equal to the height of the tower.
Commercial WECS are prohibited within 1000 feet from the Ordinary High Water level from any lake, within 500 feet from the Mississippi River, within 300 feet from any river or stream.

Commercial WECS are permitted in all zoning districts, except as noted in subsection (b), upon issuance of a conditional use permit, and are subject to the provisions of section 78-668. They are prohibited in environmental overlay districts, Mississippi National River Recreation Area (MNRRA), Rum River Wild and Scenic District, and in floodplain or shoreland areas. summary: The Traverse County Wind Energy Ordinance explicitly requires that each Commercial WECS must have a comprehensive Decommissioning Plan detailing the dismantling process and associated costs, including removal procedures, site restoration, and cost estimates (Section 11). Full funding equal to three times the estimated decommissioning cost per turbine must be deposited prior to permit issuance, managed in escrow accounts, with periodic audits and supplementary funding required if funds are insufficient (Section 12.f). The County may file liens against property if decommissioning costs are not covered, and no permit shall be issued without landowner agreement to such liens (Section 12.f.6). All decommissioning activities must comply with approved plans, and deviations require County approval. Enforcement and penalties apply for non-compliance. These requirements apply specifically to Commercial WECS defined as systems with 1 megawatt or more capacity (Section 2.d).

No external tower lighting is permitted unless required by the FAA. Security lighting must be minimized and, where applicable, shielded or controlled to reduce visibility from the ground. Lighting shall be designed to minimize danger to bat populations or migrating birds while maintaining minimum requirements to protect aircraft.

Section 350-103: Standards, subsection 9 - Physical Security requires that each Wind Energy Conversion Unit shall: (a) Not have any climbing pegs, tower ladders or other climbing device of any kind attached closer than fifteen (15) feet from the ground; (b) Have a locked anti-climbing device installed on the unit; (c) If the property owner submits a written request that fencing be required, a minimum six-foot (6') high fence with a locking portal shall be required to enclose each tower or group of towers.

Section 350-105: Decommissioning requires that at the end of its useful life, or when necessary, an individual turbine or entire project must be decommissioned, including dismantling and removing all above-ground components and certain buried components, restoring the site to pre-construction conditions, and obtaining all applicable permits. The Applicant and successors are responsible for all decommissioning costs and must provide a Decommissioning Plan and financial assurance prior to approval. The plan must include estimated costs, funding methods, and restoration procedures. Failure to notify or remove discontinued or decommissioned systems results in penalties and potential use of financial surety by the Town for removal. Restoration must minimize ground disturbance and re-establish native vegetation or crops in agricultural areas. The decommissioning plan must comply with New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets regulations where applicable.

Section 350-103: Standards, subsection 4 - Lighting requires that the final project design shall incorporate measures for visual impact minimization, including the use of aircraft detection lighting system(s) (ADLS) or other similar lighting minimization technologies. Details of the ADLS technology shall be submitted to the Town Board and its consultants along with the FAA’s approval of the specific system used. If ADLS is not permitted by the FAA, the applicant must provide FAA’s determination and rationale. If ADLS is not used, a mitigation plan proposal for other measures, such as light shields, must be approved prior to commencement of project operations. Prior notification of any changes in the lighting plan must be communicated to the Town Planning Board and approved for good cause or to comply with statutory and regulatory requirements. If minimum lighting requirements change during operation, the applicant shall alter the lighting plan and install lighting at a level equal to revised minimum requirements.
The total tip height for each Wind Energy Conversion Unit cannot exceed seven hundred (700) feet as measured from the base of the unit to the tip of the unit’s longest blade.

The level of noise produced by or from the operation of the Wind Energy Conversion System shall not exceed 45 dBA Leq 8-hour at non-participating structures and 40 dBA Leq night (10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.) outside at non-participating structures. The most restrictive maximum noise level allowed is 40 dBA during night hours. Additional noise standards include limits on audible prominent tones and human perceptible vibrations. Units are expressed in dBA, a standard noise measurement unit.

All Wind Energy Conversion Units shall only be located, installed, or constructed on the subject parcel in accordance with the following set backs: A distance not less than 1.5 times the tip height of the Wind Energy Generating Unit as measured from the property lines of any Non-Participating Property.

All Wind Energy Conversion Units shall only be located, installed, or constructed on the subject parcel in accordance with the following set backs: A distance not less than 1.5 times the tip height of the Wind Energy Generating Unit as measured from any and all public roadways or above ground power lines in the vicinity of said unit, to the base of such unit.

The Wind Energy Conversion System shall be designed such that shadow flicker from an individual Wind Energy Conversion Unit will not fall on any portion of a residential or commercial building in excess of twenty five (25) hours per year. If an individual residence is being impacted by multiple Wind Energy Conversion Units, the cumulative effect of said impact shall not exceed twenty-five (25) hours per year.

Section 350-101 requires "a landscape plan showing all existing natural land features, trees, forest cover and all proposed permanent changes to these features, including size and type of plant material and erosion control measures, to be included in the project upon completion. Also to be included are temporary erosion control methods to be used during the construction of the WECS." It also requires "Plans to prevent the pollution of surface or groundwater, erosion of soil both during and after construction, excessive runoff, and flooding of other properties," including a "Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) in accordance with NYSDEC General Permit requirements." Section 350-105(11) mandates restoration of the project site after decommissioning, including minimizing ground disturbance and restoring the site to its original condition, with re-establishment of native seed mix or crops. Section 350-106(1) requires that "upon completion of installation, the site shall be returned as close as possible to its natural state, and in conformity with applicable State and Federal regulations and guidelines, including, but not limited to restoring the subsoil and topsoil to preconstruction condition and reforestation for any woodlands that have been cleared." These requirements apply to Wind Energy Conversion Unit/Wind Turbine (Large Project) as defined in Section 350-98.

summary: Large wind energy systems, referred to as Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS), are permitted only within designated Wind Energy Overlay Districts and require a Special Use Permit issued by the Town Board. Section 350-99 states that Wind Energy Overlay Districts may be created in any zoning district but only upon application for WECS Special Use Permits. Section 350-100 clarifies that no WECS may be constructed or operated except in a Wind Energy Overlay District and pursuant to a Special Use Permit and Building Permit. Section 350-103 reiterates that WECS and related structures may only be constructed with prior Special Use Permit approval from the Town Board.

This distance may be reduced for WECS Small Projects.

All Wind Energy Conversion Units shall only be located, installed, or constructed on the subject parcel in accordance with the following set backs: A distance not less than 1.5 times the tip height of the Wind Energy Generating Unit as measured from any and all public roadways or above ground power lines in the vicinity of said unit, to the base of such unit.

Section 350-101(A)(8)(A) requires a visual impact study assessing the visibility of the project from key viewpoints within a five (5) mile radius of the location of such project, digitally enhanced to simulate the appearance of the as-built project. Additional visual impact mitigation measures are required as part of the application, including a landscape plan and proposed mitigation measures for visual impacts of all components, structures, and materials related to the Wind Energy Conversion Project.

summary: §13 Required Safety Measures includes climbing prevention provisions applicable to WECS, such as: A six-foot-high (6') fence with a locking portal shall be required to enclose each substation and each tower or group of towers, unless the applicant demonstrates in its Application that the Tower(s) is non-climbable and otherwise safe; No climbing pegs or tower ladders shall be located closer than twelve (12') feet to the ground level at the base of the structure for freestanding single pole or guyed towers; WECSs shall be designed to prevent unauthorized external access to electrical and mechanical components and shall have access doors that are kept securely locked at all times.

All structures in a project shall be finished in a single, non-reflective matte finished color or a camouflage scheme. WECSs within a multiple WECS project shall be constructed using wind turbines whose appearance, with respect to one another, is similar within and throughout the Project, to provide reasonable uniformity in overall size, geometry, and rotational speeds. No lettering, company insignia, advertising, or graphics shall be on any part of the tower, hub, or blades.

§10(10) requires a decommissioning plan including anticipated life, estimated costs, funding methods, periodic cost re-estimation, and site restoration. §17 mandates removal of non-functional WECS after 12 months, including removal down to 4 feet below grade and associated facilities. Owners must maintain a Decommissioning Fund or bond payable to the Town for removal and restoration, adjusted every three years for cost changes and inflation. Removal must commence within 30 days of Town directive or the Town may use the Decommissioning Fund to remove the WECS.

Additionally, §5.A requires that all construction and restoration of any Wind Energy Facility, including WECS, located in agricultural areas will be done to the extent practicable according to the New York State Dept. of Agriculture and Market Guidelines for Agricultural Mitigation for Windpower Projects.

summary: Subsection H(7) "Climb prevention/locks" requires that "Wind turbines shall not be climbable up to 15 feet above ground surface" and that "All access doors to wind turbines and electrical equipment shall be locked or fenced, as appropriate, to prevent entry by nonauthorized persons." These requirements apply to wind energy facilities defined as "An electric generating facility whose main purpose is to supply electricity, consisting of one or more wind turbines and other accessory structures and buildings."
Wind turbines shall be a nonreflective, nonobtrusive color such as white, off-white or gray.

The facility owner and operator shall, at its expense, complete decommissioning of the wind energy facility, or individual wind turbines, within 12 months after the end of the useful life of the facility or individual wind turbines. Decommissioning shall include removal of wind turbines, buildings, cabling, electrical components, roads, foundations to a depth of 36 inches, and any other associated facilities. Disturbed earth shall be graded and reseeded, unless the landowner requests in writing that the access roads or other land surface areas not be restored. An independent and certified professional engineer shall be retained to estimate the total cost of decommissioning without regard to salvage value of the equipment, and the cost of decommissioning net salvage value of the equipment. The facility owner or operator shall post and maintain decommissioning funds in an amount equal to net decommissioning costs, with a minimum of 25% of decommissioning costs. Decommissioning funds may be in the form of a performance bond, surety bond, letter of credit, corporate guarantee or other form of financial assurance acceptable to the Town of Benton. If the facility owner or operator fails to complete decommissioning within the prescribed period, the landowner has six months to complete it. If neither completes decommissioning, the Town of Benton may take necessary measures to complete it. The escrow agent shall release the decommissioning funds when decommissioning has been satisfactorily completed or upon written approval of the municipality.

Wind energy facilities shall not be artificially lighted, except to the extent required by the Federal Aviation Administration or other applicable authority that regulates air safety. Lighting shall not be a nuisance to surrounding residences and, when installed on multiple turbines, shall not be synchronized but rather designed to flash independently.
Turbine height shall not exceed 407 feet (base to top of extended blade). This is the maximum turbine height allowed for wind energy facilities as defined in the ordinance.
Audible sound from a wind energy facility shall not exceed 50 dBA, as measured at the exterior of any occupied building on a nonparticipating landowner's property.

All wind turbines shall be set back from the nearest property line a distance of not less than the normal setback requirements for that zoning classification or 1.25 times the turbine height, whichever is greater. The setback distance shall be measured to the center of the wind turbine base. Property owners must adhere to all setbacks. The only exception to this is in the event where there are two adjacent participating landowners, property line setbacks may be waived between the two landowners' properties by way of a written document where the two landowners agree to the waiver. The Planning Board must also agree to the waiver.
section: § 110-15.1. Wind Energy Facilities Overlay (W-E-F) District, Setbacks

summary: All wind turbines shall be set back from the nearest public road a distance of not less than 1.25 times the turbine height, as measured from the right-of-way line of the nearest public road to the center of the wind turbine base.

Wind turbines shall not display advertising, except for reasonable identification of the turbine manufacturer, facility owner and operator at the base of the tower in no larger than six-inch letters. A clearly visible warning sign concerning voltage must be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations. Visible, reflective, colored objects such as flags, reflectors, or tape shall be placed on the anchor points of guy wires and along the guy wires up to a height of 10 feet from the ground.

The ordinance requires that the permit application for wind energy facilities include "a revegetation plan that complies with NYS Ag and Markets restoration guidelines" addressing restoration of temporarily disturbed areas during construction and after decommissioning, and "a drainage plan for construction and operation as well as an erosion plan" must be submitted for approval. Section U outlines detailed soil, erosion, and sediment control requirements for wind power construction projects in agricultural districts, including siting guidelines to "minimize impacts to normal farming operations," construction guidelines such as "culverts and waterbars shall be installed to maintain natural drainage patterns," and restoration guidelines requiring that "all disturbed agricultural areas will be decompacted to a depth of 18 inches" and seeded. It also mandates a "two-year monitoring and remediation" period to address any remaining agricultural impacts. These requirements apply to commercial-scale wind energy facilities as defined in the ordinance.

Wind energy facilities shall be permitted in an overlay zone encompassing A-R-1 districts. No wind energy facility shall be constructed unless a special use permit has been issued approving construction of the facility under these regulations. Special use permits will only be considered within the boundaries of the overlay zone. Wind energy facilities shall not be permitted/constructed in L-R, A-R-B and Hamlet Center Districts.

Wind turbines shall be set back from the nearest occupied building located on a participating landowner's property a distance of not less than the normal setback requirements for that zoning classification or 1.25 times the turbine height, whichever is greater. For occupied buildings on nonparticipating landowners' properties, the setback is at least 2.5 times the turbine height, measured from the center of the wind turbine base to the nearest point on the foundation of the occupied building.

Wind turbines shall be set back from the nearest occupied building located on a participating landowner's property a distance of not less than the normal setback requirements for that zoning classification or 1.25 times the turbine height, whichever is greater. The setback distance shall be measured from the center of the wind turbine base to the nearest point on the foundation of the occupied building.
section: § 110-15.1. Wind Energy Facilities Overlay (W-E-F) District, Setbacks

summary: The minimum distance between the ground and any part of the rotor blade system shall be thirty (30) feet. This applies to all WECS, including Commercial Wind Energy Systems (Large WECS).

All WECS’s shall use monopole construction. All structures in a project shall be finished in a single, non-reflective matte finished color or a camouflage scheme. Individual WECS’s shall be constructed using wind turbines whose appearance with respect to one another, is similar within and throughout a Site, to provide reasonable uniformity in overall size, geometry, and rotational speeds. No lettering, company insignia, advertising, or graphics shall be on any part of the tower, hub, or blades.

Section 17 (Abatement) requires removal of any commercial wind energy facility that remains non-functional or inoperative for a continuous period of 12 months, including removal of the entire above-ground structure and related equipment, at the applicant's expense. Section 18 (Decommissioning Bond or Fund) mandates that the applicant or successors maintain a fund or bond payable to the Town for the removal of non-functional towers and appurtenant facilities, in an amount to be determined by the Town every two years for the period of the life of the facility and until its removal. Section 19 (Permit Revocation) provides that if a WECS is not repaired or brought into compliance after notice, the Town may order removal of the WECS within 90 days and use the security posted pursuant to Section 18 to remove the WECS.
section: Section 17: Abatement; Section 18: Decommissioning Bond or Fund; Section 19: Permit Revocation

Security lighting shall be designed to minimize light pollution, including the use of light hoods, low glare fixtures, and direction lights at the ground. The statistical sound pressure level generated by a WECS shall not exceed L10 – 50 dBA measured at the closest exterior wall of any residence existing at the time of completing the SEQRA review of the application. Each WECS shall be setback from Site boundaries, measured from the center of the WECS, a minimum distance of: Setbacks from adjacent property lines, rights-of-way, easements, public ways or power lines (not to include individual residential feed line) shall be one and one-half times the maximum structure height or 1 ¾ times the maximum engineer-calculated ice or blade throw distance to the maximum point of impact, whichever is greater.

summary: The ordinance requires submission of an Erosion Control Plan and compliance with the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation SPDES General Permit for Storm Water Discharges from Construction Activity if the project disturbs over 1 acre, including filing a Notice of Intent and a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan prior to construction. Storm-water run-off and erosion control, both during construction and thereafter, shall be managed in a manner consistent with all applicable state and Federal laws and regulations and with the Erosion Control Plan provided for in Section 7 of this local law. It also requires no fewer than four (4) color photos taken from locations within a three (3) mile radius, selected by the Town, and computer-enhanced to simulate the appearance of the as-built above ground facilities (7.A.14). Additionally, a visual impact study of the proposed WECS as installed, including a computerized photographic simulation demonstrating any visual impacts from strategic vantage points, color photographs depicting existing conditions, color treatment of the system’s components, and any visual screening intended to lessen visual prominence, must be submitted (7.A.19.b). summary: Each WECS shall be setback from Site boundaries, measured from the center of the WECS, a minimum distance of 100 feet from the state-identified wetlands. This distance may be adjusted to be greater or lesser at the discretion of the Town Board, based on topography, land cover, land uses, and other factors that influence the flight patterns of resident birds.
Minimum allowable height above finished grade at the lowest point of the arc of a rotor blade shall be fifteen (15) feet.
Tower climbing ladders, stairs or similar devices shall be no lower than twelve (12) feet from the ground.

A maximum allowable total height for a wind energy conversion system shall be one hundred five (105) feet unless otherwise restricted or prohibited by federal, state or local laws, rules, or regulations.
The maximum level of sound created by the wind energy conversion system as measured at the lot line shall be no greater than fifty-five (55) decibels (db).

A wind energy conversion system setback shall be a distance that is the greater of either the total height of the wind energy conversion system or the required setback. The total height for a vertical axis rotor installation is the tower height plus one-half the rotor diameter, and for a horizontal rotor installation is the distance from the base at finished grade to the top of the unit.
At least one sign shall be posted at the base of the wind energy conversion system warning of high voltage.

summary: Access to the WECS shall be limited by means of a fence eight feet high with a minimum six inches of security wire on top surrounding the tower base with a locking gate monitored by a security device and tower climbing apparatus to no lower than 15 feet from the ground or a locked door to internal stairs if so equipped.
WECS color will be determined by the Town of Brunswick Planning Board unless an agency of the state or federal government mandates otherwise.
section: E. General regulations for commercial WECS

summary: A decommissioning and site restoration plan is required (D(13)). Any WECS which has ceased service for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months shall be removed from the premises to a place of safe and legal disposal. Additionally, all structures, guy cables, guy anchors and/or enclosures accessory to such WECS shall also be removed. The site shall be restored to a natural condition to a minimum depth of three feet or as otherwise instructed by the Town's Buildings and Code Inspector or as required by the Planning Board. Such removal shall be completed within 18 months of cessation of active use and at the owner's expense. The owner of a WECS shall submit acceptable surety sufficient to ensure the removal of the WECS. This estimate will be reviewed and updated every two years by the Town, and the owner must increase the amount of such guarantee if required. If transmission services are discontinued for over 12 months, the owner must notify the Town's Buildings and Code Inspector within 30 days. Failure to notify and/or remove the obsolete or unused tower in accordance with these regulations shall be a violation of this chapter. The security shall be maintained until the WECS and all associated equipment is removed and the site restored. The surety will be used to guarantee removal and site restoration if the owner fails to comply.

Section D(11) requires applicants for commercial WECS to submit a lighting plan that describes all lighting required, including any lighting required by the FAA, specifying the number, location, color, flashing status, and mitigation measures to control light spillover. Section E(4) states that no WECS shall be artificially lighted unless such lighting is required by a state or federal agency, and FAA-required stroboscopic lighting must be subject to on-site field testing before Planning Board approval.
The maximum height of a WECS shall be no greater than 100 feet. This applies to Wind Energy Conversion System – Utility as defined in the ordinance.
WECS shall be permitted on lots of two acres or more. This minimum lot size applies to Wind Energy Conversion System – Utility as defined by the ordinance.

section: E   General regulations for commercial WECS

Proposed mitigation measures for visual impacts of the WECS should also be submitted. In addition, the applicant should submit a digital-elevation-model-based project visibility map showing the impact of visibility of the project from other locations to a distance radius of three miles from the WECS.

To prevent unauthorized climbing, climbing pegs must be removed from the lower ten feet of the turbine, or ladder access must be restricted. All access doors to wind turbines and electrical equipment must be locked or fenced, as appropriate, to prevent entry by unauthorized persons.
Wind turbines must be a non-obtrusive and non-reflective color, such as white or off-white. The facility owner or operator must maintain the paint on wind turbines at all times in good repair.

A wind farm or wind turbine that has reached the end of its useful life must be removed within six months of such determination. A wind energy system is considered to have reached the end of its useful life when it has been inoperable for six consecutive months. Wind turbines may not be artificially lighted unless otherwise required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) or any other governmental authority. If lighting is required, the lighting must, to the extent feasible, cause the least disturbance to the surrounding areas.

During normal operation, wind turbines may not exceed five dBA over ambient sound as measured at the closest neighboring inhabited dwelling in existence at the time of application for the wind farm. This sound level may be exceeded during short-term events, such as utility outages and storms.

Wind turbines must be set back from all lot lines a distance of 110% of the turbine tip height, as measured from the nearest point on the foundation of the occupied building to the nearest point on the outside edge of a tower. Turbine tip height is measured from the base of the tower to the tip of a prop at maximum vertical rotation.

A wind turbine may not cause shadow flicker to fall upon any window of an inhabited dwelling that exists at the time of application for the wind farm, effectively prohibiting shadow flicker on such windows (0 hr/year).

A  "Danger, High Voltage"  sign must be installed where it is clearly visible by persons standing near the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations. No additional signs or advertising are permitted on the turbine aside from identification of the turbine manufacturer or the facility owner and operator.

Lighting of tower. No tower shall be lit except to comply with FAA requirements. Minimum security lighting for ground level facilities shall be allowed as approved on the Wind Energy Facility development plan.

The applicant shall meet all FAA requirements for lighting.

Appropriate warning sign shall be posted. The type and placement signs shall be determined on an individual basis, as safety needs dictate. This applies to Wind Energy Facilities, which are defined as any Wind Turbine or array of Wind Turbines designed to deliver electricity to the power grid for sale with a combined production capacity of more than 100 kilowatts.

For Wind Energy Facilities only: A decommissioning plan that provides for an estimation of decommissioning costs, the method of ensuring that funds shall be available for decommissioning and restoration of the Site and any off-site areas disturbed by or utilized during decommissioning, the method by which the decommissioning cost estimate shall be kept current, and the manner in which the Wind Energy Facility shall be decommissioned. If any Wind Tower stops converting wind energy into electrical energy for a continuous period of twelve (12) months, the permittee shall remove said system at its own expense following, if applicable, the requirements of the decommissioning plan required under this Law or any Permit.

Wind towers shall not be artificially lighted except as required by the Federal Aviation Administration. No tower shall be lit except to comply with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) requirements. Minimum security lighting for ground level facilities shall be allowed as approved on the Wind Energy Facility development plan.
section: 4.17 Wind Towers and 4.17.5 Wind Energy Facility Development Standards

summary: Wind Energy Facility Wind Turbines shall not exceed 500 feet in Total Height. This height includes the highest point of any wind turbine blade above the tower.
Predicted Wind Turbine Only Sound at off-Site property lines shall not exceed 50 dB(A), and Wind Turbine only noise at Residences shall not exceed 45 dB(A). The units are decibels A-weighted (dBA).

Each Wind Turbine associated with a Wind Energy Facility shall be set back a distance no less than the greater of one and a half (1.5) times the total height of the Wind Turbine or 500 feet from off-Site property boundaries.

Each Wind Turbine associated with a Wind Energy Facility shall be set back a distance no less than the greater of one and a half (1.5) times the total height of the Wind Turbine or 500 feet from Public Roads.
No advertising signs are allowed on any part of the Wind Energy Facility, including fencing and support structures.

Storm water run-off and erosion control shall be managed in a manner consistent with all applicable state and federal laws and regulations and such standards as shall be applied by the Planning Board on the advice of the Town consultants.

Wind Energy Facilities are allowed throughout all areas of the Town of Halcott subject to the requirements of this law. No Wind Energy Facility shall be constructed, reconstructed, modified, or operated except by first obtaining site plan and special use permit approvals by the Town of Halcott Planning Board. The Land Use Schedule lists Wind Towers as subject to special use permit. "All wind towers including Wind Energy Facilities... shall be allowed throughout all areas of the Town subject to the requirements of this law."

Each Wind Turbine associated with a Wind Energy Facility shall be set back a minimum distance of 1,500 feet from Residences. Wind Energy Facility is defined as any Wind Turbine or array of Wind Turbines designed to deliver electricity to the power grid for sale with a combined production capacity of more than 100 kilowatts.

Compliance with the State Environmental Quality Review Act ( "SEQRA" ) shall be required. The Planning Board may require, as part of this review, the following: Visual Impact Analysis, including: (a) Mapping of scenic resources of statewide significance, as defined by the NYS Department of Environmental Conservation Visual Policy (Policy DEP-00-2.), and of local significance, as officially listed in the Town of Halcott Comprehensive Plan. (b) Viewshed mapping and/or cross section analysis to identify areas (including the significant resources identified above) with potential views of the project. (c) Description of the character and quality of the affected landscape. (d) Photographic simulations of what the proposed project will look like from a reasonable number of representative viewpoints within the 5 -mile radius study area to be selected in consultation with the Planning Board. (e) Evaluation of the project's visual impact based on the viewshed mapping and photographic simulations described above. (f) Recommended visual mitigation measures (in accordance with DEC Policy DEP -00-2), if warranted, based on the results of the impact evaluation described above.
The minimum height of the end of rotor blades above ground surface shall be 30 feet.
All wind power facilities must be protected by anti-climbing devices such as fences with locking portals at least 6 feet high or anti-climbing devices 12 feet vertically from the base of the tower.

Towers and blades shall be painted a non-reflective, unobtrusive color that should be selected to blend in with the surrounding environment. No advertising or commercial logos or insignias shall be visible on the structures.

Prior to the granting of a special permit for project development, the Owner or Operator shall formulate a decommissioning plan for review and approval by the Planning Board. The Decommissioning Plan shall include: provisions describing the triggering events for decommissioning of wind power facilities; provisions for the removal of structures, debris and cabling, including those below the soil surface; provisions for the restoration of the soil and vegetation; a timetable approved by the Planning Board for site restoration; an estimate of the decommissioning costs certified by a Professional Engineer; financial assurance, secured by the Owner or Operator, for the purpose of adequately performing decommissioning, in an amount equal to the Professional Engineer’s certified estimate of removal and decommissioning costs; identification of and procedures for Town of Hamilton access to Financial Assurances; a provision that the terms of the Decommissioning Plan shall be binding upon the Owner or Operator or any of their successors, assigns, or heirs; a provision that the Town of Hamilton shall have access to the site, pursuant to reasonable notice, to effectuate or complete removal and decommissioning; removal of machinery, equipment, tower, and all other materials related to the project is to be completed within one year of decommissioning.
To minimize collisions with wildlife the lighting system for the site shall be designed in accordance with latest USF&WS guidelines.

The Applicant shall provide documentation that the minimum noise level generated by wind power facilities shall be no more than 50 dBA as measured at the property lines. The Owner or Operator will provide results of annual noise testing demonstrating compliance with the minimum noise level. Failure to meet minimum noise level may result in revocation to the special permit for the facility.

All towers shall be set back a distance of 1,000 feet from the right-of-way line of public roads. In circumstances where a Wind Power Project is proposed to be on both sides of a public road, the Planning Board may waive this setback requirement but only where the waiver furthers the mitigation of impacts and in no case shall towers be located closer than two times the wind power tower height from public roads.
A reasonable warning sign concerning voltage must be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations.

Section 6.10–2 N.1 requires the Applicant to demonstrate the Project will not infringe upon any designated wetlands and that appropriate measures will be taken to minimize soil erosion and watershed impacts. Appropriate State/Federal wetland permits need to be filed and approved and submitted with the application. Section 6.10–1 A.3 requires a site plan including soil protection/restoration locations. Section 6.10–2 P.3 requires provisions for the restoration of the soil and vegetation in the decommissioning plan.

Commercial wind power facilities require a special permit from the Planning Board (Section 6.10–1). The Town of Hamilton Use Table shows that Wind Power Equipment is permitted by special permit (SP) in the Agricultural-Residential and Commercial Districts, but not permitted (NP) in the Residential and Hamlet districts.

All towers shall be set back at least 1,000 feet from any primary structure. The Planning Board may waive the setback requirement, but in no case shall a tower used for commercial power generation be located closer to a primary structure less than two times the wind power tower height. No wind turbines shall be located within eight (8) rotor hub heights of an existing residence, unless shadow flicker impacts are mitigated by documentation or legally binding agreements.

All towers shall be set back a distance of at least 1.5 times the wind power tower height from any other wind power tower. The unit is a multiplier of the wind power tower height, which is measured in feet.
All towers shall be set back at least 1,000 feet from third party transmission lines and communication towers.

Section 6.10–2, subsection I "Viewscape impacts" requires the Applicant to provide a digital elevation model visibility map showing the impact of the project on the viewscape within a five-mile radius, 3x5"  color photographs illustrating the view from the proposed project site in a 360 degree arc and from all primary structures within one mile, and allows the Planning Board to assess the viewscape impact with regard to the number of properties and primary structures impacted. The Planning Board may require digitally enhanced simulation photos illustrating proposed facilities on the project site.
The minimum distance between the ground and any part of the rotor or blade system shall be thirty-five (35) feet.

Section 5.6 "Required Safety Measures" includes climbing prevention provisions applicable to WECS, such as: "No climbing pegs or tower ladders shall be located closer than twelve (12) feet to the ground level at the base of the structure for freestanding single pole or guyed towers." and "WECSs shall be designed to prevent unauthorized external access to electrical and mechanical components and shall have access doors that are kept securely locked."

All structures in a project shall be finished in a single, non-reflective matte finished color or a camouflage scheme. Individual WECS shall be constructed using wind turbines whose appearance, with respect to one another, is similar within and throughout the Wind Overlay District, to provide reasonable uniformity in overall size, geometry, and rotational speeds. No lettering, company insignia, advertising, or graphics shall be on any part of the tower, hub, or blades.

Section 5.10 titled "Decommissioning" requires removal of any WECS that remains non-functional or inoperative for a continuous period of one year at the applicant's expense. An application for a Wind Energy Facility permit must include a decommissioning and site restoration plan providing for removal of all Wind Turbines, structures, hazardous materials, electrical facilities, and foundations to a depth of not less than 48 inches below grade, restoration of the Project Parcels to farmland of similar condition, estimated decommissioning cost, financial security of no less than 125% of the cost, and written authorization for Town access to implement the plan if the permit holder fails to do so. The plan also requires that any non-functional or inoperative utility scale WECS be removed within 180 days of becoming non-functional or permit revocation, with the Town authorized to use the decommissioning fund to remove and restore the site if the permittee fails to do so.

Lighting of tower. No tower shall be lit except to comply with FAA requirements. Motion-sensitive on-demand lighting is required. Minimum-security lighting for ground level facilities shall be allowed as approved on the Site plan. The application should include a Lighting Plan showing any FAA-required lighting and other proposed lighting. No building permit for any lighted facility may be issued until such determination is submitted.

Section 5.5.14 states: 'The maximum Total Height of any WECS shall be 500 feet.' This is a clear and specific maximum height limit applicable to Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS), defined as machines converting wind kinetic energy into electricity with rated capacity over 100 kW.

The equivalent level (LEQ) generated by a Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) shall not exceed 35 dBA at nighttime (8 PM to 7 AM) when measured at the nearest off-site dwelling existing at the time of application. The noise limits are specified in Table 1, with the most restrictive being 35 dBA nighttime A-weighted level. The noise analysis must be performed according to the International Standard for Acoustic Noise Measurement Techniques for Wind Generators (IEC 61400-11) or other procedure accepted by the Town Planning Board.
section: 5.8. Noise Standards for Wind Energy Conversion Systems

summary: Each WECS shall be setback measured from the center of the WECS a minimum of five times the total height of the proposed WECS from the nearest site boundary property line. Where multiple lots are in single ownership or are combined through an Easement Agreement, the combined lots shall be considered as one for the purposes of the setback requirements imposed by this Law. However, in no instance shall the Easement provide for a setback between a WECS and a residence that is less than five times the total height of the WECS.
Each WECS shall be setback measured from the center of the WECS a minimum of five times the total height of the proposed WECS from the nearest public road.

No advertising signs are allowed on any part of the Wind Energy Facility, including fencing and support structures. Appropriate warning signs shall be posted. At least one sign shall be posted at the base of the tower warning of electrical shock or high voltage. A sign shall be posted on the entry area of fence around each tower or group of towers and any building (or on the tower or building if there is no fence), containing emergency contact information, including a local telephone number with 24 hour, 7-day week coverage. The Town Planning Board may require additional signs based on safety needs.
section: 5.5. Standards for WECS and 5.6. Required Safety Measures

summary: Section 5.5.9 requires WECS to be designed to minimize the impacts of land clearing and the loss of open space areas, with compliance required with the New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets Guidelines for Agricultural Mitigation for Wind Power Projects. Section 5.5.12 mandates that storm-water run-off and erosion control shall be managed in a manner consistent with all applicable state and Federal laws and regulations, also requiring compliance with the New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets Guidelines for Agricultural Mitigation for Wind Power Projects. Section 5.10.3.1 requires removal of all foundations to a depth of not less than 48 inches below grade and restoration of the Project Parcels to farmland of similar condition to that which existed before construction of the WECS.

Large Scale Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS) shall only be permitted within the boundaries of the Wind Overlay District and only after receipt of a Special Permit issued by the Town Planning Board pursuant to the provisions of this section. No WECS shall be constructed, reconstructed, modified, or operated in the Town of Hammond except in the Wind Overlay District pursuant to a Special Permit. The Wind Overlay District boundaries are defined by the Town Board and described in the local law.

Each WECS shall be setback measured from the center of the WECS a minimum of five times the total height of the proposed WECS from any non-WECS structure or residence. Residence means any dwelling suitable for habitation existing in the Town of Hammond on the date an application for a Wind Energy Facility Permit is received, including multi-dwelling buildings, hunting camps, seasonal residences, hotels, hospitals, motels, dormitories, sanitariums, nursing homes, schools or other buildings used for educational purposes, or correctional institutions. Building permits shall not be issued for new construction on the same parcel as a permitted WECS when the proposed construction is located at a distance of five times the height of any WECS tower on the parcel unless an easement is signed and recorded permitting such proximity.

Each WECS shall be setback measured from the center of the WECS a minimum of five times the total height of the proposed WECS from any non-WECS structure or any aboveground utilities. All power transmission lines from the tower to any building or other structure shall be located underground unless a variance is granted by the Board of Appeals.

Section 5.2.15.2 requires that applications shall include a visual impact study of the proposed WECS as installed, which shall include a computerized photographic simulation, demonstrating any visual impacts from strategic vantage points. Color photographs of the proposed Site from at least two locations accurately depicting the existing conditions shall be included. The visual analysis shall also indicate the color treatment of the system's components and any visual screening incorporated into the project that is intended to lessen the system's visual prominence.
section: 5.2. Applications for Wind Energy Conversions Systems

summary: Each WECS shall be setback measured from the center of the WECS a minimum of two times the total height of the proposed WECS from state and federal wetlands. WECSs shall be located in a manner consistent with all applicable state and Federal wetlands laws and regulations.
The minimum distance between the ground and any part of the rotor or blade system shall be 30 feet.
No climbing pegs or tower ladders shall be located closer than 15 feet to the ground level at the base of the structure for freestanding single pole or guyed towers.

Section 4(e) states that "All structures in a project shall be finished in a single, non-reflective matte finished color or a camouflage scheme." This requirement applies to wind turbines as defined in the ordinance.
section: 4) The following standards shall apply to wind energy facilities in the Town of Hancock, unless specifically waived by the Planning Board.

summary: A decommissioning plan that addresses the anticipated life of the wind turbine, the estimated decommissioning costs, the method of ensuring funds shall be available for decommissioning and restoration, the method by which decommissioning cost shall be kept current, and the manner in which the wind turbine shall be decommissioned and the site restored. If any wind turbine remains non-functional or inoperative for a continuous period of 24 months, the applicant shall remove said system at its own expense following the requirements of the decommissioning plan. The applicant, or successors, shall continuously maintain a fund or bond payable to the Town, in a form approved by the Town for the removal of non-functional towers and appurtenant facilities, in an amount to be determined by the Town, for the period of the life of the facility.

No tower shall be lit except to comply with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) requirements. Minimum security lighting for ground level facilities shall be allowed as approved on the wind energy facility development plan. The statistical sound pressure level generated by a wind turbine shall not exceed L10 – 30 dBA measured at the property line, with independent verification by a certified acoustical engineer. If ambient noise exceeds this standard, the limit is ambient dBA plus 5 dBA. Ambient noise is measured as the highest whole number sound pressure level in dBA exceeded for more than six minutes per hour.

Each wind turbine shall be set back a distance of 500 feet or 1 ½ times the total height of the largest wind turbine, whichever shall be greater, from site boundary lines (property lines, lot lines, parcels, or subdivisions). No wind turbine shall be located within its own total height of a site boundary line.
Each wind turbine shall be set back a distance of 500 feet or 1 ½ times the total height of the largest wind turbine, whichever shall be greater, from any public road.

No shadow flicker shall be permitted on any off-site residences, effectively setting the maximum allowable shadow flicker at zero hours per year for wind turbines as defined (rated capacity over 100 kW intended for power distribution on the utility grid).

No advertising signs are allowed on any part of the wind energy facility, including fencing and support structures. Warning signs shall be posted at the entrances to the wind energy facility and at base of each tower warning of electrical shock or high voltage and containing emergency contact information.

Each wind turbine shall be set back a distance of 500 feet or 1 ½ times the total height of the largest wind turbine, whichever shall be greater, from any off-site residence, lodging facility, public building, church and other institution.

A complete application and site plan for a wind energy facility shall include, in addition to other applicable site plan requirements, ... j) A visual impact study of the proposed wind turbines as installed, which may include a computerized photographic simulation and digital elevation modes demonstrating visual impacts from strategic vantage points.
The minimum distance between the ground and any part of the rotor blade shall be thirty (30) feet.

Section G.8. Security Provisions states: 'No climbing device of any kind shall be attached to the outside of a WECS. Only internal ladders with locked doors. All towers or poles must be unclimbable by design or protected by anti-climbing devices.' This explicitly enacts climbing prevention requirements for Utility Scale WECS in the Town of Hanover.
WECS shall be painted a non-obtrusive (e.g. light environmental color such as white, gray or beige) color that is non reflective.

Section G.11 (Abatement) requires that any WECS which has not been generating energy for a period of one (1) year shall be removed from the premises within six (6) months after one year of non-use, including all structures, guy cables, guy anchors and or enclosures accessory to such WECS. The site shall be restored to as natural a condition as possible. The permittee is responsible for removal. All successful applicants shall furnish and file with the Town Clerk a performance bond and a Decommissioning Bond for removal and decommissioning costs. The Decommissioning Bond shall remain valid during the entire time the facility is permitted to operate and for an additional period of two years thereafter. The applicant shall submit a decommissioning plan including the anticipated life of the WECS, estimated decommissioning costs, method of ensuring funds availability, and the manner of decommissioning and site restoration.
Lighting shall be in compliance with FAA regulations.
WECS shall not exceed a total height of 495 feet including the turbine and blades.

The statistical sound pressure level generated by a WECS shall not exceed L10–50 dBA measured at any off site Residence existing at the time of the application. If the ambient sound pressure level exceeds 48 dBA, the standard shall be ambient dBA plus 5 dBA. Independent certification shall be provided before and after construction demonstrating compliance with this requirement.
section: E. Zoning District And Bulk Requirements

summary: No permit or other approval shall be required under this Article for WECS utilized solely for agricultural operations in a state or county agricultural district, as long as the facility is set back at least one and a half times its Total Height from a property line. Each WECS shall be setback as measured from the center of the WECS a minimum distance of 500 feet from the nearest site boundary property line.

section: E. Zoning District And Bulk Requirements

summary: The ordinance explicitly requires for utility scale WECS: a landscape plan showing all existing natural land features and erosion control measures; justification for any clearing required; a report showing soil logs, soil profile analysis and storm water run-off calculation for the area being disturbed (to be provided in the SWPPP and EIS); and plans to prevent pollution of surface or ground water, erosion of soil, both during and after construction, excessive run-off and flooding of other properties, including pre-construction and post-construction drainage calculations by a New York State licensed engineer showing there will be no increase of run-off from the site.

Wind Energy Facilities (WECS) shall not be constructed, reconstructed, modified, or operated except in a Wind Energy Overlay District with a Special Use Permit approved pursuant to this Local Law. WECS facilities may be permitted in the Wind Overlay Zoning District, which may be created in the Agricultural Residential (A-1) District, upon the issuance by the Hanover Town Board of a Special Use Permit. All applications require a site plan. Wind Measurement Towers and Small Wind Energy Conversion Systems also require a Special Use Permit. Exemptions exist for WECS utilized solely for agricultural operations in a state or county agricultural district under certain conditions.

Each WECS shall be setback a minimum distance of 1,000 feet from the nearest off-site residence, school, church or historic structure existing at the time of application, as measured to the exterior of such structure. Residence is defined as any dwelling suitable for habitation including seasonal homes, hotels, hospitals, motels, dormitories, nursing homes, senior housing, schools or other buildings used for educational purposes.
section: E. Zoning District And Bulk Requirements

summary: Each WECS shall be setback as measured from the center of the WECS a minimum distance of 500 feet from easements and power lines and 500 feet from electric or gas distribution lines unless waived in writing by the property owner and applicable utility owner.
section: E. Zoning District And Bulk Requirements, 2.) Setbacks

summary: Section F (Application Requirements) mandates submission of visual impact materials such as photography assessing visibility from key viewpoints within a three-mile radius, digitally enhanced to simulate the 'as built' appearance; a landscape plan showing existing natural features and proposed changes; a digital elevation model-based project visibility map showing visibility impacts within a three-mile radius, to be provided in the Environmental Impact Statement (EIS); and proposed mitigation measures for visual impacts of the tower facility. WECS are considered a Type I action under SEQRA and require a full Environmental Assessment Form (EAF) including a visual EAF. These requirements apply to utility scale WECS, with waivers possible for Small WECS.

Each WECS shall be setback as measured from the center of the WECS a minimum distance of 100 feet from state-identified wetlands. section: E. Zoning District And Bulk Requirements

summary: Tower owners shall remove all towers that have not been used for a 12-month period. Removal shall be within 6-months of written notification. Owners may request a Special Use Permit hearing to ask for an extension for just cause. Compliance with Parts B1, B2, B3, B7 and B8 shall be required for commercial windmills.

The base of a tower shall be at least 100 feet or 30% of the tower height, whichever is greater, from all property lines. This setback applies to commercial towers and is selectively utilized in the review of commercial windmills.
All wind energy generating facilities shall be set back from all side and rear lot lines at least the height of the tower plus the blade when fully vertical.
section: Section 665         Major Wind Energy Generating Facilities

summary: All wind energy generating facilities shall be set back from all road lines at least the height of the tower plus the blade when fully vertical.

summary: Wind Energy Generating Facility, Major requires a special use review prior to the issuance of a special permit (SP) in the AR-1 and H-1 zoning districts. All structures in a project shall be finished in a single, nonreflective, matte-finished color. No lettering, company insignia, advertising, or graphics shall be on any part of the tower, hub, or blades.

Section I ('Decommissioning') requires removal of any WECS that remains nonfunctional or inoperative for a continuous period of one year at the applicant's expense. The applicant must maintain a fund no less than 125% of estimated costs, secured by cash deposit and irrevocable bond. The Town may access the site and implement decommissioning if the permit holder fails to do so, using the posted fund. Removal and restoration must occur within 180 days of nonfunctionality or permit revocation. The Town may recover costs exceeding the fund amount from the permit holder.

Lighting of tower. No tower shall be lit except to comply with FAA requirements. Motion-sensitive on-demand lighting is required. Minimum-security lighting for ground level facilities shall be allowed as approved on the site plan. The application should include a lighting plan showing any FAA-required lighting and other proposed lighting.

The maximum total height of any commercial/industrial wind energy conversion system (WECS) shall not exceed 450 feet, as explicitly stated in subsection H(15): 'Notwithstanding the foregoing, no wind tower total height shall exceed 450 feet.' This height is measured as the total height from the finished ground elevation to the furthest vertical extension of the turbine rotor plane.

The equivalent level (LEQ) generated by a commercial/industrial wind energy conversion system (WECS) shall not exceed 35 dBA at night (8:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.) when measured at the nearest off-site residence existing at the time of application. The noise analysis must be performed according to the International Standard for Acoustic Noise Measurement Techniques for Wind Generators (IEC 61400-11) or other procedures accepted by the Town Board. The maximum noise level for any WECS measured from the property boundary lines of any school shall not exceed 40 dBA.

From property lines: A minimum two times the total WECS height from any property line excluding adjoining lot lines of the project participants. This means the minimum spacing between individual turbines is five times the rotor diameter of the largest rotor in the facility.

The applicant shall submit a decommissioning plan, which shall include: 1) the anticipated life of the WECS; 2) the estimated decommissioning costs in current dollars; 3) how said estimate was determined; 4) the funds for decommissioning and restoration will be secured in a bond, escrow account or any other fund consistent with requirements set forth in section 21.D; 5) the method, such by annual re-estimate by a licensed engineer, that the decommissioning cost will be kept current; 6) the manner in which the WECS will be decommissioned and the Site restored, which shall include removal of all roads, structures and debris to a depth of four (4) feet, restoration of the soil, and restoration of vegetation (consistent and compatible with surrounding vegetation), less any fencing or residual minor improvements requested by the landowner; and 7) a description for how the applicant will comply with the Department of Agriculture and Markets decommissioning and restoration requirements for WECS and associated utility lines on farmland. If any WECS remains non-functional or inoperative for a continuous period of one (1) year, the applicant agrees that, without any further action by the Town, it shall remove said system at its own expense. Removal of the WEFs and site restoration shall include: all above ground components removed; foundations and buried project components removed to a depth of four (4) feet; buried collection lines removed to a depth of three (3) feet; ground disturbance minimized and site restored to original contours; disturbed soils and vegetation restored; roads restored; access roads, fencing and residual minor improvements may remain with written consent from the landowner. The applicant shall maintain the required financial assurance payable to the Town for the removal of non-functional or inoperable WECS and appurtenant facilities in an amount to be determined by a qualified independent engineer, reviewed every two years, in the form of a bond, escrow account or other approved form. The total sound pressure level generated by a WECS shall not exceed forty (40) Leq A-weighted decibels ("dBA") at ten (10) minute intervals at the nearest non-participating property line, school, hospital, place of worship or public building existing at the time of the application. Independent certification shall be required before and after construction demonstrating compliance with this requirement. If the ambient noise level measured at the nearest property line or structure exceeds the standard, the standard shall be equal to the ambient noise level plus 3 dBA. In the event the audible noise due to WECS operation is determined to contain a steady pure tone, the standards shall be reduced by five (5) dBA.

summary: Appropriate warning signs shall be posted. At least one sign shall be posted at the base of the tower warning of electrical shock or high voltage. A sign shall be posted on the entry area of fence around each tower or group of towers and any building (or on the tower or building if there is no fence) containing emergency contact information, including a local telephone number with twenty-four (24) hour, seven (7) day a week coverage. The Town Board may require additional signs based on safety needs.

The local law explicitly enacts soil, erosion, and sediment control requirements for Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS). It requires that "all top soil disturbed during construction, reconstruction or modification of WECS shall be stockpiled and returned to the site, regraded and reseeded upon completion of the activity which disturbed the soil" (§13.I). Storm-water run-off and erosion control must be "managed in a manner consistent with all applicable State and Federal laws and regulations" (§13.L). The applicant must adhere to "the New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets Guidelines for Agricultural Mitigation for Wind Power Projects" (§13.M). Upon decommissioning, removal and site restoration must include "restoration of the soil, and restoration of vegetation" and "ground disturbance must be minimized to the extent practical and the site restored to its original ground contours if possible" (§21.C). These requirements apply to WECS with rated capacity over 100 kW, i.e., commercial-scale wind energy facilities.

Wind Energy Facilities (WEF) are permitted only within designated Wind Overlay Zones, which must be created by the Town Board. Construction, reconstruction, modification, or operation of WEF outside these Wind Overlay Zones is not permitted. WEF within these zones require a WEF Permit approved pursuant to this local law. The Town Board has authority to create these zones and to vary certain requirements but cannot issue use variances to allow WEF outside the Wind Overlay Zones.
section: §10. Permits Required and ARTICLE III: WIND ENERGY CONVERSION SYSTEMS

summary: Each WECS shall be setback one and one-half times the total height of the proposed WECS from state and federal wetlands or bodies of water. This distance may be adjusted to be greater at the discretion of the Town, based on topography, land cover, land uses and other factors that influence the flight patterns of resident birds, bats or other creatures. Wind Energy Facilities shall be located in a manner consistent with all applicable State and Federal wetland laws and regulations.
section: §18. Setbacks for Wind Energy Conversion Systems

summary: The minimum height of the lowest part of the blade sweep area shall be thirty (30) feet above the highest existing major structure or tree within a one-hundred-fifty (150) foot radius of the base of the wind energy conversion unit. The units for this minimum blade clearance are feet.
Each Wind Energy Conversion Unit shall: not have any climbing device of any kind attached closer than fifteen (15) feet from the ground, and have a locked anti-climbing device installed on the unit.

Upon approval and prior to the construction of any portion of such wind energy conversion system, each approved wind energy conversion system shall require a decommissioning plan and related financial surety be filed with the town. Such plan and surety shall include the anticipated life of the project, the estimated decommissioning cost in current dollars, the method and schedule for updating the costs of decommissioning and restoration, the method of ensuring that funds will be available for decommissioning and restoration, and the anticipated manner in which the project will be decommissioned and the site restored. The applicant shall provide an appropriate and adequate demolition bond or similar financial surety such as a letter of credit or cash, to be utilized by the Town in removing the Wind Energy Conversion System in the event the Applicant fails to do so as required. The Applicant shall notify the Code Enforcement Officer within thirty (30) days of the discontinuance of use of the Wind Energy Conversion System or any portion thereof. The Applicant shall remove any discontinued, decommissioned, obsolete or unused wind energy conversion system or portions thereof and restore the site to pre-construction conditions, or make the wind energy conversion system or portion thereof fully operational, within one hundred eighty (180) days of delivery or receipt of the notification. Failure to notify and/or remove any the discontinued, decommissioned, obsolete or unused wind energy conversion system or portion thereof in accordance with this local law shall be in violation of this local law and subject the applicant to penalties. The cost of removing the offending system shall be drawn against the financial surety posted by the applicant. Any costs incurred by the Town that exceed the surety shall be the responsibility of the applicant and may become a lien on the property.

No Wind Energy Conversion Unit shall be artificially lighted unless such lighting is required by a local, state or federal statue, rule or regulation. The use of nighttime and overcast daytime condition stroboscopic lighting shall be the minimum required by law to satisfy the lighting requirements as issued by the Federal Aviation Administration. Light shields, if commercially available, or other devices to block downward lighting shall be used to minimize the amount of light visible at ground level. The Applicant shall submit a study of the potential impact of the proposed lighting, as well as any required alterations as determined and required for approval hereunder, on the area surrounding the subject project. Prior notification of any changes in the lighting plan for the project must be communicated to the Town Planning Board prior to installation of such new lighting scheme, and such alterations shall only be approved for installation for good cause shown or in order to bring such project into compliance with any and all statutory and regulatory requirements. If the minimum lighting requirement, as determined by applicable federal, state or local rules, regulations or statutes change during the course of operation of the wind energy conversion system, the applicant shall alter the lighting plan and install such lighting in the wind energy conversion system that that is at a level equal to such revised minimum requirements in accordance therewith.
The total tip height for each wind energy conversion unit cannot exceed five-hundred (500) feet as measured from the base of the unit to the tip of the unit’s longest blade.

The level of noise produced by or from the operation of the Wind Energy Conversion System shall not be persistent in excess exceed of 45 decibels (dbA) for more than 25 minutes in duration measured at a distance of 1000 feet from the base of the wind energy conversion unit or that portion of the wind energy conversion system causing the noise level that is in violation of these requirements.

Setback from adjacent property lines or lot lines must be at least equal to the tip height of the wind energy conversion unit. Specifically, 'A distance not less than that equal to the tip height of the wind energy conversion unit as measured from the adjacent property lines of the parcel on which said unit is to be sited.' Also, 'The installation shall not be erected nearer to any lot line than the total height of the structure,' where total height is defined as tower height plus one-half the rotor diameter. No additional static distance is added to this setback.
