summary: All Wind Energy Conversion Units shall only be located, installed, or constructed on the subject parcel in accordance with the following set backs: A distance not less than that equal to the tip height of the wind energy conversion unit as measured from any and all public roadways ... to the base of such unit.

If an individual residence is being impacted by multiple wind energy conversion units, the cumulative effect shall not exceed twenty-five (25) hours per year. If shadow flicker exceeds these conditions, the source wind energy conversion unit shall be shut down until the offending condition is remedied.

The applicant for a Commercial WECS shall include the following information regarding decommissioning of the WECS and restoring the site: anticipated life of the project; estimated decommissioning costs in current dollars; method and schedule for updating the costs of decommissioning and restoration; method of ensuring that funds will be available for decommissioning and restoration; anticipated manner in which the project will be decommissioned and the site restored. The WECS shall comply with tower lighting, marking and/or painting requirements as set forth by the Federal Aviation Administration. Upon request by the Building Inspector, the owner or operator of the WECS shall submit evidence of compliance with Federal Aviation Administration requirements.
The Total Height of a WECS shall not exceed 200 feet for a Commercial WECS. This is explicitly stated in section 4.5.4.14(1) and the units are feet as indicated in the text.
A minimum lot of 5 acres is required for Commercial WECS in the A5A district, as indicated by the notation '/5' meaning 'A minimum lot of 5 acres required for this use in this district.'

Every WECS shall meet the requirements of any applicable federal, state, and local noise regulations. The noise emitted from the WECS shall not exceed 50 dba, as measured at the boundaries of all abutting parcels.
Every WECS shall be set back from any property line a distance greater than its Total Height. A Commercial WECS shall be set back not less than 2500 feet from a zoning district boundary.

At least one sign shall be posted at the base of the tower warning of site hazards, and providing contact information with regard to the owner/operator, including name and phone number. The posted sign shall not exceed four square feet in size.

Commercial WECS require a Special Permit and Planning Board approval. Every WECS shall be set back from any property line, aboveground utility line or other WECS a distance greater than its Total Height. The ordinance explicitly requires climbing prevention measures for Industrial wind energy conversion systems, including that applications must provide documentation on "Anti-climb devices for the structure and any guy wires" (§ 205-47.D.(5)(a)(iv)) and that "No climbing pegs or tower ladders shall be located closer than 15 feet to the ground level at the base of the tower structure" (§ 205-43.5.H.(22)). summary: § 205-43.5, subsection I (Decommissioning) requires that if any WECS remains nonfunctional or inoperative for a continuous period of one year, the applicant shall remove said system at its own expense. An application must include a decommissioning and site restoration plan providing for removal of all wind turbines, structures, hazardous materials, electrical facilities, and foundations to a depth of not less than 60 inches below grade, restoration of the project parcels to farmland of similar condition, estimated decommissioning cost, financial security to secure completion of decommissioning, and written nonrevocable authorization for Town access to implement decommissioning if the permit holder fails to do so. The plan requires maintaining a fund no less than 125% of the estimated cost, with a cash deposit and irrevocable bond. Removal and restoration must occur within 180 days of nonfunction or permit revocation, with the Town authorized to use the fund if the permittee fails to act.

Lighting of tower. No tower shall be lit except to comply with FAA requirements. Motion-sensitive on-demand lighting is required. Minimum-security lighting for ground-level facilities shall be allowed as approved on the site plan. The application shall include a lighting plan showing any FAA-required lighting and other proposed lighting.
The maximum total height of any WECS (Wind Energy Conversion System), which includes commercial/industrial wind energy conversion systems, shall not exceed 200 feet under any circumstances.

No wind generation facility shall be measured or modeled to emit A-weighted sound levels in excess of 6 dB above preexisting daytime or nighttime A-weighted background noise levels, with Lmax defined as the maximum instantaneous sound level modeled within a one-second period, modeled according to ISO 9613-2 and IEC 61400-14 standards. This applies specifically to commercial/industrial wind energy conversion systems as defined in the ordinance.

Industrial wind energy conversion system, as defined by § 205-11BB, is a permitted principal use in the Industrial District, provided it complies with all dimensional and other requirements of this chapter (§ 205-40.A.(8)). Commercial/industrial wind energy systems are restricted to the Industrial District only (§ 205-43.5.H.(1)(a)).

Industrial wind energy conversion systems shall be prohibited in all districts other than Industrial (I) (§ 205-11BB(2)). No commercial/industrial wind energy systems shall be allowed in any zoning district other than Industrial (§ 205-43.5H(1)(a)). Additional prohibitions include no commercial/industrial wind energy systems within the Town of Somerset LWRP boundary areas, areas likely to have material adverse impacts on certain land use plans, and within three miles of the Lake Ontario shoreline, LWRP boundary areas, or any planned or existing public park (§ 205-43.5H(1)(b)-(d)). The maximum total height of any WECS shall not exceed 200 feet (§ 205-43.5H(15)). Setbacks and location restrictions further prohibit siting closer than specified distances from residences, public roads, and other sensitive areas (§ 205-47D(1)(b)). These prohibitions apply unconditionally and have no expiration date.

Setbacks for industrial wind energy conversion systems require a minimum distance from property lines where the property owner has not entered into an agreement with the developer of the greater of 1/2 mile or six times the height of the turbine. Specifically, no commercial/industrial wind energy systems shall be allowed within the following setbacks: "the greater of 1/2 mile or six times the height of the turbine" from any property line. Additionally, tall structures with moving parts, including wind energy facilities, shall maintain a property line setback of 5.5 times the total structure height, measured from the outermost turbine blade or structural base, whichever is further from the tower axis. These setbacks "shall not be waived by any person or entity" and apply to all structural foundations, appurtenances, and turbine parts, excluding guy wires and anchors.

The minimum setback from any public road for commercial/industrial wind energy conversion systems shall be the greater of 1/2 mile or six times the height of the turbine. This setback is mandatory and non-waivable. Specifically, "The minimum setback from any residence, structure, public road, or property line where one property owner has not entered into an agreement with any person or entity seeking to develop or operate a wind energy conversion system shall be 1/2 mile or six times the height of the turbine, whichever is higher." Additionally, tall structures with moving parts, including wind energy facilities, "shall not be permitted ... within the greater of 1/2 mile or six times the height of the turbine of any residence, structure, public road, or property line where one property owner has not entered into an agreement with any person or entity seeking to develop or operate a wind energy conversion system." The setback measurement starts from the outermost point of any turbine blade or the outermost edge of the structural base, whichever is further from the tower's central vertical axis.

summary: No advertising signs are allowed on any part of the wind energy facility, including fencing and support structures. Appropriate warning signs shall be posted. Stormwater runoff and erosion control shall be managed in a manner consistent with all applicable state and federal laws and regulations. [§ 205-43.5 H(13)] This requirement applies to commercial/industrial wind energy conversion systems (WECS) defined as any machine or wind facility that converts the kinetic energy in the wind into electricity and where the electricity is primarily produced for commercial sale.

Industrial wind energy conversion system, as defined by § 205-11BB, is a permitted principal use in the Industrial District (I) (§ 205-40.A.(8)) and must comply with all other requirements of the chapter, including permits. Agricultural wind energy facilities require special use permits (§ 205-47.B.(9)), but this pertains to agricultural uses. The minimum setback from any residence, structure, or property line where one property owner has not entered into an agreement with any person or entity seeking to develop or operate a wind energy conversion system shall be the greater of 1/2 mile or six times the height of the turbine. This setback is mandatory and cannot be waived. Additionally, if a greater setback is necessary to ensure noise limits (Lmax not exceeding 6 dB above background noise) at a residence, that greater setback applies. For wind energy facilities, the setback measurement shall start from the outermost point of any turbine blade or the structural base, whichever is further.

Applications shall include a visual impact study of the proposed WECS as installed, which shall include a computerized photographic simulation, demonstrating any visual impacts from strategic vantage points. Color photographs of the proposed site from at least several locations accurately depicting the existing conditions shall be included. The visual analysis shall also indicate the color treatment of the system's components and any visual screening incorporated into the project that is intended to lessen the system's visual prominence.

No commercial/industrial wind energy systems shall be allowed within three miles of the Lake Ontario shoreline, the boundary areas of the Town of Somerset LWRP, or any planned or existing public park. The maximum level of sound created by the wind energy conversion system as measured at the lot line shall be no greater than 55 decibels (db).

Setback from any existing residential structures, not owned by participants in a wind generating project, shall be three times the combined height of the tower and rotor blade length.

This establishes that the setback distance equals the maximum of the district setback (threshold) and the multiplier-based setback, but the district setback value itself is not specified in feet or any other unit in the provided text.

The outside of the wind turbine generator towers shall not be climbable.

The towers and generators of the wind turbine generators shall have a non-reflective, painted steel finish in a neutral color, subject to any applicable standards of the FAA or other regulatory requirements. The blades of the wind turbine generators are not covered by this section.

Each wind turbine generator and all related improvements shall be removed within 12 months of the date when the use of the particular wind turbine generator has been discontinued or abandoned by developer/permitee, or upon expiration of this agreement, whichever is earlier. The wind turbine generators shall not be artificially illuminated except as required by the FAA or any other applicable authority. If lighting is required, the lighting alternatives and design chosen will seek to minimize the disturbance to the surrounding views.

The developer/permitee shall maintain a noise level attributable to the wind turbine generators of not more than 45 dB(A) within a reasonable margin of error as measured at existing non-participating residences.

The ordinance explicitly enacts decommissioning requirements for commercial wind energy systems under section 507.46, subsection E. Decommissioning. To the extent not inconsistent with or preempted by statute, the following provisions shall apply to decommissioning. a) The Owner, Operator, Developer is required to notify the Township immediately upon cessation or abandonment of the operation. The WEF shall be presumed to be discontinued or abandoned if no electricity is generated by such system for a period of twelve (12) continuous months. b) The Owner, Operator, Developer shall then have twelve (12) months in which to dismantle and entirely remove the WEF including all surface and subsurface wind related equipment or appurtenances related thereto, including but not limited to buildings, cabling, electrical components, roads, fences, foundations, wind facility connections and other associated facilities in accordance with agreements with the Property Site Landowner and good industry practice. c) To the extent possible the materials shall be re-sold or salvaged. Materials that cannot be re-sold or salvaged shall be disposed of at facility authorized to dispose of such materials by federal or state law. d) Any soil exposed during the removal shall be stabilized in accordance with applicable erosion and sediment control standards. e) Any access drive paved aprons from public roads shall remain for future use unless directed otherwise by the Property Site Landowner. f) The WEF site area shall be restored to its pre-existing condition, suitable for its prior use, except the Property Site Landowner may authorize, in writing, any buffer landscaping or access roads installed to accommodate the WEF to remain. g) Any necessary permits, such as Erosion and Sedimentation and NPDES permits, shall be obtained prior to decommissioning activities. h) At the time of issuance of SALDO approval for the construction of the WEF, the Owner, Operator, Developer of the WEF shall provide financial security in the form and amount acceptable to the Township, to secure obligations under this Section. i) The Owner, Operator, Developer shall, at the time of the SALDO application, provide the Township with an estimate of the cost of performing the decommissioning activities required herein, and shall provide financial security of 110% of the estimated cost of decommissioning. On every 5th anniversary of the date of providing the decommissioning financial security the Owner, Operator shall provide an updated decommission cost estimate, with adjustments for inflation and cost changes. Section 1749 Decommissioning explicitly enacts decommissioning requirements for Large Wind Energy Systems (LWES). It states that the owner or operator is responsible for decommissioning and all associated costs, defines the end of useful life as no electricity generation for 12 continuous months, requires decommissioning to begin within 8 months and be completed within 18 months after the end of useful life, and mandates removal of all facilities and site restoration to pre-construction conditions. It also requires filing a decommissioning plan and estimated costs prior to operation, allows the Board to require financial assurance after 10 years, and authorizes the Board to take action if decommissioning is not completed.
Towers shall be marked as required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). There shall be no lights on the towers other than what is required by the FAA.

Noise level produced by the LWES shall not exceed forty-five (45) dBA, average A-weighted sound pressure at the perimeter of occupied residences existing at the time the permit application is filed, unless a signed waiver or easement is obtained from the owner of the residence.

Section 1727(3) states: 'Distance from any property line shall be not less than five hundred (500) feet or one point one (1.1) times the system height, whichever is greater, unless appropriate easement has been obtained from adjoining property owner.' This establishes a minimum setback distance of 500 feet or 1.1 times the system height for Large Wind Energy Systems (LWES) from property lines.
Distance from right-of-way (ROW) of public roads shall be not less than five hundred (500) feet or one point one (1.1) times the system height, whichever is greater.

When determined appropriate by the County a Shadow Flicker Control System shall be installed upon all turbines which will cause a perceived shadow effect upon a habitable residential dwelling. Such system shall limit blade rotation at those times when shadow flicker exceeds thirty (30) minutes per day or thirty (30) hours per year at perceivable shadow flicker intensity as confirmed by the Zoning Administrator are probable.

Section 1219 requires submission of a soil erosion and control plan at least forty-five (45) days prior to commencement of construction. Section 1225(7) mandates that permittees shall develop a Soil Erosion and Sediment Control Plan prior to construction and submit the plan to the County Zoning Office no less than forty-five (45) days prior to commencing construction. The plan shall address erosion control measures for each project phase, including grading, construction and drainage of roads and turbine pads; necessary soil information; detailed design features to maintain downstream water quality; a comprehensive re-vegetation plan that uses native plant species to maintain and ensure adequate erosion control and slope stability and to restore the site after temporary project activities; and measures to minimize the area of surface disturbance.

An application for a WESF License shall include a detailed shadow flicker and blade glint assessment model and plan containing the following information and meeting the following requirements. The model shall be prepared by a registered professional regularly engaged in this type of work with not less than three years experience. The model study area will examine areas where shadow flicker will occur within a one mile radius of the Project Parcels. The model shall calculate the locations and durations of shadow flicker caused by the proposed WESF within the study area. Wind Turbines shall be sited such that shadow flicker will not fall on a receptor, except that shadow flicker expected to fall on a roadway or a residential parcel may shall be acceptable if all of the following conditions are satisfied: The flicker will not exceed 10 hours per year at any one receptor measured as the sum of those times during which shadow flicker occurs during any calendar year. Blade glint, defined as the intermittent reflection of the sun off the surface of the blades of a Wind Turbine, is prohibited. The applicant shall submit a paint sample that demonstrates the color, texture and gloss of the proposed surface coating. The applicant shall also submit a certification by the manufacturer stating that the proposed surface coating will not create a reflective surface conducive to blade glint.

summary: If an applicant fails to remove a wind energy conversion system in accordance with this section, the County shall have the authority to enter the subject property and physically remove the facility. Prior to obtaining a certificate of occupancy from the County and on every tenth (10th) anniversary of the commencement of the operation of the project, the applicant shall provide to the County an estimate of the projected salvage value of the turbines and other equipment to be removed from the project site ("salvage value"), as well as the projected cost of removing the turbines and other equipment from the site as determined by an independent engineer mutually agreeable to the applicant and County ("gross decommissioning cost"). Based on this determination, applicant shall post and maintain decommissioning funds in an amount equal to net decommissioning cost, which is gross decommissioning cost minus salvage value. The Towns of Brighton and Eau Pleine have enacted Wind Energy Facility Licensing Ordinances that require a license before construction or operation of any Large Wind Energy Facility (LWEF). These ordinances impose restrictions more stringent than state regulations, including a maximum noise limit of 35 decibels enforceable through shutdown orders, minimum setbacks of one mile or ten times turbine height, requirements to guarantee no loss in property value within two miles, prohibitions on signage, and decommissioning within 3 months after condemnation or non-generation. The ordinances make it "effectively impossible" for any applicant to receive a license for a wind energy system in these towns, constituting an effective prohibition or ban. There is no expiration date for these prohibitions. The ordinances violate Wisconsin law because they are more restrictive than PSC Chapter 128, which prohibits localities from enacting more restrictive regulations than the state. The plaintiff seeks declaratory and injunctive relief to prevent enforcement of these ordinances.

The only zoning district mentioned is the Farmland Preservation Zoning Districts (EA), where no permit shall be approved unless certain standards and conditions are met, but it does not explicitly state that Large Wind Energy Systems are permitted there as a special use. Therefore, the ordinance does not explicitly define specific districts where Large Wind Energy Systems are permitted as special use or similar.

For Large Wind Energy Systems, setbacks from occupied dwellings, buildings, structures, and/or residences shall be the lesser of 1,250 feet or 3.1 times the maximum blade tip height. The setback distances are measured as a straight line from the vertical centerline of the wind turbine tower to the nearest point on the permanent foundation of a building or dwelling. The owner of a nonparticipating dwelling or occupied community building may waive the applicable setback distances to a minimum of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height.

For Large Wind Energy Systems, the setback distance from participating dwellings is 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height. The setback distances are measured as a straight line from the vertical centerline of the wind turbine tower to the nearest point on the permanent foundation of a building or dwelling.
The vertical distance from ground level to the tip of a wind turbine blade when the blade is at its lowest point must be at least 35 feet, except for PERSONAL WIND ENERGY SYSTEMS.
A WIND TOWER, including any climbing aids, must be secured against unauthorized access by means of a locked barrier or security fence.

The exterior surface of any visible components of a WIND ENERGY SYSTEM must be a non-reflective, neutral color. WIND TOWERS and turbines in a WIND FARM SYSTEM that are located within one mile of each other on a PARTICIPATING PROPERTY must be of uniform design, including tower type, color, number of blades, and direction of blade rotation.

Section 6.0 ABANDONMENT AND RESTORATION requires that a WIND ENERGY SYSTEM that is out of service for a continuous 12-month period will be deemed abandoned and must be removed within 3 months of the Notice of Abandonment or within 6 months of providing Notice of Termination of Operations. The owner must remove all wind turbines, foundations, underground electrical wires, and hazardous materials and reclaim the site to a depth of 4 feet below the surface. If the owner fails to remove the system and reclaim the site, the County may remove the system and recover costs from financial assurance or place a lien on the property. Section 4.0 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS mandates that the owner must provide a performance bond, completion bond, or other financial assurance of at least $20,000 for each LARGE WIND ENERGY SYSTEM to guarantee restoration.

A WIND TOWER and turbine may not be artificially lighted unless such lighting is required by the Federal Aviation Administration. If lighting is required, the lighting must comply with FAA minimum requirements and, whenever possible, be at the lowest intensity allowed, avoid the use of strobe or other intermittent white lights, and use steady red lights. If more than one lighting alternative is available, the alternative that causes the least visual disturbance must be used.

The total height of a WIND ENERGY SYSTEM shall not exceed 150 feet unless a greater height is approved by the COMMITTEE. This applies to WIND FARM SYSTEMS, which are defined as wind energy systems that include more than one wind tower.

LARGE WIND ENERGY SYSTEMS and WIND FARM SYSTEMS may be located only in areas zoned Agricultural One (A-1), Agricultural Two (A-2), Forestry One (F-1), and Industrial One (I-1) provided that the parcel has a minimum size of five acres.

The noise generated by the operation of a WIND ENERGY SYSTEM may not exceed the ambient noise level by more than 5 dB(A) as measured at any point on property adjacent to the parcel on which the wind energy system is located.

LARGE WIND ENERGY SYSTEMS and WIND FARM SYSTEMS may be located only in areas that are zoned Agricultural One (A-1), Agricultural Two (A-2), Forestry One (F-1) and in the Industrial One (I-1) zone district provided that the parcel has a minimum size of five acres.

A WIND ENERGY SYSTEM shall not be located closer than 1.1 of its total height from lot lines. Reduced setbacks may be allowed if written permission is granted by the affected property owner and recorded with the Sawyer County Register of Deeds.

A WIND ENERGY SYSTEM shall not be located closer than 1.1 of its total height from public road right-of-way. Reduced setbacks may be allowed if written permission is granted by the affected property owner and recorded with the Sawyer County Register of Deeds.

No wind turbine, tower, building, or other structure associated with a WIND ENERGY SYSTEM may be used to advertise or promote any product or service. No word or graphic representation, other than appropriate warning signs and owner or landowner identification, may be placed on a wind turbine, tower, building, or other structure associated with a WIND ENERGY SYSTEM so as to be visible from any public road.

LARGE WIND ENERGY SYSTEMS and WIND FARM SYSTEMS may be located only in areas that are zoned Agricultural One (A-1), Agricultural Two (A-2), Forestry One (F-1) and in the Industrial One (I-1) zone district provided that the parcel has a minimum size of five acres. Approval is required by the COMMITTEE and any other committee of the Sawyer County Board of Supervisors with jurisdiction over that property and the approval of the Sawyer County Board of Supervisors.

The WIND ENERGY SYSTEM in a LARGE WIND ENERGY SYSTEM and each WIND ENERGY SYSTEM in a WIND FARM SYSTEM shall be setback at least 300’ from the residence of a NONPARTICIPATING PROPERTY unless written permission is granted by the affected property owner for a specific lesser setback and recorded with the Sawyer County Register of Deeds.
A WIND ENERGY SYSTEM shall not be located closer than 1.1 of its total height from power or telephone line right-of-way (buried or above ground).
A WIND ENERGY SYSTEM shall not be located closer than 300’ from the ordinary high-water mark of navigable waters. This applies to WIND FARM SYSTEMS as defined in the ordinance.
The blade tip of a Commercial Wind Turbine shall, at its lowest point, have ground clearance of no less than seventy-five (75) feet.

section: 21.06 General Requirements for Wind Energy Facilities

summary: From any wetland, water body, environmental significant or scenic area, each Wind Turbine total height shall have a minimum setback of two (2) times its total height or one thousand (1,000) feet whichever is greater.
An owner shall take appropriate measures to ensure that a wind turbine is not readily climbable except by authorized personnel.

An owner of a wind energy system shall decommission and remove the wind energy system when the system is at the end of its useful life. A wind energy system is presumed to be at the end of its useful life if the wind energy system generates no electricity for a continuous 360-day period. When decommissioning is required, the owner shall begin decommissioning within 360 days after the wind energy system has reached the end of its useful life and complete decommissioning within 540 days. The owner of a wind energy system with a nameplate capacity of one megawatt or larger shall maintain proof of the owner's ability to fund the actual and necessary cost to decommission the wind energy system and ensure availability of funds necessary for decommissioning throughout the expected life of the wind energy system and through to completion of the decommissioning activities. The owner shall ensure that the property is restored to preconstruction condition unless otherwise provided in a contract signed by an affected landowner. An owner shall file a notice of decommissioning completion with Walworth County and the Commission when a wind energy system approved by the County has been decommissioned and removed.

An owner shall install lighting at a wind energy system that complies with standards established by the Federal Aviation Administration. Walworth County may not establish lighting requirements for a wind energy system that conflict with standards established by the Federal Aviation Administration. Walworth County may require use of shielding or control systems approved by the Federal Aviation Administration to reduce visibility of lighting to individuals on the ground.

The ordinance requires that the owner shall operate the wind energy system so that the noise attributable to the wind energy system does not exceed 50 dBA during daytime hours and 45 dBA during nighttime hours, measured at the outside wall of a nonparticipating residence or occupied community building. The most restrictive maximum noise level is 45 dBA during nighttime hours.

An owner shall design and construct a wind energy system using the wind turbine setback distances shown in Table 1. The setback distance from nonparticipating property lines is 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height. An owner shall measure wind turbine setback distances as a straight line from the vertical centerline of the wind turbine tower to the nearest point on the property line or feature, as applicable. The owner of a nonparticipating property may waive the applicable wind turbine setback distance from a nonparticipating property line.

An owner shall design and construct a wind energy system using the wind turbine setback distance of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height from public road rights-of-way. The setback distance is measured as a straight line from the vertical centerline of the wind turbine tower to the nearest point on the public road right-of-way.

An owner shall design the wind energy system so that computer modeling indicates no nonparticipating residence or occupied community building will experience more than 30 hours per year of shadow flicker under planned operating conditions. The owner shall operate the wind energy system in a manner that does not cause more than 30 hours per year of shadow flicker at a nonparticipating residence or occupied community building, with operational curtailment required if this limit is exceeded.

An owner shall place appropriate warning signage on or at the base of each wind turbine. An owner shall post and maintain up-to-date signs containing a 24-hour emergency contact telephone number, information identifying the owner, and sufficient information to identify the location of the sign within the wind energy system. An owner shall post these signs at every intersection of a wind energy system access road with a public road and at each wind turbine location.

The setback distances for large wind energy systems from occupied dwellings, buildings, structures, and/or residences are specified in Section 65-13(1)(a) Table 1. For Occupied Community Buildings and Nonparticipating Residences, the setback distance is "the lesser of 1,250 feet or 3.1 times the maximum blade tip height." For Participating Residences, the setback distance is "1.1 times the maximum blade tip height." Setbacks are measured as a straight line from the vertical centerline of the wind turbine tower to the nearest point on the permanent foundation of a building or residence (Section 65-13(1)(b)). Owners of nonparticipating residences or occupied community buildings may waive the applicable setback distances to a minimum setback distance of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height (Section 65-13(1)(d)).

The setback distance from participating residences for large wind energy systems is 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height. The maximum blade tip height is defined as the nominal hub height plus the nominal blade length of a wind turbine. Setbacks are measured as a straight line from the vertical centerline of the wind turbine tower to the nearest point on the permanent foundation of a building or residence.

An owner shall design and construct a wind energy system using the wind turbine setback distance of 1.1 times the maximum blade tip height from overhead communication and electric transmission or distribution lines (not including utility service lines to individual houses or outbuildings). The setback distance is measured as a straight line from the vertical centerline of the wind turbine tower to the nearest point on the feature.

Section 65-30(2) requires that an application for a wind energy system include "Wind energy system description and maps showing the locations of all proposed wind energy facilities" and "Information regarding the anticipated effects of the wind energy system on existing land uses within one-half mile of the wind energy system." Additionally, Sections 65-30(5) and (6) require notice to property owners and residents and at least one public meeting to obtain comments on and to inform the public about a proposed wind energy system. These requirements constitute explicit visual impact assessment requirements for Large wind energy systems.

The vertical distance from the ground level to the tip of a wind generator blade, with the blade at its lowest point, shall be at least thirty (30) feet. This applies to both residential and commercial wind energy systems.

The ordinance requires that commercial wind energy systems' wind towers "shall be designed and installed so as to not provide step bolts or a ladder readily accessible to the public for a minimum height of eight (8) feet above the ground." This climbing prevention requirement applies to both residential and commercial wind energy systems. Additionally, all ground mounted electrical and control equipment shall be labeled or secured to prevent unauthorized access.
The wind generator and tower shall remain painted or finished the color or finish that was originally applied by the manufacturer, unless approved in the Land Use Permit.

Section 12.04, Standard 5 states: "Lighting: A wind tower and generator shall not be artificially lighted unless such lighting is required by the Federal Aviation Administration." This lighting requirement applies to both residential and commercial wind energy systems as defined in the ordinance.

Section 22 states that "Commercial wind energy systems are prohibited in all zoning districts." This prohibition is absolute and not conditional on compliance with other provisions. There is no expiration date or time limit provided for this prohibition.
A wind tower for a commercial wind energy system shall be set back a distance equal to its total height from all property lines.

A wind tower for a residential or commercial wind system shall be set back a distance equal to its total height from any public road right-of-way, unless written permission is granted by the affected utility.

Both residential and commercial wind energy systems shall be subject to the following requirements: Signs: All signs, other than the manufacturer’s or installer’s identification, appropriate warning signs, or owner identification of a wind generator, tower, building, or other structure associated with a residential wind energy system that shall be visible from any public road shall be prohibited.

The blade tip of any wind turbine, shall, at its lowest point, have ground clearance of no less than 75 feet.
Wind turbines shall not be climbable up to 15 feet above ground level. All access doors to wind turbine towers and electrical equipment shall be lockable.
Wind turbines shall be painted a nonreflective, nonobtrusive color, and shall not be artificially lighted, except to the extent required by the FAA or other applicable authority.

Upon cessation of the operation of the solar, wind energy facility or turbine, the individual panels, facility or turbine and other related improvements to the property shall be removed. Such fiscal surety shall be for a period not to exceed five years and will be renewed thereafter upon a favorable review of the operation and maintenance of such facility or turbine by the zoning committee and corporation counsel and updated cost estimates furnished by the applicant.

Wind turbines shall not be artificially lighted, except to the extent required by the FAA or other applicable authority. Wind energy systems are prohibited in Waushara County except for repair or maintenance of existing systems. Minimum standards include setbacks, nonreflective paint, lockable access, and warning signage.

Sec. 54-66 explicitly prohibits wind energy systems in Waushara County, stating that 'Wind energy systems... are prohibited' and 'No permit shall be issued for the construction or operation of any wind energy system within Waushara County.' The prohibition is absolute and unconditional, with the only exception being for 'repair or maintenance of any wind energy system existing prior to the effective date of this ordinance.' There is no expiration date or moratorium period specified.

Wind turbines shall be set back from the nearest nonparticipating property line a distance no less than 1.1 times their total height, unless appropriate easements are secured from adjacent property owners.

Appropriate warning signage shall be placed on solar substation facilities, wind turbine towers, electrical equipment, and wind energy facility entrances.

Operational noise impacts at the Project Boundary shall not exceed fifty (50 dBA) decibels where abutting residential or Planned Area Development use districts, identified wildlife corridors, or where abutting parcels with dwellings existing at the time of Board of Supervisors approval of the Solar Facility. This must be demonstrated by a noise analysis prepared by a qualified expert or by submission of manufacturer documentation showing noise level compliance with the fifty (50 dBA) decibels standard, as determined satisfactory by the Development Services Director.

Setbacks for Utility-Scale Solar Facilities from property lines, lot lines, facility perimeters, parcels, and/or subdivisions are specified as fixed distances. The primary setback is five hundred (500) feet from any parcels zoned R1L, RMM, R1, RCU, R2, RS, C1, C2, C3, PAD, RCD, or OS (F.2.a) and five hundred (500) feet from any parcel zoned PM, M1, or M2 (F.2.b). Additionally, there is a setback of six hundred fifty (650) feet from each parcel corner on land parcels with checkerboard ownership arrangements (F.2.j), three hundred (300) feet from the official street Right-of-Way line of any State or Interstate highway (F.2.k), and a minimum of one hundred (100) feet front, rear, interior side, and exterior side setbacks in all other cases (F.2.l). The most restrictive setback directly pertaining to parcels and property lines is 500 feet.

The ordinance requires a setback of one thousand (1,000) feet from federally protected lands (e.g., National Park, National Monument, Conservation Lands), and five hundred (500) feet from other federally managed lands, unless such adjacent lands have leased or planned uses deemed compatible by the Board of Supervisors. It also requires one thousand (1,000) feet from County open space, parks, and other Recreational Resources. These setbacks apply to the Development Area of the Utility-Scale Solar Facility, including fencing and PV panels, but not landscaping unless a waiver is granted.

The ordinance requires a setback of three hundred (300’) feet from the official street Right-of-Way line of any State or Interstate highway for Utility-Scale Solar Facilities. In all other cases where the above setbacks do not apply, the front, rear, interior side, and exterior side setbacks shall be a minimum of one hundred (100’) feet.

summary: The ordinance explicitly requires vegetative buffer and screening for Utility-Scale Solar Facilities. A buffer zone "shall be established and mapped in the Development Plan for the purpose of mitigating the effects of the Solar Facility upon surrounding properties, wildlife, and resources" and "shall be an area reserved for open space, wildlife corridors, natural vegetation, and landscaping." Screening measures must "provide adequate relief from ground level views and activity" and may include "existing vegetation, topography, buildings, open space," "vegetative landscaping" with "evergreen and deciduous trees, shrubs, and/or cacti or succulents" native to Yavapai County and 4 to 6 feet in height at planting, berms with a "three-to-one (3:1) horizontal-to-vertical ratio, four (4’) feet to six (6’) feet above the adjacent grade," and fencing that is "at least seventy-five (75%) percent visually solid" but "shall not be the primary method" and "shall not be used to screen more than thirty (30%) percent of the views required to be screened." Additional screening may be required for dwellings within 1,000 feet of the Project Boundary. The Landscaping Plan must include "specifications of proposed ground cover (including seed mixes), screening materials (including identification of appropriate plant species and spacing), and proposed herbicides used if any," and "design and specifications of proposed additional vegetative screening." Berms and fencing must be "continuously maintained and repaired or replaced if damaged." Screening must not impede wildlife corridors, and fencing must be wildlife-friendly. These requirements apply to Utility-Scale Solar Facilities as defined in the ordinance and are separate from Small-Scale Solar Use standards.

Any signs associated with the Solar Facility shall be designed to comply with Section 601 Sign Code and a sign permit must be obtained for all proposed signs. Only signs related to Solar Facility use and safety will be permitted, including directional signs for emergency purposes proposed in consultation with the Fire District, Sheriff’s Office, and Emergency Management staff.

The ordinance requires a Stormwater Management Plan that includes "erosion and sediment control regulations for land disturbing activities" (subsection D.2.e.(3)) and must be approved by the Flood Control District prior to construction permits. Ground Cover and Vegetation Preservation standards mandate "preliminary erosion control, site maintenance, noxious weed control and management, and native plant preservations and revegetation plans" as part of the Landscaping Plan (subsection F.5). The project must "maintain the local ecosystem by minimizing grading and site disturbance and to maximize retention of native vegetation, topsoil, and landforms," with disturbed areas seeded with "a certified weed free native revegetation seed mix" and maintained for the permit duration. During decommissioning, the plan must include "plans for stabilizing the soils; ripping the soil to loosen the compaction areas prior to native reseeding, and replanting" and disturbed land must be reseeded and re-vegetated with certified weed free native seed mixes within one year of removal of structures (subsection M). These requirements apply to Utility-Scale Solar Facilities as defined, with Small-Scale Solar Use standards excluded from this section.

Solar Facilities are required to be located in the RCU (Residential; Rural) zoning district. The operation of a Solar Facility shall require a Solar Facility Use Permit approved by the Board of Supervisors, applied for in the same manner as a rezoning (zoning district change). A waiver request shall be required for consideration to locate a Solar Facility in any other zoning district. The Board of Supervisors may also require these criteria when considering whether to approve the waiver request. This indicates that Solar Facilities are permitted as a special use in the RCU district and may be conditionally permitted in other districts upon waiver approval.

The ordinance requires a setback of five hundred (500) feet from any dwellings (existing or under permit) or any parcels zoned R1L, RMM, R1, RCU, R2, RS, C1, C2, C3, PAD, RCD, or OS for Utility-Scale Solar Facilities. Additional vegetative screening may be required for dwellings located one thousand (1,000) feet or less from the Project Boundary. Other setback distances apply to parcels zoned PM, M1, or M2 (500 feet), federally protected lands (1,000 feet), County open space and parks (1,000 feet), forested or heavily vegetated areas (500 feet), ravines or canyons (500 feet), hillsides with slopes of 10% or greater (150 feet), significant archaeological sites (500 feet, possibly up to 1,000 feet), parcel corners in checkerboard ownership (650 feet), and state or interstate highway rights-of-way (300 feet).

Subsection D.2.f Visual Impact Analysis requires "a visual impact analysis demonstrating project siting and, if necessary, proposed mitigation and screening to reduce impacts on the visual character of the surrounding area." The applicant must provide "accurate, to scale, photographic simulations showing the relationship of the Solar Facility to its surroundings" from "prominent locations, adjacent roads, nearby highways, existing dwellings (from closest adjacent property line), and other residential, scenic, cultural, and Recreational Resources". The number and perspectives of simulations are established by the Development Services Director after the pre-application meeting, chosen to establish visual impacts upon sensitive areas potentially receiving the greatest impacts. These requirements apply to Utility-Scale Solar Facilities as defined in Section 608, which excludes Small-Scale Solar Use. Glare restrictions are addressed separately and are not part of this visual impact assessment requirement.

Five hundred (500’) feet from any lake, creek, perennial or intermittent stream, river, major tributaries, riparian areas, wetlands, or seeps, as measured from the top edge of the bank, or from the outer edge of any delineated Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Floodplains. Minor tributaries may warrant a reduced buffer setback to be no less than one hundred fifty (150’) feet as determined by the Board of Supervisors.

The ordinance lists four utility land use types for solar systems: Utility, Minor (Tier 1, roof-mount/ground up to ½ acre); Utility, Accessory (Tier 2, < 15 percent of parcel size up to 5 acres, whichever is less); Utility, Intermediate (Tier 3, < 30 percent of parcel size up to 20 acres, whichever is less); and Utility, Major (Tier 4, ground-mounted system for power generation). § 84.29.070 Decommissioning Requirements requires the project owner to prepare a Closure, Revegetation, and Rehabilitation Plan and submit it to the Planning Division for review and approval prior to building permit issuance. All aboveground structures and facilities shall be removed to a depth of three feet below grade and removed offsite for recycling or disposal. Concrete, piping, and other materials below three feet may be left in place. Graded areas shall be restored to original contours unless a community benefit for altered grading is shown. Native succulent plant species shall be salvaged and maintained for later transplanting, and shrubs and other plants shall be revegetated by seed collection and reseeding. Decommissioning must comply with other plans and permits including Water Quality Management Plan, Erosion and Sediment Control Plan, Drainage Report, Notice of Intent and Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan, Air Quality Permits, Biological Resources Report, Incidental Take Permit, and Cultural Records Report. The County may require a Phase 1 Environmental Site Assessment at the end of decommissioning to verify site conditions.

summary: The ordinance requires that the proposed commercial solar energy generation facility "will minimize site grading, excavating, and filling activities by being located on land where the existing grade does not exceed an average of five percent across the developed portion of the project site, and by utilizing construction methods that minimize ground disturbance." It also mandates that the facility "will be designed, constructed, and operated so as to minimize dust generation, including provision of sufficient watering of excavated or graded soil during construction to prevent excessive dust," with watering "at a minimum of three times daily on disturbed soil areas with active operations, unless dust is otherwise controlled by rainfall or use of a dust palliative, or other approved dust control measure." Additionally, "all clearing, grading, earth moving, and excavation activities will cease during period of winds greater than 20 miles per hour... or when dust plumes of 20 percent or greater opacity impact public roads, occupied structures, or neighboring property, and in conformance with Air Quality Management District (AQMD) regulations." Unpaved roads and access ways "will be treated and maintained with a dust palliative or graveled or treated by another approved dust control method to prevent excessive dust." These requirements apply to commercial solar energy generation facilities, including those 15 acres or greater.
