SES-C systems must be designed and constructed to minimize glare on adjacent properties and roadways, and not interfere with vehicular traffic, including air traffic (§ 155.135(E)(9)(a)). SES-C projects located within 500 feet of an airport or within approach zones must complete a glare analysis through a qualitative analysis of ocular impact in consultation with the FAA (§ 155.135(J)).
section: § 155.135 Development Standards for Solar Energy System-Commercial and § 155.137 Design and Construction - WESC and SES

summary: The height of any SES-C system on a property is limited to twenty-five (25) feet above ground level when the SES-C system’s arrays are at full tilt. Roof-mounted SES-C, SES-A, and Integrated Solar Energy Systems may exceed the maximum allowed building height of the building or structure in which it is located by up to three (3) feet in all zoning districts. This height limit applies specifically to commercial solar energy systems, including large ground-mounted systems intended for offsite electricity generation or sale.
section: § 155.135 Development Standards for Solar Energy System-Commercial

summary: The ordinance states: 'A project owner may not install or locate a SES-C system unless the project owner demonstrates that the SES-C system will operate in a manner such that the sound attributable to the SES-C system will not exceed an hourly average sound level of fifty (50) A-weighted decibels, as modeled at the outer wall of a dwelling located on an adjacent nonparticipating property.' This is the explicit maximum noise level allowed for commercial solar energy systems, including Ground Mounted SES, Large. The units are standard noise measurement units, dBA (A-weighted decibels). The requirement may be waived with written consent of the adjacent nonparticipating property owner.
section: § 155.135 Development Standards for Solar Energy System-Commercial

summary: Setbacks — Commercial solar arrays must meet the following setbacks, measured as a straight line from the nearest outer edge of the SES-C system’s solar panels, as follows: The property line of any nonparticipating property is at least fifty (50) feet. Other setback distances include 40 feet from federal/state/county highway rights-of-way, 30 feet from collector roads, and 10 feet from local roads, but these do not pertain to property lines. If a SES-C system is within 250 feet of a dwelling on a nonparticipating property, a landscape buffer must be installed between the solar panels and the nonparticipating property line facing the panels, unless waived by written consent of the affected property owner.
section: § 155.135 Development Standards for Solar Energy System-Commercial

summary: Commercial solar arrays must meet the following setbacks, measured as a straight line from the nearest outer edge of the SES-C system’s solar panels, as follows: The nearest edge of the right-of-way for any federal interstate highway, federal highway, state highway, or county highway is at least forty (40) feet. Other options include 30 feet from collector roads and 10 feet from local roads.
section: § 155.135 Development Standards for Solar Energy System-Commercial (E) Site Design: 2. Setbacks

summary: Section 155.135(E)(2) requires that if a SES-C system is installed within two hundred fifty (250) feet from a nonparticipating property with a dwelling, the project owner shall install a landscape buffer in the area between the nearest outer edge of the SES-C system’s solar panel and the nonparticipating property owner’s property line that faces the SES-C system’s solar panels. The landscape buffer must be in a location that is not on the property of the nonparticipating property owner. The landscape buffer and screening must be constructed from such materials as set forth in a plan submitted to the Putnam County BZA during the permitting and approval process. Vegetation or another type of buffer can be proposed. Screening shall not be required along highways or roadways, or along property lines within the same zoning district, except where the adjoining lot has an existing residential use. Additionally, SES-C are required to plant, establish, and maintain for the life of the SES-C system perennial vegetated ground cover on the ground around and under solar panels, and the project site buffer areas, with encouragement for pollinator seed mixes and native or naturalized species. A vegetation plan must be submitted that provides for planting of noninvasive species, site preparation and maintenance practices designed to control invasive species and noxious weeds, and use of native or naturalized species if appropriate. Projects certified and maintained as pollinator-friendly compliant are exempt from landscaping requirements and post-construction stormwater management controls unless required due to special conditions by the Plan Commission or Board of Zoning Appeals. Section 155.137(A)(4) requires WESC and/or SES to maximize the use of building materials, colors and textures designed to blend with and/or to harmonize with the natural surroundings. Section 155.137(A)(8)(h) authorizes the Planning Director or designee to determine appropriate screening for outside storage if approved through Site Plan Review.
section: § 155.135 Development Standards for Solar Energy System-Commercial

summary: All SES-C and their appurtenant structures shall contain a standard metal road sign no larger than four (4) square feet in order to provide the name(s) of the owner(s) and operator(s) of the SES-C as well as emergency phone number(s) and the address of the site. This sign shall be visible from the access point of the site — but shall be located just outside of the road right-of-way, outside of the sight triangles in either direction — and shall not be lighted, unless lighting is required by applicable law, rule, or regulation. A four (4) square foot warning sign concerning voltage must also be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations in a conspicuous location. No other signage, including advertising, shall be permitted.
section: § 155.135 Development Standards for Solar Energy System-Commercial

summary: The ordinance explicitly requires that SES-C projects, which include Ground Mounted SES, Large, must "plant, establish, and maintain for the life of the SES-C system perennial vegetated ground cover on the ground around and under solar panels, and the project site buffer areas" to "reduce stormwater runoff and erosion at the site" (§ 155.135(E)(6)(a) and (b)). It mandates a vegetation plan with native or naturalized species and invasive species control. Additionally, "all damage to waterways, drainage ditches, field tiles, or other drainage related infrastructure caused by the construction, installation, or maintenance of a SES-C system must be completely repaired" (§ 155.135(E)(10)(a)). All Solar Energy Systems must comply with "the Putnam County Code of Ordinances regarding drainage and erosion control and Nonpoint Pollution Discharge Elimination Systems (NPDES) permit requirements" (§ 155.135(E)(10)(b)). For sites with one acre or more of land disturbance, a drainage and erosion control plan must be developed in consultation with the Putnam County Soil and Water Conservation District and a Notice of Intent submitted to IDEM (§ 155.142(D)(9)). These requirements apply to commercial solar energy systems serving off-site electric demands, including Medium and Large Ground Mounted SES, as defined under SES-C. Other options such as SES-A (accessory systems) and smaller systems are not subject to these specific soil, erosion, and sediment control requirements.
section: § 155.135 Development Standards for Solar Energy System-Commercial

summary: § 155.135(A) states that 'SES-C projects are permitted in all districts with a special exception from the Board of Zoning Appeals.' Additionally, § 155.135(D) notes that in 'Agricultural Zones and Uses: For areas zoned Agricultural (A1, Ag)... the Board of Zoning Appeals can make the special exception time-limited, to coincide with the proposed length of time that the SES-C will remain on the site — and with a condition that the site be returned to an agricultural use at the end of the life of the solar installation.' Other options mentioned include SES-A (accessory systems) which are permitted accessory uses in all zoning districts where structures are allowed, subject to requirements, but these do not apply to SES-C. Solar overlay districts are excluded from this analysis.
section: § 155.135 Development Standards for Solar Energy System-Commercial

summary: A project owner may not install or locate a SES-C system on a property unless the distance, measured as a straight line, from the nearest outer edge of the SES-C system’s solar panels to the nearest point on the outer wall of a dwelling located on a nonparticipating property is at least two hundred fifty (250) feet. If a project owner installs a SES-C system within two hundred fifty (250) feet from a nonparticipating property with a dwelling, the project owner shall install a landscape buffer in the area between the nearest outer edge of the SES-C system’s solar panel and the nonparticipating property owner’s property line that faces the SES-C system’s solar panels. The distance requirement and the requirement for a landscaping buffer may be waived with respect to the siting of any one (1) SES-C system subject to the written consent of the owner of each affected nonparticipating property. Other setback options include 40 feet from federal/state/county highways, 30 feet from collector roads, 10 feet from local roads, and 50 feet from property lines of nonparticipating properties, but these do not pertain to occupied dwellings directly.
section: § 155.135 Development Standards for Solar Energy System-Commercial

summary: The ordinance requires that the location of all above-ground utility lines within a radius equal to two (2) times the height of the proposed SES-C system be identified in the application. Specifically, § 155.142(D)(1) states: 'The location of all above-ground utility lines within a radius equal to two (2) times the height of the proposed Mini WECS, SWECS, WECS, or SES-C.' No other multiplier values or static distance adders are provided for setbacks from overhead electrical transmission lines, overhead utility lines, utility easements, utility lines, power lines, electrical lines, or transmission lines for Ground Mounted SES, Large. Additionally, § 155.137(A)(3)(a) states that ground-mounted SES shall not be located over an existing utility easement unless approval is obtained from the applicable utility providers, and all utilities except certain equipment must be installed underground.

§ 156.664(Q) Decommissioning plan: Prior to approval, a decommissioning plan must be formulated and approved by the County Commissioners and the applicant, outlining the means and cost of removing a SES at the end of its serviceable life or upon becoming discontinued or abandoned. Applicants must provide a bond or other financial responsibility sufficient to satisfy the decommissioning agreement, with cost estimates updated every five years. The plan must include written assurance of proper decommissioning, contractor cost estimates including salvage value, and cost adjustments for inflation. Owners/operators shall not store hazardous or unused materials on site. SES are considered discontinued after six months without energy production unless a plan to return to service is approved, and abandoned after three months without maintenance. Upon discontinuation or abandonment, removal of all physical material to six feet below ground level must occur within 365 days, and the site restored to near pre-construction condition unless otherwise agreed. Written notice and a reasonable period for negotiation are required before enforcement actions. This applies to Primary SES, which includes Large-Scale SES defined as "a primary solar energy system that covers ten acres or more and converts sunlight into electricity for the primary purpose of wholesale sales."

Perimeter fencing for the site shall not include barbed wire designs and shall preferably use wildlife-friendly fencing standards that include clearance at the bottom. Perimeter fencing is required on all sides of a primary SES project. All fencing must be approved by the Board of Zoning Appeals. A perimeter fencing plan shall be submitted that identifies the type of fencing and location of fencing. Fencing plans that provide for straight lines of fencing or fencing that provides for continuity of the land are preferred. Primary SES operators shall maintain all fencing in good repair at all times.

No primary SES project shall produce noxious glare or light on non-participating properties or rights-of-way. All security and other lighting at the SES project site shall be certified as dark sky friendly. Emergency lighting systems shall not be subject to this provision but must comply with industry standards. Additionally, all systems using a reflector to enhance solar production shall minimize glare from the reflector affecting adjacent or nearby properties.

No primary SES shall exceed 20 feet in height as measured at maximum design tilt. This applies to Large-Scale SES as they are defined as a type of Primary SES. The relevant text states: 'No primary SES shall exceed 20 feet in height as measured at maximum design tilt.'

No primary SES project shall be located on a site that is less than five acres in size. This minimum acreage applies to primary SES, which includes large-scale SES as defined. The relevant text states: 'No primary SES project shall be located on a site that is less than five acres in size.' The unit is explicitly given as acres.

The ordinance states: 'At all times, the noise level of a primary SES shall be no greater than 50 decibels measured from each surrounding property line.' This applies to Primary SES, which includes Large-Scale SES as defined in the text. The unit for noise level is conventionally understood as dBA. No other noise level restrictions for Large-Scale SES are provided.

Setbacks of all primary SES structures from the property line of any non-participating property line shall be a minimum of 50 feet. Setbacks of all primary SES structures between separate parcels, both of which are participating in the project, may be waived upon mutual agreement. Other setbacks include 40 feet from federal or county highways, which is less restrictive, and 400 feet from any housing or dwelling unit of a non-participating landowner, which relates to structures, not property lines. The 50 feet setback from non-participating property lines is the fixed minimum distance directly applicable to Large-Scale SES.

Setbacks of all primary SES structures from all federal interstate highway, federal highway, or county highway shall be a minimum of 40 feet. Setback distance shall be measured from the edge of the solar energy system array at maximum design tilt, including security fencing, screening, or berm, to the right-of-way or edge of pavement if right-of-way does not exist. Setbacks listed represent minimum setbacks allowed and do not restrict the Board of Zoning Appeals authority to impose more restrictive setbacks. Utility rights-of-way or ingress/egress easement setbacks may be waived by the beneficiary by filing a written consent/waiver.

All primary SES shall be fully screened on all sides of the SES site. Any visual buffer must be approved by the Board of Zoning Appeals. A landscape plan shall be submitted that identifies the type and extent of proposed buffer and screening. Vegetation or another type of buffer can be proposed if it fully screens the SES. Non-participating parcel owners, not including owners of parcels that are across rights-of-way from the SES site, may waive landscaping requirements by filing a written consent/waiver with the Zoning Administrator or body.

Primary SES that are mounted on the ground are required to install one of the following alternatives for ground cover: (1) Alternative A: perennial ground cover, which must be planted, established, and maintained for the life of the SES project and include a diverse seed mix of native species consistent with guidance from the Soil and Water Conservation District office or the Indiana Native Plant Society; or (2) Alternative B: pollinator friendly ground cover, which must comply with the definition of pollinator-friendly solar energy and demonstrate habitat quality based on guidance such as the Purdue University 2020 Indiana Solar Site Pollinator Habitat Planning Scorecard. Additionally, a detailed drainage plan prepared and certified by a licensed engineer must be submitted and approved prior to construction, describing the overall approach for managing stormwater runoff with post-construction runoff at least 80% of pre-construction runoff.

Setbacks of all primary SES structures from any housing or dwelling unit of a non-participating landowner shall be a minimum of 400 feet. This setback may be waived by a non-participating landowner filing a written waiver with the Zoning Administrator or body. For primary SES structures the distance, measured as a straight line, from the nearest outer edge of the SES system to the nearest point on the outer wall of a dwelling. Other setback options include: 50 feet from non-participating property lines; 40 feet from federal interstate highway, federal highway, or county highway; 100 feet from a cemetery; and waivers may apply for setbacks between participating parcels or utility rights-of-way.

The ordinance explicitly requires SES-3 owners/operators to submit and enter into a Decommissioning-Restoration Plan and Agreement with the County Commissioners prior to receiving an Improvement Location Permit. The owner/operator must give written notice of intent to abandon use at least 120 days prior to discontinuation of electrical production. An SES is considered abandoned after one year without energy production unless a Rehabilitation Plan is approved. The SES owner/operator must remove all physical material above and below ground within 365 days of discontinuation or abandonment, recycle broken or end-of-life panels, and restore the site to as near as practicable to the original condition. Hazardous materials must be identified and properly handled during removal. A performance guarantee in the form of a cash bond equal to 150% of estimated decommissioning and restoration costs must be provided and updated every five years. The County may remove the SES using bond funds if the owner/operator defaults. Written notice and a negotiation period of up to 60 days are required before enforcement actions. The owner/operator is liable for all costs incurred by the County if removal is necessary. These requirements apply specifically to SES-2 and SES-3 systems. Other options or conditions include the Rehabilitation Plan for damaged or abandoned SES, and possible variance requests if agreements differ from these requirements.
section: S. Decommissioning-Restoration Plan and Agreement (for SES-2 and SES-3)

summary: All ground-mounted SES-2 and SES-3 shall be completely enclosed by a minimum six (6) foot high chain link fence with a locking gate accessed by a keypad or Knox box with key. The fence should be located at the setback distance. Any required landscaping or buffer may be outside the fence. A fence in an agriculture zone located on the property lines is the sole responsibility of the SES owner/operator.

The ordinance explicitly enacts glare restrictions for SES-3 systems. It requires that "solar energy panels, regardless of how they are mounted, shall be oriented and/or screened year-round so that glare is directed away from adjacent properties, structures, and roadways" to the extent reasonably possible. Additionally, "the SES shall remain painted or finished in the color or finish that was originally applied by the manufacturer provided the exterior surface of any visible components are non-reflective, a neutral color like black, white, gray or another non-obtrusive color. Finishes shall be matte or non-reflective." The property owner has "the burden of mitigating any glare produced so as not to have significant adverse impact on adjacent uses either through siting or mitigation." The Executive Director's determination on compliance is conclusive. These requirements appear under provisions applicable to SES-2 and SES-3 systems. Other options or conditions related to glare include the use of colors, materials, textures, screening, and landscaping to blend into settings and avoid visual blight. These restrictions are part of the broader safety, design, and installation standards for SES-2 and SES-3.
section: D.e.6 and D.5 Color, Finish and Glare

summary: The ordinance explicitly states: 'Ground-mounted SES arrays shall not exceed fifteen (15) feet in height when oriented at maximum tilt.' This applies to SES-2 and SES-3 systems. Additionally, it notes that in residential zone districts the maximum height of a ground-mounted SES shall be 10 feet, which is more restrictive but applies only to residential zones. The 15 feet limit is the general maximum for SES-3. The units are feet as specified in the ordinance.

SES-3 systems are defined as 10 to 300 acres (not including required buffers) and/or greater than 16 MW/ac. The ordinance explicitly states: 'No SES larger than 300 acres shall be permitted.' Additionally, SES-2 or SES-3 projects, either singly or as a combination of contiguous parcels, shall not exceed 10 acres or 300 acres respectively (not including required buffers). The unit of measurement for maximum lot size is acres.

SES-3 is defined as systems occupying "10 to 300 acres (not including required buffers) and/or greater than 16 MW/ac" with a clear minimum size threshold of 10 acres. The ordinance states "No SES larger than 300 acres shall be permitted." This sets a minimum lot size of 10 acres for SES-3 systems. Other system types include SES-1 (5 acres or less and/or less than 1 MW/ac) and SES-2 (up to 10 acres maximum and less than 1 MW/ac or 5 to 10 acres including buffers and/or more than 1 MW/ac and less than 15 MW/ac). The units for the minimum lot size are explicitly given as acres.

No operating SES shall produce noise that exceeds any of the following limitations except during construction or maintenance. Adequate setbacks, barriers, enclosures, use of quieter equipment, or other effective means of reducing noise shall be used to comply with these limitations: (a) Fifty dBA, as measured at the property line of any adjacent residentially zoned lot; (b) Forty-five dBA, as measured at any existing adjacent residence between the hours of nine p.m. and seven a.m.; and (c) Sixty dBA, as measured at the property lines of the project boundary, unless the owner of the affected property agrees to a higher noise level. The most restrictive value is 45 dBA measured at any existing adjacent residence between 9 p.m. and 7 a.m. The units for noise level are dBA.

A three-mile neutral zone is required between each SES-3 project. Additionally, SES-3 requires a 1320' setback and separation distance from property line or ROW to fencing. Setbacks for SES-3 are 1320' from any adjoining road or from the property line of a non-participating homeowner to the beginning of the project/fencing. The three-mile neutral zone (3 miles = 15,840 feet) is the most restrictive minimum separation distance explicitly stated for SES-3 projects.

The ordinance specifies a fixed setback distance of 1320 feet from the property line of a non-participating homeowner to the beginning of the SES-3 project/fencing. This setback applies to the entire SES-3 facility including solar panels, racking, underground cabling, fencing, access roads/lanes, and other power equipment. Other setback options include SES-1 with setbacks equivalent to building setbacks (currently 30 feet) and SES-2 with 100 feet setback from property line or ROW to fencing except in commercial zones.
section: D. Safety, Design, and Installation Standards for SES-2 and SES-3 Zoning, 1. Setbacks and Siting of Facilities

summary: For SES-3, a 1320' setback and separation distance from property line or ROW to fencing is required. Minimum setbacks are measured from the centerline of the road right-of-way (ROW) or the property line where there is no ROW present. Setbacks apply to the entire SES including solar panels, racking, underground cabling, fencing, access roads/lanes, and other power equipment. Driveway cuts for ingress/egress roads into a SES-3 shall be no closer than 100 feet from the property line of an adjoining landowner unless waived. The fence should be located at the setback distance. Other options include SES-2 with 100' setback and SES-1 with setbacks equivalent to building setbacks (30 ft currently).
section: I.D.1. Setbacks and Siting of Facilities

summary: The ordinance explicitly enacts signage requirements for SES-3 systems. It states: 'No portion of the SES shall contain or be used to display advertising. The manufacturer's name and equipment information or indication of ownership shall be allowed on any equipment of the SES. Appropriate Warning signs will be allowed.' Further, under signage requirements for SES-2 and SES-3, it provides: 'An identification sign relating to a SES may be located on each side of the fenced facility area provided that there shall be no more than one (1) sign located on any side of the SES fenced facility area unless additional identification signs are required to provide reasonable notice to the general public.' It also requires: 'A sign shall be securely posted on each gate entry point clearly displaying an emergency telephone number(s) and other contact information.' Additionally, 'All ingress/egress roads to a SES shall have posted in a conspicuous location a 911 address road sign indicating the assigned address for that location.' Warning signs must comply with applicable laws, and all signage must be durable, weatherproof, and have a distinct, high contrast background to promote safety. These requirements apply specifically to SES-3 as part of the technical requirements and special use permit conditions. No other options or conditions for signage requirements are provided in the ordinance.

The ordinance explicitly enacts soil, erosion, and sediment control requirements for SES-3 systems. It requires "an erosion control plan shall be developed in accordance with protocol of the Natural Resources Conservation Services (NRCS), and any storm water quality management plan adopted by the applicable jurisdiction(s)." The area beneath the ground-mounted SES is considered pervious cover, and "Natural (pervious) ground covers are required beneath the solar arrays." For SES-3, "Damages, including but not limited to damming, cutting, removing, and blocking, to surface, subsurface drains, or any other drainage infrastructure... must be restored by the SES-3 owner to a condition that is equal to or better than the preexisting conditions within three (3) months after receipt of notice of such damage." The SES-3 owner is responsible for all expenses related to repairs, relocations, reconfigurations, and replacements of drainage infrastructure and systems that are damaged. The SES-3 owner must post a "5A" surety bond payable to the Drainage Board to address drainage tile repair, replacement or rerouting caused by construction activities or installation of the Project, with the bond remaining in effect for 30 years after operation begins. Additionally, prior to issuing an Improvement Location Permit, the applicant must provide a Drainage Agreement approved by the County Commissioners that "must prescribe or reference provisions to address field tile damages and repairs thereof for any field tile owned by Rush County." The petitioner must "restore the drainage infrastructure or system to pre-existing conditions or better within a period of three (3) months after receipt of notice of such damage unless such repair is rendered impractical by weather or other natural force." The petitioner is responsible for all expenses related to repairs, relocations, reconfigurations, and replacements of drainage infrastructure and systems damaged as a direct result of the Project and must post a surety bond to address these repairs. The petitioner must fully comply with Indiana Code requirements regarding legal drains except as otherwise approved by the Drainage Board and any other necessary bodies.
section: U. Erosion Control Plan; 20. Sub-surface and surface drains (regulated and non-regulated)- Applies to SES-3; T. Drainage Agreement, and Road Use and Maintenance Agreements

summary: SES-3 systems (10 to 300 acres and/or greater than 16 MW/ac) require approval for a special use by the Board of Zoning Appeals prior to issuing a building permit. The ordinance states: 'SES-2 and SES-3 systems must be approved for a special use by the Board of Zoning Appeals prior to issuing a building permit.' Additionally, 'No more than 10% of a SES-3 may be located on A- Farmland as designated,' and a letter from NRCS or a qualified source must be included with the application. The ordinance also imposes setbacks of 1320 feet from property lines or roads for SES-3. Other system types include SES-1 (property/homeowner/agriculture use, 5 acres or less and/or less than 1 MW/ac; can be larger with special exception) and SES-2 (commercial use or sale, up to 10 acres and less than 1 MW/ac, or 5 to 10 acres including buffers and/or more than 1 MW/ac and less than 15 MW/ac; can be larger by special exception). SES-1 can be approved by the planning office via Improvement Location Petition, while SES-2 and SES-3 require special use approval by the Board of Zoning Appeals. The ordinance applies to all unincorporated areas of the County.

The ordinance requires a 1320-foot setback and separation distance from the property line of a non-participating homeowner to the beginning of the SES-3 project/fencing. This setback applies to the entire SES including solar panels, racking, underground cabling, fencing, access roads/lanes, and other power equipment. Other setback options include SES-2 with 100 feet from the property line of a non-participating homeowner. The relevant text states: 'Setbacks are as follows: SES-2 - 100' from the property line of a non-participating homeowner (setback and separation distance of any part of SES); SES-3 - 1320' from any adjoining road or from the property line of a non-participating homeowner to the beginning of the project/fencing. Setbacks apply to the entire SES including solar panels, racking, underground cabling, fencing, access roads/lanes, and other power equipment.'
section: I.e.4.1.a. Setbacks and Siting of Facilities

summary: The furthest horizontal extension of a SES-2 or 3, excepting the SES collection system, SES transmission lines, ingress/egress road and SES access roads/lanes, shall not extend ... nor be less than fifteen (15') feet from any structure or public right-of-way easement for any above ground telephone line, electrical transmission line, electrical distribution line or other above ground communication or transmission line. Other relevant provisions include: no setback requirements from property lines for poles carrying overhead wiring and underground wiring located within recorded easements; ground-mounted SES shall not be placed within any legal easement or right-of-way without written permission; power and communication lines between solar panel banks and substations shall be buried underground except for lines between the project and the point of interconnection with the transmission system which may be overhead.
section: D. Safety, Design, and Installation Standards for SES-2 and SES-3 Zoning

summary: No SES-3 facility shall be sited within three miles of any FEMA/DNR floodplain, major named creek, and river, and any natural flowing spring well.

The cumulative area of all land within the CSES Overlay District shall be limited to one percent (1%) of the total acres of cropland in Shelby County, Indiana as determined by the latest available data provided by the Census of Agriculture. Additionally, only one (1) individual CSES project shall be permitted within a ten (10) year period, beginning at the date of final CSES Overlay District approval of the first project. The unit 'percent' refers to the proportion of total cropland acres, not a fixed acreage number.

Any CSES which has discontinued commercial operation or has ceased electrical power generation or transmission for at least six (6) consecutive months shall be removed at the expense of the applicant or its successor in compliance with a decommissioning plan approved by the County. The decommissioning plan shall include: removal of all surface and subsurface physical improvements; restoration of surface grade, soil, drainage infrastructure, and vegetation to pre-construction conditions; disposal of all CSES equipment and materials in compliance with laws; a decommissioning cost estimate prepared by a State licensed professional engineer; and financial assurance in the form of a performance or surety bond issued by an AM Best Company with an A or A+ rating. The bond must name the Shelby County Commissioners as beneficiary and be updated every three years. Partial decommissioning is required if triggered for a portion of the CSES, with the remaining portion subject to the plan. Amendments to the plan require approval by the Zoning Administrator. The decommissioning plan must be submitted with the TAC Site Plan application.

Security fencing surrounding any CSES shall be agricultural fencing which is of woven wire composition and wood posts. Fencing shall be a minimum height of six (6) feet and shall not exceed a height of eight (8) feet. Razor wire shall be prohibited. If Federal or State requirements conflict with County fencing standards, the Federal or State requirements shall supersede. All ground-mounted electrical and control equipment for CSES shall be fenced and labeled or secured to prevent unauthorized access. The solar array and/or modules shall be designed and installed to prevent access by the public with fencing in accordance with Section 3.15 G, and access to same shall be through a locked gate.

Section 3.15 J states: 'Any CSES shall be situated to eliminate concentrated glare onto abutting structures and roadways.' Section 3.15 O requires that 'For any CSES located within 660 feet of an airport or within approach zones of an airport, the applicant must complete and provide the results of a glare analysis through a qualitative analysis of potential impact, field test demonstration, or geometric analysis of ocular impact in consultation with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Office of Airports.' These provisions explicitly impose glare-related requirements for Commercial Solar Energy Systems. No other glare-related options or conditions are provided in the text.
section: 3.15 CSES District Procedural and Development Standards

summary: The height of any CSES ground mounted solar equipment is limited to 20 feet, as measured from the highest natural grade below each solar panel.

Sound attributable of any CSES shall not exceed an hourly average sound level of forty (40) A-weighted decibels, as modeled at the perimeter boundary line of the CSES. The unit is expressed as dBA, which is the standard unit for noise measurement.

The Commercial Solar Energy System (CSES) Overlay District is intended to enable Shelby County to regulate the permitting of commercial solar energy systems and allow for the orderly development of land. It "should be used to allow for CSES facilities in sparsely populated rural areas and in industrial areas along the I-74 corridor." The text states, "All permitted uses in the base zoning district are permitted in the CSES District," indicating that CSES are permitted as a primary use within this overlay district. No other districts or abbreviations are mentioned as permitting CSES as a primary use without special conditions or approval. The overlay district exempts CSES from maximum lot coverage requirements and limits height to 20 feet, among other standards.
section: 3.12     CSES District Intent, Effect on Uses, and Effect on Standards

summary: Any CSES ground mounted equipment and buildings, excluding any security fencing, poles, and wires necessary to connect to facilities of the electric utility, shall be located a minimum of 660-feet from the property line of any non-participating property, including the property line of properties not adjacent to the CSES. Any non-participating property owner may reduce the setback requirement from their property lines by filing written consent with the Shelby County Recorder. Such consent, when recorded, shall run with the property for the life of the CSES zoning overlay district. At a minimum, the written consent shall include: (a) The setback requirement agreed upon by the non-participating property owner and the applicant. The agreed upon setback shall not be less than the required minimum setback for a primary structure in the base zoning district; (b) A legal description of the non-participating property and parcel number(s); (c) A property map showing all property lines and agreed upon setback lines.

Any CSES ground mounted equipment and buildings, excluding any security fencing, poles, and wires necessary to connect to facilities of the electric utility, shall be located: 1. A minimum of 500 feet from the centerline of any public road.

Section 3.15 F Landscape Buffer: "Any CSES shall be required to install a landscape buffer along the side and rear property lines adjacent to the CSES of any adjacent non-participating property which includes a dwelling unit." The buffer must include "One (1) evergreen tree... for every five (5) feet of contiguous boundary with the adjacent lot," planted within fifteen (15) feet of the property line, and "at least five (5) feet in height at the time of planting." Non-participating property owners may reduce or waive the landscaping requirement by filing written consent with the Shelby County Recorder, which must include the agreed landscaping requirement, legal description, and a landscaping plan if not waived entirely. Section 3.15 G Fencing requires "Security fencing surrounding any CSES shall be agricultural fencing which is of woven wire composition and wood posts," minimum six (6) feet and maximum eight (8) feet in height, with razor wire prohibited. Section 3.15 Q Groundcover requires groundcover to be free of invasive species, prohibits insecticide use except in limited circumstances, and mandates pollinator-friendly management practices on prime farmland, with a required groundcover plan approved by qualified professionals. These requirements explicitly apply to Commercial Solar Energy Systems (CSES) as defined in the ordinance.
section: 3.15 CSES District Procedural and Development Standards

summary: All signs, other than the facility maintenance contact information, manufacturer’s or installer’s identification, appropriate warning signs, or owner identification on a solar panel array and/or modules, building, or other structure associated with any CSES shall be prohibited.

Section 3.15 A 3 requires the applicant to submit a commercial site plan to the Shelby County Storm Drainage, Erosion and Sediment Control Ordinance Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) for review. The plan should be submitted in accordance with the Class 1 Site Plan requirements as listed in Table A of the Shelby County Storm Drainage, Erosion and Sediment Control Ordinance. Additionally, a Groundcover Plan is required in accordance with U.D.O Section 3.15 Q, which includes standards such as: groundcover shall be free of invasive species prohibited by Indiana law; no insecticide use except in limited circumstances; legally applied herbicides permitted; and for prime farmland, management must adhere to guidance on pollinator-friendly management practices or best management practices for creating pollinator habitat. The Groundcover Plan must be approved by a DNR wildlife biologist, local Soil and Water Conservation District professional, or other qualified professional as determined by the Zoning Administrator. These requirements apply explicitly to Commercial Solar Energy Systems (CSES) as defined in the ordinance.
section: 3.15 CSES District Procedural and Development Standards

summary: The text states that "All special exception uses permitted by special exception in the base zoning district are permitted by special exception in the CSES District." However, it does not explicitly list any specific base zoning district names or abbreviations where Commercial Solar Energy Systems (CSES) are permitted as special use or similar. The CSES District itself is an overlay district intended to regulate permitting and placement of CSES, but specific base districts and their special exception uses are not named in the provided text.
section: 3.12     CSES District Intent, Effect on Uses, and Effect on Standards

summary: Any CSES ground mounted equipment and buildings, excluding any security fencing, poles, and wires necessary to connect to facilities of the electric utility, shall be located a minimum of 660-feet from the property line of any non-participating property, including the property line of properties not adjacent to the CSES. Any non-participating property owner may reduce the setback requirement from their property lines by filing written consent with the Shelby County Recorder. Such consent, when recorded, shall run with the property for the life of the CSES zoning overlay district. At a minimum, the written consent shall include: (a) The setback requirement agreed upon by the non-participating property owner and the applicant. The agreed upon setback shall not be less than the required minimum setback for a primary structure in the base zoning district; (b) A legal description of the non-participating property and parcel number(s); (c) A property map showing all property lines and agreed upon setback lines. The ordinance does not specify a fixed setback distance directly from non-participating occupied dwellings, buildings, structures, or residences themselves, but rather from the property lines of non-participating properties.

The ordinance requires a Decommissioning Plan to be submitted with the Development Plan to ensure proper decommissioning of CSES-1 projects. The plan must include a contractor cost estimate from a licensed engineer, a detailed plan for removal of all infrastructure and restoration of the site to its natural state, and financial assurance of 125% of the decommissioning costs in cash and bonds before issuance of any Improvement Location Permit. The Decommissioning Plan must be updated and approved every three years. Decommissioning must be initiated within six months and completed within twelve months after the end of the project life or abandonment. The plan must include proper disposal of hazardous materials and obtaining a reclamation permit from the Indiana Department of Natural Resources. Decommissioning is triggered if the facility operates at less than 25% capacity for six months or less than 10% for three months. The Decommissioning Plan must be recorded in the Office of the Spencer County Recorder. The ordinance defines CSES-1 as "Greater than 20 acres Electricity sold to utility transmission lines."

All solar panels and accessory buildings for the project must be fenced in with a fence not less than ten (10) feet in height. The fence shall not be topped with razor/barbed wire. The fencing shall be landscaped with native and non-invasive plant materials consisting of an evergreen and deciduous mix as approved by county staff, except to the extent that existing vegetation and natural landforms on the site provide such screening as determined by Spencer County.
