summary: Properties containing CSECS may be enclosed by perimeter fencing to restrict unauthorized access. Wildlife-friendly fencing, such as a barb-wire fence with smooth wires for the top and bottom strings, or woven wire or other permeable fencing, shall be used where possible. Where wildlife-friendly fencing is not utilized, additional wildlife corridors, including escape corridors, may be required in areas prone to grassfires or flooding. Critical electrical and communications equipment may be fenced with chain-link fence topped with barbed wire when such measures are deemed necessary to ensure public safety and provide additional security for the equipment. Unless waived by the property owner, a 25-foot-deep buffer area shall be provided and maintained along property lines between the systems and adjoining non-participating residential properties, or along the Site Area fencing for participating residential properties, for the purpose of screening the residential portion of the property. The buffer may include a combination of berms, fences, and/or vegetation and may occur within the required setbacks on the facility property. Perimeter fencing shall incorporate appropriate safety signage, at a minimum spacing of every 500 feet.

All solar panels must be constructed to minimize glare or reflection onto adjacent properties and adjacent roadways and must not interfere with traffic, including air traffic, or create a safety hazard as per any Local, State, and Federal laws and regulations. Examples of measures that can be utilized to limit glare include, but are not limited to: textured glass; anti-reflective coatings; screening; distance; or positioning units in a manner that reduces glare.

Solar panels shall not exceed fifteen (15) feet in height, measured when oriented at maximum tilt; exceptions include appurtenant enclosed structures which must comply with the height limit for the zoning district, and the Planning Commission may approve modifications to allow greater height if necessary to accommodate slopes or agrivoltaics, provided the height does not negatively impact nearby land uses or the character of the area.

The ordinance defines Commercial/Utility-Scale Solar Energy Conversion Systems (CSECS) as systems that do not exceed 640 contiguous acres in area occupied by solar modules within 1 mile of each other. It explicitly states that the CSECS Site Area shall be limited to 640 acres as defined by the total occupied space of the solar modules proposed, and not permitted within an adjoining CSECS facility within one mile of the applicant. The size is measured with the panels in their most horizontal position and excludes access drives, batteries, transformers, ancillary structures, or their required setbacks. Limited Scale Solar Energy Conversion Systems (LSECS) have a separate maximum of 20 contiguous acres, but this does not apply to CSECS. The units for the maximum lot size are acres.

The operational noise generated from the solar installation equipment, including inverters, components, and associated ancillary equipment shall not exceed a noise level of 60 decibels (60 dBA) as measured at the property line or 500 feet from an existing residence (building permit plans have been submitted or the residence is on-site at time of conditional use permit approval) with GPS locations. Applicants must submit equipment and component manufacturer noise ratings at the time of application to demonstrate compliance with this maximum permitted noise level. Transformers, inverters, or other sound or vibration-generating equipment must be placed so that low-level recurring ambient noise does not exceed this limit. Noise levels can be minimized with type of equipment or placement interior to the site, shielded by solar panels and/or noise- and vibration-deadening fences, landscape, or other efforts.

Unless waived by the property owner, a 25-foot-deep buffer area shall be provided, and maintained, along property lines between the systems and adjoining non-participating residential properties, or along the Site Area fencing for participating residential properties, for the purpose of screening the residential portion of the property. The buffer may include a combination of berms, fences, and/or vegetation and may occur within the required setbacks on the facility property.

Temporary construction barriers shall be installed along the perimeter of the drip-line of a protected stand of mature trees, or 200 feet from the historic trail, or at the boundary of other protected environmentally sensitive lands. This fencing is to be signed with the following requirement: ‘Grading, vehicles, equipment, or the storage of materials is not permitted beyond the construction fence line.’ This fencing must remain in place until construction is complete.

The ordinance requires that Commercial/Utility-Scale Solar Energy Conversion Systems (CSECS) utilize existing terrain, vegetation, and structures to screen the project from off-site view to the extent possible, with additional screening required if this is not possible. A 25-foot-deep buffer area shall be provided and maintained along property lines between the systems and adjoining non-participating residential properties, or along the Site Area fencing for participating residential properties, for the purpose of screening the residential portion of the property. The buffer may include a combination of berms, fences, and/or vegetation and may occur within the required setbacks on the facility property. A landscaping plan detailing all proposed changes to the landscape of the site required to accommodate buffering or screening from adjacent properties must be submitted, including installation, establishment, and maintenance of buffering or screening landscaping. Wildlife-friendly fencing such as barb-wire fence with smooth wires or woven wire shall be used where possible, and wildlife corridors shall be provided as determined necessary. Vegetation under and around solar panels must be planted and maintained in perennial vegetated ground cover or agricultural plants to prevent erosion and runoff, with clearing of natural vegetation limited to what is necessary. These requirements apply explicitly to CSECS and are part of the conditional use permit standards.

Perimeter fencing shall incorporate appropriate safety signage, at a minimum spacing of every 500 feet. Signage, including addresses for each fenced area, shall be provided as required by the Emergency 911 dispatch.

The ordinance explicitly enacts soil, erosion, and sediment control requirements for Commercial/Utility-Scale Solar Energy Conversion Systems (CSECS). It requires that "all grading and construction activities shall preserve existing topsoil," with "topsoil... stockpiled on the site" and "redistributed uniformly on the surface of all areas to be vegetated." Grading on Capability Class 3 or above soils "shall be limited to maintain the natural topography" and "shall not exceed 5% of the site area unless a modification is granted by the Planning Commission." The system must have "ground around and under solar panels/arrays and in designated buffer areas... planted and maintained in perennial vegetated ground cover or agricultural plants that are managed to prevent erosion and runoff." A "stormwater management plan with supporting calculations" is required, including "storage and controlled release at points of discharge from the site" if recommended by the County Engineer. A "KDHE-approved SWPPP (Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan)" must be provided. The "vegetation management and agrivoltaic plan" must include "installation, establishment, and maintenance of ground cover and other vegetation to minimize erosion, maintain soil health." A "soil sampling plan" is required to characterize soil health and contamination before construction, after construction, prior to decommissioning, and following reclamation, with remediation plans if contamination occurs. These requirements apply to CSECS projects defined as solar farms up to 640 acres intended for electricity sales and connected to larger electrical networks. The ordinance also provides for modifications to grading limits and other standards upon approval. Smaller or personal solar systems are exempt from these standards.

The solar panels/array and appurtenant structures shall be located a minimum of 5280 feet from any existing residence (building permit plans have been submitted or the residence is on-site at time of conditional use permit approval), as measured from the dwelling, unless a lesser setback is agreed to by the owner of the residence. Buffering or screening landscaping, fencing, agricultural uses, and access drives may be within this setback. Written evidence of the setback agreements, including any additional landscaping, shall be provided to the Planning Office as part of the conditional use permit application and, with the approval of the conditional use permit, shall be filed with the Register of Deeds by Developer.

The ordinance explicitly requires visual impact assessment for Commercial/Utility-Scale Solar Energy Conversion Systems (CSECS) as part of the conditional use permit application. Key issues to be evaluated include 'Visual impact as provided for in the Comprehensive Plan' (12.16.04). The system must 'Utilize existing terrain, vegetation, and structures to screen the project from off-site view to the extent possible. If this is not possible, additional screening may be required' (12.16.05). A landscaping plan is required detailing 'installation, establishment, and maintenance of buffering or screening landscaping' designed to 'buffer the view of the facility from the residence and the residential portion of the property' (12.16.06). Lighting must be limited to 'mitigate visual impacts' with specific height and shielding requirements. Public outreach and detailed site plans showing existing and proposed conditions, including vegetation and topography, are also required to support the assessment of visual impacts. These requirements apply specifically to CSECS and are part of the conditional use permit process.

summary: Section III-D.6.pp.(6)(z) requires Applicant to provide a SECS site and facility decommissioning and reclamation plan which "indicates the planned life of the SECS and the means by which the facility and its site will be decommissioned and reclaimed at the end of the SECS's life." The plan "shall be updated every five (5) years until site decommissioning and reclamation is complete" and "shall provide that, at the end of the project's life, or any component of a SECS, all, or the appropriate portion, of the site’s equipment and access roads shall be removed from the site and the site shall be returned to original condition, or restored to such condition as to allow a Use compatible with surrounding Uses as determined by the Planning Department, or to such condition as agreed to by the landowner." The landowner may choose to have access roads left intact. Section III-D.6.pp.(6)(aa) further requires the decommissioning plan to include: financial assurance covering the full estimated cost without regard to salvage value, recalculated every five years; notification to the governing body of ownership changes; continuity of financial assurance binding on new owners; estimated dates for cessation of power generation and decommissioning timelines; notification to the governing body at key stages; removal of any SECS or portion thereof not in service for six months (with exceptions); removal of all equipment, structures, panels, fencing, and cables within twelve months after cessation of power generation (except items four feet or more below grade if permitted by the landowner); regrading and reseeding to natural condition within twelve months; and required groundwater and soil testing. These requirements apply to Large-Scale SECS, defined as having a Project Area of fifty (50) acres or more. Other SECS classifications include Small-Scale (10 acres or less) and Medium-Scale (more than 10 but less than 50 acres).

The ordinance defines Large-Scale SECS as having a Project Area of fifty (50) acres or more. It requires that the concept plan submitted by the Applicant include 'the location of proposed fencing' (Sec. III-D.6.pp.(5)(a)(3)). Furthermore, it mandates that 'All SECS Structures, with the exception of any photovoltaic panels, shall be enclosed by security fencing at least 8 feet in height to restrict unauthorized access' (Sec. III-D.6.pp.(6)(q)). Other classifications include Small-Scale SECS (Project Area of ten (10) acres or less) and Medium-Scale SECS (Project Area of more than ten (10) acres but less than fifty (50) acres), with the fencing requirement applying to all SECS structures except photovoltaic panels.

Section III-D.6.pp.(6)(h) requires Applicant to provide a Solar Glare Hazard Analysis utilizing the latest version of the Solar Glare Hazard Analysis Tool (SGHAT), or its equivalent, to evaluate the solar glare aviation hazard. The full report must be submitted at least 30 days before the public hearing for Conditional Use approval. If solar glare is predicted, Applicant shall provide mitigation measures including textured glass, anti-reflective coatings, Screening, distance, and angling of solar PV modules/panels to reduce glare to surrounding land uses of non-participating property owners. Additionally, subsection (x) states: 'No SECS shall be placed such that concentrated solar glare casts onto adjacent properties or roadways.' These requirements apply to all SECS, including Large-Scale SECS, which are defined as having a Project Area of fifty (50) acres or more. Other SECS classifications include Small-Scale SECS (10 acres or less) and Medium-Scale SECS (more than 10 acres but less than 50 acres).

The SECS shall not exceed twenty-five feet (25’) in height; provided, however, said height restriction shall not apply to substation facilities or transmission lines. Additionally, the maximum height of the lowest edge of any photovoltaic panel shall not exceed ten feet (10’).

No SECS Project Area shall exceed fifteen-hundred (1500) acres. Large-Scale SECS are defined as having a Project Area of fifty (50) acres or more. Other classifications include Small-Scale SECS (10 acres or less) and Medium-Scale SECS (more than 10 acres but less than 50 acres). The maximum area limit of 1500 acres applies to all SECS Project Areas, including Large-Scale SECS. The unit of measurement for the maximum size is acres.

A Large-Scale SECS shall have a Project Area of fifty (50) acres or more. Other classifications include Small-Scale SECS with a Project Area of ten (10) acres or less, and Medium-Scale SECS with a Project Area of more than ten (10) acres but less than fifty (50) acres. The unit for the Project Area is acres.

No SECS Project Area boundary shall be nearer than two (2) miles to any other SECS Project Area boundary. This distance shall be measured in a straight line from the closest Project Area boundary of one SECS to the nearest proposed Project Area boundary of any other SECS. This regulation shall not apply to any Small-Scale SECS that does not connect to the private transmission lines or collection lines of any other SECS, nor shall the two (2) mile calculation include any such Small-Scale SECS's that do not connect to the private transmission lines or collection lines of any other SECS. Large-Scale SECS are defined as those with a Project Area of fifty (50) acres or more, so this minimum separation distance applies to them. The units are miles as explicitly stated in the text.

All SECS Structures shall be Setback at least one-hundred feet (100’) from the project boundary lines, adjacent public road Section Lines or rights of way (whichever provides a greater setback) and private road rights of way. This applies to Large-Scale SECS as defined by having a Project Area of fifty (50) acres or more. No multiplier based on structure height is mentioned. Other setbacks include a 250 feet setback from any Dwelling Unit not included in the Facility Area, but dwellings are not equivalent to property lines unless explicitly stated.

All SECS Structures shall be Setback at least one-hundred feet (100’) from the project boundary lines, adjacent public road Section Lines or rights of way (whichever provides a greater setback) and private road rights of way. Additional Setbacks may be required to mitigate site specific issues or to provide for access, road or commercial corridors.

The ordinance requires that for Large-Scale SECS (Project Area of fifty (50) acres or more), the concept plan must include "the location and nature of proposed buffers and Screening elements, including vegetative and constructed buffers, and existing landforms... intended to be used as a buffer or Screening." Additionally, "the SECS should be located to make maximum use of existing terrain, vegetation and Structures to Screen the SECS from offsite views." Landscaping and/or Screening "may be required during review and approval to help screen the SECS." Screening "shall be provided along any side or rear property line when the SECS is located Adjacent to a Dwelling Unit." Other requirements for Large-Scale SECS include submission of a concept plan, detailed project narrative, grading plan, landscape plan, visual impact analysis, community impact assessment, and various other plans and assessments as part of the Conditional Use approval process.

Section (6)(t) states: 'There shall be no signage allowed on the SECS with the exception of safety and emergency contact Signs, warning Signs, directional or project identification Signs. All SECS’s shall install Signs warning that solar and other electrical equipment is located on the property. Additionally, Signs providing a twenty-four (24) hour emergency contact phone number shall also be installed. The required signage shall be installed on private property at all driveway access points to the SECS.' This applies to all SECS, including Large-Scale SECS, which are defined as having a Project Area of fifty (50) acres or more. Other signage is prohibited except for the specified types.

Section III-D.6.pp.(6)(j) requires Applicant to provide information that "addresses: storm water drainage, soil erosion, sediment control, and will detail how same will be addressed, prevented or enhanced by grading, re-vegetation or other standard construction practices in accordance with the reclamation recommendations of the Sedgwick County Department of Environmental Resources." Additionally, section III-D.6.pp.(5)(c) requires submission of a draft grading plan including "existing and proposed contours," "locations and amount of topsoil to be stripped and stockpiled onsite," "percent of the site to be graded," and "an earthwork balance designed to limit the import or export of soil." The ordinance defines Large-Scale SECS as having a Project Area of fifty (50) acres or more and applies these requirements to all SECS, including Large-Scale SECS. Other scale classifications include Small-Scale SECS (10 acres or less) and Medium-Scale SECS (more than 10 acres but less than 50 acres).
All SECS Structures, including any photovoltaic panels or any BESS, shall be located at least two-hundred fifty feet (250') from any Dwelling Unit not included in the Facility Area.

Large-Scale SECS (Project Area of fifty (50) acres or more) are subject to a visual impact analysis requirement as part of the Conditional Use approval process. The applicant "shall submit a visual impact analysis demonstrating project siting and proposed mitigation, if necessary, so that the proposed facility minimizes impacts on the visual character, viewsheds, and/or vistas of the City or County." The analysis must include "accurate, to scale, photographic simulations showing the relationship of the SECS and its associated equipment and development to its surroundings," from locations such as property lines, roadways, and scenic viewsheds/vistas as deemed necessary by the Zoning Administrator. The number and perspectives of simulations are "as reasonably established by the Zoning Administrator." Visual representations must be in color and include "actual pre-construction photographs and accurate post-construction simulations of the height and breadth of the facility," including existing and proposed buildings and tree coverage. Other SECS classifications include Small-Scale SECS (Project Area of ten (10) acres or less) and Medium-Scale SECS (Project Area of more than ten (10) acres but less than fifty (50) acres), with the visual impact analysis requirement applying to both Medium-Scale and Large-Scale SECS. All Renewable Energy Systems are considered Conditional Uses and subject to review procedures.

The ordinance requires a "decommission plan and land reclamation detailing recovery or removal of structures and underground installation specific to the proposed method of assurance regarding maintenance and repair to public roads, bridges or culverts during decommission process" for Commercial Solar Energy Conversion Systems (CSECS). Additional requirements for CSECS include: height not exceeding thirty-five (35’) feet (except substations or transmission lines), perimeter fencing at least 8 feet (8’) tall, setbacks of at least forty feet (40’) from project boundary lines and public rights-of-way, and two hundred fifty feet (250’) from non-participating landowners’ residential structures, prohibition of concentrated solar glare onto adjacent property or roadways, and underground installation of electrical lines except for connections to transmission lines or culturally sensitive areas.

Commercial Solar Energy Collection System Facilities shall meet the following requirements: Shall be enclosed by perimeter fencing at least 8 feet (8’) tall to restrict unauthorized access. No outdoor storage of any material or equipment is permitted except for construction equipment and material during construction.

summary: The ordinance applies to Commercial Solar Energy Collection System Facilities (CSECS) and includes a glare restriction: 'No CSECS shall be placed such that concentrated solar glare casts onto adjacent property or roadways.' Other relevant requirements include height limits ('Shall not exceed thirty-five (35’) feet in height; provided, however, said height restriction shall not apply to substation facilities or transmission lines'), perimeter fencing ('Shall be enclosed by perimeter fencing at least 8 feet (8’) tall'), setback requirements ('setback from the project boundary lines and public rights-of-way at least forty feet (40’)' and 'set back two hundred fifty feet (250’) as measured from the nearest portion of any existing and non-participation landowners’ residential structures'), underground electrical lines except for certain exceptions, and various development plan and safety documentation requirements.

Commercial Solar Energy Collection System Facilities shall meet the following requirements. 1. Shall not exceed thirty-five (35’) feet in height; provided, however, said height restriction shall not apply to substation facilities or transmission lines.

All CSECS structures shall be setback from the project boundary lines and public rights-of-way at least forty feet (40’). Additionally, all CSECS structures shall be set back two hundred fifty feet (250’) as measured from the nearest portion of any existing and non-participation landowners’ residential structures at the time of application. (Note: setbacks from residential structures are not equivalent to property or parcel lines.)

summary: The Development Plan Required by the Regulations for Commercial Solar Energy Conversion Systems (CSECS) shall include "stormwater management and erosion control including 100-year floodplain boundaries." Additional requirements include providing "a legal description of the perimeter boundaries," project details such as "location of the project, scale and north arrow, acreage of the site," and other operational and safety information. CSECS facilities "shall not exceed thirty-five (35’) feet in height" (except substations or transmission lines), "shall be enclosed by perimeter fencing at least 8 feet (8’) tall," and have setback requirements of "at least forty feet (40’)" from project boundaries and public rights-of-way, and "two hundred fifty feet (250’)" from non-participating landowners’ residences. Electrical lines must be installed underground except in certain cases. The plan must also include a "Plan for ongoing dust and weed control" and a "decommission plan and land reclamation."

All CSECS structures shall be set back two hundred fifty feet (250’) as measured from the nearest portion of any existing and non-participation landowners’ residential structures at the time of application. Additionally, all CSECS structures shall be setback from the project boundary lines and public rights-of-way at least forty feet (40’). The 250 feet setback from residential structures is the most restrictive setback related to occupied dwellings, buildings, structures, and/or residences.

summary: The ordinance requires Commercial Solar Energy Conversion Systems (CSECS) to provide "an accurate computer-generated visual simulation from vantage points as agreed by the developer and Seward County staff" as part of the Development Plan. Other requirements include providing detailed project information, such as "solar technology to be used," "approximate number of solar modules/panels," "system mounting," "maximum height of any new utility poles," and "power capacity of the system in both DC and AC watts." Additionally, CSECS must not exceed thirty-five (35’) feet in height (except substations or transmission lines), be enclosed by perimeter fencing at least 8 feet tall, have setbacks of at least forty feet from project boundaries and public rights-of-way, and 250 feet from non-participating landowners’ residences. Electrical lines must be installed underground except in certain cases. The visual simulation requirement explicitly constitutes a visual impact assessment requirement for utility-scale solar energy systems.

Commercial Solar Energy Conversion Systems are "specifically prohibited until June 1, 2028." This prohibition is an active moratorium that applies broadly without conditions or exceptions based on compliance, location, district, prior approvals, or other factors. The ban remains in effect as of December 5, 2025, and will expire on June 1, 2028.

The Woodson County Board of County Commissioners has enacted a moratorium and prohibition on Commercial Renewable Energy Projects in the unincorporated area of Woodson County. Specifically, the resolution directs the suspension of acting on any application for a Conditional Use Permit or permits for the erection and construction of any Commercial Renewable Energy Project (Section 1), prohibits the establishment of any such project (Section 3), and declares such establishment a violation of public interest while the resolution is in effect. No applications for Conditional Use permits shall be set for public hearing prior to 12 months from adoption (Section 2). The moratorium may be extended, terminated earlier, or amended by subsequent resolution (Section 5). The resolution "shall remain in effect until the end of February 2026" (Section 6). There are no stated conditions or exceptions limiting the prohibition to specific areas, prior approvals, or compliance status. The moratorium is currently in effect as of December 5, 2025.

Section 2, subsection F requires a decommissioning plan that "describes the manner in which the CSES will be decommissioned and the site restored," prepared by a third-party engineer licensed in Kentucky and inclusive of the estimated cost of removal net of salvage value. The decommissioning estimate must be updated every five years. During the second year of operations, a surety bond or decommissioning security must be issued to the Ballard County Fiscal Court for the cost of removal net of salvage value. The bond or security must cover decommissioning costs after the end of use and be increased if the estimate changes. "All decommissioning shall be in accordance with Kentucky state law, pursuant to 2023 HB 4." Decommissioning must occur "within twelve (12) months of the cessation of energy generation by the CSES."

summary: Commercial Solar Energy Systems (CSES), including those intended for selling electric energy, are defined as ground-mounted systems occupying ten (10) or more contiguous acres. This sets a minimum parcel size of 10 acres for such commercial solar energy systems. The unit is explicitly stated as acres in the definition section.

The CSES facility shall comply with the following setback requirements, as measured between the Setback Feature and the CSES footprint: Adjoining properties line(*) 100 feet. Setbacks are not required where the property line is shared by two or more participating landowners. The setback provisions above can be waived in writing by the adjacent property owner to whom the property line or residence setback is applicable. Other setback distances include 250 feet from dwellings not owned by the applicant, 250 feet from churches, schools, business parks not located on project properties, 1,000 feet from centers of certain unincorporated town limits, and 1,500 feet from city limits, but these relate to structures or municipal boundaries rather than property lines or parcels.

The ordinance specifies setback distances from roadways (primary and secondary) for Commercial Solar Energy Systems (CSES) including Siting Board Regulated systems (≥ 10 MW). Specifically, 'Roadways (primary and secondary) Primary: 50-feet from centerline Secondary-25-feet- secondary from c/1'. The most restrictive setback from roads is 50 feet from the centerline of primary roadways. Other setback options include 25 feet from the centerline of secondary roadways.

The CSES facility shall comply with the following setback requirements, as measured between the Setback Feature and the CSES footprint: A. Dwelling not owned by CSES applicant/owner or participating landowner in the project: 250 feet. B. Church, school, schoolyard, business, park (not located on project properties): 250 feet. Other setback options include: C. Center of unincorporated town limits: 1,000 feet; D. City limits: 1,500 feet; E. Downstream public works supply surface intake: 1,000 feet; F. Roadways: Primary 50 feet from centerline, Secondary 25 feet from centerline; G. Adjoining property line: 100 feet. Setbacks can be waived in writing by the adjacent property owner. These setbacks apply to Commercial Solar Energy Systems (CSES) defined as systems occupying ten or more contiguous acres and intended for selling electricity, consistent with Siting Board Regulated CSES (≥ 10 MW).

Decommissioning: A decommissioning plan shall be submitted at the time of either the submittal of a Conditional Use Permit application or a Site Plan application, whichever is first. Other than as specified by the Board of Adjustment or other authority having jurisdiction, decommissioning shall begin no later than six (6) months after a ground mounted solar energy system has ceased to generate electricity or thermal energy. All structures and facilities associated with the solar energy system, including any underground wiring, conduits, equipment, shall be removed within six (6) months from the beginning of the decommissioning operation. In the City of Florence, a decommissioning plan or statement shall be submitted with all Conditional Use Permit applications, Site Plan applications, and Zoning Permit applications. The same timing and removal requirements apply. Tier 2 or Tier 3 solar energy systems shall follow the Site Plan procedures identified in ARTICLE 30. Other options include Integrated and roof mounted solar energy systems and Tier 1 solar energy systems, which follow different permitting procedures.

For Tier 3 solar energy systems, fencing requirements include: 'All fences in the front yard, as measured from the front lot line to the closest solar array, shall meet the requirements of SECTION 3655.D.'; 'Fences used as security shall have a maximum height of eight (8) feet and shall not be placed along the perimeter of the property.'; and 'All other fencing shall meet the requirements of SECTION 3655.' These requirements apply to both Unincorporated Boone County and the City of Florence. No alternative fencing options or conditions are provided beyond these stated requirements.

For ground mounted solar energy systems, the maximum height for Tier 2 and Tier 3 solar energy systems is explicitly limited to 20 feet, measured from the average grade below each solar panel to the top of each solar panel. This applies in both Unincorporated Boone County and the City of Florence. Other height limits mentioned include 10 feet maximum for Tier 1 systems adjoining residential or agriculturally zoned property, and 20 feet maximum for Tier 1 systems not adjoining such properties, but these do not apply to Tier 3 systems.

The footprint of a Tier 2 or Tier 3 solar energy system shall be set back a minimum of two hundred (200) feet from an adjoining property that is zoned with an agricultural, recreation, conservation, residential, or public facility district. Other setback options include: 100 feet from an adjoining property zoned business, employment, airport, small community, or special study district; 50 feet from the right-of-way line of any public street; and 500 feet from a residential or school building other than those on the property where the system is located.

summary: The footprint of a Tier 2 or Tier 3 solar energy system shall be set back a minimum of fifty (50) feet from the right-of-way line of any public street. Other setback options include: 200 feet from adjoining property zoned agricultural, recreation, conservation, residential, or public facility district; 100 feet from adjoining property zoned business, employment, airport, small community, or special study district; and 500 feet from a residential or school building not on the property where the system is located.

The ordinance requires that "The perimeter of the footprint of a Tier 2 or Tier 3 solar energy system shall be provided with a Buffer Yard C." Additionally, "Any tree that is planted in the required Buffer Yard shall have a minimum height of six (6) feet when planted and shall have an expected mature growth height of a minimum of fifteen (15) feet." These requirements apply explicitly to Tier 3 solar energy systems in both Unincorporated Boone County and the City of Florence. No other screening or vegetative buffer options or conditions are provided for Tier 3 systems in the text.

For Tier 2 and Tier 3 ground mounted solar energy systems, "Compaction of soils associated with the location of roads and installation staging areas... shall be minimized to the extent possible." Additionally, "all temporary roads shall be removed and all disturbed areas shall be graded and reseeded with short-term cover crops and sustainable, non-weed native vegetation in order to establish an effective ground cover and to minimize erosion and sedimentation." These requirements apply in Agricultural districts upon completion of construction and installation. Other options or conditions are not provided for soil, erosion, or sediment control in the text.

Other setback options include 200 feet from adjoining properties zoned agricultural, recreation, conservation, residential, or public facility districts, and 100 feet from adjoining properties zoned business, employment, airport, small community, or special study districts, but the 500 feet setback from residential or school buildings is the most restrictive for occupied dwellings or residences.

summary: Merchant Electric Generating Facilities (≥ 10 megawatts) must submit a decommissioning plan that meets the requirements of KRS 278.706(2)(m). Other specific use standards include location restrictions to Light Industrial (LI), Heavy Industrial (HI), or Industrial Business Development (IBD) Districts; a maximum total allowable coverage of 2,000 acres in Boyle County; setbacks of at least 500 feet from residential districts, uses, or structures; and a minimum 50-foot landscape buffer along rights-of-way and adjacent to residential land uses. Facilities must also comply with local, state, and federal requirements, submit applicable construction-related permits, and ensure fire protection standards are met either through public water lines and hydrants or an approved alternative fire protection plan.

Merchant Electric Generating Facilities are limited to a total maximum allowable coverage of 2,000 acres in Boyle County. Once this total allowable acreage has been met, no further requests for additional Merchant Electric Generating Facilities shall be considered, and there shall be no variance from this limit. The unit for this maximum lot size is explicitly stated as acres.

summary: All Merchant Electric Generating Facilities shall be setback a minimum of 500 feet from public rights-of-way. Additionally, a minimum landscape buffer width of 50 feet is required along all rights-of-way. Loading and unloading areas must be oriented away from public streets. Facility entrances must be located on a public street with a minimum pavement width of at least 18 feet.

All Merchant Electric Generating Facilities shall comply with the landscape requirements set forth in Article 4, Section 4.6.8.D. The minimum landscape buffer width for Merchant Electric Generating Facilities shall be 50 feet along all rights-of-way and adjacent to other residential land uses.

Merchant Electric Generating Facilities must be located in Light Industrial (LI), Heavy Industrial (HI) or Industrial Business Development (IBD) District. A Site Development Plan Application and Approval is required for any proposed Merchant Electric Generating Facilities. Facilities must adhere to specific use standards including setbacks of at least 500 feet from residential districts and structures, a maximum total coverage of 2,000 acres in Boyle County, compliance with local, state and federal requirements, and submission of a decommissioning plan. Zoning Permit Applications are not required, but all applicable construction-related permits must be submitted to the Planning Commission prior to construction commencement.

All structures shall be at least 500 feet from any residential district, adjacent residential use or adjacent residential structure. summary: The 2025 Ordinance applies to Large Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems (SES), defined as those with a footprint of more than forty (40) acres or any non-exempt SES that constitutes a Merchant Electric Generating Facility. It requires a decommissioning plan prepared by a registered engineer, updated not less than once every three (3) years, including: the anticipated life of the project and defined conditions upon which decommissioning will be initiated; the estimated decommissioning costs including removal of the SES and restoration of the property; the manner and timetable for decommissioning; component disposal plans; and any contracts regarding decommissioning. The company must provide a surety instrument sufficient to cover decommissioning costs, continuously maintained until full decommissioning. Decommissioning must begin no later than twelve (12) months after the SES ceases to generate energy, with removal of all structures within six (6) months. Materials shall be recycled or reused to the extent reasonably practicable, and disturbed areas reclaimed, revegetated, and restored. Failure to comply allows the County to claim against the surety and take legal action. The ordinance excludes Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, Small-Scale SES, Intermediate Scale SES with approved site plans, and Large Scale SES with construction begun prior to the ordinance's effective date under certain conditions.

The 2025 Ordinance applies to Large Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems (SES), defined as systems with a footprint of more than forty (40) acres or any merchant electric generating facility (10 MW or more). It requires that "Access to the site must be controlled by a fence of at least eight (8) feet in height with a vegetative landscape buffer provided between the fencing and the property line." The fence must be equipped with screening consisting of "an eight (8) foot tall fence and a double row of staggered evergreen trees (minimum five (5) feet in height at planting and maturing to a minimum of fifteen (15) feet in height);" with trees planted exterior to the fence and setback no less than fifteen (15) feet from any property line. Screening must achieve "an opacity of 90% to a height of no less than eight (8) feet within three (3) years of planting" and be maintained until decommissioning is complete. The ordinance also prohibits barbed wire or sharp pointed fences along boundaries adjoining residential properties in the 2022 Ordinance, which was repealed but had similar fencing requirements for Level 3 SES (the largest category in that ordinance). Other SES categories include Level 1 (up to 5 acres, permitted use), Level 2 (intermediate size), and Level 3 (largest, conditional use requiring approval). The 2025 Ordinance supersedes the 2022 Ordinance and applies specifically to Large Scale SES, excluding Integrated, Rooftop, Small-Scale, and Intermediate Scale SES with approved site plans or prior construction. The fencing requirements are part of the "Perimeter Access and Screening" standards.

The 2022 Ordinance explicitly states: 'The height of any ground mounted SES shall not exceed twenty-five (25) feet as measured from the highest natural grade below each solar panel (excludes utility poles, substations and antennas constructed for the project).' This applies to Level 3 SES, which are conditional uses in Agricultural or Commercial/Heavy Industrial Zones and require approval by the Breckinridge County Fiscal Court. The 2025 Ordinance repealed the 2022 Ordinance but does not provide any explicit maximum structure height restriction. Therefore, the 25 feet limit from the 2022 Ordinance is the only explicit maximum height restriction for Large Scale Ground Mounted SES. The units are feet.

The 2025 Ordinance requires that the SES footprint shall be setback no less than 1,000 feet from any non-participating property line. Other setback distances include 1,000 feet from any right-of-way for a publicly maintained roadway or rail-line, and no less than 2,000 feet from any church, school, hospital, residential building or any incorporated city limit. The ordinance also allows the Breckinridge County Fiscal Court to require more or less stringent setbacks on a case-by-case basis.

The SES footprint shall be setback no less than 1,000 feet from any right-of-way for a publicly maintained roadway or rail-line. This applies to Large Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems (SES) as defined in the ordinance. Other setbacks include 1,000 feet from any non-participating property line and 2,000 feet from any church, school, hospital, residential building or any incorporated city limit. The ordinance does not specify any height-based multiplier for setbacks from roads.

The 2025 Ordinance applies to Large Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems (SES), defined as systems with a footprint of more than forty (40) acres or any merchant electric generating facility subject to review and approval by the Kentucky State Board on Electric Generation and Transmission Siting. It requires that "Access to the site must be controlled by a fence of at least eight (8) feet in height with a vegetative landscape buffer provided between the fencing and the property line." Screening must consist of "an eight (8) foot tall fence and a double row of staggered evergreen trees (minimum five (5) feet in height at planting and maturing to a minimum of fifteen (15) feet in height);" the trees "shall be planted exterior to the fence and shall be setback no less than fifteen (15) feet from any property line;" and "Screening shall achieve an opacity of 90% to a height of no less than eight (8) feet within three (3) years of planting." Screening must be installed within 180 days of the start of physical construction and maintained until decommissioning is complete, with replacement of unhealthy or dead plantings within ninety (90) days. The ordinance also specifies setback requirements and other conditions. The ordinance does not apply to Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, Small-Scale SES, Intermediate Scale SES with an approved site plan, or Large Scale SES where physical construction began prior to the effective date and meets certain conditions.

The 2022 Ordinance (Exhibit 1) explicitly states in section 4.3.7.3.d: 'There shall be no signs permitted except those displaying emergency information, owner contact information, warning or safety instructions exceed five (5) square feet in area.' This applies to Level 3 SES, which are large-scale systems requiring approval by the Breckinridge County Fiscal Court. The 2025 Ordinance (Exhibit 2), which applies to Large Scale SES defined as 'a ground mounted SES with a footprint of more than forty (40) acres' or 'any non-exempt SES that... constitutes a Merchant Electric Generating Facility,' includes detailed requirements for setbacks, screening, lighting, decommissioning, and site plan approval but does not explicitly mention signage requirements.

The 2025 Ordinance applies to Large Scale SES, defined as ground mounted solar energy systems with a footprint of more than forty (40) acres or any merchant electric generating facility of 10 MW or more. It requires Fiscal Court approval prior to construction, including "approval of a soil erosion plan showing compliance with all existing federal, state, and local environmental restrictions. Said plan is to be reviewed by NRCS to determine compliance." The ordinance excludes Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, Small-Scale SES, Intermediate Scale SES with an approved site plan, and Large Scale SES with physical construction begun prior to the ordinance's effective date under certain conditions. Other requirements include setbacks, screening, lighting, decommissioning plans, and surety instruments.

Level 2 and 3 SES, as set forth below, shall be a conditional use in all Agricultural or Commercial/Heavy Industrial Zones. Those seeking a permit for Level 3 SES must be granted approval by a majority vote of Breckinridge County Fiscal Court. Level 1 Solar Energy Systems that comply with the requirements of Section 4.3.7 shall be allowed in all zoning districts. The ordinance applies to Large Scale SES facilities in all unincorporated areas of Breckinridge County, Kentucky, excluding Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, Small-Scale SES, Intermediate Scale SES with approved site plan, and Large Scale SES with prior construction begun before the ordinance effective date under certain conditions.

The 2025 Ordinance requires that 'The SES footprint shall be setback no less than ... 2,000 feet from any church, school, hospital, residential building or any incorporated city limit.' This is the most restrictive setback distance directly pertaining to non-participating occupied dwellings, buildings, structures, and/or residences for Large Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems. The 2022 Ordinance had a less restrictive setback of 300 feet from any residential structure, nursing home, church, or school for Level 3 SES. The 2025 Ordinance repealed the 2022 Ordinance and applies to Large Scale SES, defined as ground mounted SES with a footprint of more than forty (40) acres or merchant electric generating facilities (10 MW or more).

The ordinance explicitly enacts decommissioning requirements for Large-Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems (Large-Scale SES). It requires "a decommissioning plan, prepared by a registered professional engineer at the expense of the applicant, and updated not less than once every five (5) years," containing details such as "the anticipated life of the project and defined conditions upon which decommissioning will be initiated," "the estimated decommissioning costs," "the manner in which the project will be decommissioned," and "a copy of any contract containing specific agreements regarding decommissioning." The applicant must also provide "a surety instrument in an amount and form acceptable to the Calloway County Judge Executive, upon recommendation of the Fiscal Court, sufficient to cover the costs of decommissioning the SES." The timeline mandates that "the applicant shall begin decommissioning no later than twelve (12) months after an Intermediate-Scale SES or Large-Scale SES has ceased to generate electricity or thermal energy," with removal of all structures within six months. Failure to comply allows the County to "invoke the surety instrument" and take legal actions, including license revocation. The ordinance applies to Intermediate-Scale SES and Large-Scale SES, but not to Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, Small-Scale SES, or projects with physical construction begun prior to the ordinance's effective date (with conditions).

Section 4.A.2 of the ordinance states: 'Access to the site must be controlled by a fence of at least eight (8) feet in height with a vegetative landscape buffer provided between the fencing and the property line. The fence shall be equipped with screening to help shield the facilities and equipment from view. Screening shall consist of: An eight (8) foot tall fence and a double row of staggered evergreen trees (minimum five (5) feet in height at planting and maturing to a minimum of fifteen (15) feet in height); Evergreen trees shall be planted exterior to the fence and shall be setback no less than fifteen (15) feet from any property line; Screening shall achieve an opacity of 90% to a height of no less than eight (8) feet within three (3) years of planting; Screening shall be installed within 180 days of the start of physical construction and shall be maintained until the decommissioning of the SES is completed; and All unhealthy, dead, or noncompliant plantings shall be repaired or replaced within ninety (90) days of such occurrence.' These fencing requirements apply to Intermediate-Scale SES and Large-Scale SES as defined in the ordinance. Other types of SES such as Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, and Small-Scale SES are excluded from the ordinance's requirements. Additionally, Intermediate-Scale SES and Large-Scale SES where physical construction began prior to the effective date of this ordinance are exempt provided construction is completed within two years and the footprint is not enlarged.

The SES footprint shall be setback no less than 2,000 feet from any non-participating property line. (Section 4.A.1) This setback is defined as the minimum distance measured from the property line of a non-participating property to the nearest portion of an SES Footprint or other regulated SES feature, and must be contained within the boundary of a participating property. Other setback references include rights-of-way for publicly maintained roadways or rail-lines, but these are excluded from this summary as per instructions.

The SES footprint shall be setback no less than 2,000 feet from any non-participating property line and any right-of-way for a publicly maintained roadway or rail-line. This applies to Intermediate-Scale SES and Large-Scale SES, which includes Large-Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems with a footprint of more than forty (40) acres or those constituting a Merchant Electric Generating Facility.

The SES footprint shall be setback no less than 2,000 feet from any non-participating property line and any right-of-way for a publicly maintained roadway or rail-line. This setback applies to Intermediate-Scale SES and Large-Scale SES. No multiplier based on structure height is mentioned. The setback is a fixed distance requirement.

Section 4.A.2 of the ordinance requires that "Access to the site must be controlled by a fence of at least eight (8) feet in height with a vegetative landscape buffer provided between the fencing and the property line." The screening shall consist of "An eight (8) foot tall fence and a double row of staggered evergreen trees (minimum five (5) feet in height at planting and maturing to a minimum of fifteen (15) feet in height);" with the evergreen trees "planted exterior to the fence and shall be setback no less than fifteen (15) feet from any property line;" and the screening "shall achieve an opacity of 90% to a height of no less than eight (8) feet within three (3) years of planting;" Screening "shall be installed within 180 days of the start of physical construction and shall be maintained until the decommissioning of the SES is completed;" and "All unhealthy, dead, or noncompliant plantings shall be repaired or replaced within ninety (90) days of such occurrence." These requirements apply to Intermediate-Scale SES and Large-Scale SES, which includes "a Ground Mounted SES with a footprint of more than forty (40) acres" or any SES that "constitutes a Merchant Electric Generating Facility" as defined. The ordinance also includes other provisions such as setbacks, lighting, decommissioning plans, and surety instruments, but these are not directly related to vegetative buffer or screening requirements.

The ordinance requires a decommissioning plan for Large-Scale SES, prepared by a registered professional engineer, including "the estimated cost for removal of the SES facility, the costs for restoring the land to its original condition, including soils," and "the revegetation and restoration of the property to its original condition." It mandates that "disturbed areas shall be reclaimed, revegetated, and restored to like-kind soil quality and overall condition as the areas were prior to the installation of the Intermediate or Large-Scale SES." The decommissioning plan must be updated every five years and a surety instrument maintained to cover decommissioning costs. Failure to comply allows the County to invoke the surety instrument and take legal action. Other requirements include setbacks, fencing, screening, lighting, and licensing procedures, but these do not explicitly address soil, erosion, or sediment control. The ordinance applies to Intermediate-Scale and Large-Scale SES, excluding Integrated, Rooftop, Small-Scale SES, and projects with physical construction begun prior to the ordinance effective date (with conditions).

Section 156.07 DECOMMISSIONING REQUIREMENTS AND SURETY explicitly requires that when a facility ceases to be operational for nine months, decommissioning shall be enforced unless the owner/operator is diligently working to restore operation. The owner/operator must return the land to its original natural state, remove all surface and subsurface materials, notify the power company, and recycle materials to the greatest extent possible. Decommissioning must be completed within six months after notice of inactivity, or the county may remove the facility at the owner's cost. A bond or letter of credit covering the entire estimated cost of decommissioning, determined by an independent licensed engineer, must be posted prior to construction and maintained, with reassessment every three years. Failure to comply results in forfeiture of the bond or letter of credit. Other related requirements include semi-annual activity statements to ensure the facility is producing electricity and specific conditions on the bond or letter of credit provider's rating and non-cancelability.
Facilities shall not be constructed and sited, whether entirely or partially, in the Agricultural Zone in Clark County, Kentucky.

The minimum setback distance of a facility from any property boundary shared with any tract on which no such facility is located shall be at least 2,000 feet. Other setback requirements include a 150 feet setback from any river or stream, but this does not pertain to property lines or parcels. These setback requirements shall also apply to all equipment associated with the facility and shall not be subject to modification by the Board of Adjustments.

The minimum setback distance between a facility and any river or stream is 150 feet. These setback requirements shall also apply to all equipment (electrical or otherwise) associated with and necessary for the operation of a facility. No other setback distances from lakes, reservoirs, or wetlands are specified.

Section 6(i) states: 'upon application and notice, decommissioning shall begin no later than twelve (12) months after a Ground Mounted SES has ceased to generate electricity or thermal energy.' For permitted uses without a conditional use permit, 'all structures and facilities associated with the SES shall be removed within six (6) months of the beginning of decommissioning' and 'the disturbed areas shall be reclaimed, revegetated, and restored.' For Ground Mounted SES allowed under a conditional use permit, decommissioning shall be 'according to the terms of this ordinance and with reference to 6 (j) (1) above.' Section 7(a)(8) requires a decommissioning plan prepared by a registered professional engineer, updated every ten years, including: 'the anticipated life of the project and defined conditions upon which decommissioning will be initiated,' 'the estimated decommissioning cost,' 'the manner in which the project will be decommissioned,' 'the party responsible for decommissioning,' and 'a performance bond, letter of credit, or other financial assurance payable to the Fiscal Court, sufficient to cover the net costs.' These requirements apply to Large Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems, defined as those with a footprint greater than ten (10) acres.

This restriction applies to Large Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems as defined by a footprint greater than ten (10) acres.

Setback provisions cannot be waived by adjacent property owners, are required even where a property line is shared by two or more participating landowners, and may not be waived or reduced regardless of existing or proposed visual screening. Setback requirements may be expanded by the Fiscal Court as a condition of approval for a Conditional Use Permit. Other options include Intermediate SES setbacks of 100 feet from property lines of various uses, and setbacks from the centerline of public roads, but these are not the focus for Large Scale SES.

It also mandates that "Upon completion of construction and installation of the Ground Mounted SES, all temporary roads constructed by the applicant shall be removed, and all disturbed areas shall be graded and reseeded with native vegetation in order to establish an effective ground cover and to minimize erosion and sedimentation." summary: Decommissioning of Level 3 SES shall be as follows: (1) The developer shall post a Surety Bond with the Henderson City-County Planning Commission for the abandonment of the site and in the event the Commission must remove the facility. Abandonment shall be when the SES ceases to transfer energy on a continuous basis for twelve (12) months. The surety bond shall be one (1) percent of the total cost of the installed SES. (2) A decommissioning plan shall be submitted at the time of application by the party responsible for decommissioning and the land owner and must include the following: (1) Defined conditions upon which the decommissioning will be initiated. i.e. there has been no power production for 12 months, the land lease has ended, or succession of use of abandoned facility, etc.; (2) Removal of all non-utility owned equipment, conduit, structures, fencing, roads, and foundations; (3) Restoration of the property to its original condition prior to development of the SES; (4) The time frame for completion of decommissioning activities; (5) the party currently responsible for decommissioning, and; (6) Plans for updating the decommissioning plan. For Level 3 Solar Energy Systems (SES), the ordinance states: 'There shall be no signs permitted on Level 3 SES except those displaying emergency information, owner contact information, warning or safety instructions or signs that are required by a federal, state or local agency. Section 4(b) "Parameter Access and Screening" requires that access to the site be controlled by a fence of at least eight (8) feet in height with a vegetative landscape buffer provided between the fencing and the property line. The fence shall be equipped with screening to help shield the facilities and equipment from view. Screening shall consist of: an eight (8) foot tall fence and double row of staggered evergreen trees (minimum five (5) feet in height at planting and maturing to a minimum of fifteen (15) feet in height); evergreen trees shall be planted exterior to the fence and shall be setback no less than fifteen (15) feet from any property line; screening shall achieve an opacity of 90% to a height of no less than eight (8) feet within three (3) years of planting; screening shall be installed within 180 days of the start of physical construction and shall be maintained until the decommissioning of the SES is completed; and all unhealthy, dead, or noncompliant plantings shall be repaired or replaced within ninety (90) days of such occurrence. These requirements apply to Large Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems (Large Scale SES) as defined in the ordinance. Other options and conditions mentioned include: Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, Small-scale SES, Intermediate SES, and Large Scale SES where physical construction began prior to the effective date of this Ordinance with conditions on completion and enlargement, which are exempt from these requirements.

The ordinance requires a decommissioning plan for Large Scale SES that includes "the estimated decommissioning costs, including removal of the Solar Energy System and related foundations, pads, underground collector lines and roads, transmission lines, and the revegetation and restoration of the property, including soils, to its original condition" (Section 4(d)(b)). It also mandates that "disturbed areas shall be reclaimed, revegetated, and restored" after decommissioning (Section 5). The surety instrument must cover the costs of decommissioning and restoration. The ordinance applies to Large Scale SES defined as ground mounted systems with a footprint of more than 40 acres or those constituting a Merchant Electric Generating Facility. Other SES types such as Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, Small-scale SES, and Intermediate SES are excluded from these requirements. Physical construction must not have begun prior to the ordinance's effective date unless completed within two years and not enlarged by more than 5%.

Access to the site must be controlled by a fence of at least eight feet in height with a vegetative landscape buffer provided between the fencing and the property line. For intermediate and large scale ground mounted energy systems, screening shall consist of: 1. An eight (8) foot fall fence and a double row of staggered evergreen trees (minimum of five (5) feet in height at planting); 2. Evergreen trees shall be planted exterior to the fence and shall be setback no less than fifteen (15) feet from the nearest property line; 3. Screening shall achieve an opacity of 90% to a height of no less than eight (8) feet within three years of planting; 4. Screening shall be installed within 180 days of the start of physical construction and shall be maintained until the decommissioning of the SES is completed; and 5. All unhealthy, dead, or noncompliant plantings shall be repaired or replaced within ninety (90) days of such occurrence.

summary: Section II.A.1 states: 'Ground Mounted SES shall not exceed fifteen (15) feet in height as measured from the highest natural grade below each solar panel without approval by the Fiscal Court.' This height restriction applies to all Ground Mounted SES, which includes Large Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems (defined as having a footprint of more than ten (10) acres). The height limitation excludes utility poles, substation structures, and antennas constructed for the project. A Ground Mounted SES may exceed fifteen (15) feet in height upon a finding that the SES would be more productive, use less land, or provide other environmental, economic, or other benefits if the height limitation is increased.

summary: Upon completion of construction and installation of the Ground Mounted SES, all temporary roads constructed by the applicant shall be removed, and all disturbed areas shall be graded and reseeded with short-term cover crops and sustainable, non-weed native vegetation in order to establish an effective ground cover and to minimize erosion and sedimentation. The permanent location of solar arrays on impermeable surfaces, including but not limited to gravel and asphalt, is prohibited. Temporary roads may remain upon request by the property owner.

The Todd County Fiscal Court hereby establishes the following minimum setback requirements for solar energy systems which are governed by KRS 278.704, as measured from the outer edge of the nearest solar panel: 'Any residence, building or structure or appurtenance thereto existing at the time of application for permits with the Kentucky Electric Generation and Transmission Siting Board' requires a minimum setback distance of 2,000 feet. Other setback distances include 2,000 feet from boundary lines of adjacent property, 1,000 feet from public road right-of-way, 2,000 feet from designated scenic highways and byways, 1,000 feet from other rights-of-way such as railroads and public utility easements, and 2,000 feet from cemeteries. Affected private property owners may modify or waive these setback requirements by notifying the Todd Fiscal Court in writing of the modification or waiver.

The Todd County Fiscal Court hereby establishes the following minimum setback requirements for solar energy systems which are governed by KRS 278.704, as measured from the outer edge of the nearest solar panel: 'Other rights-of-way, such as railroads and public utility easements, measured from the edge of the right-of-way' require a minimum setback distance of 1,000 feet. Affected private property owners may modify or waive these setback requirements by notifying the Todd Fiscal Court in writing of the modification or waiver. Other setback distances listed include 2,000 feet from boundary lines, residences, buildings, designated scenic highways, and cemeteries; and 1,000 feet from public road rights-of-way. However, only the 1,000 feet setback from public utility easements is directly applicable to overhead electrical transmission lines, overhead utility lines, utility easements, utility lines, power lines, electrical lines, and/or transmission lines for Large Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems.

The ordinance requires a 'decommissioning plan, prepared by a registered professional engineer at the expense of the applicant, and updated not less than once every five (5) years,' which must include 'the anticipated life of the project and defined conditions upon which decommissioning will be initiated,' 'the estimated decommissioning costs, including removal of the Solar Energy System and related foundations, pads, underground collector lines and roads, transmission lines, and the revegetation and restoration of the property, including soils, to its original condition,' and 'the manner in which the project will be decommissioned, including provision and a timetable (such timetable not to exceed five years) for the removal of all structures and foundations, and for the revegetation and restoration of the property to its original condition.' A surety instrument is also required to cover decommissioning costs and must be updated every five years. Decommissioning must begin no later than twelve (12) months after a Large-Scale SES has ceased to generate electricity or thermal energy, with all structures removed within six (6) months of starting decommissioning. Failure to decommission as required allows the County to invoke the surety instrument and take legal action. License revocation may occur for failure to decommission, with a 12-month deadline to complete decommissioning after revocation. The ordinance applies specifically to Large-Scale Ground-Mounted Solar Energy Systems (Large-Scale SES) with a footprint of more than forty (40) acres or those constituting a Merchant Electric Generating Facility. The ordinance does not apply to Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, Small-Scale SES, Intermediate-Scale SES, or Large-Scale SES where physical construction began prior to the ordinance's effective date and meets certain conditions.

The ordinance explicitly requires that "Access to the site must be controlled by a fence of at least eight (8) feet in height with a vegetative landscape buffer provided between the fencing and the property line." The fence "shall be equipped with screening to help shield the facilities and equipment from view," consisting of "an eight (8) foot tall fence and a double row of staggered evergreen trees (minimum five (5) feet in height at planting and maturing to a minimum of fifteen (15) feet in height)." The evergreen trees "shall be planted exterior to the fence and shall be setback no less than fifteen (15) feet from any property line," and the screening "shall achieve an opacity of 90% to a height of no less than eight (8) feet within three (3) years of planting." Screening "shall be installed within 180 days of the start of physical construction and shall be maintained until the decommissioning of the SES is completed," with all unhealthy, dead, or noncompliant plantings to be "repaired or replaced within ninety (90) days of such occurrence." These fencing and screening requirements apply specifically to Large-Scale Ground-Mounted Solar Energy Systems (Large-Scale SES) as defined in the ordinance. Other types of SES such as Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, Small-Scale SES, and Intermediate-Scale SES are explicitly excluded from the ordinance's requirements. The ordinance also includes other provisions related to setbacks, lighting, decommissioning plans, surety instruments, and licensing, but these do not pertain directly to fencing requirements.

Large-Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy System (Large-Scale SES) means a Ground Mounted SES with a footprint of more than forty (40) acres. Other categories include Small-Scale SES with a footprint of less than 2,500 square feet and Intermediate-Scale SES with a footprint between 2,501 square feet and forty (40) acres. The minimum lot size for Large-Scale SES is thus explicitly set at more than 40 acres.

The SES footprint shall be required to be at least one thousand (1,000) feet from the property boundary of any adjoining property owner. Other setback distances mentioned include two thousand (2,000) feet from any non-participating residence, school, hospital, or nursing home facility, but these do not pertain to property lines.

The SES footprint shall be required to be at least one thousand (1,000) feet from the property boundary of any adjoining property owner and two thousand (2,000) feet from any non-participating residence, school, hospital, or nursing home facility. The setback distance is measured from the boundary of a public roadway (rights-of-way) to the nearest portion of the SES footprint or other regulated SES feature, and must be contained within the boundary of a participating property.

Section 4(b) Perimeter Access and Screening requires access to the site to be controlled by a fence of at least eight (8) feet in height with a vegetative landscape buffer provided between the fencing and the property line. The fence shall be equipped with screening to help shield the facilities and equipment from view. Screening shall consist of: (1) An eight (8) foot tall fence and a double row of staggered evergreen trees (minimum five (5) feet in height at planting and maturing to a minimum of fifteen (15) feet in height); (2) Evergreen trees shall be planted exterior to the fence and shall be setback no less than fifteen (15) feet from any property line; (3) Screening shall achieve an opacity of 90% to a height of no less than eight (8) feet within three (3) years of planting; (4) Screening shall be installed within 180 days of the start of physical construction and shall be maintained until the decommissioning of the SES is completed; and (5) All unhealthy, dead, or noncompliant plantings shall be repaired or replaced within ninety (90) days of such occurrence. These requirements apply to Large-Scale Ground-Mounted Solar Energy Systems (Large-Scale SES) as defined in the ordinance. Other types of SES such as Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, Small-Scale SES, and Intermediate-Scale SES are excluded from this ordinance's requirements.

The ordinance provides "reasonable safeguards which mitigate potential nuisances such as soil erosion, water runoff and erosion" caused by Large-Scale Ground Mounted Solar Energy Systems (Large-Scale SES). It requires a "decommissioning plan, prepared by a registered professional engineer" that includes "the estimated decommissioning costs, including removal of the Solar Energy System and related foundations, pads, underground collector lines and roads, transmission lines, and the revegetation and restoration of the property, including soils, to its original condition." The plan must be updated "not less than once every five (5) years" and secured by a "surety instrument" to cover decommissioning costs. After cessation of operation, "disturbed areas shall be reclaimed, revegetated, and restored." The ordinance applies to Large-Scale SES defined as ground-mounted systems with a footprint of more than forty (40) acres or any non-exempt SES constituting a Merchant Electric Generating Facility. It does not apply to Integrated SES, Rooftop SES, Small-Scale SES, Intermediate Scale SES, or Large-Scale SES where physical construction began prior to the ordinance's effective date under certain conditions.

The SES footprint shall be required to be at least two thousand (2,000) feet from any non-participating residence, school, hospital, or nursing home facility. Other setback options include at least one thousand (1,000) feet from the property boundary of any adjoining property owner.

A ground-mounted solar panel system is not permitted as the primary use of a property in the Agricultural District on tracts less than 10 acres in size (701.3.J) and in the Conservation District on tracts less than 10 acres in size (702.3.G). This minimum tract size requirement applies to utility-scale solar energy systems as primary uses. Other sections (703.5.F and 704.4.G) address accessory or smaller-scale systems and do not specify minimum lot sizes.
