summary: Section 106.10 Decommissioning requires that "The PSES owner is required to notify the Township immediately upon cessation or abandonment of the operation." The PSES is "presumed to be discontinued or abandoned if no electricity is generated by such system for a period of twelve (12) continuous months." The owner "shall then have twelve (12) months in which to dismantle and remove the PSES including all solar-related equipment or appurtenances related thereto, including, but not limited to, buildings, cabling, electrical components, roads, foundations and other associated facilities from the property." If the owner fails to remove the system within the timeframe, "the municipality may complete the decommissioning at the owner's expense." At permit issuance, "the owner shall provide financial security in the amount of 110% of the total proposed decommissioning costs and in a form acceptable to the Township to secure the expense of dismantling and removing said PSES and restoration of the land to its original condition." This security must be updated every 5 years with an independent professional engineer's estimate, and the owner is responsible for administrative, legal, and engineering costs incurred by the Township for review. The security may be in the form of cash deposit, surety bond, irrevocable letter of credit, cashier's check, or escrow amount from a federal or Commonwealth chartered lending institution. The owner must also provide proof of liability insurance with a policy limit of at least One Million Dollars naming the Township as an additional named insured. Additionally, "Solar Energy Project Owner shall enter into a decommissioning agreement with the Township outlining the responsibility of the parties under this Ordinance as to the decommissioning of the Solar Energy Project Owner."

Section 106.16.1 states: 'All ground mounted PSES shall be completely enclosed by a minimum eight (8) foot high fence with a self-locking gate.' Section 106.16.2 requires: 'A clearly visible warning sign shall be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations and on the fence surrounding the PSES informing individuals of potential voltage hazards.' These fencing requirements explicitly apply to Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES) as defined in the ordinance. No alternative fencing options or conditions are provided for PSES.

Section 106.11 states: 'All PSES shall be placed such that concentrated solar radiation or glare does not project onto nearby structures, roadways, and/or affect operations of the Beaver County Airport.' The applicant 'has the burden of proving that any glare produced does not have significant adverse impact on neighboring or adjacent uses either through sitting or mitigation. Accordingly, a glare study shall be required.'

Section 106.12.1 states: 'Noise from a PSES shall not exceed a noise dwibel of 8 as measured at the property line.' A noise study must be performed by an independent noise study expert and paid for by the applicant. The unit is assumed to be dBA as the standard unit for noise levels. No other maximum noise level values for PSES are provided in the ordinance.

Section 106.15.2.2 states: 'All PSES shall be located at least fifty (50) feet from all Non-Participating Landowner property lines.' Other setback distances mentioned include 250 feet from Non-Participating Landowner Residential Homes (Section 106.15.2.3) and 75 feet from public roadways (Section 106.15.2.5), but these do not pertain to property lines. The 50 feet setback from non-participating property lines is a fixed distance and is not subject to waiver.

Section 106.15.2.5 states: 'All PSES shall be located at least seventy-five (75) feet from public roadways.' This is a fixed setback distance specifically for Principal Solar Energy Systems. Other setback distances mentioned in Section 106.15.2 relate to property lines (50 feet), residential homes (250 feet), and buildings (50 feet), but these do not pertain to roads.

Section 106.15.4 Visual Mitigation/Screening requires that "Vegetative buffering, to the extent practical, shall be located between the outermost PSES and any abutting Non-Participating Landowner's Residential Home or public roadway." It further states that "The retention of existing trees within a setback area shall constitute a vegetative buffer, if the view at ground level has visual mitigation." Vegetative buffering "shall be installed along the exterior side of the fencing" and "shall be designed to emulate the mix of native species and appearance of existing tree lines, hedge rows, and wooded areas already in existence within the landscape where the PSES is proposed," with preference for evergreen trees. The buffering "shall be of sufficient height, density, and maturity to reasonably mitigate the visual impacts of the PSES within thirty-six (36) months of the installation." A combination of natural topography and vegetation can serve as a buffer, but "Earthen berms may not be created to serve as a Buffer." Section 106.15.9 states that "Ground-mounted PSES shall be screened from adjoining residential uses or zones according to the standards found in this Ordinance." Section 106.15.10 requires "Vegetative Screening shall be provided on all property lines facing a public or public use roadway." These requirements apply explicitly to Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES) as defined in the ordinance. No other options or conditions for screening or buffering for PSES are provided in the text.

Section 106.16.2 requires that "a clearly visible warning sign shall be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations and on the fence surrounding the PSES informing individuals of potential voltage hazards." Section 106.7 states "No portion of the PSES shall contain or be used to display advertising. The manufacturer's name and equipment information or indication of ownership shall be allowed on any equipment of the PSES provided they comply with the prevailing sign regulations."

Section 106.15.5.1 states that where solar panels are mounted above the ground allowing for vegetation below, the horizontal area of the panel may be considered a Disconnected Impervious Area (DIA) with no increase in runoff coefficient if: natural vegetative cover is preserved/restored using PA DEP Stormwater BMPs; vegetative cover has a minimum uniform 70% perennial cover capable of resisting accelerated erosion and sedimentation; panels on slopes 0-15% maintain minimum 4" vegetative cover height; panels on slopes >15% cannot be considered DIA; vegetated areas are not subject to chemical fertilization/herbicide/pesticide except as necessary and in accordance with an approved erosion and sedimentation control plan; and panel arrangement allows runoff passage and vegetation growth beneath. Section 106.15.6 treats horizontal areas not meeting DIA conditions as impervious for runoff analysis and requires Post-Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) BMPs. Section 106.15.8 requires any system disturbing over one (1) acre to apply for an NPDES permit with the Beaver County Conservation District. Section 106.10.3 requires restoration of land to its original condition, including forestry plantings, upon decommissioning. These requirements apply to Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES) as defined in the ordinance. Other related provisions include Section 106.15.12 prohibiting placement within stormwater conveyance systems or easements that would alter or impede runoff, and Section 106.15.7 encouraging low maintenance vegetative surfaces as best management practice for stormwater management.

Section 106.1.1 states that "PSES shall be permitted in Industrial & Commercial, Retail, Sales and Service District only." The text uses the phrase "subject to the terms and conditions of this Ordinance" but does not explicitly categorize Ground-Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems as a special use or require approval by a zoning appeals board or similar special permitting process. Other related provisions include setback, height, and lot size requirements detailed in Section 106.15, but these do not explicitly indicate a special use designation. Accessory Solar Energy Systems (ASES) with power ratings over 15kW must comply with Section 106 (Principal Solar Energy System), but smaller ASES are permitted by right in all zoning districts. No solar overlay districts are included in this determination.

All PSES shall be located at least two hundred fifty (250) feet from any Non-Participating Landowner Residential Home as the required setback. All inverters and electric transformers shall be located at least five hundred (500) feet from any Non-Participating Landowner Residential Home. All PSES shall be located at least fifty (50) feet from all buildings not part of the project. The setback for a Non-Participating Landowner for their Residential Home may be waived by the Non-Participating Landowner, but the setback for inverters or electric transformers is non-waivable.

Section 4.416(e) requires that "Security fencing of at least 8-feet is required around the entire solar facility, inside the perimeter of any screening." Other conditions for Large Solar Energy Facilities include minimum lot size of 10 acres (4.416(a)), maximum panel height of 14 feet (4.416(b)), setbacks from property lines and roads (4.416(c)), surface area limits (4.416(d)), screening requirements (4.416(f)), noise limits (4.416(g)), lighting restrictions (4.416(h)), cabling burial or concealment (4.416(i)), glare remediation (4.416(j)), and documentation and approval conditions (4.416(k) and (l)).

Section 4.416(j) states: 'Glare from the Solar facility determined to be nuisance to adjacent properties or roadways shall be prohibited. The Solar facility owners shall remediate any nuisance glare claims within six (6) months of being notified.' Other conditions for Large Solar Energy Facilities include minimum lot size of 10 acres (4.416(a)), maximum panel height of 14 feet (4.416(b)), setbacks from property lines and roads (4.416(c)), coverage limits (4.416(d)), security fencing (4.416(e)), screening requirements (4.416(f)), noise limits (4.416(g)), lighting restrictions (4.416(h)), and cabling requirements (4.416(i)).

Section 4.416(b) states: 'The maximum height of solar panels is 14 feet. This height shall be measured from the highest point during a panel’s full rotation needed to maximize exposure to the sunlight throughout the day.' This is the explicit maximum height restriction for Large Solar Energy Facilities. Other height-related provisions apply only to Small Solar Energy Facilities or underlying district requirements and are not relevant here.

The minimum lot size for a large solar energy facility is 10 acres. Contiguous lots under the same owner, that together are larger than 10 acres, shall meet this condition. This is explicitly stated in section 4.416(a) for Large Solar Energy Facilities. The unit 'acres' is used as the area measurement for the minimum lot size.

The facilities shall not generate noise which exceeds fifty-five (55) decibels (dBA) nor ten (10) dBA above ambient noise in any one hour, whichever is higher. Noise is measured from the property line of all neighboring properties with a habitable structure.

Solar panels and support equipment shall be set back a minimum of 50-feet from all property lines. Other setbacks mentioned include 100-feet from all road right-of-ways and 150-feet from residential properties or uses, but these do not pertain to property lines or parcels. This applies specifically to Large Solar Energy Facilities as defined in the ordinance.

Solar panels and support equipment shall be set back a minimum of 100-feet from all road right-of-ways. Other setback distances include 50-feet from all property lines and 150-feet from residential properties or uses, but only the 100-feet from road right-of-ways applies to roads.

Section 4.416(f) requires that "The perimeter of the project areas, including all solar panels and associated equipment, shall be screened from adjacent residential and commercial properties, uses and roadways." Additionally, 4.416(e) mandates "Security fencing of at least 8-feet is required around the entire solar facility, inside the perimeter of any screening." Other conditions for Large Solar Energy Facilities include minimum lot size of 10 acres (4.416(a)), maximum panel height of 14 feet (4.416(b)), setbacks of 50 feet from property lines, 100 feet from road right-of-ways, and 150 feet from residential properties or uses (4.416(c)), coverage limits (4.416(d)), noise limits (4.416(g)), lighting restrictions (4.416(h)), cabling burial or concealment (4.416(i)), glare remediation (4.416(j)), and various documentation and approval conditions (4.416(k) and (l)).

Large Solar Energy Facilities are listed as Conditional Uses in the R-A Residential Agricultural District and the I Industrial District. The ordinance states: 'Large Solar Energy Facilities (4.416)' under Conditional Uses for both districts. Section 4.416 details conditions such as minimum lot size of 10 acres, maximum panel height of 14 feet, setbacks from property lines and roads, security fencing, noise limits, lighting restrictions, and requirements for screening and electrical cabling. Other districts either do not mention Large Solar Energy Facilities or list only Small Solar Energy Facilities as permitted or conditional uses. For example, the R-U Residential Urban District and C-H Commercial Highway District list only Small Solar Energy Facilities as conditional uses. The text also notes that the Granville Township Supervisors may attach additional conditions in its approval of conditional use and land development plans for Large Solar Energy Facilities.

Section 4.416(c) states: 'Solar panels and support equipment shall be set back a minimum of 50-feet from all property lines and a minimum of 100-feet from all road right-of-ways and a minimum of 150-feet from residential properties or uses.' The 150-feet setback from residential properties or uses is the relevant and most restrictive distance for Large Solar Energy Facilities from occupied dwellings, buildings, structures, and/or residences.

§ 420-147 Vacation, abandonment and/or decommissioning: "Discontinuation/abandonment is presumed when a solar PV system has been disconnected from the net metering grid for a period of six continuous months without being connected to a battery system or has not produced electricity for a period of six months." "A solar PV system including its solar PV related equipment must be removed within 12 months of the date of discontinuation or abandonment or upon the termination of the useful life of the solar PV system." "For ground-mounted and building-mounted systems, removal includes removal of all structural and electrical parts of the ground or building-mounted system and any associated facilities or equipment and removal of all net metering equipment." "If the owner fails to remove or repair the vacated, abandoned or decommissioned solar PV system within six months, the municipality reserves the right to enter the property, remove the system and charge the landowner and/or facility owner and operator for all costs and expenses, including reasonable attorney's fees, or pursue other legal action to have the system removed at the owner's expense." "Any unpaid costs resulting from the Municipality's removal of a vacated, abandoned or decommissioned solar PV system shall constitute a lien upon the property against which the costs were charged."

Ground-mounted systems may not exceed 10 feet in height in any zoning district where the solar PV system is to be installed. This is the explicit maximum height restriction for ground-mounted solar photovoltaic systems up to 3,000 kilowatts (3 MW). Other height restrictions mentioned apply only to building-mounted systems, such as: (1) building-mounted systems on sloped roofs facing the front yard must be installed at the same angle as the roof with a maximum distance of six inches perpendicular to the roof; (2) building-mounted systems on sloped roofs shall not exceed the highest point of the roof; and (3) building-mounted systems on flat roofs shall not exceed six feet above the roof. The units for the ground-mounted system height restriction are feet.

Ground-mounted systems are permitted in all zoning districts as an accessory use upon issuance of the proper permit, provided that the minimum lot size is 1.5 acres. This is explicitly stated in § 420-137 B. The unit 'acres' is the standard area measurement used for the minimum lot size.

Section § 420-142 Screening and visibility states: 'Ground-mounted systems are required to be properly landscaped and buffered from adjoining properties.' This is the explicit vegetative buffer and/or screening requirement applicable to ground-mounted solar photovoltaic (PV) systems up to 3,000 kilowatts (3 MW). Building-mounted systems on a sloped roof 'shall not be required to be screened.'

No signage or graphic content may be displayed on the solar PV system except the manufacturer's badge, safety information and equipment specification information. Said information shall be depicted within an area no more than 36 square inches in size.

Section 4.A.13 Decommissioning: "The PSES owner is required to notify the Borough/Township immediately upon cessation or abandonment of the operation. The PSES shall be presumed to be discontinued or abandoned if no electricity is generated by such system for a period of twelve (12) continuous months." "The PSES owner shall then have twelve (12) months in which to dismantle and remove the PSES including all solar related equipment or appurtenances related thereto, including but not limited to buildings, cabling, electrical components, roads, foundations and other associated facilities from the property. If the owner fails to dismantle and/or remove the PSES within the established timeframes, the municipality may complete the decommissioning at the owner’s expense." "At the time of issuance of the permit for the construction of the PSES, the owner shall provide financial security in the form and amount acceptable to Greene Township to secure the expense of dismantling and removing said PSES, regrading as necessary and revegetation/seeding of any disturbed areas to provide erosion control." The ordinance distinguishes these requirements from those for Accessory Solar Energy Systems (ASES), which also have decommissioning rules but apply to smaller or on-site primarily use systems. The PSES decommissioning requirements apply to systems "principally used to capture solar energy... and supply electrical or thermal power primarily for off-site use" and permitted in Industrial and A-1 zoning districts.

The ordinance explicitly enacts decommissioning requirements for Large-Scale Solar Electric Energy Facilities. Section 11 states: 'The Facility Owner and Operator shall, at their expense, complete decommissioning of the Solar Electric Energy Facility or individual Solar Electric System within twelve (12) months after the end of the useful life of such Facility or System. A Solar Electric Energy Facility or System will be premised to be at the end of its useful life if no electricity is generated for a continuous period of twelve (12) months.' Decommissioning includes 'removal of all Solar Electric Energy Systems, buildings, cabling, electrical components, roads, foundations and any other associated facilities,' and 'Disturbed earth shall be graded and re-seeded, unless the landowner requests in writing that the access roads or other land surface areas not be restored.' The estimated cost of decommissioning 'shall be secured by a Bond or such other security to ensure the completed decommissioning of the Solar Electric Energy components,' with the bond amount adjusted every three years to factor inflation and salvage values. Additionally, Section 6.B.5 requires the permit application to include 'Documents relating to decommissioning, including a schedule for decommissioning. The projected cost of decommissioning must be set forth with supporting estimates by a qualified expert or company.'

All ground-mounted PSES shall be completely enclosed by a minimum seven (7) foot high fence with a self-locking gate. A clearly visible warning sign shall be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations and on the fence on the surrounding the PSES informing individuals of potential voltage hazards. (Section 4 - PRINCIPAL SOLAR ENERGY SYSTEMS, B. Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems, 7. Security)
section: SECTION 4 - PRINCIPAL SOLAR ENERGY SYSTEMS (PSES), B. Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems

summary: A Solar Electric Energy Facility shall be enclosed by a fence with a minimum height of seven (7) feet, barrier or other appropriate means to prevent or restrict unauthorized persons or vehicles from entering the property. Welding wire fencing is preferred over chain link fencing. Clearly visible warning signs shall be placed on the fence, barrier or Solar Electric Energy Facility perimeter to inform individuals of potential voltage hazards. Where in the judgment of the Board of Supervisors, and concerns of neighboring property owners, natural vegetation may be required along the perimeter fencing. In the event that natural vegetation is dead, it shall be replaced within ninety (90) days of said event, or in the event of winter, by the first of May.

Section 4.A.8 states: 'All PSES shall be placed such that concentrated solar radiation or glare does not project onto nearby structures or roadways.' Additionally, 'The applicant has the burden of proving that any glare produced does not have significant adverse impact on neighboring or adjacent uses either through siting or mitigation.' This glare restriction applies explicitly to Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES), which are defined as systems 'principally used to capture solar energy, convert it to electrical energy or thermal power and supply electrical or thermal power primarily for off-site use.' Other options include Accessory Solar Energy Systems (ASES), which also have glare restrictions under Section 3.A.7 stating: 'All ASES shall be placed such that concentrated solar radiation or glare does not project onto nearby structures or roadways,' but the focus here is on PSES. The ordinance also details various requirements for PSES including lot size, setbacks, height, screening, security, and decommissioning, but the explicit glare restrictions are found in Section 4.A.8.

Section 4, Part B, subsection 3 states: 'Ground mounted PSES shall not exceed 15 feet in height.' This is the explicit maximum height restriction for Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES). Other height restrictions mentioned in the ordinance apply to Accessory Solar Energy Systems (ASES) or roof/wall mounted systems, which are not relevant to PSES. The unit for this height restriction is feet.
section: SECTION 4 - PRINCIPAL SOLAR ENERGY SYSTEMS (PSES), B. Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems

summary: The ordinance explicitly states: 'The solar farm shall be located on a parcel or combined parcels of land with a minimum acreage of eighteen (18) acres.' This minimum acreage applies to Large-Scale Solar Electric Energy Facilities, defined as facilities whose main purpose is to generate and supply electricity for sale into the electric grid. The unit of measurement is acres, a standard area unit.

Section 4.A.9 states: 'Noise from a PSES shall not exceed fifty (50) dBA, as measured at the property line.' This is the explicit maximum noise level allowed for Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES), which includes ground mounted systems intended primarily for off-site use. No other noise level restrictions for PSES are provided in the text.

Section 4.A.1 states: 'PSES shall be permitted as a use by right in the Industrial & A-1 Zoning Districts upon issuance of the PSES Solar Photovoltaic Permit specified in this Ordinance.' The ordinance distinguishes Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES) from Accessory Solar Energy Systems (ASES), which are permitted as accessory uses by right in all districts but not as principal uses. No other districts or solar overlay districts are mentioned as permitting PSES as a primary use by right.

The PSES shall comply with the setbacks of the underlying zoning districts for principal structures, and the PSES shall be located a minimum of one hundred (100) feet from adjacent R1, R2 districts, and/or non-affiliated residential structures in the underlying zoning district.
section: SECTION 4 - PRINCIPAL SOLARENERGY SYSTEMS (PSES), B. Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems

summary: All Solar Electric Energy Systems shall be located one hundred (100) feet from all property lines where the System is located. These distances shall be measured from the closest edge of the Solar Electric Energy System to the property line.

Section 4.B.5 states: 'Ground mounted PSES shall be screened from adjoining residential uses and R1 and R2 Zoning Districts. The screen shall consist of two rows of evergreen trees on 15’ staggered centers which provide a visual screen. Evergreens shall be a minimum of 3’ tall when planted. Immediate replacement of dead trees shall be required.' This is the explicit vegetative buffer/screening requirement for Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES).
section: SECTION 4 - PRINCIPAL SOLAR ENERGY SYSTEMS (PSES), B. Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems

summary: Section 4.B.7 requires that "All ground-mounted PSES shall be completely enclosed by a minimum seven (7) foot high fence with a self-locking gate." It also mandates that "A clearly visible warning sign shall be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations and on the fence on the surrounding the PSES informing individuals of potential voltage hazards." Additionally, Section 4.A.7 states: "No portion of the PSES shall contain or be used to display advertising. The manufacturer’s name and equipment information or indication of ownership shall be allowed on any equipment of the PSES provided they comply with the prevailing sign regulations in the zoning district." These are the explicit signage requirements for Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES).

Section 7.D.2 requires that "Clearly visible warning signs shall be placed on the fence, barrier or Solar Electric Energy Facility perimeter to inform individuals of potential voltage hazards." This is the explicit signage requirement for Large-Scale Solar Electric Energy Facilities. Other related provisions include fencing requirements (7.D.1) and visual appearance restrictions on advertising (7.C.2), but these do not constitute signage requirements. No other explicit signage requirements are stated in the ordinance.

The ordinance requires that for Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES), the applicant "shall submit a Stormwater Management Plan that demonstrates compliance with the municipal stormwater management regulations." It also mandates that "if a ground mounted PSES is removed, any earth disturbance resulting from the removal must be graded and reseeded." Additionally, ground-mounted PSES "shall not be placed within any legal easement or right-of-way location, or be placed within any storm water conveyance system or in any other manner that would alter or impede storm water runoff from collecting in a constructed storm water conveyance system."
section: SECTION 4 - PRINCIPAL SOLAR ENERGY SYSTEMS (PSES), B. Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems

summary: The ordinance states that "PSES shall be permitted as a use by right in the Industrial & A-1 Zoning Districts upon issuance of the PSES Solar Photovoltaic Permit specified in this Ordinance." It sets conditions including minimum lot size, setbacks (including a minimum of 100 feet from adjacent R1, R2 districts, and/or non-affiliated residential structures), height limits (not exceeding 15 feet), impervious coverage calculations, and screening requirements. There is no mention of Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES) being permitted as a special use or requiring approval by a zoning appeals board or similar conditional use process in any district. Accessory Solar Energy Systems (ASES) are permitted by right in all districts as accessory uses, with various conditions, but this does not apply to PSES. Solar overlay districts are excluded from this analysis as per instructions.

The PSES shall be located a minimum of one hundred (100) feet from adjacent R1, R2 districts, and/or non-affiliated residential structures in the underlying zoning district. Additionally, the PSES shall comply with the setbacks of the underlying zoning districts for principal structures. This 100-foot setback is a fixed minimum distance specifically for Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES).
section: SECTION 4 - PRINCIPAL SOLARENERGY SYSTEMS (PSES), B. Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems

summary: The ordinance explicitly enacts decommissioning requirements for Solar Electric Energy Facilities, defined as facilities generating and supplying electricity and built on 2 acres or more, excluding on-site residential or commercial use. Section 9 states: 'The Facility Owner and Operator shall, at its expense, complete decommissioning of the Solar Energy Facility, or individual Solar Collectors, within twelve (12) months after the end of the useful life of the Facility or individual solar collectors.' Decommissioning includes removal of solar collectors, buildings, cabling, electrical components, roads, foundations to a depth of thirty-six (36) inches, and other associated facilities. Disturbed earth must be graded and re-seeded unless the landowner requests otherwise in writing. An independent Professional Engineer must estimate decommissioning costs, and financial assurance (performance bond, surety bond, or other acceptable form) must be posted before construction. If the Facility Owner or Operator fails to decommission, the landowner has six months to complete it, and if neither completes it, the County may take necessary measures. The escrow agent releases funds upon satisfactory completion or County approval. In the event of sale or transfer, the acquiring entity must adhere to the original decommissioning requirements.

A Solar Electric Energy Facility "shall be enclosed by a fence, barrier or other appropriate means to prevent or restrict unauthorized persons or vehicles from entering the property." Additionally, "clearly visible warning signs shall be placed on the fence, barrier or Solar Electric Energy Facility perimeter to inform individuals of potential voltage hazards." These requirements are found under the Design and Construction provisions, specifically subsection D. Warnings. The ordinance defines a Solar Electric Energy Facility as "a facility that has a main purpose of generating and supplying electricity and that consists of one or more Solar Electric Systems and other accessory structures and buildings," excluding systems meant for on-site residential or commercial use, thus applying to utility-scale systems.

All Solar Electric Energy Systems shall be located 50 feet from all property lines where the System is located. These distances shall be measured from the closest edge of the Solar Electric Energy System to the property line.

Section 7.D states: 'Clearly visible warning signs shall be placed on the fence, barrier or Solar Electric Energy Facility perimeter to inform individuals of potential voltage hazards.' This applies to Solar Electric Energy Facilities defined as facilities with the main purpose of generating and supplying electricity, built on 2 acres or more, and not meant for on-site residential or commercial use. The ordinance regulates construction, operation, and decommissioning of such facilities and includes permit requirements, design and construction standards, and decommissioning obligations.

Within the R Zoning District, the maximum lot coverage of the PSES shall not exceed sixty-five percent (65%). All PSES features and system components that are impervious, including but not limited to panels and their actual surface area, buildings, roads, etc., shall be considered in the lot coverage determination. This is the only explicit maximum land coverage limit provided for PSES. No other numerical maximum land coverage values for PSES are given.

The ordinance explicitly enacts decommissioning requirements for Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES). It states: 'The PSES owner and operator shall, at its expense, complete decommissioning of the PSES within six (6) months after the end of its useful life or the useful life of the panel(s), whichever comes first.' Decommissioning includes 'removal of all panels, buildings, cabling, electrical components, foundations, and any other associated features, facilities, or related components in their entirety whether above, equal to or below ground.' Disturbed earth must be 'graded and re-seeded unless the landowner requests in writing that the access roads or other land surface areas not be restored.' An independent, certified professional engineer must estimate 'the total cost of decommissioning (the  "Decommissioning Costs" ) without regard to salvage value of the equipment, and the cost of decommissioning net salvage value of the equipment (the  "Net Decommissioning Costs" ).' The PSES owner or operator must 'post and maintain Financial Security for Decommissioning in an amount equal to Net Decommissioning Costs ... before or contemporaneous with the Township’s final approval of the Land Development Plan.' If the owner/operator fails to decommission timely, the landowner has six months to complete it, and if neither completes it, the Township may use the financial security to complete decommissioning. The escrow agent releases the financial security only when decommissioning is satisfactorily completed or upon written municipal approval. These requirements apply specifically to PSES, defined as systems 'to generate electricity or otherwise convert solar energy into a different form of energy for the primary purpose of using the energy for commercial or other off-site use.'

The PSES shall be enclosed with an eight (8) foot tall, chain-link fence having self-locking gates. The minimum lot size for placement of a PSES shall be twenty (20) acres. PSES ground mounted systems shall not exceed twelve (12) feet in height. Buildings constituting or relating to the PSES shall comply with the underlying zoning district requirements for maximum building height. The PSES shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, including but not limited to building, construction, fire and life safety requirements. Landscape screening shall include a minimum of two rows of native, green evergreen trees at least eight (8) feet in height at the time of planting, planted fifteen (15) feet on center and staggered, with specific planting requirements depending on zoning district. Other design, installation, and operation regulations apply, including compliance with industry standards and safety labeling. Decommissioning requirements and submission requirements for PSES are also detailed.

The ordinance defines Principal Solar Energy System (PSES) as "an alternative energy system consisting of ground mounted solar collection devices and solar energy related equipment to generate electricity or otherwise convert solar energy into a different form of energy for the primary purpose of using the energy for commercial or other off-site use." Under Section 503.36 PSES, it states: "The panels shall be positioned to prevent glare upon all neighboring properties, public streets, and private streets." Other relevant regulations include height limits ("PSES ground mounted systems shall not exceed twelve (12) feet in height"), setback requirements, lot coverage limits, fencing, landscape screening, compliance with federal, state, and local laws, and submission requirements such as a "glare analysis report prepared and sealed by an engineer licensed in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, which shows that glare will not be projected onto any public street or any building on a property, other than the property where the PSES is located." The ordinance also includes decommissioning requirements and other operational standards. Accessory Solar Energy Systems (ASES) are separately regulated with different conditions, such as a maximum area of 1,000 square feet and height limits, but glare restrictions are explicitly stated only for PSES.

The ordinance states: 'PSES ground mounted systems shall not exceed twelve (12) feet in height.' It also specifies that 'Buildings constituting or relating to the PSES shall comply with the underlying zoning district requirements for maximum building height.' This 12 feet limit applies explicitly to ground mounted PSES. No other maximum height values for PSES are provided. The units are feet as indicated in the text.

The minimum lot size for placement of a PSES shall be twenty (20) acres. This is explicitly stated in Section 503.36 (PSES). The unit 'acres' is used as the area measurement for this minimum lot size requirement. No other minimum lot size values for PSES are provided in the text.

Within the I Zoning District, if the PSES is upon a lot that adjoins another lot with an existing residential use then all features and system components shall be setback a minimum of fifty (50) feet from that shared boundary line. Within the R Zoning District, the placement of all features and system components constituting the PSES shall be setback a minimum of fifty (50) feet from all property lines and street right of way lines. Other options include compliance with the setback requirements of the I Zoning District generally, and the 50 feet setback applies specifically to shared boundary lines with residential uses in I District and all property lines in R District.

Within the R Zoning District, the placement of all features and system components constituting the PSES shall be setback a minimum of fifty (50) feet from all property lines and street right of way lines. Other setback requirements include a 50 feet setback from shared boundary lines adjoining residential uses in the I Zoning District, but the specific setback from roads is the 50 feet in the R Zoning District.

Landscape screening shall include a minimum of two rows of native, green evergreen trees at least eight (8) feet in height at the time of planting, planted fifteen (15) feet on center and staggered, and shall be installed as follows: i. Within the I Zoning District, along all of the property lines of the lot where the PSES is situated that abut or is across from an existing residential use; or ii. Within the R Zoning District, along all of the property lines of the lot where the PSES is situated. iii. Planting species shall be native, and the use of white pine is prohibited.

The ordinance requires that "the actual surface area of all panels shall be considered impervious and require stormwater management design complying with the Greenwich Township Stormwater Management Ordinance." It prohibits locating the PSES "on soils designated as prime agricultural soils as determined by the current soil survey of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Floodplain Area(s) as defined in the Greenwich Township Floodplain Ordinance No. 2012-004, wetlands, or slopes exceeding twenty-five percent (25%)" and states that "clear cutting of wooded areas for placement of the PSES shall not be permitted." Upon decommissioning, "disturbed earth shall be graded and re-seeded unless the landowner requests in writing that the access roads or other land surface areas not be restored." These requirements apply specifically to Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES).

The minimum lot size for placement of a PSES shall be twenty (20) acres. Within the I Zoning District, the placement of all features and system components constituting the PSES shall comply with the setback and maximum lot coverage requirements of the aforementioned district. If the PSES is upon a lot that adjoins another lot with an existing residential use then all features and system components shall be setback a minimum of fifty (50) feet from that shared boundary line. Within the R Zoning District, the placement of all features and system components constituting the PSES shall be setback a minimum of fifty (50) feet from all property lines and street right of way lines. Within the aforementioned district, the maximum lot coverage of the PSES shall not exceed sixty-five percent (65%). PSES ground mounted systems shall not exceed twelve (12) feet in height. Buildings constituting or relating to the PSES shall comply with the underlying zoning district requirements for maximum building height. The PSES shall be enclosed with an eight (8) foot tall, chain-link fence having self-locking gates. Landscape screening shall include a minimum of two rows of native, green evergreen trees at least eight (8) feet in height at the time of planting, planted fifteen (15) feet on center and staggered, with specific planting requirements depending on the district. These detailed conditions indicate that PSES are allowed uses in these districts but must comply with zoning and permitting conditions, implying a special use or similar approval process. Other districts mentioned in the text only reference Accessory Solar Energy Systems (ASES), not PSES.

The ordinance requires the applicant proposing to erect a PSES to submit a Scenic Viewshed Mitigation Plan addressing if and how the outlooks along Kittatinny Ridge and the Appalachian Trail will be impacted. This is part of the submission requirements along with a Land Development Plan, project summary, glare analysis report, decommissioning documents, and other relevant studies or agreements. Additionally, landscape screening with native evergreen trees is mandated along property lines adjoining or across from residential uses or within the R Zoning District. The PSES must comply with setbacks, maximum lot coverage, height limits, and other design and operational standards. The relevant text states: 'and/or a Scenic Viewshed Mitigation Plan addressing if and how the outlooks along Kittatinny Ridge and the Appalachian Trail will be impacted.'

Section 7 - Decommissioning Principal Solar Energy Systems requires: an affidavit or similar evidence signed by the property owner and PSES facility owner affirming a lease agreement with a decommissioning provision binding Successors and Assigns; notification to the Township immediately upon cessation or abandonment of operation; presumption of abandonment if no electricity is generated for twelve (12) consecutive months without remedial action; removal of the PSES within eighteen (18) months of cessation or abandonment or Township may commence action; posting a bond or surety before construction to ensure proper decommissioning; submission of a new estimate of decommissioning cost every ten (10) years with revised surety bond; and restoration of any earth disturbance to an environmentally stable condition.
section: Section 7 - Decommissioning Principal Solar Energy Systems

summary: All ground mounted PSES shall be completely enclosed by fencing that consists of a minimum six (6) foot high fence to prevent entry by unauthorized persons. Screening between Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy System facilities and adjoining residential properties may consist of at least six feet high opaque decorative fencing, or a double staggered row of evergreen trees, or other locally available tree, at least four feet high planted and spaced to create a continuous visual buffer within 5 years, a natural wooded buffer least 25 feet in width, or other acceptable screening approved by the Township.

Section 6(f) states: 'All PSES shall be situated to minimize glare onto nearby structures and roadways.' This is an explicit glare restriction applying to Principal Solar Energy Systems. Other relevant standards for PSES include setbacks, screening, maintenance, and safety requirements, but these do not specifically address glare.

The ordinance explicitly states: 'No Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy System facilities shall exceed a height of 25 feet.' This is the maximum structure height allowed for Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES). No other height restrictions for PSES are provided. The unit of measurement is feet.

No Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy System facilities shall be located within 50 feet of a property line or the right of way of a public roadway. This shall not preclude the location of driveways or fencing which shall be setback a minimum of 10 feet from property lines. If the PSES occupies two or more adjacent properties, setbacks between the adjacent properties shall be waived along the shared property boundaries so that the PSES may be installed continuously and make the most efficient use of the project area.

No Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy System facilities shall be located within 50 feet of a property line or the right of way of a public roadway. This shall not preclude the location of driveways or fencing which shall be setback a minimum of 10 feet from property lines. If the PSES occupies two or more adjacent properties, setbacks between the adjacent properties shall be waived along the shared property boundaries so that the PSES may be installed continuously and make the most efficient use of the project area. Additionally, unless specific permission is obtained from the holder of an easement or right-of-way, ground mounted PSES shall not be placed within any legal easement or right-of-way location where solar would impede the operation of the facilities occupying the easement or right-of-way. At a minimum, a 25’ wide access road must be provided from a state or township roadway into the site, with a minimum 12’ wide cartway for maintenance and emergency vehicles.

Screening shall be required between Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy System facilities and adjoining properties on which residential uses are located. This screening may consist of any of the following: at least six feet high opaque decorative fencing, or a double staggered row of evergreen trees, or other locally available tree, at least four feet high planted and spaced to create a continuous visual buffer within 5 years, a natural wooded buffer least 25 feet in width, or other acceptable screening approved by the Township. All ground mounted PSES shall be completely enclosed by fencing that consists of a minimum six (6) foot high fence to prevent entry by unauthorized persons.

Section 6(c) states: 'Appropriate safety/warning signage concerning voltage shall be placed at ground mounted electrical devices, equipment, and structures.' This signage requirement applies explicitly to Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES) as defined in the ordinance. No other specific signage requirements for PSES are mentioned in the text.

Section 6(b) states that before construction may commence all Principal Use Solar Energy Systems developments must comply with all applicable Federal, State and local regulations and have permits required by any governmental regulatory agency with jurisdiction over any aspect of the development. Such requirements shall include, but shall not be limited to, Soil Erosion and Sedimentation Plans, and NPDES Plans, and Uniform Construction Code permits. Section 6(a) requires that plans for the development meet the requirements of the Township’s Stormwater Management Ordinance, Floodplain Management Ordinance, and all other applicable Township Ordinances and comply with plans approved in accord with those applicable regulations. These provisions explicitly enact soil, erosion, and sediment control requirements for PSES developers. Other options or conditions mentioned include compliance with the Uniform Construction Code and other fire and life safety requirements, but these are not directly related to soil, erosion, or sediment control.

No Ground Mounted Principal Solar Energy System facilities shall be located within 300 feet of any residential building. (Section 6(i)) Other setback requirements include a 50 feet setback from property lines or public roadway rights of way (Section 6(h)), but this does not pertain to occupied dwellings or residences.

Principal Use Solar Energy Systems shall not be permitted in (a) designated Floodplain Districts as determined by FEMA, (b) wetlands, (c) within 200 feet of the banks of streams, lakes and watercourses, or (d) within Prime Farmlands as designated by the Natural Resources Conservation Service of the US. Department of Agriculture or other Federal or State Agency.

The ordinance specifies a maximum land coverage of 50% for Solar Farms under the Minimum Lot Requirements sections (51.5.4 and 51.9.4). The text states: '9. Solar Farm 10 acres 100 50%' and '4. Solar Farm 10 acres 100 50%'. This 50% refers to the maximum land coverage allowed, expressed as a percentage of the lot area, for Solar Farms defined as large-scale installations generating electricity for commercial use.

summary: The ordinance explicitly sets a minimum lot size of 10 acres for Solar Farm as a conditional use. This is stated in sections 51.5.4 and 51.9.4 under 'Minimum Lot Requirements' for 'Conditional Uses' with the entry: '9. Solar Farm 10 acres 100 50%' and '4. Solar Farm 10 acres 100 50%'. The unit 'acres' is used to specify the area for the minimum lot size.

Other districts only mention 'Personal Solar Panels' as Accessory Uses, which do not apply to large or commercial solar farms. No solar overlay districts are included in the text.

summary: The owner or operator of a Major Energy System or the landowner shall complete decommissioning within 12 months after the end of the useful life. Decommissioning includes removal of panels, buildings, electrical components, roads to a depth of sixty (60) inches, and any foundation to a minimum depth of sixty (60) inches below grade or to bedrock. The site must be stabilized, graded, and cleared of debris, and seeded if not used for agriculture. If decommissioning is not completed timely, the Township may designate a contractor to complete it, charging the violator and/or placing a lien on the property. A bond must be provided if the system is not owned by the landowner. An independent certified engineer will estimate decommissioning costs, and the owner/operator/landowner must post and maintain Decommissioning Funds equal to or greater than net decommissioning costs, with a performance bond made out to Hanover Township. Failure to maintain the bond is a violation and may result in ceasing operation until reposted. The Township may take necessary measures to complete decommissioning if the owner/operator/landowner fails to do so. These requirements apply specifically to Major Solar Energy Systems as defined in the ordinance.

The ordinance defines a 'solar energy farm' as an installation where energy generated is sold for use on an energy grid system. It sets forth specific standards for solar energy farms, including that if any solar energy farm is not in service for 12 continuous months, the solar panels and all related equipment must be removed. The applicant must demonstrate the manner of abandonment and removal, and if removal is not completed within six months after the 12-month abandonment period, the Township will issue a written notice to remove within 30 days. To secure removal and restoration obligations, the applicant must provide a bond or other financial assurance. Other conditions include minimum lot size, setback and height requirements, fencing, buffering, landscaping, compliance with codes, underground wiring, and operational agreements, among others.
section: SECTION 5: The Hanover Township Zoning Ordinance Chapter 185 is hereby amended by amending Section 185-54.E Specific Standards for Conditional Uses

summary: All aboveground solar energy farm facilities shall be surrounded by a minimum eight-foot-high fence with a self-locking gate to prevent or restrict unauthorized persons or vehicles from entering the property on which the facility is located. Warning signs shall be placed on the fence, barrier, or system at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations to inform individuals of potential voltage hazards.
section: Section 185-54.E(37)(e) Specific Standards for Conditional Uses - Solar energy farm

summary: A Major Energy Solar System shall require a minimum lot size of not less than 30 acres. This is explicitly stated in section M. No other minimum lot size values are provided for Major Solar Energy Systems in the text. The unit 'acres' is the standard area measurement used.

Section 185-54.E(37)(a) states: 'Solar energy farms shall be located on properties with a minimum lot size of five acres.' This minimum lot size applies specifically to solar energy farms, defined as installations where energy generated is sold for use on an energy grid system rather than consumed on site, i.e., utility-scale solar energy systems.
section: Section 185-54.E Specific Standards for Conditional Uses

summary: A Major Solar Energy System shall be a minimum of one thousand (1,000') feet from any zoning district boundary line and property line of existing residential or public use. It shall not be located within five hundred (500') feet of a public or private road right-of-way, nor within one hundred (100') feet from all other property lines. Additionally, it shall provide a fifty (50') foot planted buffer/screen along all property lines.

A twenty-foot-wide landscaped planting strip shall be provided along all front, side and rear property lines except as otherwise required under Subsection (f) above (§185-54.E(37)(g)(a)). All required trees, shrubs and yard ground cover "shall be native trees and shrubs from a list developed by the Hellam Township Environmental Advisory Council (EAC)." Vegetative screen must provide "a minimum capacity of 80% in winter and 80% in summer." The ordinance provides three planting arrangement options: (a) three staggered rows including one row of fast-growing needled evergreens spaced not more than 12 feet on center and two rows of deciduous trees spaced not more than 25 feet on center; (b) two staggered rows with 75% fast-growing needled evergreens planted 10 feet on center and 25% deciduous trees in staggered clusters spaced 25 feet apart; (c) two staggered rows with 75% fast-growing needled evergreens planted 10 feet on center, 15% deciduous trees in staggered clusters 25 feet on center, and 10% staggered shrub masses as understory plants with shrubs spaced four feet on center. Additionally, under "Sensitive Receptor Requirements," a "Buffer Strip width must be 30 feet wide," with "a fence of 8 feet high with no more than 2"  openings," and "all plantings must be at 75% growth at planting." The buffer strip and fence must extend for the total length of the adjacent parcel, or a minimum of 50 feet if the parcel line is longer. These requirements apply to PSES, defined as large-scale solar energy systems intended for off-site use, typically 20 MW or higher output. The ordinance also states "Ground mounted PSES shall be screened per the applicable zoning district."

Signage requires that "Clearly visible warning signs (no smaller than one (1) square foot) shall be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations, and on the fence surrounding the PSES, at intervals of 100 feet, informing barrier or perimeter of large-scale solar energy systems, to inform individuals of potential voltage hazards." It also states that "A solar energy system shall not be used to display advertising, including signage, streamers, pennants, spinners, reflectors, ribbons, tinsel, balloons, flags, banners or similar materials." However, "The manufacturers and equipment information, warning, or indication of ownership shall be allowed on any equipment of the solar energy system, provided they comply with the prevailing sign regulations." These requirements apply explicitly to Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES), which include Large-Scale Solar Systems normally referred to as Utility Grid Scale Systems with output normally 20 MW or higher, intended for off-site use. Other signage-related provisions for smaller systems (ASES) prohibit use for advertising and allow manufacturer's or installer's identification and warning signs if compliant with Township sign regulations, but these apply only to small solar energy systems (25 kW max).

The ordinance requires that "The applicant shall submit a Stormwater Management Plan that demonstrates compliance with the municipal stormwater management regulations." It further states that "Earth disturbance and grading activities shall be minimized and natural vegetative cover preserved and/or restored using native species as specified in applicable township ordinances." Low impact construction techniques must be utilized "in accordance with the latest edition of the Pennsylvania Stormwater Best Management Practices Manual." Vegetative cover must have "a minimum uniform 90% perennial vegetative cover between rows and 80% under panel arrays with a density capable of resisting accelerated erosion and sedimentation." Additional conditions include: meadows of native species for slopes of 5 to 15%, vegetation not cut or grazed below 4 inches, limited chemical applications, and gravel considered impervious unless it has an engineered pervious grid system. Panels must be placed on slopes of 15% or less with a minimum vertical clearance of 3 feet to promote vegetative growth. Agrivoltaics projects require a "Written Erosion and Sediment plan" to be developed and approved to control runoff. Upon removal of a ground-mounted solar energy system, "any earth disturbance as a result of the removal... shall be graded and reseeded within three (3) months or as soon as weather permits." During decommissioning, "Any soil exposed during the removal shall be stabilized in accordance with applicable erosion and sediment control standards and requirements." These requirements apply to Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES), including Large-Scale Solar Systems (Utility Grid Scale Systems) as defined by the ordinance.

Materials that cannot be re-sold or salvaged shall be disposed of at a facility authorized to dispose of such materials by federal or state law. summary: Any public solar-energy facility which has reached the end of its useful life or has been abandoned shall be removed. The owner or operator shall physically remove the installation no more than 150 days after the date of discontinued operations. The owner or operator shall notify the Code Enforcement Officer by certified mail of the proposed date of discontinued operations and plans for removal. Decommissioning shall consist of: (1) Physical removal of all solar-energy systems, structures, equipment, security barriers and transmission lines from the site. (2) Disposal of all solid and hazardous waste in accordance with local, state and federal waste disposal regulations. (3) Stabilization or revegetation of the site as necessary to minimize erosion. (4) Absent notice of a proposed date of decommissioning or written notice of extenuating circumstances, a public solar-energy facility shall be considered abandoned when it fails to operate for more than one year without having first obtained the written consent of the Code Enforcement Officer. (5) At the time of approval, the applicant/developer for a public solar-energy facility shall submit a performance guarantee (in the form of a letter of credit or a bond) to be renewed yearly in the amount of 10% of the estimated demolition costs of the facility, such cost to be determined by an independent engineer, licensed in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and approved by the Township Engineer. Prior to the 15th anniversary of the issuance of the building permit, the applicant shall provide an updated estimate for the decommissioning of the project prepared by an independent engineer licensed in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and approved by the Township Engineer and shall adjust the amount of the performance guarantee (letter of credit or bond), to be renewed yearly, to be equal to 100% of the estimated demolition cost of the system. The owner or operator may apply to the Township for release of the guarantee at such time that it or its assigns remove the facility and associated abandoned structures, and such completed removal is found to be satisfactory by the Code Enforcement Officer. (6) If the owner or operator of the public solar-energy system fails to remove the installation in accordance with the requirements of this section within 150 days of abandonment or the proposed date of decommissioning, the Township retains the right to use the performance guarantee and all other available means to cause an abandoned, hazardous, or decommissioned public solar-energy facility to be removed.

This applies specifically to Solar Energy Facilities (SEFs) as defined in the ordinance, which are "areas of land used for a solar collection system principally to capture solar energy, which is converted to electrical energy or thermal power and supplied primarily for offsite use."

summary: Section 3.F (Decommissioning) requires an affidavit or similar evidence signed by the property owner and PSES facility owner affirming a lease agreement with a decommissioning clause providing sufficient funds to dismantle and remove the PSES, including all solar-related equipment or appurtenances, and a successors and assigns clause binding successors. If the owner fails to dismantle and remove the PSES within 18 months, the Township may complete decommissioning at the owner's expense. The PSES owner must post a bond at application, in an amount determined by the Township's Engineer, to ensure proper decommissioning. The applicant must execute an agreement providing financial security equal to 125% of the estimated decommissioning cost, prepared by the applicant and approved by the Township Engineer. Financial security may be funds deposited with Juniata Township, a bond acceptable to Juniata Township, or an irrevocable letter of credit acceptable to Juniata Township. This agreement and financial security remain in effect until decommissioning and land restoration are complete. A new engineer's estimate and revised surety must be submitted every five years during operation. These requirements apply specifically to Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES), defined as systems principally used to supply power off-site, including ground-mounted systems. Other options or conditions mentioned include routine maintenance or replacements not requiring a permit, and that PSES constructed prior to the ordinance's effective date are not required to meet these terms unless expanded.

Section 3, Ground-Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems, subsection (7) Security And Warnings states: "In accordance with the National Electric Code (NEC), all ground-mounted PSES shall be completely enclosed by fencing with a locking gate. Current NEC code requires a minimum six-foot-high fence with barbed wire or a seven-foot-high fence." Additionally, subsection (5)(c) requires: "Perimeter fence shall be placed between shrubs and solar panels." These are explicit fencing requirements for Ground-Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems. Other related provisions include setback requirements for fencing: "fencing shall comply with the setbacks of the applicable Subdivision And Land Development Ordinance and zoning district."

The ordinance explicitly enacts glare restrictions for Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES), defined as systems "principally used to capture solar energy, convert it to electrical energy or thermal power and supply electrical or thermal power primarily for off-site use." Specifically, it states: "All PSES shall be situated to eliminate concentrated glare onto nearby structures or roadways." This is found in Section 3.A.(12). Other relevant provisions for PSES include setback requirements, height limits ("Ground-Mounted PSES solar panels shall not exceed Eighteen (< 18’) feet in height"), and stormwater management. The ordinance also includes glare restrictions for Accessory Solar Energy Systems (ASES), but those apply to smaller, primarily on-site use systems and are not relevant to PSES. The PSES glare restriction is a clear, direct requirement that an energy system developer must abide by.

The ordinance explicitly states: 'Ground-Mounted PSES solar panels shall not exceed Eighteen (< 18’) feet in height.' Other height limits mentioned, such as 25 feet, apply only to Ground-Mounted Accessory Solar Energy Systems (ASES), which are smaller or non-commercial systems and thus not applicable here. The unit for this height restriction is feet.

The ordinance states: 'The minimum lot size of each property upon which the PSES is to be installed shall be at least Thirty-Five (> 35 acrs.) acres.' This provision is intended to prohibit the joinder or combination of one or more contiguous lots so as to meet the minimum size requirement imposed by this provision. Shrubs shall be planted adjacent to or outside of the road right-of-way. Solar perimeter fence shall be placed between shrubs and solar panels." For residential buffer screening, it "may be slat fencing or a row of evergreen conifers or broadleaf evergreens spaced in accordance with the chosen species to achieve a continuous visual barrier reaching six feet to eight (6’ — 8’) feet in height within Two (< 2 yrs.) years of planting." Screening may be a combination of plantings and/or structures with prior approval by the Township. Reasonable modifications to these requirements may be requested through Section 4(C), Modifications. The perimeter fence shall be placed between shrubs and solar panels. Widespread use of herbicides to control ground cover growth is prohibited.

The ordinance explicitly requires signage for Ground-Mounted Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES) under section 3, paragraph (7) 'Security And Warnings': 'a clearly visible warning sign shall be placed at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations and on the fence surrounding the PSES informing individuals of potential voltage hazards.' Additionally, paragraph (11) states 'Signage shall comply with the prevailing sign regulations.' These are the explicit signage requirements for PSES. No other signage options or conditions are provided.

The ordinance requires that "all PSES Applications after the effective date of this Ordinance shall be required to meet the terms and conditions of the Juniata Township Code, including but not limited to any rules and regulations pertaining to Stormwater Management and the Subdivision And Land Development Ordinance’s Observance Of Performance Standards." It further states that "Stormwater runoff from a PSES shall be managed in accordance with the requirements of either the Huntingdon County Stormwater Management Ordinance and/or the Pennsylvania Stormwater Management Act, whichever requirements are most exacting." Additionally, "all necessary stormwater plan approval, Erosion And Soil Permits, and National Pollutant Discharge Elimination Permits must be approved prior to receiving final Council approval of the Land Development Plan." Upon removal of a Ground-Mounted PSES, "any earth disturbance as a result of the removal of the Ground-Mounted solar energy system must be returned to an environmentally stable condition." These requirements apply specifically to Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES), which are defined as systems "principally used to capture solar energy, convert it to electrical energy or thermal power and supply electrical or thermal power primarily for off-site use."

The ordinance states: 'The maximum lot coverage shall be 75% and the area of the solar collectors shall be included in the calculation of lot coverage.' This applies to commercial solar power generation facilities with a minimum parcel size of 10 acres, consistent with utility-scale solar energy systems. The coverage is expressed as a percentage of the lot area.

The applicant shall provide details about anticipated glare from the facility, including the time of day, time of year and direction of peak glare periods and document how potential nuisances to area properties and on public roads shall be controlled. This applies to solar power facilities with a minimum parcel size of 10 acres, which are commercial solar power facilities.

The ordinance states: 'The minimum parcel size shall be 10 acres.' This minimum parcel size applies to solar power facilities, which are described in the text as commercial solar power generation facilities, implying utility-scale systems. No other minimum lot size values are provided for utility-scale solar energy systems in the text.

The setback for solar collectors, all structures, equipment containers and any associated mechanical facilities shall be 100 feet from property lines. This applies to commercial solar power facilities with a minimum parcel size of 10 acres, indicating utility-scale systems intended for offsite electricity generation or sale.

Section C(3) Landscaping states: 'Landscaping may be required to screen as much of the solar power facility ground features as possible, the fence surrounding the support structure, and any other ground level features (such as a building), and in general buffer the solar power facility ground features from neighboring properties.' The Township may permit 'any combination of existing vegetation, topography, walls, decorative fences or other features instead of landscaping, if the same achieves the same degree of screening as the required landscaping.'

Section C(12) requires "a clearly visible warning sign concerning voltage" at the base of all pad-mounted transformers and substations. It also mandates that "visible, reflective, colored objects, such as flags, reflectors, or tape shall be placed on the anchor points of guy wires and along the guy wires up to a height of 10 feet from the ground." Section C(13) states that "No advertising material or signs other than warning, manufacturer and equipment information or indication of ownership shall be allowed on any equipment of structures." These signage requirements apply to commercial solar power facilities with a minimum parcel size of 10 acres, consistent with utility-scale solar energy systems.

The ordinance regulates the construction, operation, and decommissioning of Large-Scale Solar Electric Energy Facilities. It applies to any Solar Energy Facility of two (2) acres or more. Section 9 (Decommissioning) requires the Facility Owner and Operator to notify Lake Township immediately upon cessation or abandonment of the operation. Decommissioning must be completed within twelve (12) months after the end of the useful life, including removal of all Solar Electric Energy Systems, buildings, cabling, electrical components, roads, foundations, and restoration of disturbed earth to its original condition. The Facility Owner and Operator must obtain an independent professional engineer's appraisal to determine decommissioning costs and provide a financial security (letter of credit or surety bond) covering at least 110% of the estimated costs. The security must name Lake Township as sole payee and be maintained until restoration is complete, with reviews every five years. The ordinance excludes Solar Electric Energy Systems meant for onsite residential or commercial use and does not apply retroactively to facilities constructed before the ordinance's effective date unless materially altered.

The facility owner and operator shall, at their expense, complete decommissioning of the solar electric energy facility or individual solar electric systems within 12 months after the end of the useful life of such facility or system. A solar electric energy facility or system will be presumed to be at the end of its useful life if no electricity is generated for a continuous period of 12 months. Decommissioning shall include removal of all solar electric energy systems, buildings, cabling, electrical components, roads, foundations and any other associated facilities. Disturbed earth shall be graded and re-seeded, unless the landowner requests in writing that the access roads or other land surface areas not be restored. The estimated cost of decommissioning shall be secured by a bond or such other security to ensure the completed decommissioning of the Solar Electric Energy components. The estimate will be reevaluated every three years to maintain the correct bond or security amount is accurate for decommissioning costs.

Section 7.D.1 states: 'A Solar Electric Energy Facility shall be enclosed by a fence, barrier or other appropriate means to prevent or restrict unauthorized persons or vehicles from entering the property.' This fencing requirement applies to Large-Scale Solar Electric Energy Facilities, defined as facilities whose main purpose is to generate and supply electricity and which are not meant for onsite residential or commercial use. No other fencing options or conditions are provided in the ordinance.

A solar electric energy facility shall be enclosed by a fence with a minimum height of seven feet, barrier or other appropriate means to prevent or restrict unauthorized persons or vehicles from entering the property. Welding wire fencing is preferred over chain link fencing. Clearly visible warning signs shall be placed on the fence, barrier or solar electric energy facility perimeter to inform individuals of potential voltage hazards. Where in the judgment of the Board of Supervisors, and concerns of neighboring property owners, natural vegetation may be required along the perimeter fencing. In the event that natural vegetation is dead, it shall be replaced within 90 days of said event, or, in the event of winter, by the first of May.

The ordinance defines a solar farm as being located on a parcel or combined parcels of land with a minimum acreage of 20 acres. This is explicitly stated in the definition section: 'The solar farm shall be located on a parcel or combined parcels of land with a minimum acreage of 20 acres.' The units are acres, a standard area measurement.

Section 8.A states: 'All Solar Electric Energy Systems shall be located one hundred feet (100’) from all property lines where the System is located. These distances shall be measured from the closest edge of the Solar Electric Energy System to the property line.' No other setback distances or multipliers based on height or other factors are provided for property lines, lot lines, facility perimeters, parcels, or subdivisions.

§ 382-44 D (Fencing and warnings) requires that "clearly visible warning signs shall be placed on the fence, barrier or solar electric energy facility perimeter to inform individuals of potential voltage hazards." This is the only explicit signage requirement for Large-Scale Solar Electric Energy Facilities (Solar Farms) in the ordinance. §27-1703, Paragraph 5, Decommissioning requires: an affidavit signed by the property owner and PSES facility owner affirming a lease agreement with a decommissioning clause providing sufficient funds to dismantle and remove the PSES and related equipment; the PSES owner must notify the Township immediately upon cessation or abandonment of operation, with abandonment presumed if no electricity is generated for 12 continuous months without remedial action; if the PSES owner fails to dismantle and/or remove the PSES within 18 months, the Township may complete decommissioning at the property owner’s expense; the applicant must execute an agreement with the Municipality providing financial security equal to 125% of the estimated decommissioning cost, subject to Municipality approval and adjustment every five years; financial security options include funds deposited with the Municipality, a bond, or an irrevocable letter of credit from an acceptable entity; the agreement and financial security remain in effect until decommissioning and land restoration are complete; costs not covered by financial security are the owner's liability; all costs incurred by the Municipality in reviewing estimates or enforcing the agreement must be paid by the PSES owner within ten days of billing.
